product_title: Clarks Men's Wave Scree Easy Slip-On Shoe
review_headline: Great Looks, Good Buy, Needs Breaking In
review_body:
I love Clarks shoes. I know what size to buy, even on line, and they are always very comfortable (eventually). I say eventually since they all come a little tight for me in width, but within a few months they are perfect. And after 3 - 5 years, they are downright loose and have to be replaced. I especially like Clarks slip-on shoes since that's the kind of guy I am, but I always put these kind of shoes on with a long shoe horn. Yes, as one person mentioned, these shoes are a little tight on the top of the foot at first, but this is the way all Clarks slips-ons start. And since these particular shoes are waterproof, I would expect them to be a little stiffer than the others. After a few months, these shoes will fit like a glove, just like all of my other Clarks slip-ons. What sold me on this particular style was the looks and the bargain basement price. Maybe because this style is being phased out. However, in a few years, I suspect that I will regret not buying a second pair to replace these. I was originally after the nice looking Wave Quest GTX from Clarks, but at $160.00 a pair, I'll wait for them to come down in price, maybe next year. I'll do an update if I feel differently about these shoes in a month or two. As an aside, I was only able to get these from the vendor called "What's Hot" and they sent me a pair of shoes that didn't even come close to matching. Thanks to Amazon, the return and replacement was a breeze, but be carful when ordering from this vendor. They are probably OK, just an absent minded employee.
Update: 11/8/15 - These are now my most comfortable shoes, as expected after break-in. Yes, at first there was some tightness across the top of these shoes as a few have mentioned, but this is normal for well fitting slip-ons. The advantage of a slip-on is no laces to tie, but the disadvantage is that you have to use a shoehorn to get them on easily, especially if you want them to fit like a glove after break-in. Slip-ons that are too loose don't support you foot very well, especially when walking down hill. Love these shoes now. Might just buy another pair for when these wear out since the price is right.at are too loose don't support you foot very well, especially when walking down hill. Love these shoes now. Might just buy another pair for when these wear out since the price is right.

product_title: Minnetonka Women's Silverthorne Thong Sandal
review_headline: I love the look and comfort, but the shoe is not holding up
review_body:
For years, friends have raved about comfortable Minnetonka shoes are. Since I found this sandal and loved the look, I purchased them with high expectations.

Pros:
- love the look. they are my most versatile summer shoe.
- comfort. Very comfortable.
- sizing. I usually wear a size 9B and these are a size 9B

Cons:
- quality of the bed of the shoe

I have worn these quite a bit over the past year, but not enough for the shoes to begin falling apart. The material under the big toe on my right foot started flaking off and showing a very stark white color. Every time I wear them, a bit more comes off (now a little larger than the size of a nickel) and now the same spot on my left foot is starting to flake. Early on, it was limited to directly underneath the toe, so as long as you had the sandal on your foot, it didn't show. Since one of the things I love about summer sandals is the ability to slip them off to get extra comfortable, this was definitely a negative. Now, the flaking is extending all the way to the inside edge of the bed so the white shows even when the sandal is being worn. I am going to try to buy some black nail polish to cover it and see if that helps. The rest of the shoe is wearing exactly as I would expect but unless I can darken the BRIGHT white now showing, they will be unwearable. I will definitely be hesitant to purchase additional shoes from this company that I would plan on wearing daily. Would be fine for less frequent usage, I would think.

product_title: Wolverine 1000 Mile Men's Wolverine 1000 Mile Boots
review_headline: Would probably buy another pair, but expect to have to customize them a bit again.
review_body:
I bought a pair of these boots in early 2012 from a local vendor....so this is a post-three year review. They were the black leather ones. I've worn them through several Boston winters and the uppers held up perfectly fine as long as you take care of them....salt in particular will mess up leather...even the nicest of leathers....so some care/upkeep is needed on these...but again that goes for all nice things. The only real (minor) issue with the leather is that the dye is not very deep...minor scrapes on black (or I imagine other off-natural colors) immediately shows and only shoe polish of the right color takes care of it.

The laces that shipped with broke after a year, so I replaced them with more durable ones. Meh no biggie.

The original heel was junk and wore out exceedingly quick....this is sort of expected since I walk five miles a day or so routinely on concrete, but was still sorta weird how quick it went....I had it replaced at the four month mark. What was a bit more disappointing was that the outsole went bad really quickly. In particular the outsole on these did not do well with any sort of moisture...be it from a rainy fall/spring or winter. Now I know these are "dress boots", but all it took was a few rainy days of walking into work on concrete to cause legit wear to the outsole... (and yes I do dry my boots every night after I wear them...)Thankfully I monitored this and then went and got rubber outsoles put on the boots after the first six months. They look fine...better I'd say actually and have been far more durable....basically they've lasted ~3 times as long as the original outsole...same with the second heel I got...although I'll need to be replacing that again soon too.

The uppers on these have been fantastic and have broken in very nicely...no complaints there. I have probably walked 1000 miles in these things, albeit with different heels and outsoles based on what they shipped with. I am considering getting another pair in a different color, but I just wish they'd ship these things with a more practical heel and outsole rather than keep the ones that are on now. I'd even bet the things would be slightly cheaper since you'd be using rubber rather than whatever leather/stuff they use now. This is the one thing preventing me from just buying another one....it'll cost ~$60 to refit these boots once I get them with a heel and outsole that will last and at that point I might as well just be shopping for a slightly better pair.

Oh well.ering getting another pair in a different color, but I just wish they'd ship these things with a more practical heel and outsole rather than keep the ones that are on now. product_title: BCBGMAXAZRIA Women's Printz Pump
review_body: GORGEOUS shoe; beautiful deep blood red color.  The snake embossed leather is nice, although no one will mistake it for actual snakeskin.  The only complaint I have - but it's a HUGE one - is in the design of the padded footbed.  It is amazingly soft and thick, and at first glance appears to be a MOST comfy shoe.  However, the problem lies in the fact that the padding doesn't span the entire bottom of the shoe.  It stops shy of the edge by about 1/8 of an inch all around, including the toe box.  So, when you stand in the shoe, the ball of your foot actually misses the padded portion and lands in a rock-hard valley between the padding and the wall of the shoe. Also, toes slip on and off the padding as weight is distributed during a step.  They are beautiful, but totally unwearable.  I am REALLY disappointed!

product_title: RFID Wallet Wristlet with Front Pocket in Leather - RFID Blocking Wallets for Women
review_headline: Ultimate wallet/wrislet for travelers and shopping
review_body: This is an absolutely GREAT and attractive wallet/wristlet.  I am very picky about quality and utility and this hits all the marks.  I travel extensively for work and this wallet has made my life so much easier in airports, and give me peace of mind with the RFID blocking. It is the perfect size to find by feel in the "mother ship" (my purse).  The wristlet holds my 4 most important credit cards plus my drivers license, and has a separate pocket for cash.  I just checked and have 17 bills in the cash pocket, and there is no impact on closure and no bulging.  The cash is easy to get in and out. A change pocket is not available and would be nice to have, but would probably defeat this design.  The credit cards are a little tight in the pockets, but I actually prefer this.  When the wallet is unzipped while checking in luggage, etc., the tightness means the cards do not slip out of the pockets and on to the floor.  As far as phones, I have a Blackberry Z30 which is large and barely fits in the phone pocket.  It does "just" fit however and the magnetic closure is strong enough to hold it in without any fear whatsoever of the phone slipping out.  One of the best things about this wristlet is to be able to grab it out of the "mother ship" to go shopping without a heavy purse on my shoulder.  It is so light on my wrist, however, I have to make sure it is there sometimes.  This is a good thing.  I have had this wristlet in heavy use over 3 months (and many miles) and it still looks brand new.  Very, very happy.  I get a lot of compliments on it also.  I paid $32 for this 3 months ago and am very happy to see it for $18 now!!!  I thought I was getting a deal at $32! I put another in to my cart before writing this review as I want to make sure I have a backup in the future.  Cannot recommend this highly enough for a frequent traveler.

review_headline: They performed beautifully. When I got home
review_body: I bought a pair of these shoes to wear on a trip to France last summer where I expected to be walking in wet, muddy conditions.  They performed beautifully.  When I got home, I ordered another pair right away as I loved them so much.  Unfortunately in the interim, Merrell changed the lining from Gore Tex to something cheaper that is nowhere close to waterproof.  Pure crap.  Feet soaked every day to the point that after a few months the shoes came unglued at the inner ball-of-foot area. Smelled like hell and I had to throw them away.  I am so disgusted.  I feel like a victim of the classic bait and switch.  Shame on you Merrell, I will never buy another pair of your shoes, nor will I ever recommend anyone else do so.

product_title: Ray-Ban RB2140 Original Wayfarer Sunglasses
review_headline: Original Wayfarer vs "New Wayfarer"... It's all about attitude
review_body:
I've been wearing the Original Wayfarer sunglasses for over 35 years. Back then, you didn't need to call them "Original", because there was only one Ray-Ban Wayfarer. Ray-Ban now makes a newer version that they say is a modern interpretation of the Original.

They say the "New Wayfarer" looks more natural on your face. The angles of the lenses are drastically toned down, and the lenses are smaller and more natural looking. I couldn't agree more. That's why I don't like the "New Wayfarer".

A friend told me he always loved my Wayfarers, but never bought a pair because he didn't think they looked natural on his face. That's when I explained to him that they don't look natural on ANYONE'S face, and that's the point. People wear them BECAUSE they look don't look natural.

That's why so many A-List celebrities wear Original Wayfarers. It's all about attitude.

When I explained this to my friend, he finally "got it", and that changed everything for him. He realized they didn't look any more natural on my face than his, but they did fit my attitude. I wear them with pride, and I'm equally comfortable wearing them in T-shirts and jeans as I am at a black tie event.

product_title: BARON of MALTZAHN Men's biker wallet Wallet with chain BLOOMBERG brown leather
review_headline: I've owned this wallet a year, offers unrivaled durability and storage
review_body:
I purchased this walker about a year ago and I could not be any happier with it. Although I'm no biker, the wallet is still perfect for me. It is the best wallet I have ever owned. I say this for several reasons.
The 1st deals with the craftsmanship of the wallet. The wallet in question consists of hand proccesed, unrefined natural bovine leather along with gun metal fittings.
The 2nd reason I'm so fond of this wallet is deal with storage. There are two protected id compartments, a large coin pocket, two inner flaps for cards and documents, 12 card slots, two extra compartments, and two slots for bills.
The 3rd reason I've grown to love this wallet deals with its durability, like I said I've owned it a year and it's still in great shape, I've owned so many wallets (ones that cost significantly more than this) only to have them rip, fray, or tear after a couple months or in some cases even weeks after purchasing, not this one. You can feel the quality of this wallet just upon holding it.
I should note that this is a relatively bulky wallet, you will know it's in your pocket at all times, something I actually like.
With all that being said, if you're in the market for a wallet that offers unrivaled durability and storage, I highly suggest you give this one a shot, you won't be disappointed, it's a year later and I'm still pleased.

review_headline: A WORKHORSE FOR A BUSY WOMAN
review_body: It's not feminine, not necessarily pretty, but an AWESOME, INDESTRUCTIBLE bag. You can STUFF it to the gills. Even the most disorganized person can find her stuff easily! You can not believe how much this bag holds. I would imagine it will last for years! Excellent quality, zippers never fail, you can move the strap length easily, and it is water resistant. I'm in my mid-50's and while I sometimes wish the bag was more fashionable, for what I have to carry, this bag is just unbeatable. It's "OLD RELIABLE" for sure! I work outdoors, and I;ve went through my fair share of eyewear over the years. And I've bought sunglasses near around the $30 price point that really weren't as good as these.

Like I said, they've been pretty durable. Unlike some other brands I've tried, these haven't fallen apart because of the heat. And the lenses are quite scratch resistant. Though it's obviously not scratch proof. The frame itself is light enough that I barely notice I'm wearing anything on my face. The entire unit is designed well enough that it has the all important feature of keeping direct sunlight out of my unprotected eyeballs. So basically these do everything that I needed them to do. So I can't say anything more than that these are a great pair on sunglasses for the price point.

review_headline: Does NOT fit like Originals Men's SL 72
review_body:
These shoes are comfortable and stylish.

Interestingly these shoes do not fit like these SL 72 shoes: http://www.amazon.com/Adidas-SL-Mens-Running-Shoes/dp/B00G4BU9BO

The linked to SL 72 shoes lean significantly to the inside. I've bought two pairs of the linked SL 72s and they both lean a bit to the inside.

The item being sold here does not lean to the inside, which I prefer.

A big downside of these shoes is that Adidas will certainly either discontinue them quickly, or at least Adidas will again keep the name and redo the sneaker making unwary buyers buy something different from last purchase (kind of like ROM sneaker from 2005 which became more like SAMBA sneaker a few years back). It's already confusing that there are two sneakers with different fits that are both named SL 72. But even worse is when Adidas will cancel and not say what new sneaker fits like this one. Great manufacturing, great quality, good prices, awful marketing.

product_title: Nike Men's Air Zoom Structure 18 Running Shoes
review_headline: Intially felt good, heel is squishy, sole wears extremely fast.
review_body:
These shoes are very good at first, but with age, they feel more like bedroom slippers.

The sole wore out very fast, and I don't even run on pavement.

Initially, I thought these were an improvement over my Brooks Adrenaline, but I feel otherwise now.

The main problem I have with them is the squishy heel. The bevel canting seems to control pronation well, but the midsole is squishy enough in the heel that I think it is extra strain on my Achilles.

If you have good and loose Achilles tendons, go for it. It is more of a forefoot type shoe, I'd suggest something else if you are a heavy runner.ed these shoes is really on their game. I am glad to have my legs feel young again. It is unbelievable. There is plenty of room in the toe box, and you will find yourself progressively tightening the laces for the first runs. The cushioning in the forefoot is slightly better than the Adrenalines. You will still feel large gravels if you run on dirt roads, but not as acutely. The shift of the foot plant to the forefoot will give you better placement accuracy on gravel. I also think these are slightly cooler then the Adrenalines, perhaps due to the thinner tongue. My feet do not do well with hot shoes. This is an incredible shoe that has changed my life. I am wearing the same size in this as I did the Adrenaline, but this seems a wee larger. In fact, as I progressively tighten the laces every couple of runs, I am wondering if I would have done better to go one size smaller.

product_title: David Tate Women's Country Pumps Shoes
review_headline: Perfect width, needed to replace liner for arch support and comfort
review_body: These shoes are well made, fit as I expected in the 10WW.  However, my feet hurt on the bottom of the foot.  There is not enough arch support either (my arch is rather high), so I took out the removable liner and replaced it with the liner from Vionic 10 W suede moccasins that I own.  Problem solved.  Vionic's liner provides needed support in the arch, and provides cushioning for my aging feet bottoms that have lost much of their own natural cushioning.  I am tall and 68 years old, and don't want to completely give up on shoes with heels.  Once the Vionic liners were in, I feel I can walk and stand at work in these David Tate shoes.  I have a pair of Tate low heel pumps, and I have had to do the same thing with them so that the shoe bottoms are well cushioned for my feet.  I do like the double width that David Tate shoes offer though, so it is worth it for me to make these small adjustments in the liners.  I was lucky to get these shoes in WW, which is hard to find.  So, ladies who might have very wide, problem, or aging feet, don't give up on Tate shoes.  I was able to purchase this pair for $40, which was over $60 less than the original price.

product_title: Zubits - magnetic lacing solution - Never Tie Laces Again! Size #1 Kids / Size #2 Adults / Size #3 Performance
review_headline: Not worth the Hassle...unless you like semi-snug or loose-fitting shoes.
review_body:
I had some reservations in the beginning. Could this product really work? Isn't it kinda pricey? I mean, really...$22 so I don’t have to tie my shoelaces. Really??? Then they were delivered.

First thing I did was look for the instructions. Ha! There were none. No big problem. I just Googled “Zubits Instructions” and there they were. But wouldn’t you think for twenty-two bucks there would be instructions? I did. Seems you would want your customers to be able to start using your product right out of the box. That’s just good business sense.

If you think all you have to do is re-lace your shoes to accommodate the Zubits, you would be wrong. It is a trial and error fit and the instructions (now that I had them) even suggests you may have to tie, retie, and retie your laces again for the best fit.

Finally, my shoes were laced into the Zubits and it worked as advertized...sorta. You have to be careful when closing the Zubits that they do not grab anything between the underneath side of the Zubits and the top surface of your shoe. The magnets are strong and if you are not careful, they will grab the surface of your shoe and not provide the needed magnetic seal.

Knowing what I now know, I would not recommend Zubits...unless it is really-really worth $22 to you not have to have to deal with shoelaces ever-ever again. Personally, I think you are trading one hassle for another.

====================== The Next Day ======================

I tried them in earnest...REALLY. I figured if the Zubits would keep my laces from getting snagged when riding my bike, it might be worth the $22, but I never got that far. I took five steps out of the house and the Zubits separated. I reconnected the Zubits, took four steps and they separated again. I am returning them today. Too bad.

product_title: Timberland Men's Chocorua Trail Gore-Tex Mid Hiking Boot
review_headline: Quality gives off great first impression.
review_body:
I'm not qualified to review these boots from the perspective of a knowledgeable hiker; I purchased these in the hopes of getting my first pair of reasonable boots to begin the transition from day hikes to real hikes, and boy have they excelled so far.

In Florida, there isn't much rocky/steep terrain to test these against, but they've definitely proven they can keep grip in the wet stuff. Which is good, because you run into a lot of wet stuff around here. The waterproofing has so far proven true to the advertising. I haven't treated these with mink oil (yet) but for the one hike they've been out on, they've kept my socks dry even in two inch deep water.

Lately I've been breaking them in by wearing them during a normal day and they have succeeded in giving me confidence that I can wear them for a full 14 hours without feeling worn out or getting sore, tired feet. With high arches, I do experience a bit of fatigue late in the day, but it's mitigated by the lacing options of the boots.

The lacing eyelets seem to follow what I would expect to see on a hiep terrain king boot. I've no other previous boots to base my experience on but the hot button issue with these seems to be the quick lacing eyelets for the ankle and the quality of them. So far, I've approached them cautiously, but even with a good tightening they seem to hold sturdy.

It's not falling apart but it's not thick, heavy, beautifully made leather either. The insoles are also very light and I know I would want to add some cushioning if I intended to wear them all day.

4. The inside is fuzzy which makes these comfortable to wear with socks or with shoes.

Cons
1. None yet but I'll likely update my review if things go wrong.

Like other reviewers have noted, these do squeeze your feet a little bit so they're probably not for people who need wide slippers. They also provide little arch support but I knew this buying them. They're slippers, not running shoes =)

Overall, I love these things and I finally feel like I have a comfortable pair of slippers that's going to last me a while. I've been wearing them since they got here and I've not problems with them whatsoever. Good price too!

review_headline: Beautiful and comfortable with a great fit!
review_body:
These Sanita shoes are my first. They are extremely comfortable.
I usually wear a size 10 Australian shoe (42) which is the same as a US 10. These are true to size. I also wear a 10 in Born shoes (which I love) to give you an idea of the fit. These are just as comfortable though the leather is not as soft. It does, however, look as though it will not stretch as quickly (which is a good thing). They are fully lined in leather and are worth the price.
They are quite elegant and look great with a dress or pants.They don't have a clunky wide look at the toes like a lot of my shoes, but they still fit my wide foot and long toes.
I was surprised yesterday to realise that I was looking my several-inches-taller-than-me friend right in the eyes as, they are so comfortable, I forget I am wearing heels. The 'wooden' pattern on the heel looks great and the diagonal strap is very attractive, giving the Mary Jane a less childish look.
I thoroughly recommend these shoes- beautiful and comfortable.

product_title: Merrell Women's Pace Glove 3 Trail Running Shoe
review_body:
I now own three pair and these are just as good as my previous running Merrells. If you are buying zero drop shoes for the first time, take a moment to read the rest of this post. If not, you know the drill...
These are supposed to be like wearing no shoe at all but you have a bit of arch support and a small amount of padding. Zero drop means that your forefoot and heel are the same distance from the ground.
Wear them for about 30 minutes at a time for a while and gradually increase. Please don't run in them right away if you haven't worn this type of shoe before. It truly is better for your feet/legs/back but it takes a short while to build up to them. Your body is used to a different style of shoe.
There are many sites online for more research.

review_body: I love this purse organizer!  I didn't even know these existed and came across this product while searching for a way to better organize my purse. product_title: SPIRA Men's Stinger XLT Running Shoe
review_body:
The marketing pulled me in. Springs that will improve efficiency, making the run feel easier? Count me in! The wide toe box was an added bonus and I couldn't wait to run in these.

Upon first trying them on I could definitely feel those springs. The shoes have a bouncy feel and I thought I'd found a pair of winners. A bit of walking around and a short slow jog and I was completely sold.

Unfortunately, once I ran a bit faster everything went to crap. It's funny that many of the reviews here say that the shoes are too narrow; I have the opposite problem. The left one fits more or less perfectly, and the right one is way too wide. Shoddy workmanship, I guess? When I run a bit faster than a jog, I feel like my right foot is slipping and rolling around, even when I really lock down the laces. You might blame my feet or gait for this, except that none of my other five pairs of running shoes exhibit this problem. I've never had anything like it before, and I have to say that it's incredibly unpleasant.

Aside from the sliding/rolling issue, the ground feel and transition when attempting higher speeds is just really clunky. I just can't seem to get into a smooth rhythm when I'm wearing these shoes. I feel like I'm constantly fighting the ground and like I have to push a lot HARDER than usual to run fast. It's the exact opposite of what I hoped these shoes would do for me. After a run in these things my ankles burn in ways they never have before.

Finally, there's the issue of look and feel; the materials and construction just seem very cheap and plastic-y. These aren't cool looking shoes. I wouldn't care at all about their looks if they were performers, but it's worth mentioning given my other complaints. And based on the feel of the materials I can't imagine them lasting long.

All in all, I think if you want something for a comfortable long walk and/or light jogging these might work well for you IF you manage to get a matching pair. (Best of luck. Chinese manufacturing at its best.) If you're doing any kind of speed work, I'd look elsewhere.ching pair. (Best of luck. Chinese manufacturing at its best.) review_headline: I was very happy with how they turned out
review_body:
Purchasing this shoe was the first time I ever wore Merrell's. I went with high top due to tall grass, snakes, and rocks. I was very happy with how they turned out. The sole was soft, could feel some rocks here and there, but all around sturdy. Nearly slip resistant, unless your stupid (which Merrell cannot fix). I went to Montana and hiked quite a bit in ENNIS, while camping at and visiting many of the lakes around it. I was happy with the shoe, wore it nearly everyday all day long and didn't have a problem with them.

One thing I would do differently, however, would buying the waterproof version. This shoe was tall, and could handle a puddle and some dew on the grass. But anyting more than that it was wet soggy shoes. I will give it to them, they dry very fast, I stepped in a creek, and they were comfortably dry 2 hours after the incident. Once again, I would need the waterproof version of the boot to compare the air flow. If I could go back, I would probably purchase the waterproof just to be safe. Unless you are desert hiking, get the waterproof.

I hiked over 100 miles in two weeks. Broke the shoe in the first 30 minutes, wore comfortably the rest of time. No blisters, or foot pain. Happy with the product, will buy Merrells Again! It's worth the money.

product_title: Timberland PRO Men's Rigmaster Wellington Work Shoe
review_headline: Fantastic boot for just about an weather - especially cold
review_body: This is my third set of Timberland PRO boots - but this is my first Rigmaster Wellingtons. So far these are my favorite for field work where they need to be taken off and on (going into and out of a clean office regularly) - they are easy to get in and out of but they aren't too loose. They are perfect for cold weather, better than the other Timberlands that I own. They get a bit warm indoors and on hot days but I'm never sweltering. By now I've gotten used to the warmth and it doesn't bother met at all, even after hours of surveying on broken rock in the field during +70 degree weather. Absolutely no water has gotten through my boots and I'm frequently walking through ankle-deep water, snow, and mud. My only gripe has to do with the ladder lock - I work almost entirely in a rough terrain environment without few ladders, it tends to get hung up very easily on rocks. I'm sure for anyone working around ladders it's fantastic, but for hiking it's obnoxious.  Update (8-2-16): I bought these about a year and half ago, and they are just now starting to wear out. The threads are starting to pop near the heel patch on both boots. There's still plenty of tread on the sole and the tips are pretty worn down but serviceable. I'm ordering my second pair of Rigmaster today to replace the ones I wore out. All things said, these are the best work boots I've ever owned. Great traction, very comfortable, easy to pull on and take off (unlike those monster Matterhorns common in mining).   They are totally water proof. I was skeptical about buying "wellington" pull up boots, since lace-up boots and Xtratufs are industry standard for mining - but both are uncomfortable and a pain to put on. I have big calves, small ankles, and big heels. Those dimensions make the Extratuffs cut into my calves and the lace up boots are a pain to take on and off, especially after they have some miles on them. These wellington pull up boots were perfect - easy to take on and off, snug when I'm hiking in the pit, and I've never had water issues since I wasn't plodding through more than 8 inches of water.    They are also insulated just well enough to be good for working for several hours in the arctic circle but breathable enough for working in moderate to warm temperatures without getting too hot. I wouldn't recommend these for desert weather as they do have about 600g per boot of Thinsulate, so you'll want to go with an boot that lacks insulation for that, naturally. I bring it up because the description for most Timberland boots doesn't mention if they are insulated or not, and how much insulation they have.   I liked my last pair enough that I hate to retire them - but they are just boots afterall. Two thumbs up. I highly recommend these boots for anyone working in colder environments.

product_title: JOLLYCHIC PU Leather Multi Pockets Crossbody Bag Travel Shoulder Purse Black
review_body:
Fantastic little purse! I've always been one to carry around a purse the size of a small piece of luggage - but, just had foot surgery and ended up taking just my cellphone case with a credit card in it to the store. After doing that for awhile, I realized how wonderful it is to not be loaded down with a big, heavy bag. I've already put items in it, and here's my advice for making this purse work for you: girls, lose your wallet. Take your driver's license, credit cards, medical cards, paper currency and coins - put them in the interior zipper pocket. There is plenty of space for a cellphone, small hairbrush, gum, a few makeup items and a little bottle of hairspray inside. It's not like we need to carry a checkbook now! Take everything off your key chain except essential ones (who knows what those keys opened, anyway) and the outer zipper pocket holds those.
The purse itself is very sleek in design - would go with just about anything. It's easy to make the straps conform to the perfect length to either use as a shoulder purse, or a cross-body one. I will use it until it wears out, then buy another!

review_headline: Alegria shoes were recommended to me by the foot therapist who works with ...
review_body:
About a year ago, Alegria shoes were recommended to me by the foot therapist who works with me on my foot issues. My daughter inherited similar foot issues so I suggested Alegrias to her as well. We both bought several pairs as we found they were the most comfortable shoes we could wear. A few months ago, I would have given the shoes 5 stars because of their styling and comfort. Today, however, I am forced to give them 1 star. In the past month, my daughter and I have each had a pair crack in half. When we complained to the shoe store, we were told that a lot of people come in with the same complaint.

Shoes should last more than a year, especially shoes at this price. BEWARE of buying Alegrias if you are going to wear them more than occasionall Stitching comes loose, the footbed cracks in half. Alegrias do NOT last! I won't be purchasing them again.

product_title: Wellco Men's Hot Weather Jungle Boot
review_body:
I'm writing this review as an informative post about the boots after doing some research.

Many different manufacturers make exact copies of this same boot (as well as the standard, full leather, lug sole combat boot) but they are all made in China. Altama used to be the original manufacturer of this style of boot and made a boot in the USA that would last until the soles wore down to nothing (I had mine for 7/8 years). I went to find these again and it was remarkably difficult to find them at all except for the small stocks that a few surplus stores had (none in my size), so I did a little digging.

Altama was bought by Original Footwear in 2014, and they promptly closed the Altama plant in Lexington, TN in June of that year. Original Footwear owns Original S.W.A.T. as well as Wellco and their research division, RoSearch. When I contacted them about Altama dealers, I was told that the Altama brand would be coming back in 2016 when facilities were moved to Morristown, TN. Wellcos (and RoSearch) are currently made in Morristown, although it looks like they were having these boots made in China for a bit while they transitioned the Altama line to Morristown (or more likely, simply buying the cheap knockoff boots in bulk and rebranding them).

The quality issues people are seeing here are probably due to the fact that whatever stocks of Altama were left when they closed the plant were probably rebranded as Wellco (or later made in China), and people who know they're about to lose their jobs tend to not care about quality. According to what I read on some forums, the employees were laid off and the plant phased out over the course of a couple of years, and everyone knew what was coming.

I have a strong feeling that these boots are going to "become" Altamas when the manufacturing facilities are finished moving, and hopefully being made in the US with the old equipment again will mean a return to the same quality standard.So, if you're looking for this style of combat boot, wait until 2016 to see if the US manufacturing picks up and gets back to the old quality standard. I wouldn't buy these OR the Altamas that are still floating around due to the aforementioned issues.

product_title: KEEN Men's Vendetta WP Shoe
review_headline: very nice looking BOOT, but very rigid and hot
review_body:
Fit: I normally wear 11 in Keen, 11 in Adidas, and 11.5-12 in Nike. I found these pretty much true to size albeit they felt slightly wider through the mid and forefoot area than my other Keens. The upper is vulcanized rubber and quite rigid. I was hoping for a little more of a sneaker feel, but these are just boots. While the sole is from a sneaker and provides decent cushion, the upper thickness and rigidity end up having a much bigger impact on the overall feel of the shoe. The thickness of the upper causes it to be harder than normal to tighten the laced consistently. One of the shoes is also cutting into my heel, but this is a frequent issue that I have with most types of shoes and the issue is so slight in this one, I feel it might go away with a little more break-in time. The ankle area is also quite stiff - it provides support, but it can also be just a bit uncomfortable. I need to wear hiking socks that go above the top of the ankle, otherwise this shoe rubs excessively.

product_title: Dansko Women's Pro Xp Mule Shoe
review_headline: Long shifts? These make your legs and back less sore and achy!
review_body:
I wore these for the first time last night. I am in the hospitality industry, and I work 12+ hours on my feet on any given day- standing, walking, etc. At first glance, you an tell the shoes have plenty of cushioning. These are not super shiny patent leather, but a solid, polished black that is very professional. When I tried the shoe on originally (sans sock, just to test) I was worried it would be a little big. With my socks it seems to fit just right. I wear between an 8& 9 in women's shoes. and opted for the slightly bigger option- I figured I could always add a little padding if they were slightly too small. Since I have only worn them for one shift, I cannot say much yet but here's what I can say:

1. These have a lot of arch support. I have a fairly average arch, and I could feel the support. I don't think it is too much. but if your arch is on the lower side, I would not purchase these shoes.
2. There is definitely a break in period. I saw some people say they didn't have to break theirs in, but I absolutely did. By the end of my 14 hour shift last night, my feet hurt from breaking the shoe in (and that is to be expected!).
3. I can immediately tell a difference. My feet hurt still (to be honest, I think it was mostly break-in pain), but much much less than my former shoes, and my whole body was less tired. My legs and back felt less sore and achy.

I cannot wait to break these in fully, and when I do, I will post an update!

product_title: Honeystore Women's Office Platform Patent Leather Pumps
review_body:
Like another reviewer said, can you love shoes? I am obsessed. I guess it's past love, as much as it costs me. Reading the reviews on these babies, I was quite frankly scared! But as soon as I opened the box and saw these nude pumps I fell in love all over again. I noticed that all the reviews that say these come damaged, or bearing an odor are from 2013 or 2014. I guess, the seller has fixed the issue by now. Because, I received a "to-die-for" pair of nude pumps, and extra goodies. It came with gel insoles, sole protectors and a small mirror.
I am a US size 8.5 and I got the same in these, and it fits true to size. Also, I am not a huge fan of wearing high heels since it hurts my feet a lot. I usually never try on more than 2 and a half inch heels. Seeing these, I knew I had to give them to my sister because I won't be able to walk for more than a few minutes. But, amazingly these have awesome arch support. I felt no pain even though I had them on for more than 6 hours. The shoe is designed so that the base is raised due to the platform underneath (I do not know the technical terms, some love lol).
Color wise, I got the nude ones. The sole is the same color as the rest of the shoe and is done neatly. I didn't find any rough or unclean cuts or paint. The leather is also clean and smooth with no scratches. Because, its a neutral color I can wear it with pretty much any dress and any color.
Now the most important part, the sole. It is very comfy. It has a foamy soft feel to it so it won't hurt my feet. I guess that's why they feel so comfortable. Some heels have a hard sole so they get uncomfortable after a while. This ones has padded soles so you can have them on for longer durations.
In terms of shipping, I got it within two weeks and it came in a clean box.
Overall, I am very pleased with these shoes and would totally recommend them!

product_title: ACORN Men's Polar Moc Slipper
review_body:
I was looking for a slipper that could be worn all the time I'm at home. (I work from home a lot so that's a lot of hours.) I also wanted to be able to go check in the mail while wearing the slippers.

These slipper fit the bill wonderfully. First, they are very comfortable. There is a thin layer of foam padding in the bottom of the slipper that conforms a bit to your foot. Nothing major but just enough cushion without adding any weight.

Second, the rubbery bottom allows me to walk outside in them even if it's wet out.

The one very slight annoyance with the slipper is the embroidered acorn logo that's under the heel on top of the foot bed. It looks nice but for the first month or so that I had the slippers it felt like I had something stuck to my foot or caught in my shoe. Either I got used to it or the stitching settled down because I don't notice it any longer but it drove me crazy for a while.

Other than that, I really love these slippers. They're exactly what I was looking for. Also, as an extra bonus, I can put them on while standing up.

product_title: Vivienne Westwood by Melissa Women's Riding Rain Boot
review_headline: Assuming these are irregulars & not lined inside?
review_body:
Ok, I have a lot to say about these boots and how they tore apart my feet. 1st off I’ve never had issues with Vivienne Westwood/Melissa shoes in the past. I have several pairs & they are all super comfortable, except for these ones. I’m thinking that Amazon might get “irregulars” of Vivienne Westwood products (I also ordered a Westwood necklace & it was broken) because after inspecting this shoe closer I realized it’s unfinished! I seriously think these are unfinished boots! Vivienne/Melissa shoes are usually of superb quality and I hate to write a negative review about their shoes but these have to be unfinished! My Vivienne/Melissa “protection cowboy” boots are NOTHING like these! They are lined on the inside, top and bottom of the shoe & feel like you’re walking on clouds, so comfy!

So I got these in April & had tried them on & walked around the house & they felt ok. I felt it was odd that the soles of the shoes popped out on one when I took one boot off but figured I got them cheap so I’d deal with it. Little did I know how uncomfortable they’d be to wear in the future! On July 3rd I attended an outdoors art exhibit and much to my dismay these boots MANGLED my feet, esp my left one. I apologize in advance for the photos of my ugly, torn up foot but I want Amazon to see what these boots did to my feet! Esp my left foot. I actually had to leave the art exhibit after spending under 2 hours walking around because my feet were in so much pain! I swear that these boots are unfinished or irregular & that’s why they’re for sale so cheap! When I got home and took off the boots and then took off my socks my skin came off my left pinky toe! Under my big toe there was a mark on my foot, a cut, and my foot was bruised and discolored there. The other foot has bruises and cuts in the same parts as the other foot but not as extreme. I was expecting to change shoes and return to the art exhibit but was unable to because my left pinky toe is pulsating, missed a 4th of July part and plan to see my primary doctor tomorrow, yes it hurts that much! It almost feels like a burn since the skin came off.

I advise people not to buy these boots on Amazon. I’ve purchased my other Vivienne/Melissa boots from 6pm, yoox, Melissa’s direct page & Westwood’s too. I’ve never had an issue like this! Also these did not come with a dust bag as all my others have. There’s definitely something wrong with these shoes. I’d also like to point out that after wearing them for under 2 hours that the sole is coming off the right shoe. I also took a photo of that & a photo of the inside of the shoe. It appears the shoe parts are glued together but there’s some weird, hay looking threads coming out from the sole, where it connects to the boot, and also inside the boot too.

I notice there is one other negative review and a couple positive ones. I’m thinking that maybe some of the shoes Amazon sent out were defective and some were fine? I’m sure it’s not Amazon’s fault, unless they knew they were irregulars. I’m sure they didn't check each shoe individually but it appears I am not the only person to have had an issue with these shoes. I’m wondering if the other reviews were written after the people had tried them on & prior to walking in them for over an hour lol. Or possibly I just got a bum pair of unfinished boots. So if you do purchase these from Amazon I suggest you wear them around your house for longer than an
hour to see how they feel! And check inside of them, check to make sure there is a lining and that the soles liners are not coming out of the boots. So disappointed with these, esp since this happened 3 months after purchasing them. You’d think when you buy a quality product that you wouldn't have to worry about not wearing the item until a couple months later and find out it’s faulty and be sh*t out of luck! Buyer beware!

review_headline: Motorcycle riders, peeps that expect a boot to be a REAL boot, beware...
review_body: Huge disappointment!  The sole is too heavy for the boot!  The opening on the side is too long and shouldn't even be there, it's useless. Once on, the boot is wide and my foot loves wide, but it's wide not only in the foot, but at the heel, so as I walked, with no support from the flimsy shaft or arch or support from the around the middle of my foot, my heel came up over an inch, entirely assisted by the incredibly heavy sole. I'm a motorcycle rider and I USE my boots every day.  If you are the same way, don't buy these boots! I expected way more from Dr. Martens... The only good thing about this transaction was that Amazon shipped and let me return for free.  6pm.com doesn't do that.  I'm on a new motorcycle boot hunt, having no luck and 6pm.com doesn't let you ship back for free, beware.

review_headline: Overall, these shoes are what I wanted
review_body:
I picked this shoe specifically because the color was exactly what I wanted....sort of a beige color. I wanted a heel but nothing too tall. This heel is just right. It gives a dressy look without feeling like I'm tottering on stilts. I bought Size 7 1/2 but had I bought this pair in a shoe store I would have tried on the Size 8's to compare. This shoe DOES fit me but with nothing to spare. My foot literally fills the entire space inside the shoe. Had I tried the 8's, perhaps they would have been too large. ??? I'll never know. I decided that the 7 1/2 shoes would suffice and I wore them today for the first time and they were quite comfortable. The insole is cushiony with fabric lining along the toe line which is nice. Because of the heel, these could never be worn all day while standing or walking----at least not by me. However, for mostly sitting with some walking, the shoe could be worn all day without discomfort. I went to lunch and then shopping in these today. After two hours my right pinkie toe began to rub and would have formed a blister if I hadn't stopped walking. I'm going to find something to adhere to the spot inside the shoe strap to fix that. If not for the rubbing, I did not seem to have any trouble with discomfort while doing a combination of sitting and walking.

Overall, I am very happy with these shoes. They are EXACTLY the look I was going for while searching for a shoe to buy. I thought the price was reasonable also.

review_body: Because of the adjustability of the toe and ankle straps, these sandals are very comfortable except for one thing - the adjustable straps! They don't feel any less sharp to my hand, but they are no longer hurting my feet or ankles. The fourth pair (periwinkle) I bought needed no breaking in at all! And I love the color much more than I thought I would. All of them are supremely comfortable to walk in and I absolutely adore them - particularly the last pair I got. product_title: Solemates Heel Protector
review_headline: In less than 10 minutes I knew I could not continue safely or comfortably. I added these heel protectors as well as ...
review_body: I used these on my heels as a bridesmaid in an outdoor wedding. On all the uneven terrain, including rocks, gravel, dirt, lawn, pave stone, hills, ditches, etc., these definitely helped my footing be more secure. I tried walking in a couple different pairs of heels WITHOUT these heel protectors during the outdoors rehearsal. In less than 10 minutes I knew I could not continue safely or comfortably. I added these heel protectors as well as some shoe straps, and my walking became much more stable, confident, and safe. After 20 minutes of practice in my heels, I spent the rest of the rehearsal in comfortable flat shoes. Wearing the heel protectors on my heels and the shoe straps around the top of my foot made walking in heels just as easy as walking in flats -- And I NEVER wear heels in my daily life. The only downside: When our heels inevitably sank in a moist lawn, the heel guards would get left behind in the mud, and I had to dig them out and re-attach them to my shoes. The lawn had been deeply watered in the morning. The wedding was at 1:00 in the afternoon, and the lawn had been shaded until that point. It wasn't soaking, and only those of us with heels knew the ground was moist. I didn't sink quite as often as the bridesmaids without heel guards, but as good as these protectors are, they simply aren't wide enough to distribute weight adequately to 100% prevent sinking in wet ground. They improve it a little, but be aware of where you're walking, and don't leave them behind in the grass if they pop off your shoes. I used a ruler to measure my heel diameter in millimeters and the sizing was perfect according to their size chart!

The flexing seems more lateral than on the sole, at least to me. Plus, as with SO MANY items in sports, these were "hot" items a few years ago and so I bought them THIS year at a significant reduction off the original price!!! Needless to say, I'm not concerned about being seen in last season's shoes on the course. product_title: Steve Madden Women's Montaukk Espadrille Sandal
review_body: I normally always order a specific high end "comfort brand" when I am choosing heels but I fell in love at first sight with the appearance of these.  I wanted them for a special occasion so I figured I could at least suffer through for a few hours if they weren't that comfortable.  However, I was SO surprised that these are INCREDIBLY comfortable.  I wore them to a wedding and reception and danced in them for hours (and hours!) with no blisters or any discomfort whatsoever.  Also, the gold is beautiful and subtle and could go with anything.  As for sizing, I normally wear a 7.5 or an 8, depending on brand.  I ordered the 8 in these because the 7.5 wasn't available in gold.  Based on the fit, I think that either one would have worked equally well.  I say this because Amazon originally sent me a size 6 by mistake and I actually got it fully onto my foot with the strap fastened before I realized their mistake (that it was a little too tight and short) so it appears there must be VERY little difference between sizes (unlike with some brands) or I never would have been able to put a size 6 on.  I loved this shoe so much that I later went back for the Navy in size 8 as well.  This wedge is perfect with sundresses, maxi-dresses and crop jeans.  I will get tons of use out of both the gold and the navy.

product_title: Merrell Women's Verterra Hiking Shoe
review_body:
I was really disappointed with these shoes. I have been wearing the Mix Master Move tennis shoe for years and loved it. I especially like Merrell's wider toe box which never caused any rubbing or discomfort on my long walks. When it came time to replace them, Merrell had replaced the model with the Mix Master Move Glide. After a long search I finally succumbed the the new model. Unfortunately it's not as comfortable. THAT'S WHY I ended up trying THIS model, in hopes it would be more like my first pair, fit-wise.
More than a few reviewers noted this model runs short, and some suggested ordering up a 1/2 size. But all the others said not to. So I ordered 8.5 as usual since that's what I've always worn in Merrell shoes. The reviewers who said these run short were absolutely right. My toes hit the front of the shoe even when I'm sitting down! So of course they're even worse when I'm on my feet. On that basis alone I had to return them.
One more thing to be aware of: Merrell seems to be moving away from the indoor walker/runner and focusing on the trail walker/runner. These shoes are much clunkier, thicker, stiffer, and hard. I guess that's better for a trail shoe, but it's dreadful for treadmill'ing.
BTW the black is suede, not the usual mesh-type fabric of an athletic shoe. I didn't notice this in the description (if it's even there) so it caught me by surprise.

product_title: KEEN Men's Marshall Mid WP Hiking Boot
review_body:
I was looking forward to this light-weight hiker. Unfortunately, it wasn't as good as I had hoped. I waited to post any review until I had ample time to try out the product. At first glance, it looks the part, but loops can be deceiving. Here are my issues:
1.The soles have very poor tread (when wet they become very slick with little or no traction).
2.The mesh size is too open. They breath well for sure. Unfortunately, any small partice (sand, fine dirt, etc) passes through to the inside. I was in West Africa putting in water systems and would 'dump' my shoes often throughout the day.
3. The tongue slides down. Typically, this isn't a problem for me with other hikers I've owned, but is a continual problem with this shoe.
4. Astetically, the brown trim on the sole is coming off. Not the trim, the color and only on one shoe.

On a good note, love the fit and the weight. Very light.

All in all, not a fan and would not recommend this shoe.

product_title: Teva Women's Terra FI Lite Sandal
review_headline: I love tevas. I usually wear a variety of Teva ...
review_body: I love tevas. I usually wear a variety of Teva mush sandals. This was my first athletic sandal. I normally wear 7s in my other tevas, which is a size smaller than my running shoes but usually. 7 for dress shoes to give you an idea how they fit. These I got in a 7 they fit but with no room to spare, unlike the mush flip flops. I probably could have gotten a 7.5, if you like any room at the end. The first day I thought these would absolutely be returned. They constricted across the top of my ankle and rubbed my little toe. I wore them around the house just to see if anything changed. After multiple strap adjustments, they are comfortable. I went for a two mile hike today carrying about 30 lb backpack and they worked great. I think the fit was my fault. I felt to be "athletic" they needed to be secured to my feet, it's amazing if you loosen the straps how they still stick to your feet. I originally bought the for backpacking camp shoes and just in case I need to switch out my boots for awhile. Now after about a week of having them they are my everything shoes. Great in the garden, pressured washed the roof, climbed ladder fine good grip, went out with jeans and these sandals last night, great around the house for cleaning (tile floors nice to have some cushion). Fortunately I got these for less than original price, but they would still be worth it if I hadn't.

product_title: Maui Jim Peahi Sunglasses
review_body:
I love these sunglasses. I bought and returned three different Maui Jim models before these. I have found that the sizing info on the Maui Jim site is wrong. For example, temple length on the the Peahi was the same as the Wassup, but the Peahi went much farther back behind my ear. I have a large head and these fit perfectly.

I always thought that glass lenses were too heavy in these larger styles. I have a pair of Maui Jim "Island Time" and after a few hours my nose is red where they sit. These Peahi's can be worn all day and they are still comfortable. I think it comes down to the fit. If they fit right, the weight isn't noticeable and they don't cause discomfort. The trouble is, when you initially try glasses on, they may feel great (my Island Times feel great the first 30 min) but after a few hours the discomfort starts. The ability to return or exchange becomes very important.

product_title: Classic Retro Polarized Sunglasses - P6290 - Tortoise Brown
review_headline: These glasses are just as good as Warby Parker ($95) and RayBan ($120)
review_body:
These sunglasses are fantastic. Polycarbonate lenses. Sturdy. Lightweight. Look and feel great. Highly recommend.

You can finally have a pair of decent sunglasses without the annoying RayBan logo across the top right that says "I'm like every other a++hole hipster sheeple, I pretend I'm poor but spend $100 on old jeans, $120 on sunglasses, and $250 on boots that I wear to the coffeehouse".

I was waffling (going back-and-forth) between buying these for about $10 (including shipping) and buying a pair of RayBans for $120. Then, I researched and discovered that a lot of RayBan sunglasses ($120) have the same material--polycarbonate--as thes $10 sunglasses. Only difference is the price tag and name brand.

I even visit the SoHo (South Of HOuston, NYC) Warby Parker sunglasses store. Once there, I asked the clerk what their lenses were made of. She said polycarbonate. That is the same material--polycarbonate--of the lenses of these $10 sunglasses. Warby Parker is overpriced and a rip off.

I decided to order these and I am glad I did. They are comfortable. Look great. Feel great. Fit great. Appear to be sturdy. All for about $10.

If you're reading this review, buy these glasses. They are great!

(Sunglasses with crystal lenses, some RayBans are crystal lenses, are probably worth the $120 price. If you do buy a pair of $120 dollar sunglasses, buy thise $10 pair of sunglasses, too, and compare them. Either way, these $10 dollar sunglasses are definitely worth buying! Highly recommend.)

product_title: Columbia Men's Woodburn Mid Hiking Boot
review_headline: Boots: Good if they work.  Warranty: 1 year but you pay shipping. Customer Service: They only do so much but don't respond
review_body:
The boots overall are good. They fit as expected (I went a size higher because everyone said it fit small, but those were too big), and overall they are pretty sturdy. After wearing these boots for about 3-4 months, however, a hole developed in the cloth area that covers the toes in one of the boots, which meant that water, rain, snow, etc. would get in and my feet would get wet (which defeats the purpose of having the boots).

I contacted customer service to see if I could get a replacement or if it can get fixed. The good news: they have a one year warranty that covers issues like this.

The bad news: you have to pay for shipping to send it out to them (for me, it was $13). Of course, they try to make it sound like a fair trade, saying that I would cover for paying for shipping the boots to them and in return, they would pay for shipping the fixed/new boots out to me.

But what good is that, especially if it is a defect? Why would I need to pay more money to use a warranty?

So in order to have a good pair of boots and use its warranty, you would need to pay more in order to utilize the warranty. So it may cost you more than what you originally paid for.

I tried to email customer service to ask them if I can talk to someone about this issue because as a consumer I should not have to pay extra to fix a product. I wanted to either get shipping covered or get a full return and take my business elsewhere. After emailing the customer representative I have been trying to contact three times, they have yet to respond. So I do not plan on returning to Columbia for future purchases unless they resolve this issue for me (again, it has to meet my minimum expectations for me to return to them).

So, good product for the most part; horrible warranty and customer service.

product_title: W107-vp Style Vault Sport Flash Mirror Sunglasses
review_body:
I now own three pairs of these glasses. I have the "Rubber White/Red Dot-Redish Gold, mirrored (which is now called 'white/purple dot-purple' or close to it) , "Crystal Gray-green Lens, Mirrored" (which I can't find one that closely resembles it), and my most recent pair "Black/green Dot-greenish Blue, Mirrored."

Every pair is, simply put, outstanding.
So far, I think I have received the most compliments on the white pair with red lenses. People are constantly asking me if I got them from Oakley or Ray Ban. I ask people what they think I bought them for and I usually get the response that they are worth anywhere from $60-$120.

Frames
The frames are sturdy, but a little creaky sometimes, especially with the white pair which has a rubbery kind of frame. My most recent pair also has a more of a rubbery frame and is sturdy, but a little less creaky at the joints. The "Crystal Gray-green Lens, Mirrored" pair has a plastic frame, but still very well made. The main differences between them is that the plastic frames are smoother and are prone to slipping down a little bit more so than the other pairs because of their 'rubberyness'. Sometimes the rubber framed lenses pull my hair a little, but they stay on very well.

Lenses
The lenses are amazing. I really like mirrored lenses and the ones I got are really great mirrored lenses. The "Crystal Gray-green Lens, Mirrored" pair that I have was scratched pretty badly, but my white pair that I have had for just as long looks almost flawless, so I'm not sure if there is a difference in quality between them or if I just took better care of the white pair. Needless to say however, my white pair has been extremely sturdy. I bought my first two pairs December of 2013 and they are both for the most part in great condition. I like to think I keep pretty good care of my glasses, and if you ask me, their lifespan has been well worth the price!!

Since my first buy in 2013, the seller has changed things only a little bit and has even brought in more variety, which is awesome. One main thing I noticed is a change in cases that come with it. Before I got a black case that they called a "Nerd Glass Pouch" which was a cool little pouch that was pretty thick and good for traveling with. Now they have changed it so that all the carrying pouches are silky, which are really just as cool or cooler.

Overall, this is an absolutely fantastic buy. You can't beat the price with the quality anywhere else. Highly recommended!

~ A very satisfied customer

review_body: I purchased these shoes expecting them to hold up to the same standards of their boots, of which I've owned several pairs over the years. The sole of the shoe is that new age foam stuff that you see on a lot of running shoes, no rubber. I didn't know this when I placed the order and initially wasn't happy about it, but they seem to be holding up rather well, with no real sign of wear yet. Years ago I didn't want to jump on The North Face band wagon, but their boots and shoes have held up better than every other brand that I've bought trying to prove they weren't as good as everyone says they are. The short of it, these shoes look great and are extremely light and fashionable.  10/10 would buy again.

review_headline: Good sunglasses with comfortable vision and good protection.
review_body: I have been wearing a pair of Cocoon MX sunglasses for some time and very happy with it. I wanted to get a 2nd pair, thus, purchasing this pair of Cocoon ML sunglasses. The Cocoon ML fits my face better. The optical clarity is as good as those designer sunglasses. The frame shields light from all sides, works exactly as the manufacturer claims to be.  The sizing guide in Cocoon website serves as good guide to find the right size if you have no chance to try them physically. Cocoon ML fits my Oakley Socket 2.0 eyeglasses very well. However, not all eyeglasses able to find a good fitting with Cocoon sunglasses. I have Oakley Coilover and Rudy Project Maya eyeglasses too. I tried all sizes of Cocoons sunglasses in shop but none of them fit properly. Overall, I am very happy with this pair of Cocoon ML (Black Frame/Blue Mirror) sunglasses.  Frame: Good nylon material that can be adjusted to have good fitting when a suitable pair (matching size) of eyeglasses is used. Lense:  Polarized lenses are very comfortable to eye and the optical clarity is very good. Durability :  It is very durable. The temple can be readjusted when it is bended unintentionally (like when the pouch with sunglasses is inside my backpack). Aesthetic/Style :  It is not as stylist as those wraparound designer sunglasses. Nevertheless, the black frame/blue mirror model looks sporty and doesn’t look like those old man’s glasses. Price :  It is a good product and is priced reasonably. Overall:  It is highly recommended. Good sunglasses with comfortable vision and good protection from all sides. It can be worn with or without eyeglasses. For eyeglasses wearer, it is a solution for the hassle of constantly switching between eyeglasses and prescription sunglasses.

product_title: Tommy Hilfiger Men's Holbrook Combat Boot
review_headline: This is a very good boot for the sale price
review_body: This is a very good boot for the sale price. Colour is about as expected - possibly a little darker than the brightly lit images. I take an average sized US12. For the most part these boots are as expected in width size, however ... I use a full foot podiatrist orthotic with a little more than half the orthotic rigid (the rest is basically 3mm thick soft material). It is cut to a standard US12. I usually have to take out any footbed and started to prise out the glued down leather insole but stopped to try the boot on with the orthotics. I have now left the insole in the boot with the orthotic (the insole is quality btw). This is an indicator that these boots are roomy. This standard orthotic that fits Rockport, Salomon, Adidas US12 size has approx 6-7 mm gap at the end of the toe box. Would have gone a half size down knowing how it fits. Will return for a smaller size. Other than the sizing issue the quality of the craftsmanship is very good and the materials are excellent. If you are used to a mid cut boot (especially hiking boots) then you will probably like this product. Good casual look and goes well with jeans. UPDATE: Have now received the 11.5US (label also indicates that it is Euro45). This size makes much more sense. I have inserted by US size 12 orthotics (without removing footbed) and it is now a very good fit. Definitely recommend half size down when ordering. Have changed to a 5 star rating. Amazon service was Excellent.

product_title: Dream Seek Infant Boys Canvas Grey Baby Shoes
review_body:
There weren't any reviews on these shoes yet, but they were cheap and looked like what I was looking for, so I took a chance and got them for my three-year-old. My hope was that they would be easy for him to get on and off by himself and that he could wear them without socks for the summer months. I really prefer Keens for protecting little toes through the summers, but my little guy is in an "I can do it myself" phase, and I'm all about fostering that by having shoes available that are easy to get on and off.

So, the pros. They're pretty cute and have held up fine to water, mud, and sand so far. We've had them for about a month. The stock pictures don't show it, but there is a velcro hinge on the other side of the shoe to make it easier for little feet to get in. They're easy for my kiddo to get on and off several times a day. Every now and then he asks for help with them, so I don't know if they are randomly harder to put on or if he just occasionally doesn't feel so independent. I'm guessing the latter.

Cons. It's odd that the velcro hinge is on the inside of the shoe rather than the outside. (What I mean by "inside" is the inside of the foot side.) It took a while for my son to get the hang of having those on the inside of the foot rather than the outside, and he was constantly putting his shoes on the wrong feet for a while. Also, I was hoping these would be magically non-stinky shoes if he wore them all day with no socks in the summertime. No such luck, but really, that was rather a lot to hope for. They haven't caused any blisters though, despite sweating in them a good bit, and they aren't really very stinky. Just enough to notice a little when he takes them off after a few hours at the playground.

Overall, these are a good pick if you're looking for cheap, sturdy shoes. My favorites for little feet are Keen sandals.... really, you need no other shoes for kids in the summer; they are the BEST (as long as you don't mind helping younger ones with them)... and Toms canvas sneakers. The Toms only hold up for one summer, though.on't mind helping younger ones with them)... and Toms canvas sneakers. The Toms only hold up for one summer, though.

review_body: I have been using these about two weeks now, both bouldering and trad/sport. They take some getting used to, and some breaking in. I am 10.5 US shoe, wear 43 in La Sportiva, 44 in 5.10, and ordered these in 44. When I tried them on, I thought they might be a tiny bit large, because there is some dead space in the heels. After climbing in them, I can't even tell the dead space is there while on the wall. The last feels quite sturdy, while still letting me smear if I need to. It also helps when edging, because the toe box feels stiff, but I could still feel a bit of what's on the wall. There's a small bump where your toes rest, feels good after a day in them. Straps feel sturdy, but the top one should be shorter, I end up with maybe 5-6 cm of it overhanging the velcro. When you're done climbing, you gotta take them off, but on the wall I don't even notice them, so they aren't painful or distracting. One thing I had to do though was trim my big toe nail, and put tape over it. No matter what, it felt like it was catching on the inside of the shoe, and did not feel good at all.

review_headline: With only one strap, it's not really a backpack
review_body: The company was lovely to work with.  The bag is pretty, but not at all functional.  I bought it in silver.  The bling is great!.  It has pretty gold accents (zips, snaps and lining on the strap), making it work with both golf and silver. It is the perfect size for an iPad and all the other random things I carry for my kids.  The zippers are good quality and pretty.  I really wanted to love this bag!  The jeweled front is actually another zipper bag that could be used as a shoulder bag.  It snaps onto the front of the bigger bag.  Even empty, the snaps do not actually hold it to the front of the bag.  The snaps are gold, so if it is used separately there are gold snaps looking for their other half on the bag: I would never use them separately.  The strap claws can be used to clip the two together as a shoulder bag or the can be tied together by their pretty d-rings for the shoulder strap.  Unfortunately, I wanted to use this as a back pack, but it  only comes with one short  strap so in spite of ample rings, it can only be used as a shoulder bag.  The strap might be useable as a cross body strap for my daughter.  The strap is not long enough to use as the backpack straps and it is too thick to fit through the top center d-ring.  A second strap would make it useable, especially with some pretty ribbon to tie the bags together.  Overall, it is extremely disappointing, especially since it is so lovely.

product_title: Hee Grand Women Crystal Diamond Open Toe Thong Sandals
review_headline: If you wear these "glass" slippers, you may find a Prince.
review_body: These shoes are made from translucent gummy plastic. There is a huge crystal toe "ring" between your big and second toe and then there are crystals embedded all around front of the ankle band.  I normally wear a 7 but after reading the reviews bought a 7.5 which fits perfectly. My foot is a normal width, I don't believe this shoe would fit a wide foot well.  The strap does not seem to be adjustable once tightened (or at least I could not figure out how to open it back up). The band has plastic ridges on one end which you pull through the buckle and it locks the band at whatever width you set. However, it's really easy to slide your foot in and out of the shoe even with the strap closed.   The sole is flat and doesn't have much support, though they seem to be molding to my feet as I wear them and are more comfortable each time I wear them.  These shoes are really gorgeous. They flatter feet and toes amazingly! The crystals are really clear and beautiful and these have been a super fun (and cheap) part of my summer wardrobe. Even better, they are perfect pedicure shoes!   I love these shoes and really recommend them.

review_headline: Please do not support Reebok by purchasing these non-durable, non-deployable boots. These are not fit for duty!
review_body: I really was excited to be able to utilize these lightweight composite toe boots in the field. However, after 6 months they are completely destroyed. They were the least durable I have ever owned. The initial issue ones were better, albeit, not as comfortable. So out of the box, they were too narrow at the toes, they seem to narrow into a point towards the composite toe. It was annoying at first and caused blisters but after a few days they broke in quick and were comfy. Then I added aftermarket sole, as the stock sole is cheap and provides zero support for people who are required to stand for 10 hours a day minimum under an aircraft. Then the breather eyelets (wire mesh holes for breathing) on the inboard side of the boots separated completely, probably now a fod hazard. Then the heel of the right boot has broken through giving way to anything that once provided a glimpse of support. Last but not least, the toe cap is now completely exposed, which every service member knows, marks the end of the boots' serviceability. Now, after all this hassle is a mere 6 months, I have to do more research and find a more superior boot. Oh, and Reebok has yet to respond to my customer service complaint or offer me some sort of discount or refund or apology for a defective product. I'm probably going back to Corcoran Marauders. My last pair lasted me two years with much abuse.

product_title: Maui Jim Banyans Polarized Sunglasses
review_headline: If not factory rejects / fake/ or damaged - they're GREAT!
review_body: The glasses themselves are GREAT (fitwise) --- even the KNOCKOFF / DEFECT / FACTORY REJECT version that I got in the mail. Now I am not saying that everything you get online is this way - it just so happened to be my luck. First off - I love Amazon deals, but in this case, some deals are just too good to be true. Saw these MJ Banyans for $159 from Direct_Express and Fulfilled by Amazon - so automatically I thought - Amazon is shipping these so they have to be real - not so much. Opened up the box and first thing I've noticed were scuffs on the brown sunglass case.. at first I thought - perhaps thats Maui Jim or Mountains (watermarked onto the case)- aahh no. just plain ol' marks that only mean that the hard case was damaged. After waiting a WEEK for these even w. Prime shipping - Bummed! - tried on glasses, looked great, everything right where it should've been but Extra Bright cloth pouch + print that wasnt as detailed as on the ones i have, which naturally started to set off alarms in my head - (I have few of these from previous glasses and material + print quality just didnt match). BUT stuff like this does happen - it's not a crucial part so could in fact change over time. Still, tried these on - and there was something about them just didnt sit right. I compared them to my Neutral Gray MJ-352-02's and sure enough these ones were a cooler lens. (grr) Then tried them on in bright daylight - as i was turning my head left - right lens / coating was making the glare worse - brighter, then some things, buildings -  looked like as if I were wearing 3D glasses. It's as if though the polarization was rotated. To confirm my suspicion I called Maui Jim and based on their sample - which seemed a bit old - (mine said Patent No. 7717557 - which is indeed correct patent for Maui Jim, but theirs said (patent pending) - go figure ) everything else seemed correct. Still, I visited one of my local glass shops and compared - right away I could tell that Lenses were better, and forsome reason so was the fit. - I've ordered another pair from Amazon and I hope that I will finally get the REAL ONES. If not then paying 220+tax just to get REAL ONES might be worth it - even for a hybrid gas is expensive dammit. P.S. IF YOU HAVE A LARGE EGG (FACE) and a BIG BRIDGE like I do - also try these - MJ-324-23 they actually fit me better but they are MORE expensive. (Definitely on my wish list)

product_title: Trotters Women's Mickey Wedge Pump
review_headline: Great Fit and Style, So-So Quality
review_body:
This is a lovely shoe. I have a wide toe box and a narrow ankle, which can make fit a challenge, but these fit beautifully. Also, they are fairly comfortable to walk in (which is always nice); the heel gives a bit of lift, but isn't hard on my knees and the ankle strap keeps the whole thing comfortably in place. The tan color is/was nice and they go with pretty much everything I wear in the spring/summer.

The reason for the three stars is that I was recently caught in a spring rain storm and got soaked. Once they were wet the dye started leaking all over my feet. I crossed my legs once I was inside and ended up with a wide orange streak across my leg. When I got home I filled the shoes with newspaper and wrapped them in tissue paper. Once they were dry it became sadly obvious that the color had changed forever. It is now more of an orange than a tan.

I contacted Trotter's customer service, but they said nothing could be done under warranty and to try taking them to a cobbler. That's fine. I'd love to have some amazing customer service story, but I realize this is completely my fault. It is just that I have never had a shoe leach the dye so much and I'm disappointed with the quality of the leather. I may try and have them dyed or just live with the new, less than ideal color.

So, by all means, buy it. Just check the weather first.
