product_title: Kelsi Dagger Brooklyn Women's Crown Heights Platform Sandal
review_body:
Cute shoes -- exactly clean and stylish as they are pictured. Beyond this, Kelsi Dagger shoes are so well made -- the ankle strap, for example, is without that flimsy-lasts-one-season feel of most summer sandals. Overall, they are as pictured, so would have satisfied my hope for a pair of everyday sandals with a slight heel, with a bit of style.

But, I am returning them. While the ankle strap and padded footbed are comfortable, the shoes are otherwise unwearable as the sizing is off. I am a true 6.5, but the footbed on these are at least a half-size too long (projecting at least 1/2 inch beyond the end of my toes, like a flipper), while the toe strap is rather tight and rubs at the nail bed-point of the toe. If they were half the price I might consider exchanging for a smaller size, but it's not worth gambling for this price point.

In general, I do recommend the brand, as I admire the quality of them, and the street-chic style.

product_title: ASICS Men's Gel-Contend 2 Running Shoe
review_body:
A member of the household bought these to replace his well-worn New Balance N5xx. These are not for running, but for distance-walking. A decent pair of sneakers will pay for themselves in reduced commuting costs. It has only been a couple of days, but the first impressions are generally positive.

- They are very light and the sole is well-padded, particularly the heel. Good for brisk walking on pavement.
- The arch support is probably adequate though not terrific and might need an insert in the future.
- The length fit as expected-- since sneakers tend to run smaller than shoes these days, we got a half-size larger than the shoe size.
- He got these in wide (2E), but feels the instep is still a bit snug. It seems to be accommodating as the material relaxes but he would get 3E or 4E next time.

Still, overall the sizing is more sensible than the NB, where he had to buy a full-size larger and extra-wide (4E) to get a reasonable fit. These are also lighter than the NBs.

As for the style, frankly we don't much care for it, but it's not a problem unique to Asic. The trend in athletic shoes these days is toward garish-- shiny or florid, particolored with rococo plastic applique and ridiculous racing swooshes. None seem to be styled for adults. The only alternatives are dull, heavy appliances that look they belong in nursing homes. These ASICs were among the least offensive sneaks having good specs.

UPDATE: 6 months later, the wearer is still enjoying these. He has

- walked at least 2 miles each working day
- saved ~$300 in commuting costs
- lost ~20 unwanted pounds (with proper diet), and
- the sneakers are still in good shape.

He has experienced none of the arch or ankle pain he had with his New Balance shoes. Of course the style is still terrible but he doesn't care. The entire family wears ASICS now, and when these shoes give it up he will be getting another pair!

product_title: New Balance Men's MW1069 Country Hiking Shoe
review_body:
I ordered size 12 4E, which is 1/2 size larger than I would normally get and they fit perfectly.

I never order less than 4E widths, which limits the brands I can choose from, so New Balance is one of my regular sources of shoes.
This particular shoe seems well made so far (after 5 days of use). They still need a bit of breaking it yet, but they are very comfortable with lots of room for my toes and my heel fits just right.

I anticipate that these will become my everyday shoes for the next 4 years.

It is a nice balance between casual and "just dressy enough" and with waterproofing on top of it.

The one downside for me (but not a huge one) is that they do not seem as breathable as other shoes I have worn so my feet are a bit grateful for taking them off in the house. With my Hush Puppies, my feet did not care one way or the other. These NB are not uncomfortable or painful at all.

I have tried, but not yet noticed any problem with the tongue digging into my foot as Dennis Crowe, DannyB, Brian and Nemo mention.
The one pleasant surprise was how comfortable they were when kneeling. The bend at the toe box was surprisingly comfortable.
If I remember, I will update this review after a year or two.

review_headline: this is a great bag, depending on what you are looking for
review_body:
This is a tough review. Overall, this is a great bag, depending on what you are looking for.

I tend to be a little obsessive with things like bags. I had a specific purpose in mind that included wanting to carry basic items like phone, glasses, etc. Also on the list was wanting space for a 10in tablet and in being able to put in a standard size folder (basically 9 in by 12 inc). According to the posted dimensions, this should accommodate all of that.

For the most part, it does, with the exception of the folder. I am not sure how the posted measurements were calculated, but it seems a bit smaller than that. The top x bottom measurements I come up with are more like 10 x 8.5 Yes, you can put in a folder but it sticks out the top a bit. Since this function is the one that I will use the least, I decided to keep the bag.

Generally speaking, the bag is well constructed and does what I want. It is easy to carry and the vertical design is nice. I can slip a water bottle in the side mesh pockets, although that is a tight fit. If I were redesigning this, I would fix the size. I would make the strap longer, and maybe make the top zipper a bit more secure (when you zip the top, there are gaps on the sides). The applique on the front is larger than in the pic, and really doesn't add anything so I would remove that also.

It sounds like I am complaining a lot given that I am leaving a high rating. That is because overall, I think it is still a good bag for the price. I looked at a lot of bags, and it seems like everything else I found was way to small, way to big or much higher priced.

product_title: Tretorn Otto Mid Suede Boat Shoe
review_headline: OH #TRETORN... Where do I begin? A shoe's quality that reflects it's arch support; NONE.
review_body:
OH #TRETORN... Where do I begin? A shoe that has a quality that reflects it's arch support, NONE. I think that as a brand they have a good sense of style, simple yet a few key tweaks to stay unique. I do agree with many of the comments on many of the shoes, as they are quite comfortable. However, the flaw, and its a big "the". Is that when you spend nearly 100$ for a shoes you expect it to last at least a week. Dare I say, at least one hundred days, of light to moderate wear. The brand would have more of a large following if it actually made quality up to its style and comfort. They could be the "Madden" shoe brand of the decade if they got their act together.

Instead, Tretorn is the Micheal Bay or Zack Snyder of shoes. Like the Movies they make, great idea, flashy, and stylish. Actors in your comfort zone that your are willing to see. But, you get a movie that has its bottom fall out from under it because of lack of plot and structure. Just like this shoe, you won't get your moneys worth, because if you were to actually wear it out, to say a movie, the shoes would be left behind at the concession stand, as it would've fallen apart before you even got half way to your seat.

review_body: FAKE FAKE FAKE... I will say as some others have mentioned, it's a pretty good fake but a fake. So if you don't mind then fine, but I checked and double checked. There is a list of things that you can check but the biggest FAIL was the TOM FORD on the lens. The font and the spacing is wrong. I took it to a TOM FORD store and put it side by side with the exact same model. The only part that they failed on was this part. If you ZOOM in on the product photo you can see for yourself. The font is wrong and the spacing between TOM and FORD is way to far apart and that is not a TOM FORD thing. The other giveaways, it didn't come in a plastic bag that has the same serial number as the one etched at the end of the left arm. That's the part that sits on your ear. I rather have the plastic have the wrong number than not have the plastic. It's easy for the vendor to mix them up as they might be showing a few to customers or for display but not to have it at all should get your interest to look into it more carefully. Also the piece folded paper that comes with the certificate (which is shaped like a business card in an envelope), well the folded piece of paper looks like a photo copy and not a good one and the TOM FORD name displayed in the front is printed the wrong way. Hope this helps if you are thinking, OH YEAH, what a deal...

product_title: Vivobarefoot Men's Ultra Pure M EVA Amphibious Shoe
review_headline: 8.7 oz the pair for men's size 43 (and they do run a bit large IMO)
review_body:
I JUST got these, so can't comment now on durability, how they feel/work when worn extended periods. But one piece of data I wanted from a review I can provide: in men's size 43 a pair of these Vibrobarefoot Ultra Pure weigh 8.7 oz.

I bought these because I plan to hike the Camino de Santiago, and "outdoor" (hiking) shoes aren't allowed for wear inside the Albergues or often in other forms of lodging. My crocs weigh just under a pound, so I'm pleased to have something that saves me about 7 oz, nearly half the weight. You can't just "slip them on" the way you can with Crocs, but I can live with that, and the flip side is that these will stay on more securely.

From just very brief walking around the house, I'm not as comfortable in them as I am in Crocs. I trimmed the inserts from an old set of trail runners and there was enough space to fit those in without squeezing my feet. That adds about 1.6 oz for the pair, but feels a lot more comfortable. If I find that I'm okay without them, I can discard them along the way, but ... FWIW, my initial reaction is that they'll be worth the weight.

Count me with the majority of reviews that suggest that these run large, i.e., that you want to size them down a bit. I got the size 43 based on that. In U.S. sizes, my feet are nominally a size 10, but I'm accostomed and typically comfortable in a size 11 or 11-1/2. These in European size 43 fit me just right. I wish they were a bit less expensive, but I'm pleased to save some needless weight in my backpack.

product_title: Osiris Men's NYC 83 VLC Skate Shoe
review_headline: Osiris Is Awesome! Regular Shoe Size Fit Perfect!
review_body:
I really love this shoe! Osiris makes a lot of nice looking skateboard shoes, but this was very first pair. I was so skeptical of the sizing because of how many people said that you should go up at least a 1/2 or full size. But, I rolled the dice and ordered my regular size. I wear a Size 7 (Men) in every type of shoe that I own (except for dress shoes - I wear a Size 8 in those). When I tried the shoes on after they were delivered, they fit me PERFECTLY! Not too much room which can cause creases and bad walking posture...and not too small that they can cause blisters by just walking down the street. They fit just right!

One thing I will say, is that they do need to get broken in a bit. They are quite stiff. But, that's pretty much any shoe, not just Osiris. I just went out to my local skate park and shredded it up for about 2 hours. And my shoes survived every Kickflip, Heelflip, and Ollie I threw at it. Not a "griptape scuff" in sight, only a little dirt from the pavement. And that came right off with a Clorox Wipe! I'm pleased as punch! Can't wait to get my 2nd pair...and 3rd and 4th! product_title: Altra Women's One2 Performance Running Shoe
review_headline: Nice and light, plenty of toe room.
review_body: For the past several years I have been running in Saucony cross country flats, which have no cushion, but were great for building foot and ankle strength while changing to a midfoot/forefoot running strike. However, my toes were always scrunched and long runs were tiresome without cushion. Altra shoes are built to encourage the midfoot strike and leave plenty of room for your toes to splay rather than be squished, and they have cushion. So I expected them to feel large. I own a pair of Altra Torin 2's and the toebox on the One2 seems wider to me, but my ankles are held nicely. They are great to run in. They have less cushion than the Torin's and are lighter which I was looking for so it wouldn't be as drastic a change from my flats. The only thing that bothers me is the embossed stripe on the toe. It stiffens the fabric and I can feel it bend across the top of my foot. After working it and bending it and trying to soften it, it is getting better. I notice it more when walking than running. I've only run in them once, but will try them in the hills tomorrow.

product_title: Saucony Girls Kinvara 5 Running Shoe (Little Kid/Big Kid)
review_headline: Excellent shoe for a young lightweight runner!  Very happy.
review_body:
My 4.5 year old runner is light and has very narrow feet. I read many, many reviews from customers and running sites and decided to try these for her. It is thought that children need as natural of a feeling on the foot as possible, like barefeet ideally, to make the proper neuromuscular connections while developing all of the small muscles that support the feet, ankles, legs, knees, hips and everything connected. I like these shoes for their perfect amount of support. Her muscles still have to work but she is comfortable and lightly supported.
My girl recently ran a race and was stomping the whole time. I later picked up her old shoes and realized how heavy and inflexible they were. She also complained of her knees being sore. Not ideal at all for a little, lightweight runner! These Saucony shoes are perfect!!! They are extremely light and very flexible. The colors are fantastic and I even had to rinse these last week after they were covered in grass and they look great still. They did run small as reviews suggested. She is about a 10.5 and an 11.5 is perfect and should fit for a few months at least. I would also recommend these laced shoes over velcro for a little athlete as they are able to be laced properly ans snuggly. (I hemmed and hawed because she cannot tie yet but a friend recommended lace over easy velcro and I agree now)
As an adult I also prefer very similar Saucony running shoes but they no longer make the particular style. I do have to wear mens though as my feet are very wide with shorter toes. It seems the brand runs a hair small and narrow in general.

product_title: Merrell Men's Moab Ventilator Mid Hiking Boot
review_body: Let me qualify the above ratings. I normally wear a 13- 4E. My right foot is sized right on the money for most shoes, however my left foot is almost a size smaller (12 EE). No one makes 4E in a decent hiking boot that I could find and 13 EE were just not wide enough for my right foot (tried several brands and styles). I went with the 14 EE in the Moab. The fit was as expected the right shoe fit pretty good and my foot swam in the left one. I almost always replace factory insoles when I get new shoes and did so with these which helped with size. I have done 2 hikes in them so far and they did pretty good. Break in hike was 6 miles without a pack over moderate terrain and the 2nd was 5 miles with a 55 lb. pack over the same course just a little shorter. My feet felt pretty good after both hikes. product_title: AK Anne Klein Women's Falicia Leather Dress Pump
review_body: I bought these and a pair of Michael Kors Flex Mid pumps (both size 8M) at the same time, comparable features/styles/price point/customer reviews. Comfort is a BIG deal to me and the MKs have a sleeker look, so I expected it to be a trade off of style vs comfort. Boy was I wrong... They look pretty similar, but the MKs fit like a glove right out of the box. The Anne Kleins on the other hand fit... just OK. Toe box and heel fit fine and are probably designed well enough. They could probably be comfortable to wear walking around the office, if only it weren't for the trim around the top edge. Very scratchy. If they don't fit perfectly I could see someone getting ankle/heel blisters while breaking them in. The leather doesn't seem as nice, nor the stitching (if it were quality they wouldn't need that trim to cover it!). Size-wise, I'm in that awkward spot right between 8 and 8 1/2 and an 8 was actually a bit long. They're also loose around the middle of the foot--like next to the arch at the instep, but also on the outside. The leather just buckles out...more slipping or chafing potential there. Obviously I can't speak to durability because I just got them and am sending them right back, but in all other categories they seem no better than adequate. Unless you're dead-set on having the (admittedly really cute) zipper on the back, at any cost, I humbly recommend skipping these and trying the MKs I mentioned, which at the time of this review are actually about ten bucks cheaper and far superior in every regard I can think of.  (Btw if you go looking for the MKs, the front photo of a kitten heel is incorrect, the Mid really is a 3" heel.) I hope this review is helpful!

I have worn NB 900 series shoes since they came out. They came in 4E(I have wide feet) and controlled my pronation.  Since I started having leg and foot problems I have tried a lot of shoes. The 990's put too much pressure on the balls of my feet and exacerbated the morton's,  I tried the NB 508's but they were painful.  For a while I used  the MW475's but after 3 or 4 hours my feet would start burning and hurting.  Recently I tried these MX608V4B. They fit perfectly and do not put pressure on my toes and the balls of my feet , and for the first time in years my right foot feels pretty good.  I can wear them all day.  I don't run anymore but I do walk and these shoes are a God Send!  I hope NB keeps making them.

product_title: Townforst® Women's Slip and Oil Resistant Jess Work Shoes No Slip Shoes
review_headline: Order up for wearing with socks!!
review_body: The review that said these shoes fit like a glove was not kidding. These fit exactly as you order them. They look like Tom's, so I ordered them in my Tom's size... which were skin tight (in a good way). Unfortunately I work in a kitchen and so I needed shoes I could wear with socks. So I returned them and bought a new pair a half size larger. They will work alright because I wear rather thin socks. I would suggest ordering a full size up for regular socks, half size up for trouser socks or tights. That said, these are incredibly comfortable shoes with a memory foam sole that is very supportive. They look very professional and I would recommend wearing them to work or even just for casual comfort. Update: I LOVE these shoes. They are excellent at being non-slip (I have really put them to this test) and do not require any kind of cautious stepping when walking on wet floors. They are also very waterproof, which is lovely. However, being low-cut shoes, big splashes and water from above are excluded. BUT they dry rather quickly and do not chafe when water does get in them. Being leather, they are also thankfully rather heat resistant! Which is great because otherwise I would have had melted shoes and/or burned feet by now. Just buy them.

review_body: I really wanted to like these shoes. Have heard so much good things about Brooks but maybe this was not the style for me. They are running shoes and I do not run but am on my feet a lot. They are narrow in the heel (which I have narrow heels) and was one of the reasons for buying the shoe and needed extra toe room as I have arthritis and my joints are a bit enlarged. Because of the enlarged joints it pushes my 2nd and third toe further than the big toe and have painful experiences when wearing shoes. With this shoes my big toe touched the top of the shoe and based on the reviews I ordered 9 and 1/2. The problem was the big toe touched the top of the shoe but didn't feel the arch was where it needed to be on my foot. But at least the other toes did not hit the outer edges of the shoes. My feet went numb wearing them. Not sure if it is just my feet or what. But for the price, I didn't think I wanted to deal with these issues and not be able to wear them for any length of time. But will check out other Brooks shoes and they look like they would be a good shoe with the right style and fit. Will need to try them on at a facility rather than order online. Once I find the right fit then ordering online will be a good idea. Glad I did not get the size 9 as my toes would have hit the tops of the shoes not just the big toe. I am 60 years old and usually wear a size 8 1/2.

review_headline: Very light  and comfortable, definitely run small, durability is just OK
review_body:
These shoes are *very* light, and very comfortable. As others have pointed out, they definitely run small. I usually wear size 9, but I found these to be both too short (length-wise) and too narrow. I ended up with 9.5W, and those fit well - a tiny bit too wide, perhaps, but the regular width were just too narrow.

Others have also pointed out they they're not very durable. I agree with that, but it also depends on how much walking you do in them. These are the only shoes I ever wear. I wouldn't call myself sedentary (my phone says I average 3,000 steps per day), but I do have a desk job, so I'm not on my feet all day. These shoes took about two years to completely wear out. I would expect longer from $100 shoes, but I think the durability is adequate, and is a fair tradeoff for the lightness they afford.

Overall, I love these shoes, and would recommend them to anyone. In fact, I just ordered another pair to replace my worn-out ones.

review_body: I have been searching for a sandal that would fit my problem feet for years. When I walk, I forget that I am even wearing shoes on my feet, because it feels as if I am walking on clouds...and this is right out of the box. My problems: flat feet, fallen arches, previous bunion surgery, arch cramps, toe on left foot turning in to the left again, toe on right foot turned out to the left almost 30 degrees (making many sandals as well as shoes almost impossible to wear), and poor little crowded toes on both feet. My weight seems to be distributed in all of the wrong places, but these sandals take care of that, and seem to spread my weight out evenly over the surface of my foot. I am so happy to be able to go for walks with people again. It is something I really missed, and I was tired of feeling like a cripple. review_headline: Glue worked great. Amazon seems to treat this glue as a shoe itself, rather than a shoe accessory.
review_body:
The guided review process treats this item as a "shoe" rather than a repair product - it does NOT 'fit as expected' or 'have any problems with arch support' - this is shoe glue.

My daughter's Converse shoes had the sole coming right off after four months - not a sign of wear anywhere. I tried a few other general glues, including silicone and latex sealants. In the end, this stuff (basically: rubber cement) worked awesomely. Apply a thin layer to two rubber surfaces, wait about two minutes, then stick them together forever.

product_title: Michael Kors Kiera Mid Pump Womens Tan Pumps Heels Shoes
review_body:
I cannot say enough negative things about these horrible piece of junk orthopedically dangerous pair of shoes!! The shoes are very stiff and rigid, and do not allow any wiggle room for your feet. My feet started killing me only after five minutes of walking in them. I gave them the benefit of the doubt and thought I just had to break them in. However, by the end of the evening (and I sat most of the day at work), my feet were throbbing and stiffened up!

And when I finally got home and took my shoes off and rested for a bit on my bed, I got the absolute worst Charlie horse cramps I've ever experienced in my life on BOTH feet, first on my right foot, then on my left foot!!!! My husband was seriously worried since I have a very high pain tolerance, and I was crying. My feet were so sore for three days afterwards. I had to wear flats to work, and I could barely tolerate those because my feet felt very bruised! I experienced a second Charlie horse crap on my right foot two days later while at a department store! I was beginning to wonder if the shoes had done some damage to my feet, and was on the verge of making a doctor's appointment but because of my work schedule, I didn't get around to it.

After lots of stretching, icing and resting, my feet finally felt better after about four days. This is not an exaggeration. I have never, ever experienced anything like this. I've had much better luck with Payless shoes, and I'm sure most 5-inch stiletto heels are much more comfortable than these terrible, terrible shoes!!

I thought I was treating myself to a good pair of shoes, then this happened. I expected so much more from Michael Kors and for the amount of money I paid for them. I am boycotting all Michael Kors shoes because of this. I would not even take these for free if someone gave them to me. I would throw them straight in the trash, where they belong! Never again!

review_body:
I like these OK -- they're not perfect, but I didn't expect perfect. They're definitely warm, and they fit nicely. I have rather large feet (size 11 W usually), and these XL slippers fit just fine. They might be a little wide for someone with a narrower foot, however.

They're washable, too, so that's a good thing. Well made, secure stitching, quality materials -- what I expect from Dearfoams.

There's not much padding in the soles. There's the faux shearling lining and maybe a little foam padding, so don't expect much in the way of support. Still, for wearing around the house, these are just fine. They're easy to slip into in the middle of the night, too -- something to remember if you have cats who like to leave their toys around!

I like this; didn't love them; solid 4 stars.

product_title: Old Friend Women's 481142 Sheepskin/Char Innersole
review_headline: Working for me and revitalized my old slippers
review_body: I was unsure about ordering these given other reviews about low quality and being thin.  Ultimately these worked for me and I'm happy with my purchase.  I had an old pair of Old Friend slippers (Women's 441120 Slipper) but the insoles were worn bare.  The new inserts are definitely thin and do not come with a foot bed.  The foot bed of my slipper was stitched to the old/worn shearling lining so my solution was to get a scissor and snip stitches so I would pull the old liner off of the footbed.  I threw out only the old lining while preserving the footbed.  I then cut the new lining to fit the old footbed and problem solved!  I was worried the liner would slip since it wasn't stitched to the footbed anymore but so far it is staying in place.  I reduced my review to 4 stars since the product required the extra effort described above.  You might check your slipper footbed before you order as I assume other slipper types may not have the removable footbed like mine did.  I also found the size markings for cutting the liner were too narrow compared to my footbed so I'd cut directly based on your previous insole.

review_headline: Pretty good, but kind of messy after a while
review_body: I got a pair of these to wear as house slippers -- cool in the summer, A-OK with socks in the winter. They're a little funny the first few times you wear them, but they break in (or you get used to them) very rapidly. The adjustable strap is, to me, essential (I'm looking at you, Nike!). Wearing them around the house, they were not subject to a lot of wear and tear. After 2 years the straps and soles are in good shape. However (!!), the nubbins are breaking off like crazy; I'm annoyed because little black rubber bits show up every time we sweep the house (domestic bliss beware). Moreover, since the beginning, the void space in between the little bits is a natural accumulator of dust and lint. After a little while they fill up with stuff, and once in a while they fall out creating more housework. I did clean them out a few times with a toothpick but -- no surprise -- this is painstaking, time-consuming, and just gross. I will not order again, though I would probably be happy with a different Adidas sandal (one without the nubs).

product_title: Steve Madden Women's Outtlaww Ankle Boot
review_headline: Flaw is in the dedication to consumers
review_body:
Did they think we wouldn't wear these or notice???
I lived in these -- and loved them--
more than any pair of boots I've ever owned in my life.
They are supple, nice leather. The studs don't fall off after using them as your favorite "ruffed up" boots either. The mistake is in the design - how can a reputable company choose to use hollow heels in their design or when piecing and pouring boot rubber?
My heels, on both pairs, wore down to holes- four of them - as the boot rubber wasn't poured as a solid piece- more like a decorative pair that tries to be pretty for a season? The heels are hollow with walls and cross pieces of rubber- and the final rubber bit that covers the surface you walk on - if you wear these too long any wear on them finally result in a hole- that grows bigger every time you walk in them- God forbid you trip on the little rubber rubbings that roll off-

- I ask the company- why bother with the real leather and solid trimmings if I couldn't even wear them for a year?
Honestly, I'd probably *begrudgingly* buy another pair - if the price were reflected in that heel- as I have several similar style boots, by other assorted companies-- and not one came close to this pair - it is unfortunate that I can't say better for the madden company anymore though- my trust is shot.

product_title: Maelstrom COMMANDO 9'' Black Military Combat Boots
review_body:
I spent 14 years in the military - in the Infantry mostly, so boots were and are something I take very seriously. I've owned several pairs of jungles in my time, some as cheap as $19 and some as expensive as $100. These boots stand toe to toe with the $100 boots, possibly even surpassing them. The fit is perfect, wiggle room at the toe, not binding across the top of the foot, not too narrow, and not too wide. I'm wearing them with simple gym socks at the moment and the fit is ridiculously comfy, but there's room in there if I needed to throw on a pair of heavier socks - which is incredibly important as it allows me to wear these when it gets cold out. One thing that helps these boots stand apart from many others I've owned is the cushion at the top of the boot, that wraps around the calf when the boot is tied. Many boots lack this entirely, while on others that have it it's very stiff. This is straight up comfy.

I received them a day early and strapped them on instantly. My wife forced me to take them off at bedtime or else I'd have probably just left them on. Just kidding.... kinda...

On the whole I couldn't possibly be happier with this purchase!

product_title: Magnum Men's Response II 8'' Side-Zip Boot
review_headline: Began falling apart at nine months
review_body:
Quite possibly the worst quality boots I've ever bought. After nine months of general wear around the station and on the ambulance the sole began separating from the upper in the toe area (on both boots!). Within a couple weeks the boots were unwearable, the upper and the sole had separated well past the balls of my toes. It looks like that outside of an inch of stitching between the plastic of the sole and the leather there's only a few spots of glue that hold everything together and when the stitching goes, the boots are toast. In addition to the separating problem, one of the metal eyelets for the laces popped out of the leather on one boot, and a seam on the upper began unraveling on the other. Had the soles not started falling off I'm pretty sure this would have killed them as well.
I've been wearing this style of Magnums for a decade plus now, I'm used to the plastic zipper tab breaking off and the Velcro degrading, that's a pretty common problem with them, but to not be able to get a year of use out of them because they start disintegrating is a little ridiculous.

product_title: Dan Post Men's Denver Western Boot
review_body:
The boots are nothing less than outstanding! The quality of the material and the quality of the boot is very nice, they fit well and they are comfortable to wear instantly out of the box but have gotten even more comfortable a few hours into wearing them. The upper leather is soft and the stitches are well done, the caiman looks and feels great, the sole is easy to walk on and provides a nice grip. I only say they felt loose due to me wearing mostly hiking boots 90% of the time and after a couple of hours there was no heel slip.
The inside is cushioned well and very comfortable as I wore them for around 6 hours right out of the box. The boot is just a very good looking and very comfortable well made product and at a great discount I would highly recommend these boots. They are good looking enough to go out with but not overly loud so they look great with a pair of jeans. Just the right mix for myself , they are not too dressy and not to plain... Just a damn fine looking boot that performs like a good boot should and looks better than I expected.
Do yourself a favor and buy an exotic skin / leather conditioner as the caiman can dry out easily so be sure to take care of your boots and they will take care of you!

review_headline: Excellent boot but the crackling sound is real and very annoying.
review_body:
This is an excellent boot, and definitely worth its price. The size is true to the Brannock Device, so for a foot that has been measured properly, it will fit as expected. While measuring, however, it is important to keep in consideration the type of socks that will be used with the boot, but that is a standard procedure recommended by the Brannock Device anyway. Of course, contrary to some of the lighter boots (that will also last much less), this is top quality leather and needs to be broken in. I have used the recommended leather dressing from Danner, and it does help in the breaking in process as stated. Quite recommended. Once the boot is broken in, it is comfortable and wearable. Some people state that they order a larger size because at first the boot feels a bit snug. However, that would seem to be a good formula for blisters. When hiking, I like to feel the boot wrap around the foot snug (not uncomfortable) so that the foot will not slide and cause blisters. Breaking in this boot will give you that type of fitting. My only reservation is the style of the tongue. It is nice and it would seem functional, but the leather, the way it is cut and sown together, seems to bunch, creating excessive volume on the top of the foot. Once laced, that may create some discomfort for those who are sensitive on the top of their feet. The outer sole is great for hiking. The way the heel is shaped provides great support when stepping over branches or rocks as the grips of the Vibram sole are continuous under the shoe. Some other soles have a slippery spot between the ball of the foot and the heel.

UPDATE: After beginning to break in these boots, unfortunately I run into the problem several other people have encountered: the right heel would make a loud crackling sound at every step. Obviously something definitely wrong with the boot. The sound is way too loud to ignore.

When I purchased these boots, I double-checked for free returns on the exact boots I was buying and it was there, but when I received the boots and found the sizing was garbage and tried to return them, I was met with a message that said they were not eligible for return...wait, what?? There was no indication of why, either.   I called Amazon and was told that they were not returnable because they were listed as hazardous materials...wait, again. What?? Did you not just ship them TO me and now you're telling me that you do not have the ability to get them shipped back? How does that make sense to ANYONE? And are they actually hazardous, or not? Do I want these things on my feet at all? No one can tell me.   Fortunately, Amazon made it right and I now have a free pair of potentially hazardous boots that are too small. Woohoo.   To top it off, the build quality of these boots is not impressive-I certainly wouldn't have tried them on in a store and been willing to pay one-sixty; everything is subpar on them.   I most likely won't be ordering shoes on Amazon again and I doubt I'll buy anything Demonia or Pleaser in the future. It's terribly disappointing to wait a week or two, with bated breath, for your awesome boots to arrive only to find out they're made-in-China-poopoo and may cause undesirable genetic mutations as, sadly, it never works out like in the movies. I'd probably end up with a frog's head sprouting from my big toe or weeping abscesses all over my body or perhaps I'd just start pooping pure cancer.   WHY is there not a zero or negative star option?? Sigh. Oh well, live and learn.

These boots are GREAT!  I love the way they lace up too.  You pull on the strings and slide the little plastic thing down to lock the laces.  I'm just hoping this lasts over time.  I am thinking of getting an extra pair since I see they have dropped in price by $20 since I bought them less than a month ago.

review_headline: Cool looking boots with a easy to fix flaw.
review_body: As with all tactical boots, its runs 1 to 1/2 size larger compare to normal footwear. There is not break in needed, but takes awhile to find the perfect ICS adjustment. The boots has alot of space inside, that i manage to add another insole on top of the insole it comes with it for added comfort for long hours of standing.  This boots isnt really good for hot summer weather, feel my feet is very hot inside the boots when wore outdoors, The vibram sole is virtually not as good as it marketed, as its extremely slippery when walking on wet floor and highly polished floors in shopping malls.  As someone to doesnt wear boots frequently, i do find heavy after walking on them for some distance  And like some other reviewers mentioned, this boots will cause pain on ankle area, .This is really true when trying to bend my foot or walking down the stairs. But i noticed this issue to cause when the boot lace at the ankle are is tighten. As when we bend our foot our ankle area will expend. So i solve is issue easily by using tactical Elastic cord as bootlace.  UPDATE: After about 2yrs owning this boots, which i didnt really wear them regularly. And i decided to change my review from 4 stars to 2. Here's why: 1. After about 1yr+ the one of the boot's stitches on the gore tex lining near the heel area has opened up, But have yet had a chance to test if it affects the waterproof. 2.The gore tex lining at the base of both boots have detach itself from the sole. 3. For some reasons, the "sponge" at the mid back of the boots have "popped" out and i have to use glue to glue it back.  Update as of 16th Aug 2016: boots rotting away. left my job since June 2015, and this boots was sitting on my shoe rack ever since. And today i decided to polish is up to wear in out for some action. But upon close look the the sole, i notice bits of the shiny rubber seems to have disappeared. And from there is saw the internal of the sole is starting to give way. product_title: Merrell Men's Bare Access 2 Minimal Trail Running Shoe
review_headline: Amazing comfort. Best shoes I've ever worn for refereeing soccer.
review_body:
I use these as a soccer referee. These are the best shoes I have ever purchased for that purpose. Here's why:

1) Very light weight - MUCH lighter than my adidas cleats (obviously). These shoes almost as light as the box they came in. I didn't think that was actually possible. These are probably just as light as the inov8 shoes I used to wear, but these are better than the inov8 shoes because...

2) Highly durable - My inov8 shoes developed holes over my pinky toes, a result of all the side-stepping I do when working as an Assistant Referee. These Merrell shoes have had no issues with holes.
EDIT: Not as durable as I thought. While the inov8 shoes lasted one season, these shoes lasted two. Still double the life of the inov8 shoes, but "highly durable" is not an accurate description.

3) HUGE toe box - Best feature of all. My toes have never been so comfortable in a pair of soccer/running shoes. I'm so spoiled by these, that I refuse to wear my adidas cleats unless a field is soaking wet, because I'd rather have comfortable toes.

4) Completely flat - I like this because it means I can put my own insole into the shoe and not have to compensate for the shape of the shoe itself. I've actually stopped using gel insoles, possibly because these shoes are so comfortable that I no longer feel the need to improve them.

Only downside: These are not waterproof AT ALL. Just like my inov8 shoes, these are not meant to be worn in the rain...or early in the morning if there is dew on the grass! product_title: Teva Men's Hurricane XLT Sandal, Black, 9 US
review_headline: Excellent and highly adjustable fit - fits very similarly to Katavi which with more padding is more comfortable
review_body:
I got in one shipment all in size mens size 11:

Teva Obern 11
Teva Toachi 11
Teva Katavi 11
Teva Hurricane 11

Hurricane - these are very nice and highly adjustable because of the way the heel and mid-foot strapping integrates together. This was only true for the Hurricanes. It was possible to get them to fit quite comfortably, in spite of the material looking like it might be harsh, because of the way these can be adjusted for fit - and because the heel strap can ride very low on the heel vs. on the ankle.

One thing I did not like in the Hurricanes was the velcro running all the way down to the sole of the shoe. For me, velcro picks up lint and fluff all the time and having that huge amount of excess ‘hook’ portion of velcro is not a good thing. I am certain that after a short time that would be just a mass of stuff picked up and stuck to the ‘hook’ velcro segment that is left exposed.

I found, however, that for me the Katavi were more comfortable than the Hurricanes because of the extra strap padding and the mesh and padded panels. Because I don’t need them for water, the Katavi made better sense. There was virtually no exposed velcro for them when they were adjusted to fit me - another plus.

Hurricane 10 1/2 oz 295g (single mens 11)

Here are the differences and comparisons of the various sandals (see photos):

Weight of single sandal (size 11):

Obern 383g (13 1/2oz)
Toachi 343g (12oz)
Katavi 308g (10 3/4oz)
Hurricane 295g (10 1/2oz)

Note that that the Katavi and Hurricane XLT weigh almost exactly the same, even though the Hurricane is billed as ultra-light and the Katavi not advertised as such so much by Teva.

The four from top, side, tread are in review photos.

Hurricane and Katavi had identical treads with different slightly foot beds. The shape and foot fit of the beds was virtually identical for the Hurricane and Katavi. The Obern was close, but had a higher arch support and was more rigid and felt a bit narrower at the middle foot. I felt the arch support too much on the Oberns. The Toachi in contrast had an extremely narrow tread and footbed and my foot could not even fit on it.

All of these were size 11 in mens - but they fit very differently.

The Hurricane and Katavi are the most similar, and the Katavi with the extra side mesh panels and suede material for the strapping was much more comfortable with and without socks. The material used for the Hurricanes was not nearly as comfortable and the expose rings added to that feeling compared to the Katavi. review_headline: Initially good, but proved to be of very poor quality.
review_body: I bought these boots for an impromptu hiking trip and I have to say I'm really happy with their support and comfort. For the price I think they are quite a value. I had to basically ditch them halfway through a hike, as it felt better to walk barefoot than to wear them. product_title: Star Flower Cotton Stonewashed Sling Crossbody Bohemian Hobo Handbag in Denim
review_headline: A Beautiful Bag - A SUPER BAG with a good Purse Organizer
review_body: I have a hard time with large bags. I'm only 5'2\\", and I have narrow shoulders so straps tend to slip off easily if they are too long. And then most somewhat large purses either look comical on me or give me the appearance of carrying a diaper bag (we are well past that stage).     However, as I care full-time for a young child I needed something that was large and easy to carry. I was also hoping to find something unique and somewhat environmentally-friendly. Often I carry my sundries (a little makeup, my wallet/keys), sunscreen/hand cleaner, a small first aid kit, several little activity books (love Dover for that purpose), wipes, some folded reusable bags, my iPhone, and sometimes a Boogie Board (to keep my daughter engaged on long trips), mints, and/or my Kindle (to keep me engaged during my kid's long classes). And it'd be nice to still have room for a small snack, too.     On a whim, I decided to try a cotton Hobo bag. They seem to be spacious, durable, and they fit along with a person's form very nicely (solving my issues with it \\"looking\\" too big and falling off my shoulder), and they have unique looks. I liked the simpleness and colors on this bag. I also like it isn't covered with a bunch of Ohm and peace symbols (no offense to my fellow yoga- and peace-lovers). I was very pleased with the aesthetics when I received it. It is indeed colorful and unique. However, I wasn't completely sure it would fit my needs.     At first, I thought it only had one pocket (on the inside). I didn't see the cell phone pocket right away. It's there! It's made from the same fabric as the handle so it blends in very nicely. It barely fits my iPhone 4s with a bulky Otterbox so it may fit larger phones if their covers/skins aren't thick. But even with the cell phone, it was very easy to lose things inside in the bag. The perfect solution was a purse organizer! Amazon sells them for $6-10, and they are wonder! They come in different colors, have handles to easily pull them out ofthe purse, and fit perfectly inside a larger bag like this.     Now I that can find all my things, this purse is perfect! It's beautiful, the strap stays put where ever I wear it (I can do cross body or just put it on one side), and it fits all my stuff with loads of room to boot! This may be one of the smartest purchases I made. I will certainly look for more bags in this style in the future!

review_headline: These boots are not the junk you buy at a department store, these are serious boots on par with the big "D" maker of boots
review_body:
I've switched from the big "D" manufacturer in boots, after they discontinued the one I had been wearing for years. These have been working well for me, and to be honest, I have really flat and messed up feet. I've had to get cortisone shots, wear orthodics, going to physical therapy, etc. so this gives you some insight. These boots are the only thing my feet will now accept. I bought this style as the black (which I wear for work) are no longer available - well, they get a pair here and there, but they seem to be out of stock most of the time. So I figured I'd give this color a try. I know it says green and brown, but it is a subtle green and after some wear it won't look green I'm sure. It looks more like a grayish green, not bright green.

So, to save a few bucks I went with this color and there are so few of these boots around, and I'm not disappointed. They fit exactly the same as the black ones. They are great boots and accept orthodics well, which most do not. They are waterproof and have a goretex liner. I've had no problems with the hardware that holds the laces onto the boot, this seems to be a non-issue. I've bought 3 pairs of the black ones and 1 pair of these brown/green.

Size: I am a true size 8.5 and got these in an 8 because the 9s were sold out and I read they ran big. I tried them on with thick socks and they fit ok. They feel a hair tight, but I think that's to be expected since they are half s size smaller and wearing thinner socks might fix it.
Looks: In terms of looks, these boots are actually cute for rain/snow boots. They look better in person than the photos here. The paisley is subtle and they are not very shiny. Though the toes are very round which make them look bulky and a bit like child's galoshes (I prefer more of a sleeker almond toe). But that's just my preference and some may like the rounded toe.
Warmth/Functionality: I haven't worn them out since I'm not sure if I'm keeping them. But they seem like would be very warm. I wore them for about 10 minutes inside with thick socks on and my feet felt hot. Since there are no zippers/seams, I don't doubt they are fully waterproof. With that said, they are a bit hard to get off with no zips, but the kicks tabs on the heels helps. But I worry how durable those would be over time. Overall they seem durable and heavy duty.
The main reason I may return is that they are extremely heavy. The bottom of the boot mainly attributes to this. I felt totally weighted down when wearing these. Also the ankle is very inflexible, so it felt like I was clunking around when wearing these.

product_title: Ariat Men's Rambler Wide Square Toe Western Cowboy Boot
review_body:
Ariat’s Rambler Boot has been one of my favorite boots I have bought so far. I purchased these boot about 4 years ago and they just ripped out this winter. Overall these boots have been my day in day out boots and been able to hold up to walking constantly and also working in them on the farm.
Durability:
The durability of these boots is great. Like I just stated before these boots have been through a lot in the last 4 years and just finally gave out. There are a lot of products out there to make your boots more water proof and also last longer, but I have never applied anything to these boots. I am saying this because they, just by themselves are durable and waterproof.
Fit:
I tried on my boots in the store but when I did try them on I also tried many different brands of boots. All different brands of boots fit differently in my opinion, but I think the Ariat boots fit the best for my feet. I have slightly wider feet and the Ariat’s all had enough room for my feet to fit perfectly. The Rambler boots also were able to be broken in very quickly. This is always a positive to anyone that is buying new boots to wear.
Overall these boots, in my opinion, are the best boots you can buy at the specific price. These boots have managed to last me a long time, and been able to standup to everyday wear and tear and also extreme wear at some times. The Rambler boot has been a great purchase of mine and I will be ordering another pair soon.

product_title: Saucony Men's Endorphin LD4 Track Shoe
review_headline: Great racing spike-even in the heat
review_body: This spike is designed for a two mile race or longer. (Using it for a one mile race works, but the Md4 is better for that) The spike performed excellently in my first race. These are incredibly light and fast. The product comes with the shoe, 8 spikes, a spike wrench to remove spikes, and a drawbag backpack for storage. I tried these on inside with the spikes in, and I chipped part of the tile. Don't wear these unless you are walking onto the track. Walking on concrete can dull them. The spikes are very sharp, but easy to lose. I would recommend getting some spares. The flex film around this show is as thin as paper. The inside material is soft and comfortable. As a result, racing barefoot in this spike is still comfortable. I've ran a few 2 mile races in these, and they work great. This is one of the best spikes you can get for a 2 mile to a 10k race. (On track only) And I don't know why that one reviewer complained of blisters on his foot after the heat. I raced in the 95 degree heat in these and my feet felt great afterwards. Some people even say spikes hurt their feet after a race, but I've never had any problem with these.

review_headline: The best boots for your dollar
review_body:
Fastest shipping ever! I ordered these shoes with regular 5-7 day free shipping.... I got them in 2 days! So no complaints there.

For those expecting sneaker quality fit... STOP looking for boots! Boots do not fit like sneakers. Boots are always made 1 size bigger so buy 1 size smaller. I'm a size 11, so I wear 10 in boots. I have regular size width in my feet so these fit like a glove. Perfect from all sides. They will be tight at first. You MUST wear all boots in over time. The fit gets better and better with time. For people complaining about creasing...call me when the world is a perfect place and cars don't crash, phones don't break, and boots don't crease.

Be honest with yourself, if you have hulk sized feet then buy hulk sized heavy duty extra wide boots....not these formal /casual fashion boots.

These boots go with light and dark gray denim, khakis, dress pants and even suits. Very versatile and worth every penny. They have decent arch support and good padding. Best with slim jeans or slim dress pants.

review_headline: Great look but sizing is way off.
review_body: I really wanted to love these shoes because I feel like a small heel makes them look a little more professional than a normal ballet. I don't think ordering a medium would have fixed the comfort issues.  They have rubber soles which is great for not slipping and soft cushioning inside.  The first pair I received must have been a Nordstrom floor model because the tags were still on them at $124 so if you can make these work it's a great value!  Just realize you may need to try on a lot of shoes before this works.

product_title: adidas Performance Men's Drehkraft Training Shoe
review_body:
I finally upgraded from my VS Oly shoes I had for years, my lifts are to the point I could benefit from a nicer shoe.
Fit: I wear a Vans classic 11.5 and that's what I ordered. They are slightly big but an 11 would probably be a little too snug. I have a narrow foot but these work just fine but I wouldn't recommend them for someone with wide feet.
Closure: The BOA system is definitely different but I love it! Plus it has a lifetime warranty so why not? If you are the person that cinches down your velcro straps until you loose circulation these won't be tight enough for you. I'm not one of those people but my foot doesn't move it all when tight. Also I don't like to walk around the gym in them so this makes it easy to slip them off to go the the restroom.
Heel: It's a little on the tall side (1" I believe) but I have long leg bones so it benefits me just fine.
Toe: The toe was easy to break in during split jerks and felt very stable.
Sole: Great grip but too early to judge durability.

Why not 4 stars? Adidas offers some beautiful designs and colors but this was the only color for this model. Not a deal breaker as I would definitely recommend them!

product_title: Altra Running Womens Superior 2 Trail Running Shoe
review_body:
Altra Superior 2.0 -- size 8.5 -- Orange-"ish"/yellow with blue
**I always wear a size 8.5 in athletic shoes but originally ordered a size 9.0 (which have been returned) in these thinking they ran small. They do not and run true to size**

Altra’s are by far the most comfortable athletic shoe I have ever worn. Roomy and flexible, no break in period needed. They have replaced all of my other sneakers for both the gym and running.

ZERO DROP transition has been pretty seamless so far but I spend a fair amount of time barefoot, so I think that helped. I did have some tightness in my Achilles and glutes but I’m neither concerned nor surprised. Altra's have made me much more aware of how my foot hits the ground which is helping to improve my running form. In turn, that is working some muscles and stretching some tendons that were not being engaged properly before.

The roomy FOOT SHAPED TOE BOX is heavenly now that my toes have learned to relax, unfurl and use the extra space. IMO the Altra Superior 2.0 is not quite as roomy through this area as the Altra Lone Peak 2.0 but it is still leaps and bounds beyond what a traditional athletic shoe offers.

I also recommend anyone who wants more room through the forefoot area to try the alternative lacing (picture included below) suggestion which can be found on the AltraRunning website. It really does make quite a difference!

The outsole traction is great. My nightly runs take me through various terrains. These easily transition from one surface to another – road, to rocky coral trails, sand, up and down flights of stairs, wet grass, etc. without losing a step.

The uppers (thankfully!) breathe very well. It’s almost always humid in my neck of the woods and these do a great job of wicking away the sweat.

Great athletic shoes! Highly recommend!

**REVIEWER INFO**
40-something years old, 5'3", 115-120lbs
Dailyweight training for eon’s now, added running about six months ago......’cause the weight training by itself just isn’t cutting it anymore. ;-)
3-5 miles, 5 nights a week
Wide forefoot and slightly high arches
Tend to under-pronate (supinate) and heel strike
Varied terrain -- pavement, gravel, wet docks, coral hardpack trails, grass, sand

I normally wore Adidas Thrashers (v1.1) (size 8.5) and an old pair of Saucony Ride (v3 I think) (size 8.5).
Upgraded to the Brooks Ghost 7 (size 8.5) when I started running. Great shoe for some but the jump to a 12mm heel-toe drop (along with my heel strike habit) had my lower back screaming within a week.
I then tried the Pearl iZUMi EM Trail N2 (size 8.5). I found these too restrictive and didn't even make it out the front door. Narrow throughout and the heel cup was uncomfortably tight. Couldn't wait to get these off my feet!
Thankfully stumbled upon Altra running shoes......aahhh yyeeaaahhhh!! Never going back to "traditional" athletic shoes again.

product_title: UGG Australia Mens Ascot Camo Slipper
review_headline: A little too warm, but hard to beat... and I've tried!
review_body:
A couple of years back my wife got me a pair of black leather Ascot slippers for Christmas. I liked them a lot and wore them almost every day, for hours and hours. A couple years later (this past Christmas in fact) we noticed that they were smelling REALLY bad. Yikes! Time to replace them, I decided.

Since the Ascots made my feet kinda hot and sweaty at times (thus the stench), I decided to try something different. I went through many different brands and styles, including Bearpaw, Sorel, Cushe, Sanuk, Oneill, and even a different UGG, the Alder. I thought the Alder would be great because they were supposed to be variant of the Ascot, but they were too narrow, and the soles were hard; it felt/looked more like a dress shoe than a slipper.

So I relented and ordered these Camo Ascots and right off the bat they are awesome. Of course, my feet are gonna sweat so I'll have to find some kind of solution to keep them from getting stinky, but it's worth it. They are so comfy and nice, and of course the quality is really great.

I was going to remove one star for the warmth factor, but that could just be my feet. Also, they run a bit small, but in this day and age you need to try on different sizes. When it come to shoes I wear anywhere from size 11.5-12.5 on average, and sometimes a 13. I got a 13 in these and they are a little tight but I know form experience that they will break in (they will stretch a bit, and the copious insulation will get matted down a bit).

Highly recommended!

product_title: PUMA Men's Cell Surin Cross-Training Shoe
review_headline: Product Review of the PUMA Men's Cell Surin Cross-Training Shoe
review_body:
I was interested in running shoes that were comfortable, reasonably priced, functional, and a style I liked. I was also looking for a shoe that was of high quality and very durable. These PUMA Men's Cell Surin Cross-Training shoes met all of my needs and were a great purchase.

Style & Price

The shoe size I ordered (size 11.5) was exactly the right size for a comfortable fit. There are a variety of different colors to choose from which was beneficial to me because I can be quite picky when it comes to the color style of my shoes. The eight shoe styles have various prices ranging from $39.99-$80.00 which provided financial flexibility when it came to choosing a style I could afford.

Drawbacks

One difficulty I encountered was that two of the shoe styles I was interested in were not available in my shoe size. Fortunately, there was another style which also interested me. Another drawback was that the prices for some of the styles were on the higher end of the price range. However, I was pleased with the shoes after receiving and wearing them.

Benefits

Some of my previous running shoes have worn out more quickly than expected. The Puma Men's Cell Surin Cross-Training shoes have lasted longer than any other pair of running shoes I have owned. I have bought running shoes priced well over $100 in the past and these lower priced Puma shoes have performed just as well as the more expensive shoes I have owned.

I hope this review was helpful to you in making a purchasing decision regarding the Men's Cell Surin Cross-Training shoe.

product_title: Mark Nason Los Angeles Men's Watford Slip-On Loafer
review_body: The Watfords are one of many shoes in the Mark Nason line of Skechers. I own seven different pair and all are fantastic. Characterized by their styling; memory foam footbed; extremely light weight; extra, contrasting shoelaces (I always use); and tri-color design, these shoes elicit compliments from friends and strangers alike.    As with any sueded upper, you'll need to exercise a little additional care. I recommend spraying with Kiwi suede/nubuck protector. Dark colors won't change at all but with the lighter ones, you'll want to spot test an unseen section of the tongue first and allow 24 hours to dry. I did this with the tan and there was no change in color. I also used Scotchguard, which had no effect on navy and chocolate brown, but it did darken the test area of my tan Watfords and light gray Emboldens.    (Here's a little tip: If you want to enhance the appearance of the shoe and maximize protection of the toe area on the light colors, take a strip of duct tape and place it about two inches up from the tip of the toe... the place where a cap toe shoe usually has a seam. Make sure the tape extends straight down the sides and onto the sole. Spray the exposed toe - top and sides - heavily with Scotchguard, let it dry and repeat several times. The tape helps create a straight line with a considerably darkened toe but the rest of the shoe retains its original light color. If done correctly [and it's hard to screw it up] you'll possess a two-tone shoe that looks exponentially more stylish.)    I walk on asphalt and concrete for up to 10 hours a day and these shoes hold up like a champ. Since there are other sites that carry the full line, I would recommend searching \\"Mark Nason Skechers\\" to check them all out. Comparison shop all you want, but don't question quality - it's there.

product_title: Altra Women's Torin 1.5 Running Shoe
review_body:
I LOVE this shoe! Right out of the box they are a dream. It's like running in your bare feet - so comfortable you don't even think about having shoes on. I have a wide foot and other running shoes always caused discomfort and pain. After running 35-45 minutes in my Asics Gel Cumulus my feet always began to burn in spots or tingle. I could never find a running shoe that did not squeeze my foot. I attempted to switch to more of a minimalist shoe and while the fit was better I need more cushion. In the past I've experienced calf pain, heel pain, and achilles tendonitis. Not anymore! I pray they never quit making this shoe.

I run with these mainly on roads and the traction is good - have done some trail running in them and they are okay - the bottom is basically smooth so i wouldn't recommend for really rocky or slick conditions. Looking into a trail version for that.

Highly recommend going to Altra's website for sizing - they have a shoe guide that will compare your shoe with theirs and recommend size. If you have a wide foot, I highly recommend these shoes.

review_body:
This is my third pair of these boots. I'm meat cutter and I'm on my feet 8-10 hours a day. Blood/water/cleaning chemicals/bleach hits them on a daily basis. I average about 2 years out of pair which is pretty good for them being under $100. Coworkers with redwings etc don't hold up as long or they have to have them resoled every 6 months @ $60 a pop.

Eventually on these boots, the lugs on the bottom wear flat, making it not so slip resistant. The rubber outsole tears away from the upper (the front of the boot where your toes are) exposing a hole for water to enter. Its been the same things every time I replace them. I don't see this as a design flaw, just from use and abuse. Order with confidence its a great boot.

product_title: Red Wing Heritage Men's Work Chukka
review_headline: Great Boot. Worth the price. Fits well. Solid Quality
review_body:
After about a week of wearing these boots, I can say that I love them!

As other reviewers have mentioned, the bridge part of the shoe (about where the bottom lace is) is very very tight the first couple days. This WILL get better, in fact, it goes away. The boot now fits perfectly and the soles are starting to adjust to my feet. Size was as expected, when you first put them on you will think they are huge as it feels like there is a lot of spare room in the toe.. which there probably is, but the boot fits in a way where this is meant to be there. Buy the size you would normally wear. RedWing also has a sizing chart.

These boots feel rock solid as far as the quality goes, I wish they came with some detailed instructions on how to properly care for them though.

Anyway, I struggled for a long time with this purchase, they aren't cheap for sure. These Chukkas (The Heritage Edition) are slightly different than the 595 Chukkas, and appear to be slightly more expensive, I think either would be a good buy. But I am not near a RedWing store, and Amazon's free return policy was hard to beat!

review_body:
I purchased these shoes for my R.I.P.P.E.D. class which has a lot of pivoting, pushups, lunges, etc. These were recommended by my instructor as an affordable shoe that works for this type of workout.

Pro: I am a classic size 8 (but a little on the narrow side) and these fit my length perfectly. They do the exact thing i purchased them for; they give me balance with a solid foot bed, good arch support, and the flatter outer sole made for pivoting. Aesthetically they look just as cute in person as they do in the picture.

Con: They are oddly wide in the pad of the foot but narrow quite a bit in the arch area. I have a semi-narrow foot so the more narrow arch and heel works great. The wide pad area of the shoe does let my foot slide a bit but not enough to make me return them. The shoe is okay quality. They are not soft and I foresee them lasting about 6-8 months. **but my pair of Nikes I paid $110 for only last 6 months in the inner sole as they broke down but the rest of the shoe is still going strong.

All in all if the sole holds up at least 6 months or more, matching my previous Nikes, then I feel it's worth ordering again to get a shoe that is made precisely for the type of exercise I do. This is a cute, supportive, solid shoe for any cross fit type exercise. I noticed a big difference the first day when I did a one legged lunge with weights. Had no trouble keeping my balance at all.

product_title: Garmont Men's Dragontail Lite Approach Shoe
review_body:
Firstly, I did not but these shoes from Amazon, but from Bergfreunde.de in Germany, delivered to the UK (I don't think they deliver to the US).

I am extremely impressed with these shoes after about a month of ownership and use. They are made in China, but are of very high quality. The uppers are relatively thick, durable suede, and linings are good quality fabric which look like they won't wear through easily. The rubber rand goes most of the way around the sidewalls of the shoes, providing excellent abrasion resistance, added stiffness and a measure of water resistance. The heel counters are very stiff and there are also rubber overlays around the backs of the heels. The pull-tabs on both the tongue and heel are good features which aid putting on and adjusting the fit, and the lace-to-toe closure offers easy customization of fit adjustment - you can have a loose fit for casual walking, and a very tight secure fit for challenging climbs.

The soles have an excellent pattern for general hiking and use, not too aggressive and fairly low profile, so with the EVA midsole they have an excellent combination of stiffness and flexibility. They bend naturally with the foot motion and allow you to get some ground feel, but protect you from sharp rocks. They give a lot of grip and confidence when hiking on slopes and rocky ground.

I have not used them in wet weather yet. I suspect that they would get soaked fairly quickly in heavy rain. There is a Goretex version available for those needing more water resistance.

Regarding sizing, they are quite a small fitting in both the length and width. My foot is 11.25 inches long and 4.3 inches at the widest point (when relaxed), so "officially" I am US 12. I ordered size 13.5 in these shoes and they fit very well, are very comfortable with NO toe bump into the front of the shoe when descending. So I would recommend going up 1 or 1.5 sizes from true size for a proper fit, especially if your feet are wider than average.

They come in a variety of very cool colours - mine are the "jeans / black" colourway. They have an athletic and stylish appearance, a hint of the "rock climber" aura and unusual enough to get noticed and commented on but not embarrassingly so.

This will definitely be my "go-to" pair of shoes for hiking and general outdoor activities!

I treated them with my Frye leather  protector as soon as they arrived. Boots will last a lifetime if you take care of them properly. Wiping salt stains off after each wear and treating often with leather protectant. The only thing that disappointed  was I had hoped there would be more arch support than there is.They have moderate insole and I have a higher arch. I do love that the removable insole is lined with the same microfiber fur lining that is throughout the boot. So warm & COZY! The boots are comfortable and stylish. Although if I am going for a long walk I add my othaheel insole for additional support. I have been wearing them daily for about a month in all types of winter conditions. Received lots of compliments on them especially with skinny jeans!

product_title: New Balance Women's WT1110 Trail Running Shoe
review_headline: New Balance - consistently what I need!
review_body:
I've been purchasing New Balance athletic shoes for many years - I have wide (2E) feet, and have found them to fit well and be very supportive for working out, walking outdoors, and running errands.

This was a new style for me, so I wasn't sure if I was going to find the same fit/quality I've had from their heavier cross-training models. I'm happy to say that I wasn't disappointed - they fit just as well as any other New Balance shoes I've owned. The width is great, the support is good, and they have no problems accommodating my arch supports.

I found this model to be very light weight, which was nice after the heavier cross trainers I've been wearing. They are also well-ventilated, which was nice during cardio at the gym.

I did wear them around the house for a couple of evenings before wearing them for a full workout at the gym, but I don't really know that I needed to. I wore them for a workout (cardio and light resistance), and had absolutely no issues. The tread is also great for walking/treadmill work.

I'd definitely buy them again!

product_title: Momo Baby Boys Soft Sole Leather Crib Bootie Shoes - 12-18 Months/4.5-5.5 M US Toddler
review_body:
Great crib shoe, and good for a little one first learning to walk. They have a soft sole that is suede to prevent slipping, which is especially handy for new walkers, and they are light weight so they don't discourage walking. They get your little one accustomed to shoes while protecting their feet. My son wore these for about two months before his first 'real' shoes and they held up to his walking/toddling/falling/crawling well and made switching to actual shoes a breeze. They are a little snug at first (like all shoes you need to break them in) but easily should fit most babies. At about 12 months you'll want to transition to a sturdier shoe anyhow so the size ranges shouldn't be a problem.

If your baby has NBA player sized feet and you're worried the weight of an actual shoe will discourage walking but these are much too snug, I've found sandals to be a good alternative. They'll protect the foot, aren't too heavy, and babies are cute enough to pull off wearing them with socks still. lol.

review_headline: Wanted to like this but I bought this for my iPhone 6 and ...
review_body:
Wanted to like this but I bought this for my iPhone 6 and just keeping everything together.

Phone Pocket:
The pocket for the phone was tight and made it hard to take the phone conveniently in and out.

Wallet Pockets:
The wallet pocket was the part I dislike the most. After putting all my cards in - which fit all the sleeves for cards - the whole wallet became really stiff and it became almost impossible to take any cards out because it just became too tight and bulky. Stacking vertically the cards may not be the best idea.

Wallet Material:
The material overall, was just okay and could have been better. I think it's because of the material that it made the pockets for the credit card so stiff and impossible to use if, especially, all the pockets are occupied.

I wouldn't recommend this product. I also bought a similar leather version of this one - Kate Spade New York Cobble Hill Louie - and it didn't work out either. For that one, the pocket was too tight and the zipper ended up too close to the phone body.

One I would recommend, which is a little bigger but more worth the money is Kate spade new york Sunset Court Sable Wallet, Black/Pebble, That one is a clutch and fit EVERYTHING I need in there at once - chapstick, phone, house key, cards, cash... perfect size and material is really beautiful!

product_title: Win8Fong Women Ladies Black Skull Diamante Crossbody Shoulder Satchel Bag
review_headline: Nice purse for under 20.00 but i wouldn't pay more than that.
review_body:
I purchased this purse from another listing last year. That listing has a slightly lower review because the price was higher. The price in this listing seems to make it a better value.
PROS: Spacious, attractive. In a year of use I never lost any of the rivets or skulls, they are attached well and are made of real metal (which does make the purse heavy.) The lining, zippers, and magnetic closures also held up the entire year and I am NOT easy on a purse.
CONS: Purse is heavy and this showed in wear in the area below where the shoulder strap attaches. This purse eventually lost it's shape causing it to flatten out when I set it down, not a big deal, but it's something you might want to know about. The handle on the top relies on the purse being totally zipped/closed/magnetic closured to be used..this was a HUGE negative for me because the magnetic closures were not quick to line up and close. I felt like it was just too much time and effort to line everything up in order to close the purse. I ended up only using the shoulder strap and leaving the top flap unsecured. It day stay covered because the skull is so heavy, but I could never use the handle and that was a big negative for me.

All that said, I do this the purse deserves 3.5 stars overall. The low price in this listing is what is making it worthy of 4 stars, I paid 10.00 more. The other listing also listed it as gray, but is in fact black. I do still have people asking about this purse though, so clearly it still looks good at a glance.

product_title: Hi-Tec Women's Apollo Multisport Shoe
review_body: I love, love, love these shoes! I was looking for a pair of comfortable hiking shoes with excellent grip because I like to do a little bouldering when I go out on my hiking excursions. These shoes have been everything that I was looking for. They are so comfortable that I even love wearing them to work on days when I don't feel like dressing up as much. As a teacher, I am on my feet for most of the day, so having comfortable shoes is a must. Whenever I wear them, the insoles are so cushiony that they even give me a little bit of a spring in my step. As for the outsoles, I got to try them out on the rocks at the Harpers Ferry overlook on Maryland Heights and they worked better than any shoe I've ever owned. The shoes held me, even on rocks with smooth surfaces and steep grades. The uppers also seem to be very sturdily constructed. Lastly, this shoe is very lightweight and, at $48, a definite bargain. Now, I haven't tried these on a long hike yet, but for the weekend warrior who also likes climbing around, these are the perfect shoe. Don't waste your money on anything more than $100, unless you absolutely need a special arch support or sole. I really hope Hi-Tec keeps making these shoes or something like them.

product_title: Merrell Men's All Out Defy Walking Shoe
review_body:
These shoes are pretty great. I ordered them without trying them on first, and they fit exactly as well as my other Merrell shoes. However, these are not quite as soft and cushy as other Merrells like the Moab are. They are more rigid and thinner, kind of like a dress shoe would be, but they still hug your foot in exactly the same way and are just as comfortable.

I love the style. They are perfect as a work shoe because they are somewhere in between the style of a dress shoe and a sneaker, with the comfort and flexibility of the latter and the form factor of the former.

I ordered these in January, and my feet are pretty cold, which I don't personally mind but it tells me that these are probably better suited as a summer shoe.

The friction of the sole is just right. I never slip or lose my balance when the subway jolts to a stop, and I'm able to pivot on my heel whenever I need to.

I did put a gel insole inside as the inside of the shoe is pretty hard. Greatly improved the comfort.
