product_title: Timberland Men's Chocorua Trail Gore-Tex Mid Hiking Boot
review_headline: Taking a while to break in but it's the black color version of my favorite pair
review_body:
I have these boots in black and brown. After breaking in and loving the brown ones so much, I decided I wanted a black pair for my everyday work shoes.

The waterproof feature of these boots with a goretex liner has worked very well for me. Been through puddles, muck, snow, spills, etc. My feet have yet to be wet while wearing them. Tread is good but not amazing, however I haven't really seen signs of wear too much on this model after extended use.

I have a slight bone spur on my foot and this boot model had done great in not irritating that. After about a month of wearing these black version, they have not broken in to the level of the other pair yet and don't feel like they are going to. They overall just feel stiffer, even the laces are a different type of stiff laces. While most people will probably love them and feel they fit right on, I just can't go 5 stars because I feel the brown same design pair I have is just a little better. If they continue to break in more and eventually become as comfortable as my others, I'll adjust to 5 stars.

EDIT: After barely a year of regular use, when they finally felt broken in around 3 months of use, I've had multiple shoe lace hooks simply break open and off, and the bottom separate from the sole heavily. I contacted Timberland, and was told they have a 12 month warranty from date of purchase, they will not replace them now as it's been 14 months. I simply can't recommend these to anyone for purchase unless you are wearing casually or only a few times outdoors. They just don't hold up. A real shame Timberland didn't make it right.

Now, given that I am 6'1" tall, add to that I have wide feet (with nay an arch to speak of), add, again, that I am pushing the maximum weight which allows me to claim weighing in at anywhere in the 200 something range, there is only so much that shoe engineering of today can design for. They will tend to That being shared, This is actually the fourth pair of Pleeser heels that I have purchased in six years. If you are a big girl, like Vivienne, there is a part of the shoe (where the polyvinyl meets the insole along either in the inside or outside edge) that may weaken. Let me be clear, IF YOU ARE a big girl, like Vivienne.

The shoe is a good buy. The fit is agreeable and I can wear them for a couple of hours without discomfort.

The M1540's were to short and I returned them and bought black M1540 size 10.5 6E. Those shoes are nearly to short and narrower than the 1123's were. In addition I cannot walk as far without pain. In the M1540’s I get about 3 miles and I am done. I could do 10 to 12 miles in the 1123’s before the pain became unbearable. Dont be fooled, the M1540 IS NOT a replacement for the M1123 no matter what the New Balance advertising states. New Balance can no longer be trusted to produce a quality product that is true to size, and functions as well as previous modles. If anyone finds a good quality motion control 6E shoe please post about it.

5 stars to Amazon for the ease of return of the first pair of M1540's.

product_title: Ariat Men's Hybrid Rancher Western Cowboy Boot
review_body:
These were my first pair of Ariat boots, I had always been more of a wolverine boots kinda guy. Best choice I ever made was going to Ariats, wont ever get anything other than them from now on and trying to get as many people as I can to at least try them to feel the comfort. Straight out of the box they looked better than I had expected, and was the most comfortable pair of boots I had ever put on for the first time. Break in period for me was about 2-3 days. Definitely wouldn't recommend the true advantage timber ones or any similar if you plan on doing a lot of walking in them without tucking in your pants legs because with them not being leather on the leg tube part there is a seam on either side where the material was sewn together and will rub the sides of your legs bad. Other than that I did notice that they make there boots longer than most and I got the extra wide ones and they were still a bit narrow for me. But just walking in them in general they are the most comfortable boots I've had, very soft sole, and once the leather stretched and fit around
my foot I can where them for days at a time without being able to take them off because of my job and won't have the least bit of pain/discomfort from it. Although, with all that being said I still wouldn't have ordered anything else because of all the compliments I get on my boots. The next pair I get tho I will be going into an Ariat store and actually getting my feet measured for best possible fitment. You won't go wrong getting these so go ahead and hit the buy button as long as they have your size or manly be in their case a half size smaller.

review_body: Decent fit, but like other some other reviews the quality of construction is sub-par. I would happily pay a little more if C-H would exercise better quality control with the contractors who make the shoes for them. Stitching was uneven, and the material used for stitching began to fray after only a few wearings, and had to be repaired at a local shoe shop after less than 45 days use. Leather was somewhat rigid and did not have the rich luster of the "real" (read: USA made) Cole Haan's of years past. Rubber heel was a cheap material.

product_title: HS 3005 CC PHOEBE Made in Italy Tan Ostrich Embossed Bucket Shoulder Bag
review_headline: Not a $525 bag, but not bad either.
review_body:
There is no way that this is a $525 retail bag. Not a chance. It is real leather, and seems of a decent quality. The quill points are very well done. I like the tanning, and I like the bag overall. However, it is a $70 bag. This isn't a LV. The liner feels very plastic-like, the sippers are rather fragile (plastic internal zippers, plastic external zippers with a metalic grasp). the center pocket is large enough to hold my 8" Tab3 in its case. The internal slip pocket is large enough to hold my S5 cell phone (in a case). The external zippered pockets are large enough to hold my key fob and work badge. The sippered inside side pocket is large enough to hold a small wallet and a ton of credit cards.

My biggest issue with the bag is the criss crossed shoulder straps. I thought they would be pretty neat, except they make the bag a challenge to get into. As you spread them apart to get into the bag, they actually close it instead. They work great on the shoulder and are rather stiff (at least new). With use, the will probably soften up a bit. The bag has enough structure to stand upright on its own. As you see it in the picture is exactly how it stands on its own in person. Because of the double rings on the back, you can sling this over your back as a backpack which is pretty neat too.

As a fashion bag, this is a nice bag. As a daily bag for shopping and such, maybe not so much.

product_title: Mixx VELVET SLOUCHY SCRUNCHED KNEE HIGH HEEL BOOTS Shoes
review_body:
**SIZING** like others have said the boots are snug around the ankle, they are actually snug around the whole foot I would definitely say these boots are for someone with a narrow foot. They are snug around the foot and ankle BUT once past the ankle the boots will give way from the ankle up as the boots have a panel that will expand and with the elastic looping these boots will fit almost any leg**

Now with all that said.....

O.M.effin'G!!!!!! I LOVE these boots. I will say I have thin legs it's almost impossible to find any boot that hugs my legs the way they should but these boots do :) These boots give the PERFECT snug fit for my legs all the way up over the knee. They are SUPER FLATTERING. They are super easy to get on and off and are soooooo comfy, I walked in these boots for hours downtown no problem and no ache the next day. It's not a very high heel, for being over the knee it's just the right height without looking too trashy. You can dress the boots or dress down, they can be worn for casual night out, date night and yes I would say even to the office.

The suede is nice, it's good quality a dark black. The inside of the boot from the ankle up has a really nice padding, it's thick but not making your legs look thicker, the padding not only comfy but will keep you warm if you decide to wear with a skirt or dress. The padding almost keeps the boots from sticking to your legs, it's one of the nicer padding in a shoe I have worn. If you plan to wear with skinny jeans make sure they are a skinny jean that hugs your legs nice.

product_title: Men's Wolverine® Brenner Steel-Toe EH Slip-On Work Shoe
review_body:
I first ordered a pair of these from Shopping Blitz through Amazon. I ordered size 11 M, which is my usual size. The shoes arrived promptly and I immediately tried them on. Way too big. I contacted Shopping Blitz and arranged an exchange for a size 10.5 M. Return shipping was at my expense, about $5.00. The second pair arrived, again too big, but just by a little bit. Since the 10.5 M was just a tad too big, I ordered a size 10 M pair so I could compare both sizes at the same time and decide which I preferred The size 10 M pair arrived on October 29, 2014, and it fit perfectly. I contacted Shopping Blitz and arranged to return the size 10.5 M for a refund. I immediately shipped the 10.5 M pair back, once more at a $5.00 cost to me. Today is January 5, 2015 and I just received notice that my return had been processed and my refund was on its way. Also today I got an email from Shopping Blitz requesting I give them a five star review. See below.

The shoes are very good. Excellent quality upper and the steel toe is solid. Traction is above average, compared to other steel-toed slip-ons I've worn. The size 10 M is quite comfortable on my foot, even though I usually wear a size 11 M. The insole, as one other reviewer noted, is stitched into the shoe and is not removable. This is too bad because I like to remove the manufacturer's insole and put in an insert that has higher arch support. The shoes don't claim to be water-resistant so if I walk in puddles or wet grass I expect to get wet. Overall, for the price I paid ($68, not counting the $10 in return shipping costs I incurred),these Wolverines are a good value.

Shopping Blitz was very easy to deal with. I returned two pair of shoes without any hassles about my reasons or motives. Though I am disappointed it took more than two months to process my refund on the second pair I bought, and it cost me an extra $10 in return postage, I give Shopping Blitz four solid stars. Wolverine only gets three stars because of their gross mis-sizing and lack of a removable insole.

product_title: EMU Australia Women's Stinger Lo Mid-Calf Boot
review_body:
I bought these Emu's after a lot of research. Was very excited to receive them but very disappointed when I realized what I was sent looked like fake Emu's. They didn't match the photos online at all.
1) The heel product label should be brown leather with special stitching. This was not the case with mine. It looked like a rubber emblem.
2) The stitching was uneven at the top of the boot. This should never happen with any top-quality boot.
3) According to the emuaustralia.com website, the insole should be removeable for the Stinger low boot. It should also have a molded heel. Mine did not.
4) There was no Emu fold-over label at the very top of the boot, which is typical of this brand.
So, sadly, my boots appear to be fake & I've notified Emu Australia directly that these were sold to me by this particular company (Fusion Apparel).
Beware when purchasing.

I am truly thankful for these Soft Shell shoes, they have "Give" to them, therefore allowing room for my foot that will forever be bigger than my other.... The lace closure is fantastic! Easy on easy off... There is even a little pocket for the end of the laces, the Velcro strap is also a plus, for adjusting the "Support" in the ankle area.... Best pair of shoes ever, I definitely recommend these shoes for every kind of activity, hiking, errands, walking and depending on where you live ~ an all season shoe.... Know what you're purchasing, and if you're wanting something different than described, buy something else. For me, these are great.

product_title: Cole Haan Women's Air Juliana 45 Pump
review_headline: Really wanted to like these pumps
review_body:
The pros - the pumps are classic, a nice color, and it's a great height for work and play. The orange interior is also a fun pop of color to keep things from feeling to staid.

Unfortunately, Cole Haan heels just don't work for me. There's something about the arch structure (it's not the height of the heel, I have higher heels) that force my foot to slide forward in the shoe and as a result, my weight rests on the ball of my foot, the toe box ends up pinching rather severely and the pumps end up straight back to Amazon. I've kept other pairs in the past, hoping that maybe I only needed to break them in, but to no avail. If you're a fan of Calvin Klein, Adrienne Vittadini, Ivanka Trump, or even Bandolino high heels, you may also struggle with these. To me, the Cole Haan high heels fit much more like Anne Klein (but even worse I'm afraid.)

product_title: Saddleback Leather Hobo Crossbody Purse - Casual, Comfortable Handbag for Women - 100 Year Warranty
review_headline: A gift so good it'll put others to shame.
review_body:
I purchased this bag for my mom for Christmas after my dad had told me she was hoping to get both a black (formal) and brown (daily) purse now that her old one had taken quite the beating. I have shopped the Saddleback store for two years after my friend got a bag from them, but have never been lucky enough to have one show up under the tree for my own use. I figured the ideal way to increase my odds for next year was to treat others as I want to be treated, and I can't overstate how great the results were when my mom opened her gift.

The black purse my dad had bought was the exact one my mom had pointed out in the store, a design she claimed to love, but when she opened the Saddleback purse she lost her mind. I have never given a gift that was so well received. The fit and finish, and most of all the smell, was unlike anything she'd ever had before. I honestly felt pretty badly for my dad when my mom wouldn't stop gushing about this bag and his lay forgotten on the floor.

Great product. Amazing quality. Olfactory delight. Worth the expense for the reaction alone, plus I expect to see her use it for decades to come!

I have duck feet. If you do not know what duck feet are then good for you. Basically my feet are quite wide... wide enough to use as flippers. I usually wear a 10 EE shoe from Johnson and Murphy and EEE in some other brands. Overall, this shoe (size 44) fits very well for my width of feet but is just a touch too long in comparison to other ECCO size 44 shoes I have purchased in the past. It still fits though.

In making this purchase, I was looking for an affordable professional Wing Tip shoe that would hold up to a lot of daily walking. I am tired of resoling my other expensive dress shoes every 6-8 months. Based on my experience with other more casual ECCO dress shoes that are of similar quality I expect these shoes and soles to last many years!

product_title: Merrell Men's Moab Peak Mid Ventilator Hiking Boot,Black Slate,13 M US
review_body: Merrell makes great shoes and boots. I have had their shoe version of these boots for over a year and they are plenty worn in. So this winter I decided that I would give the boots a try. As a Veteran I have had my fair share of boots and know what I like and dislike about them. I have had them for a few months now and I have been wearing them every day as my primary shoe. These boots are comfortable after about 2 weeks of constant wear. The break in on these seemed to me to be a bit short for what I am used to but I associate that with the Vibram soles. The grip of the tread is fantastic! In my automotive shop I have yet to find a place that they don’t grip even on the slick floors, this winter I have been walking on Ice and slick driveways and roads with very little slipping. The breathability of this boot is not top notch but it does work well. The toe cover surprised me. My shoe version of these had separation issues between the toe cover on the boot and the sole. But the stitching seems thicker on these which is a nice surprise. The eyelets are strong and solid and the top hooks are rigid and well placed. The weakest part of these is the laces, which should not really matter. I have replaced the laces on my other shoes 2 times and I am starting to see wear on the new ones already.  These boots are great overall.

product_title: ACORN Women's Polar Moc Slipper
review_body:
I have long been on the hunt for a nice pair of slippers and believe I have finally found the right pair. I've been through a few different styles over the years but lately could not find a pair that looked decent and met the following qualifications:
1) must not be backless / no clogs or flip flop style
2) must have a waterproof / resistant sole - suitable for say, walking outside to get the mail or walk my kid to the bus stop early in the morning
3) must not look like my Grandmother would pick the same ones
4) must be warm

When these Acorn slippers first arrived, I was very pleased with the pattern and look. They look just like they do online. The blue dots are kind of periwinkle, but the orange and red are nice and bright. I wear a size 7.5M and purchased the size 6 1/2- 7 1/2. When I first put them on, the padding in the sole was very thick and they seemed tight in the toe. I was afraid I'd made a bad choice. My husband said they would compress with wear and I should try them out so I kept wearing them. He was right. They are loose enough now to feel comfortable and to slip on and off with ease, however they do not fall off. I've been wearing them a couple weeks now.

They are toasty warm fleece that is soft on bare feet but are roomy enough to wear with socks. I have good traction, am not worried about slipping in the house or outside.
I've worn them first thing in the morning to walk my son to the bus stop and the rainy or dewy grass has not soaked my feet like my last pair of spandex ballet style Isotoners.
They may be a little frumpy compared to a dainty ballet style, and they are not very feminine in shape, but the pattern is so cute and bright it makes up for the shape.
I had seen Acorn brand slippers before but many of the patterns were not my style preference plus they were more than I cared to spend. I did order these on a Lightning Deal but so far am so happy I would probably pay full price next time - especially if these are as well made as they appear and last a long time. I learned this with my favorite flip flops, the Teva Olowahu. Splurged and bought those on a whim but found the quality to be worth paying more for a pair of flip flops that would last. So far I would definitely recommend the Acorn slippers if you live in a climate where it gets chilly in the winter. review_headline: Comfortable Alternative to Sneakers for Hiking
review_body: I purchased the Teva Women's Sky Lake Waterproof Hiking Shoe in grey/green and wore them on a hike a few days after receiving them. As mentioned in previous reviews, these shoes were comfortable and did not require breaking in. They are true to size and feel secure, though for those with wider feet, these could use a bit more room in the width to increase the comfort. My one issue is that they rub against my ankles, though taller socks would easily resolve this concern.    These shoes grip well on large socks on an incline and provide stability, though I have slipped on wet rocks and loose gravel when going downhill. Overall, a great shoe for low to medium impact hikers who are looking for a better alternative to sneakers.

review_body:
These shoes are adorable and provide good support for my active toddler. I tend to dress my daughter in dressier outfits and this is the first pair of sneakers I've purchased for her in over a year. She wore Saltwater Sweetheart sandals all spring and summer and has always worn Mary Janes or boots during cooler weather (Livie and Luca, Pediped, Keds, See Kai Run). She has never seemed to mind wearing her other shoes at the park or to play, but I decided she really needed a pair of shoes that could get dirty,
wet, or scuffed without me caring. I got an excellent deal on these sparkly See Kai Run Sneakers and am so glad I bought them! They are adorable, match almost everything, and are easy to put on and take off. My daughter loves the way they look and feel and we get compliments on them whenever she wears them. One thing I want to point out, which is a great IMO, is that the laces are really just elastic laces that do not tie or fasten in anyway.

product_title: Merrell Men's Trail Glove 2 Trail Running Shoe
review_headline: Terrible longevity, but a great shoe otherwise
review_body:
I have worn Merrell Barefoot running shoes since July 2011. My first 4 pairs were the original Trail Gloves. The first pair lasted through 600 miles of running before they developed holes and tearing along the side of the shoe where the mesh material meets the sole. I contacted Merrell and they replaced them for free. That pair lasted 500 or so miles before the same thing happened. I didn't bother Merrell that time though since I figured they were free. I had two other pair that I bought and the same thing happened, so I figured it must have been a flaw in the design, so when the Trail Glove 2 came out I was happy to try it.

I bought the orange pair and they looked and felt great. Unfortunately they only lasted 105 miles before they developed an angular tear on each shoe in the same area as the original TGs. I again contacted Merrell and they have since sent me a replacement pair at no charge. The TG 2 is definitely not as good as the original TG. I know 600 miles and a year of running is a lot from a shoe, but 105 miles is nothing and quite unsatisfactory. I expect at least 300-400 miles and for the first real signs of wear to appear on the sole of the shoe, not the upper.

Don't get me wrong, I like these shoes. They fit well and I love running in them. They are light weight and good for short and long runs. I've done half marathons in them and a couple 15 mile runs, so they're great for running, they just have a design flaw. The plus side is that Merrell have a great warranty and their customer service personnel are top notch, so you can easily contact them for a replacement should yours die an early death.

product_title: Le Chameau Footwear Men's Chasseur Cuir Rain Boot
review_body:
Outstanding Wellingtons. The black ones look a lot like riding boots. I love the full leather lining on the legs. I love the full-length zippers (which have properly made rubber gussets behind them so water can't get in, even if you are standing in it. The boots are heavy. My calves aren't large, and I wish we could buy in the U.S. the small-calf versions available in France. Even with my pants folded inside the boots, they aren't tight, though they are considerable trimmer than most Wellingtons, thanks to the zipper. The tread is serious and should last for years. Take the size recommendations seriously. I usually wear 10 1/2 or 11 shoes, so I ordered size 10. The only way I can wear these is with a pair of heavy winter socks over the pair of dress socks I usually wear. Of course, that's okay, as I only wear the boots in the fall and winter, and they aren't insulated. Still, I almost could have gotten by with a size 9, even with two pairs of socks.

Break in? No need. Straight out of the box (with two pairs of socks) I walked around ten miles in 3 1/2 hours while following a fox hunt through fields and woods and rocks and creeks, in hilly terrain. No blisters. I think that's the farthest I've ever walked in a day in my life.

Expensive boots. Maybe a silly purchase. But the quality is exceptional. And now I don't have to deal with wet feet and pants while fox-hunting (my girlfriend rides, but I stumble along behind her as best I can).

product_title: Powerstep Pinnacle Maxx Full Length Orthotic Shoe Insoles
review_body:
These were bought for my husband to wear in his steel-toe work boots. His job requires standing/walking on concrete floors for a straight 12 hr shift. After doing this for many years, his feet suffer. We didn't have the extra cash to drop $400 on custom orthotics, so we thought we'd give some higher quality inserts a try. We tried a variety of brands at a variety of price points, Dr. Scholls, Superfeet, store brands, etc., before giving these a try. These have been the best inserts he's been able to find, thankfully, not the most expensive. He is able to work the entire night without limping home from pain. In fact, he likes them so much, we ordered a back up pair just in case. I should also mention my husband wears a size 14 and unlike most orthotics in this size, the Pinnacle Maxx's are generous when it comes to width, so they fit his feet really well.

As a side note, we initially purchased a pair of these 3 months ago and the plastic wore through the top padding, digging into my husband's foot. I contacted Powerstep via their website and they sent me a replacement set. All they asked for was proof of purchase and a picture of the defective insert. The replacement was received 2 days after sending the email with the requested information. I think this is a true testament to a company's willingness to stand behind their product....something rare these days.

product_title: Thorogood Men's American Heritage Plain-Toe Work Boot
review_body:
So, this is actually my FIRST Amazon product review. I buy quite a bit of stuff on Amazon and like everyone else, I find reading the reviews extremely helpful when buying online. So then why haven't I taken the plunge with a review until now? Well, to be honest, I find that most of the reviews already cover most of the important issues with the items I've purchased, so I don't feel like I'm really adding anything. But...not so with these boots, so here goes.

My guess is that most of us who end up looking at this boot have looked at many of the other "Heritage" boots out there - and let's face it, there are a bunch - and asked "do I really need to spend 2-3 hundred bucks to get a decent, good looking pair of boots?" I mean, c'mon, these babies look pretty sweet and are less than $150 bucks. If you get them on sale like I did they are just over $100, which is a pretty attractive price.

So, what do you get? As others have noted, these are not heavy duty boots. This is mostly apparent in the quality and thickness of the leather. What's clear is that part of the reason these boots are not as expensive as most of the others out there is that they've saved some money on the quality of the materials. I wear these boots to kick around in and at work when I might get dirty on a job (I'm a photographer) and for that they are fine, and after a month or so they seem to be holding up very well. However, if you were going to wear these for a trade job, they might not hold up quite as well as their more expensive brethren. It all comes down to how hard you are on your boots.

Again, that mostly echoes what has already been said; but there are a couple of other things. The first, which I would have to put in the negative column, is that the upturned leather edge above the wedge sole is....fake. Yup, it's not a true stitched down leather upper. I was surprised that with all the reviews already written this had not been mentioned, because it's certainly hard to tell when looking at the photo. But if you look carefully you will see that what looks like tan leather above the black wedge sole is actually plastic, made to look like leather. Was this a deal breaker for me? No, but I was definitely a little disappointed. So now we have another reason why those other boots are more expensive, they actually use tradition construction techniques to make them. If that's important to you you may want to look elsewhere.

Another reason I was attracted to these boots is that they actually have removable insoles. If you pay attention to the details of many of those fancier boots, you will notice that because they are traditionally made they seem to all have a traditional leather foot bed as well. Meaning, you can't really put insoles in them. I use insoles in almost all my shoes so having the ability to put in real insoles is a big bonus, and as far as that goes these do not disappoint. In fact the insoles that come with them are nice and thick and cushy, so nice in fact that I haven't even switched them out yet. (I did pop in a pair of my usual Superfeet insoles just to test them and they work perfectly.) And as far as size goes, for me a half size down was spot on. I usually wear a 10 and got a 9.5 D and they were perfect width and length.

And finally, a brief encounter with customer service. Strangely, when I received the boots, they came with one lace that was shorter than the other, so one of the boots barely had enough lace to tie it at the top, which was a bit annoying for a brand new pair of boots. After a little hunting I was able to track down the customer service email and my email received a prompt reply and an apology, with a message that new laces would be sent out right away. Any they were! Very nice.

In the end, I would definitely recommend these boots. They are handsome (very nice color and I also like the look of the wedge sole instead of a big clunky heel) andcomfortable. I have received several compliments on them, for sure. Just know what you’re getting. While I think they are definitely worth the price, they are not worth more. If you get them on sale they are a good deal. But as a “Heritage” boot goes, they are a bit of a compromise. If you’re OK with that like I am, I think you will definitely be happy.

PS – If you want to know what shoe polish will match this color, I got some Kiwi Oxblood color and it matches perfectly.

review_headline: My new favorite pair of boots.
review_body: I love these boots! I like boots with suede and faux fur, but I have a hard time finding nice ones like these since they don't seem to be as in fashion as other styles. I generally don't like buying shoes online since it feels like a bit of a gamble, but I am so completely happy I decided to buy these. They fit perfectly, are very comfortable, and are very solidly constructed. I love the thick leather laces and not having a zipper ruining the look. After wearing them a couple times I've even gotten them to the point I can slip them on without completely unlacing them (which is nice, because completely unlacing and relacing them is a little time consuming). The one small thing about them I don't like is the tops seem to fall open a bit rather than staying close to my legs, so to fix this I skip the last loop for the laces and tie them higher, which seems to work well. I plan on buying a similar pair of boots from this brand as well that are half the height and come in dark brown. Then I will probably wear both pairs to death before looking for boots again. I really couldn't be happier with them.

product_title: Vibram Fivefingers Seeya Barefoot Running Shoe - Men's
review_body:
These are minimalist shoes -- no support at all. That said, reading the positive reviews made me want to try them for running. I'm a casual runner -- a few times a week for a few miles at a time. I wore the shoes in gradually per the instructions, walking around for 15 or 20 minutes the first couple days, increasing the time with the shoes on slowly, then to a short jog, then a regular run.

After about a week of trying to get accustomed to these shoes, I started getting sharp, stabbing foot pain in one of my feet. It could have just been a coincidence, but the timing was just too spot on. I went to see a podiatrist, who told me he thought I had gotten a stress fracture in my foot from the shoes. He said, "those kind of shoes are terrible for your feet. I don't know why people wear them."

So be warned! I'm now unable to do any running for the forseeable future, in addition to dealing with a lot of foot pain. Wish I could get my money and non-broken foot back...

product_title: Lowa Men's Renegade II Leather-Lined Mid Hiking Boot
review_headline: Long-time Lowa wearer; first time with leather-lining
review_body: I will note up-front that this is my fourth pair of Lowa Renegades since I bought my first pair in 1999. The other three pair have all been the low-rise model. Nonetheless, Lowa is my \\"go to\\" brand for this kind of shoe. Since a foot injury three years ago, one of my feet has intermittent plantar fasciitis that really benefits from a shoe that is rigid from ball to heel. My Lowas have been comfortable to wear even when everything else wasn't. I wear my Renegades 50-60% of the time I have shoes on my feet, for actual hiking and casual walking.    Every Lowa Renegade I've owned has required minimal break-in. That's a good thing. I hate miles of discomfort or outright pain to break-in shoes. If I'm going hiking, I don't want *anything* rubbing or pinching uncomfortably, much less for it to do so for the entire hike.    I chose to go with a boot this time because I like the additional ankle support and better resistance to snow getting in the shoe (an issue here in the Northeast U.S.). I can also wear them when riding a motorcycle. The toe is neither too thick nor too stiff for the shifter, and the ankle protection is adequate. (Yes, a true motorcycle boot is the *best* option, but it's rather specialized.)    I chose the leather lining in hopes of avoiding the musty, occasionally foul smell from the Gore-tex fabric lining that plagued my previous Lowas. I've been wearing these almost exclusively since they arrived three weeks ago. The only odor coming from the shoe is that of leather, which I like. I also notice that my feet perspire much less in these than they did in the previous Renegades I've owned, even though this pair has a boot cuff the low-rise models lacked. I usually wear wool socks in colder months, and the thinner shoe -- without the thick Gore-tex lining -- doesn't seem to result in cold feet. I like that, too.    The leather-lined shoe feels a bit wider than the Gore-tex one. I have usually found that a 2E or 3E works best for my feet, but without the bulk of the Gore-tex lining, the regular D width has fit my foot pretty well, after just a bit of walking to stretch the leather. This opens up the possibility of wearing the black shoe (my preference; see below), since the wider widths aren't available in black with the leather lining.    I also mention that a major reason I've liked the Renegade models is that they don't scream \\"hiking shoe.\\" There are no bright colors anywhere on the shoe. I'm a clergyman, and so I appreciate that, should I have these on with my black attire, they do not draw attention to themselves. Go ahead and wear them with jeans or even casual pants to the office. Lead a church service in them. They'll look rugged, but not completely out of place.    The only cons I have for my Renegades are:  1. Lowa's sole wears faster than other brands. Other reviewers have noted this, as do I. I can live with it, considering the amazing comfort of the shoe around town and on the trail. (I prefer the softer sole to sore feet.) I might try one of the resoling services when this pair's sole gets too thin.    2. Lowa's insole could offer a bit more padding. This is perhaps a matter of personal preference, and it's easily remedied with a number of aftermarket insoles (I settled on the Spenco green). The shoe is not as cushioned as Vasque's new Eriksson model, although the Lowa feels far less clunky on the foot.    All in all, I regret that I tried any other brands. Lowa works for my feet and intended uses. I'm a happy repeat customer.

product_title: DC Allie Rain Boot (Little Kid/Big Kid)
review_headline: Great winter boots, but they need to be broken in.
review_body: I bought these during the polar vortex last winter. I live in NY where it snowed about once or twice a week during that time. These boots keep my feet very warm in temperatures well below freezing, and even in calf-high snow and slush my feet and legs stayed blessedly dry. They also clean up really easily; with a few swipes of a paper towel, they were free of grime and salt. The sizing is a bit small. I usually wear a women's 6.5, so I got the equivalent 4.5 in these boots. They were murder last winter... If I wore them longer than an hour or two, my heels started to hurt really badly. Despite that, I kept them because the quality was so great (and I didn't want to buy another pair of boots).  I wore them twice last month and they're very comfortable now, even with thicker socks; I guess they just needed to be broken in. If you don't want to wait for them to break in (and I don't recommend that you do), order a half size up if you like them snug, maybe a full size up if you like breathing room.

review_headline: I have had them for almost a week
review_body:
I have received a lot of compliments on the aesthetics of the shoes, but the reason I bought these was because I had a pair of the original DVS Militia Snow Series from 2004. I ended up buying these because last month I finally wore a hole through the sole of the originals, but it was pretty impressive they lasted a decade of regular use (they even grew half a size with my foot due to materials stretching out over time). My brother and I have each owned a pair of regular DVS shoes and were appalled at the terrible construction quality, fit, and finish. My brother's pair of regular DVSs didn't even last a month before they began falling apart, while I had mine last three months before the sole separated from the shoe.

The snow series must have been made in a different factory by a different corporation with stricter quality standards and higher quality materials. If I even get 5 years of use out of these new Militia snow boot/shoe things, I'll be impressed. I don't think any shoe I own again will last as long as those original Militia Snow Series my parents bought for me 10 years ago.

product_title: Tuff Toe Polyurethane Toe Protector
review_body: Bought it from the site because of a user noting it seemed 'old'. Waited a while for it to arrive, when I finally got it I was excited I thought I found a good product. Naturally my boots were already worn and I was simply buying this to repair them. 23$ is a lot to ask for a simple boot repair when a fat bottle of Shoe Goo is sitting right next to it in the recommendations spot for 8$.    But because of the stellar reviews and their big claim they use it in all the major league baseball sports teams, I thought it'd be a good bet. I made sure to watch the video several times, all through it, repeating sections, listening to his every word like he was a pastor. Followed the instructions and tore my boots up to make sure this stuff would stick to a clean solid surface (I had placed beeswax on my boots before to protect them from the elements)    1 week, the sides are starting to come off.    Next time, I'll just buy the big bottle of Shoe Goo so when the time comes I have to repair it, I won't have to be 'dainty' with my drops because of the limited amount in the darn thing, should a piece start to come off.    I'm a commercial sheet metal roofer, my job requires a lot from my feet. Needless to say, I was sorely disappointed at the sides already coming off after a week. In spite of sanding away the toe, ensuring plenty of cover space, tearing off excess leather and cleaning the sole of the boot for proper 'sealing.'    I'll just consider it a 23$ lesson learned. Might be tough enough for a guy throwing a ball all day, but it's s*** for a guy who has to actually work to earn his living.

product_title: KEEN Women's Newport H2 Sandal
review_headline: Excellent all around summer shoes, I only want these
review_body: This was the only pair of shoes that I ever bought that had no break in period.  Normally I will wear a size 9 in most shoes.  I tried these on at a brick and mortar retailer before purchasing here to get the right size and I was a 9.5.  These shoes are very well made, I had a knock off type pair that lasted about 4 days, I am not even kidding.  I wore these shoes all spring and all summer.  I wore them in the river and running over rocks, I wore them in my computer lab where I work, but with socks.  Hey!  In Oregon you are allowed to wear socks with sandals.  It confused me at first too but now I just go with it.  But because of the toe on these shoes I am able to wear them in the lab.  I wore these suckers all over the land, walking the dogs for miles, and I bought a pair for Husband as well.  He wore his down so bad I had to get him another pair.  But it took him a while to wear the sole down that badly and he does this to all shoes in time. I think these shoes are super sturdy and that is good for me as I wear shoes out fast.  I loved them so much I did not want to give them up when it started raining... but eventually I had to.  I know these will last me at least one more summer.  They wash up good and they don't fade too much if you don't leave them out in the sun too long.  I just hosed mine off after a river trip, dried in the sun and they were good to go on Monday for work.  No river smell!  No sweaty feet for the summer.  I will buy another pair of these after I wear through the ones I have.

product_title: Columbia Women's Minx Shorty Omni-Heat Snow Boot
review_headline: Felt like my instep was in a vice
review_body:
I normally wear an 8W or 8.5M in most shoes. I ordered these boots in a 9M, due to previous experience with the Columbia Minx line: I have a 2 year old pair of the taller Minx lace-up boots in a size 8.5M. When I saw that these Shorty boots have a suede vamp, I decided to go up to a 9M, assuming the instep might be a bit snug thanks to the suede construction.

Turns out "a bit snug" was an understatement. Wearing thin wool socks, I can get my right foot into the right boot with no trouble -- but there's a lot of pressure across the top (instep) of that foot. My left foot's wider and fuller than my right. The left boot's instep is so tight, I feel like I'll lose circulation in my left foot if I wear the boot longer than 10 minutes. That's how long I was able to withstand the pain before needing to yank the boot off. It was awful.

I'm really bummed about this. I love my older taller Minx boots, and since these Shorty boots use the same Omni-Heat material, I know they'd keep my feet toasty warm during Chicago winters. If your feet aren't wide, you may want to give these a go. You can get away with thin wool socks under these boots, instead of super thick socks, and your toes won't freeze.

Also, these Minx Shorty boots feel more like a hiking boot than a winter boot. That's another plus for me, because heavy clunky winter boots make me feel tired and unsure of my footing. My taller Minx boots don't have a suede vamp and feel very lightweight, like sneakers. I wish these Shorty boots felt more like that. They're not clunky at all, but they are a bit heavier than my older Minx boots. Both the Shorty and my older boots also have the same tread, which grips pretty well.

Another positive comment about the Shorty boots: the tongue is attached up to, oh, just above the middle lacing loop. This should help keep your feet dry, unless you walk through deep snow. Since I haven't worn these outside, I don't know how waterproof they really are. But if they're like my older boots, you can wear 'em in the rain and your socks won't get soaked.

If Columbia offered these boots in a wide width, I might give them another try. For now, I'm stuck with these: right after I ordered them, I wound up taking several unexpected business trips and missing the deadline to return the boots. Sigh... review_headline: Very uncomfortable due to lack of lining
review_body: My 9 year old receives a new pair of boots every year. For many years in a row he owned a pair of Johnny Poppers. (The little kid version of this John Deere boot.) The last couple of years he has worn Justin boots. He saw these & asked for them, so we ordered them without trying them on. The fit is spot-on. However, he is complaining they're the most uncomfortable boots ever. I chalked it up to him being dramatic. We wear the same size so I wore them to prove he was over-reacting. WRONG! There is no lining to cover the rough interior seams. I've never had boots feel like this so I checked the interior of his old boots & several pairs of my boots. (Ariat & Justin) All of our boots had some sort of coverage over the rough seams. For the short time I wore his boots they left raw spots on top of my foot and ankle..even with heavy socks. Unfortunately we've worn them outside a few times so they can't be returned. Never again will I buy JD boots. I'm going to take them to an old-school shoe repair shop and see if they can affix some sort of lining over the seams just so they'll be wearable. For almost $100 I expected much better quality.

product_title: Skechers USA Men's Supreme Open Toe Slide Gladiator Sandal
review_body:
These look just like another pair of slider sandals I bought years ago from a different brand that no longer seems to exist, but they're just awful. The stiff central panel of the upper extends just beyond the front lateral strap and juts directly into your toes. It's a bizarre design decision that I can see no justification for, as these would be good otherwise. I don't like the memory foam footbeds all the Skecher slider sandals have, but I at least understand the thinking behind them. This is just baffling, and I can't imagine anyone finding it comfortable. I actually ordered a full size up and still feel this thing digging into my toes whenever I wear these.

If anyone has any suggestions for similar-looking slider sandals (i.e. without the toe thong) that aren't super tight, please leave a comment. (And no, ordering several sizes up doesn't work, as then the soles are clown-size.) All the slider sandals I can find now are designed to fit very snugly so you can walk around a lot without having them fall off, but I want slider sandals specifically as house shoes that I can slip on and off without any effort at all, as I'm often holding a baby or a pet or groping around in the dark for them. I have a pair of Adidas slippers with an adjustable strap that work alright, but I like the look of these a lot more.

product_title: Rockport Men's Cape Noble Driving Shoe
review_body:
I can't believe how well these have held up.

These shoes have become my go-to standard shoe for all occasions. They are extremely comfortable and feel like they are barely there. I've worn them while traveling, taken short hikes, gone to casual events, danced, and even ran a mile or two in them. They've been soaked through with both rain and saltwater as well as frozen, all of which are terrible for leather, but are still going strong.

That being said, these are definitely not for everyone. I don't like or need support and I would love to spend everyday barefoot. These shoes are very flexible and barely have a sole. I wouldn't say I feel every rock I step on, but I definitely am careful on rougher surfaces.

Overall though, they are unmatched in terms of reliability, comfort, and value. As long as you don't need support, I can't recommend these enough. Best shoes I've ever owned!

review_headline: First pair of Frye boots & I'm in LOVE
review_body: This is my first pair of Frye boots. I bought the black in size 5.5. I usually wear a 5 - 5.5 in most shoes. The fit is perfect. There is a little slip in the heel, which you want. The zipper is a little uncooperative on the left boot but I hope with enough use it will be ok. The right boot was a little tight across my big toe. Here's a tip. Put a little alcohol on a cotton ball and hold on the inside of the boot where you need the stretch. Hold for a few seconds and put the boot back on your foot. Problem solved. Alcohol stretches leather. Now I'm looking for a brown pair.    Update 2/13/15: I still can't wear these boots all day. They still need to be stretched on the right foot across the middle of my big toe. The alcohol/water solution was tried many more times. I have a small, slim foot (I thought) and I feel the 6 would have been too long. I also own the Phillip work boot in  5.5 and have the exact same problem with the right boot. product_title: Saucony Men's Hurricane 16 Running Shoe
review_headline: Great running shoe for wide feet
review_body:
I have been using Saucony running shoes for many years. (Approximately 30 years now)?

I was looking for something with a nice-sized toe box, and also for a wide foot.

My foot is not overly wide, but just wide enough to not feel comfortable in "normal width" shoes. I also have a neutral foot - so I am not over/under pronated, nor do I need massive arch support.

When I first put them on, I tightened the laces like I usually do. This was not good. During my run I found that they started getting tighter and tighter, and I had to eventually stop to loosen them.

I also notice noticed that the heel box was nice. Extremely nice. It cupped my heel better than any of the other Saucony models I had owned before. To the point that loosening the laces (like I mentioned above) did not cause my heel to slip around and get blisters. Just a great heel cup.

Another plus was the roomy toe box. I love my feet to "splay out" when I run. I do not like the narrow toe boxes that squish your toes together, and do not let your toes breathe. These let my feet splay out when I am running, and are also very breathable.

One of the things that I did not like was the tongue. I remember reading somewhere that a reviewer had praised the tongue for not "shifting around". But this was not my case.

Maybe it is the shape of my foot. Maybe it was the specific shoe I purchased. Maybe it was the "looser" way I tie the laces. I don't know. But the tongue of the shoe almost always gravitates to the side when I am running. (Not 100% of the time. Maybe 60% of the time).

The 8m offset is also pretty sweet for road running. (Street running). It is cushiony, and helps absorb the impact on the muscles, joints, and bones. (I use compression shorts when I run).

Overall, I like the shoes. They are airy, they give good cushioning, they are supportive, and the heel box is sweet for holding my foot.

Saucony all the way!my foot.

Saucony all the way!

product_title: Danner Men's Mountain Trail Boot
review_headline: I was ready to suffer for a couple months...
review_body: Listen, I read all of the reviews on these and was not looking forward to a few months of pain.  But they're cool looking, they have replaceable soles, and they're from Portland (where I grew up).  So I bought them and have been wearing them for about 2 weeks, initially with two pairs of socks (one thick SmartWool and one thin running sock).  I kept waiting for them to hurt, but they never did.  I'm mostly wearing them with just the SmartWools now, and I stuck in a pair of SuperFeet (blue) for even more comfort.  Gotta say, they're great boots!  Pro:  Waterproof (though I applied Obenauf's right away, which does make them a little darker), cool lookin', soft sole, heavy tongue lets you lace 'em up without cutting off circulation, and very well made.   Con:  Three things.  First, the very top of the boot tends to press on my achilles tendon when I'm sitting around writing for hours.  I expect that'll go away on its own, but I'm sure I could also stretch them out by hand.  Second, the soles are so soft that I don't imagine they'll last the TOO many years everybody talks about.  Third, the ankles are a bit loose; I pull the laces tight and there's not much play left, so if they stretch from the tight laces then I'll run out of room to tighten them.   Overall:  Buy them.

review_headline: Update of a very good trail running shoe
review_body: This is an update of the Trabuco line and it shows improvement in that it appears a little bit lighter and the top fits marginally better.  I began buying Tiger (now known as ASICS) cross country racing shoes around 1967 and I have been always been impressed with the product.  In the 1960's the Tiger training shoes were selling for half the price of comparable Adidas and were 75% as good as Adidas.  Today ASICS and Adidas sell for roughly comparable prices and are of equal quality, in my opinion.  The main difference today is that Adidas running shoes are still basically designed for track runners while ASICS sells very good track oriented shoes but it also sells a broad range of trail running shoes.  As an old guy my track racing days have been over for a long time so now I really enjoy getting out to scenic trails for my workouts.  This shoe fits my needs because it has a built in stone guard and other features that make it a great off-road shoe.

review_headline: I have plantars fasciitis from flat feet and a connective tissue disorder. These shoes have the exact support that I needed.
review_body:
I will make this short and sweet. Just bought these shoes after blowing out of my Nike Air Max's early this last summer. I have been looking for the perfect fitted tennis shoe since. I lived in my tennis shoes because of my PF before they blew out, but I had to wear an arch support even with those. With these shoes, I don't need my arch supports. YAY! and with the added arch support off the side of the shoe... everything else that I have found has (what I call) a three inch white foam sole on the inside and looked like an OLD WOMAN'S shoes.These have the same thing but it is in the teal color and it makes the shoe still look like its in style. lol (I'm not ready to make that transition because I am not OLD yet. Getting there though) :-) For all of you that are dealing with PF or flat feet, I would suggest the Saucony Triumph 11's.

I will say, that in regular shoes I usually wear an 8. But in Nike's I wear and 8.5. In these,I actually feel better in the 8's even though my toes are close to the end (but not touching) because the toe of the shoe curves up a little. So if your in between sizes... I would go with the smaller size if you have normal to narrow(er) feet. If you have a wider foot, than I would go with the size up if your an in betweener like me. :-P Hope this helps. These shoes have the added support with the extra cushion that I was soooo longing for. It's like walking on marshmallows (for me).

product_title: Clarks Women's Truffle Sandal
review_headline: Love this shoe, support and comfort, can wear it to walk miles!
review_body:
Love, love, love this sandal. So comfortable. Mind you: I can not walk in any shoe for any distance unless it's a supportive athletic shoe, so I wasn't expecting much from this sandal-- it so over delivered. I have literally walked miles in this shoe in all types of terrain and it fares just as well as my best running shoes.
I can not wear flip flops-- not only are they not supportive enough, but the thong between my toes is too painful.
My feet are very picky. I need great food bed support and structure-- this shoe delivered!
In this type of slide sandal, ANY type of top-of-the-foot detail, like buckles or accents, or sometimes even stitching, can be too painful for my sensitive tender feet, so with all the criss-crossing and detail in the photos, I was worried this sandal would give me grief. It was sheer comfort!
I literally wore this sandal EVERY SINGLE DAY all day long in the summer of 2014. They still have many more summers of wear left in them, but I'm definitely ordering another pair as a backup before they stop making them.
My only complaint is the styling definitely leans toward earth-mother hippy sandal-- I would love a similar supportive comfortable option in a more chic design, but, otherwise.... love this sandal.

product_title: Twisted Woman's ADORA Hi-Top Athletic Sneaker
review_headline: don't buy if you want to wear them more than once
review_body:
I didn't expect quality materials and workmanship for the price I paid for these shoes but I did expect them to be functional. Payless quality for a Payless price,  which usually lasts 3-6 months in my experience.  When I opened the box I was very disappointed in quality of material. The faux leather is the worst kind of faux leather possible, the type which cracks immediately. I was not expecting to see that on a pair of athletic shoes even if they're fashion sneakers. So I didn't have much hope that these shoes would last more than a couple wearings (if they had this would've been a two star review). 

However, I did expect them to last through the lace up! When I went to lace up the left sneaker and tie it, one lace ripped right through an eyelet! I had to jury rig it through another eyelet super gently to get it to tie so I could even try it out for one days wearing. Which was not the best day in a pair of shoes; the soles are comfortable and supportive but the toe box was unexpectedly narrow. Strange considering the shoe itself was unexpectedly long for an 11 (without heavy sports socks I was sliding back and forward in the shoe but it's a sneaker so there's a lot of forgiveness in wearing it oversized).I normally have no problem with narrowness but in these shoes both my pinky toes were rubbed sore to almost raw through regular thickness socks by the end of the day. Basically it was a complete waste of my money. 

I would definitely counsel against buying these shoes. Shoot, I would counsel against stocking these shoes or even manufacturing these shoes.  Since they are so bad for anyone who plans on actually wearing these shoes. Even if you just enjoy looking at shoes the pictures here in Amazon are pretty accurate, just look at those.

review_headline: Looks good, but hurts like crazy
review_body: I ordered the Moon Rock color and they looked great! However, like another reviewer mentioned, the gusseted portion of the tongue hurts like crazy! I love a gusseted tongue, but I've never felt one like this before and I've owned plenty of boots in my day. The portion that folds in like a 'V' toward your ankle is VERY hard and thick. To set the record straight, I don't have kankles and I don't have sticks for ankles; I consider myself to have average size ankles with average meat around them. If I wanted to wear these boots without tying the laces, it could have felt OK since the gusset would never press into my ankle, but for the way I intended to wear these, I needed the laces tied. I walked in my house barely 2 paces and immediately felt the pain. I thought I could make them work and tried them again later on; I even tried to adjust the tongue just right so that the 'V' would point outwards - that's how much I wanted them to work - forget it. For this much $ I'm not going to settle. Besides, the footbed was very lacking in support and I never complain about that feature in a shoe or boot - since I'm a true size 8, I could have put an insert inside these boots to deal with that issue, but without an insert, I felt like I was walking on the ground in my bare feet. Very bummed that I couldn't make them work, but something is wrong with the design of this gusseted tongue. DRATS!

review_headline: Great table tennis shoe for both my wife and me.
review_body: My wife and I play table tennis at a serious recreational level and wanted to finally get some table tennis shoes. We had looked at recommendations on various table tennis forums and many serious players said that they use volleyball shoes. The various Asics Gel-Rocket series were one of those recommended.    I normally wear 10D (medium) and these fit perfectly. My foot actually measures 10C, but those are impossible to find and I have worn D forever. My wife has a nerve problem in her foot and needs a wider shoe, so she wears women's 8-1/2 D (wide). Since men's medium is D and there is normally a 1-1/2 size difference between men's and women's shoes, she decided to order the 7D men's. They are also a perfect fit for her. We put PowerStep inserts in both shoes for extra support. I wear those in all my shoes and she wears orthotics in shoes that she will wear all day.    We have only used them for 1 time playing for about 2 hours, but they were comfortable and gave a good grip on the vinyl flooring that we play on a lot. I haven't used them on a wood gym floor yet, but I expect they will work fine.

product_title: TOMS+ Pewter Silver Sequins Women's Classics Holiday 001200B12P-PEWTR
review_headline: Fun Shoes- not sure they are authentic
review_body:
I'm writing this review because I feel like these shoes don't have the rating they deserve. I've own(ed) many Toms and so was thrilled when I saw a pair of Toms+ shoes at such a good price. I was worried that maybe they were too good to be true, and am not convinced they aren't. They came in the usual Toms box with the usual Toms flag. The shoes themselves have differences compared to my other Toms...but these are supposedly Toms+, so they should have some differences even if they are authentic. I have two main Authenticity concerns, one being the logo on the interior insert. Most Toms shoes (including the Toms+) I've seen have the tagline printed below the logo. These do not. The logo on the back of the shoe is smaller and has a slightly different blue color than my other Toms as well. However, these Toms are from the 2012 Holiday line so it is possible they have changed the Toms+ design since then. Although to be honest I'm not really sure how much it matters to me as (they were on sale when I bought them) price, craftsmanship and quality of these shoes is still good either way. I will still be wearing them from time to time, but wish there was a way to put my mind at ease about their authenticity.

I ordered them in the same size as all my other Toms, and although they are very slightly bigger than classic canvas-style Toms, they do fit rather similarly to the glitter Toms I own in the same size. That said, it doesn't surprise there is some size difference, as Toms are notorious for their inconsistent sizing. For comparison, the support seems the same as all other Tom shoes.

It should be noted that the shoes do look a little different in person. I was pleasantly surprised to find I liked them in person much more than online. They have a slight metallic finish to them, and are not as sparkly/shiny as glitter/sequin Toms, which I prefer. I also like the random placement and slight color variance of the sequins better than the look of the traditional sequin Toms. I have only worn them once so far, but I didn't notice any sequins shedding or falling off like they do on the glitter Toms, so I'm hoping that these will be more durable than the glitter Toms I've have.

review_headline: Great Ugg Alternative - High Quality, Great Price
review_body:
This is my second pair of Bearpaw's. I absolutely love them! These boots are high quality - real suede on the outside and real shearling on the inside. Highly recommend if you don't care about brand names and what a high quality product and a reasonable price. I think the soles are little thicker and/or rugged then Uggs, which I prefer.

I got my first pair for almost 10 years ago and wore them almost every day during the winter. Replacing them because the shearling inside under my feet finally wore out, but the rest of the boot is still going strong. So I would STRONGLY DISAGREE with some reviews that say these fall apart. The only thing I can think of is the vendor sold fake one's. I will update my review if I have any problems with quality with these boots.

They are extremely soft and my feet stay toasty during the Midwest's extremely cold winters - WITHOUT SOCKS! I mean I was outside for almost an hour shoveling and snow-blowing in extreme cold temperatures. They only thing that got cold were my hands.

I would say they are true to size. They might be a little snug at first, but will stretch a little and conform to your feet over use.

+ VERY comfortable
+ Affordable
+ Outstanding construction; not a single piece has failed
+ Cushioned rim around ankle
+ Extremely high quality leather
+ Laces are STILL intact years later
+ Sole is an amazing material
+ Stylish in many situations

Cons:
None!

product_title: Clarks Women's Ingalls Vicky Boot
review_headline: Extra comfort for normal and slim feet
review_body:
Blister risk: Low/none
Comfort--half day: 10/10
Comfort--all day: 10/10
Life: 9/10
Heel: medium
Fit: Normal or Narrow
Worst wear areas: Heel and sole (tip of toe)
Clarks may be a bit pricier than some other brands you'll find, but they're worth every penny. I've have a couple pairs of Clarks boots over the last few years and they've all been great. If you wear them nearly every day for a year they'll probably last the whole year, even if you use them to go hiking, horseback riding, or drag them through mud and snow.
The leather is high quality and the stitching is tough, so they'll last for ages if you take care of them.
Clarks are also high on my list for best comfort boots. They're well padded and a little insulated too so you can wear them in warm or cool weather, and they keep out damp pretty well.
I also like the medium heels on these, so if you need a bit of a heel or just want some extra lift, these are perfect, as they'll still be comfortable.
The heel tend to wear out before anything else does, if you wear it down enough, but can still be repaired for longer wear.
A thinner ankle on these means less slip and fewer heel blisters.

review_headline: Haven't worn Asics Men's Volleyball shoes for a decade
review_body: I live in an area of the country that focuses on running/cross country, basketball, and football. The only volleyball around here is women's volleyball, so finding these shoes in any local stores was impossible. I don't run or play any of those other sports, but because cross-training shoes are the most common, I've been using those for the last decade or so. Then I found these on Amazon. I use them to play racquetball--and they are excellent shoes! Good grip on the court and I forgot how much I missed the flatter soles on these compared to what cross-trainers and running shoes typically have. I get a much better feel for the court with these. My feet are also a little wider than average, and these fit nicer that way too.

review_body: I have been looking for a boot for skinny legs for a while, but didn't want a combat-style boot with laces. Having the laces in the back solves the problem! I am 5'2", and the boot hits perfectly below my knee, although I have trouble when moving my foot from the gas to brake pedal when driving due to the buckle hooking on the edge of my car seat. Seems to fit perfectly, but if you need to wear thicker socks for cold weather, you may want to order a 1/2 size up. When scratched from wear, a light grey color appears, but that is part of wearing any shoe. I am so glad I bought this shoe. Free shipping and free returns weren't a bad perk, either. I also tried the KEEN Women's Delancey WP CNX Boot in Mocha (too big in calf), and the KEEN Arabella Bern Boot (to big in calf). Both cute, both leather, but at the end of the day, I can get this boot with a great fit, and order replacement if I ever needed to.

I was a little worried that the red color might bleed onto clothing--it didn't.  And the leather is very nice and did fine even after getting wet. product_title: Caterpillar Men's Rangler MR 6" Steel Toe Work Boot
review_body: Purchased these around early march and have broke them in, changed out the original soles and continue to wear these smelly things. The front part has slowly begun to tear due to kicking materials in place and using my foot as a prop. That's expected though, I don't like the nasty black crap on my the tip of my boot that looks like a bad caulk job so I'm ok with it. As for the rubber on the soles, they grip well, even on a moist roof with a nice slope -- tread carefully though. The heel isn't in the way, the toes (ordered EE) fit comfortable, just 'knuckle up' if you're gonna kick something, or you'll regret it.    As for soles, the original sole isn't too bad but if you can find something or have something more comfy, go for it. I ended up ripping them up about 4 months in, but they weren't too bad for me. They aren't waterproof though, so if you have a problem sinking in mud, dealing with a ton of snow and ice or general rain puddles on the site, may consider some spray if this is your only pair.    UPDATE: I've had them for 8 months and the soles are still pretty good, they still do not cramp my feet. Unfortunately the leather has worn off on the front and water is seeping under the boot. This is simply from my occupation and how hard it is on the toes. I intend to get some 'tuff toe' and snoseal so I can hopefully push them through the winter.    For 100$, these boots aren't bad at all, they are comfy, easy to break in (I think it took me maybe a few days?) and the soles don't like to slip often on high slopes. I may buy again if Thorogood boots don't win out on me with their brand and quality.    UPDATE 2: After 10 months of wearing them and using all kinds of methods to seal them up and keep them from getting my feet soaked, I have finally given up the ghost on them and decided it's time to purchase a better pair of boots higher quality. Overall I will say if you treat them right and are doing warehouse work, these should last you more than a year. If they cansurvive me for 10 months, they'll survive anyone for longer!

product_title: Ellie Shoes Inc Men's Pirate Buckle Boot
review_body:
Many other reviewers have spoken on the quality of these boots, and my experience is no different. I am extremely pleased with these for the price, they are a huge upgrade from the boot covers that came with my costume that I plan to wear for Halloween.

That being said, I wanted to provide my input as far as sizing is concerned. Information is spotty and I was wary about purchasing, but I'm glad I did. First off, I did find elsewhere this sizing chart:

S: 8-9
M: 10-11
L: 12-13

I noticed several people who said they are in the 9-10 range who ordered a medium and said they fit well. My shoes are all a 9 or 9.5 so I decided to go with the small and I'm glad I did. They fit very well, almost even a little extra room, probably just enough for some inserts for the soles. When I purchased, it was Prime and they were offering free returns in accordance with the standard clothing return policy. YMMV but something to keep in mind, helped make it easy to take a chance.

I haven't worn them out and about yet so can't comment on long-term comfort or durability at this point.

product_title: La Sportiva Nago Climbing Shoe - Men's
review_body:
Do not listen to the "fits as" info that Amazon provides. It's obscure and doesn't help with decision making.

Based on my shoe size, a 43.5 is what I would need for this. a 42 is what would actually fit as far as a functional climbing shoe goes. It may be tight for you at first, but it will stretch after a few wears. I kept my 42.5 because I thought it was perfect, but after only a couple climbs it stretched enough that I'm not comfortable doing heel-hooks in them.

If in doubt, size down more, unless you want to end up with a pair of all-day trad shoes that don't fit well enough for bouldering and technical climbing.

As far as the shoe itself goes, it seems rather durable, it's well designed, and the toe box is perfect for my (apparently) somewhat wide forefoot.

It loses a star for dying my feet blood red every time I wear them, and stretching more than I anticipated.

product_title: Danner Men's Pronghorn 18" Snake Boots
review_headline: *IF* they ever wear out, will buy another pair!
review_body:
I suspect I have put a couple hundred miles on these boots over the past 3 seasons hunting/scouting. Besides some scuffs, dried blood and caked up dirt, these boots are holding up amazingly well. I may need some new insoles after this season, they are just now starting to come apart at the toe(just the insole pad, not the boot).

These boots are water proof. But don't be fooled, if you tuck in your pant legs and walk through wet vegetation, your feet will end up wet, but that is not the boots fault.

The boots lace up easily. I lace them up fully, then wrap the laces around the top of the boot and then double knot them. I have had a boot come untied when going through thickets, but it is RARE. If I were to guess, it happens less than 5% of trips and I am frequently in awful thick cypress bottoms with tangles of vines and unforgiving saw palmetto fields that wreak havoc on most boots.

They are very lightweight and comfortable, they feel like sneakers. I regularly walk 2-4 miles per trip usually for 2-3 consecutive days and have never gotten a blister while wearing these boots. They are not hot like other snake boots. They seem to 'breathe' even though they are waterproof.

These boots are not insulated, I wore them once in cold weather and my feet were freezing. You can feel the temp of the water as soon as you step into it, whether it is warm water on a chilly morning or cool water on a hot afternoon.

These boots make me a lot more comfortable(mentally and physically) while tromping through the swamp. Will update if I ever get struck by a snake!

Parting words:
WORTH EVERY PENNY!

Bought a pair towards the end of May. At first I was impressed. Decent arch. Nice cushioning. Unfortunately, here I am in the first half of October and my feet are aching.

I'm on my feet a lot so it's possible I need to switch pairs every 3 months but that seems rather aggressive. It's also possible I need to check out a podiatrist to see if I have something more serious a sneaker can't fix.

Either way, the cushioning on the insole I loved so much when purchasing is dead. The shoe itself has held up great. No tears, fraying and the stitching is all intact. The tread is fairly worn but not awful.

The sneaker gets 3 stars due to the shipping being quick and easy, being a fantastic sneaker for the first month and holding together for 4 months while being used 8 hours a day, 5 days a week.

It loses 2 stars due to the insole severely flattening out and the tread on the bottom of the shoe wearing away.

product_title: Mizuno Women's Wave Sayonara 2 Running Shoe
review_body:
I stumbled upon this shoe after Adidas discontinued the pair that I had been using for several years. I had never used a Mizuno shoe. I am so glad I found it.

To give some background, I am a 50+ year old distance runner, about 145 pounds and 5' 10\\" with average arches. I really have no pain or running injury issues, except that some shoes in the past, including the Adidas, have led to blisters and bruised toenails.

I have used the Wave Sayonara now in 6 marathons. Zero blisters. Zero hot spots. Zero bruised toenails. Zero foot pain. Two of the six were run seriously and led to Boston qualifiers by substantial margins, the last one more than 20 minutes below my qualifying time. So this is a real shoe with real performance potential.

This is an excellent shoe. It is light weight and responsive. The shoe does have a wide toe box, and this felt odd to me at first, as I was used to tight fitting shoes. It felt too loose. But it has been a blessing. I buy a half size larger than my street shoe, and I use thin, high quality running socks. The result has been foot bliss.

Do not base your opinion of the shoe on how it feels initially or how it compares in feel to something else you have run in. These are not valid benchmarks. Use the shoe, run a marathon in them, see how your feet feel afterwards - this is a valid test of the quality of the shoe. I don't think you will be disappointed in this shoe.

One piece of advice - you might consider buying 2 pair, different colors, and alternating use each day - this is what I do. I find that this gives the cushioning ample time to recover and also to dry out, and extends the life of both shoes well beyond what might be expected.

Good luck with your running and if you choose this shoe, I hope you enjoy them as much as I have.

review_headline: Look at the sole pattern if you have plantar fasciitis and low arches
review_body:
Both my wife and I have been wearing Blundstones since we saw them all over Australia (literally looked liked everybody wore them) back in 1999. I've ordered many different ones since then, but always the "traditional" model 510, then kind of fell out of love with them, and I wear them only occasionally.
In the last 2-3 years a developed a plantar fasciitis issue one my left foot and the Blunnies are the only shoes I can wear all day long (10 hours plus working on my feet) without having my foot hurt, in fact my issue was almost gone.
When I saw this model on amazon I had to say they looked pretty slick and more dressier,
although the sole pattern looks a LITTLE different, the sole height appeared to be the same,
well I was wrong, after only one day of wearing them my foot started to feel a little odd, I've should had stop then, but I decided to give it another day, very bad idea by the second evening my foot was hurting just like it used to ........
saying so it is not necessarily the Tasmanian maker's fault but if you have my same issue and kind of low arched feet be careful as they might not work for you.

review_headline: As always.. I think they are ugly and I now they will be my favorites.
review_body:

They feel slightly too tight out of the box.. but after a few days they fit like a very comfortable pair of gloves.

I recently moved to a small tourist town and now walk everywhere and knew I would need something for the snowy months. These will fit that bill... and I'm sure I'll wear them for years and years. They aren't "hiking" boots... but I think they will be awesome for snowy street and sidewalks.
