product_title: Saucony Men's Kinvara TR2 Trail Running Shoe
review_headline: Good shoe but not for me.
review_body: First I should disclose the little toe on my right foot can be an issue in shoes but usually the left is fine. So I wont knock a shoe unless it gets both feet which is the case here.    In fact every Saucony I have tried recently impacts both feet/little toes substantially both on the side and the top. I guess the shape of their shoes is not compatible with the shape of my feet. I found this is to be a narrow shoe even for Saucony....It is light and feels well made but too narrow over all and a pinkie crusher for me and that is even before running, foot swelling and toe splay come into play.  This shoe is firm, It amazes me how soft and mushy the roads shoe I tried from them are (Kinvara, Ride) and how hard  the trail shoes are (Peregrine, Kinvara TR2) I will say  it is impressive how solid yet how light both those trails shoes are.    Curious about my ongoing toe box issues with Saucony, I matched up a Kinvara 4 next to a Mizuno Hitogami side by side, the Kinvara 4 toe box looks noticeably taller and wider, yet it pushes and pressures my little toes way too much while the Hitogami fit perfect..go figure!    Sure is not easy being a running shoe whore these days...quite a challenge finding a compatible shoe. I am an older guy...5-9 150, neutral foot, high arches, midfoot/fore foot striker..average 30 to 40 miles a week mostly trail, hard pack dirt.

review_body:
You really need to order a 1/2 size up from your normal shoe size in casual athletic shoes; even if your shoe size fluctuates in the half-size range, if your feet or ankles tend to swell for any reason, order up as well.

These suedes are many degrees better than Converse, or similar cheap sneaks like Skechers, Punkrose or Pumas. If on sale, they're a STEAL. If they are full-retail $70 Forget About It!

The deeply dyed leather *does* run the first two times in the rain or the washer, so go sockless or wear ones you can trash and wash separately or buy themselves. The seude takes water=proofing products well and is easy to brush clean.

Yes, the laces are short, but every slacker/skateboarder/biker knows you leave the first holes unlaced (which solves the length problem customers here are complaining about). That's how the shoe is supposed to be worn! And, yes, they're high squeaks-- people in the grocery store could hear me 10 aisles over when I turned on my heels to double-take a good deal!

The ONLY thing keeping them from 5-star status-- and I think people already ken this-- is the lack of any real athletic support sole. But these are hipster schlubs and I LOVE THEM.

review_body: I got this bag on eBay in a glazed, distressed white which is so rock-n-roll.  That sort of crackled distressing always sheds a bit of itself in the first day or two, but then softens and feels like a suede.  The size is good for a tablet and a kindle, though it could use a thicker strap if you're going to have that much weight in there.  I use it for day trips when I'll need my kindle and a light shirt to throw on in addition to my cell phone/wallet/lippy/etc.  It is handy having the two pouches, one more secure and the other easier to get to.  I love the crossbody style for walking around all day, but I'm going to have to punch another hole or two in the strap because I'm a little short for it's length (5'3").  This is a great medium size bag - simple in design but edgy with the studs.  Well-made by Frye, as you'd expect.

product_title: Kenetrek Men's Hardscrabble Hiker Hiking Boot
review_body:
I have been eyeing these for a while but hesitated due to price. I had seen them first at a store where I tried them on and found them to be comfortable.

These replaced a pair of Asolo boots which run around $250 to replace. I finally gave in and am really sorry that I waited so long. I find these to be amongst the most comfortable I have ever worn. I am still breaking them in but even the first day with these I was extremely impressed at the fit and comfort.

The soles are thick so you may find that some think you seem much taller. They'll give you an extra inch just like an iPhone and if you are the type that needs an extra inch, they have it. I don't need an extra inch anywhere but I won't complain about having it either.

I have not been on extreme terrain nor have I tested the waterproof aspect but I am confident in both. I did order the Kenetrek wax to treat them.

I would definitely buy them again!

product_title: BOBS from Skechers Women's Keepsakes Slipper
review_body:
I wanted some "sturdy" slippers for my mom because she seems to trip a lot wearing any of the traditional type of slipper (where the longer you own them the more "floppy" they get; eventually folding under at the wrong time and tripping the wearer).

I didn't know that there'd be sparkles on-top of the print and since my mom doesn't like to wear anything too "loud" I was worried that she'd take one look at the combined "animal print + sparkly" and politely say, thanks, but no thanks!" Imagine my surprise when she put these on and said, "I cannot wear these to the grocery store! But I'll love wearing them around here." On the first day of ownership some gravy spilled onto one of the slippers so she threw it in the wash, (no dryer), afraid of what the outcome might be. She happily showed me that it cleaned beautifully and looked just as good as it's unwashed mate.

She wears an 8-1/2 to 9 and she said that the nine's fit just fine. If my sisters or I require slippers I'd happily look up Skecher's Bobs and buy whichever cute style was on sale that day.

product_title: Ariat Men's Rambler Wide Square Toe Western Cowboy Boot
review_body: These boots look good and fit pretty well, but it has a sloppy construction flaw.  The main boot portion (the leather part) is glued to the sole, and you can clearly see this glue.  It's jagged and irregular, and the real problem is that it is so unevenly applied that there are portions where the glue accumulates in noticeable white globs.  From 6 feet away, these white globs are easily seen against the black backdrop of the boot/sole and so make the boot look very cheap and poorly made.  I looked at three different pairs of boots -- 6 individual boots in total, and three of the boots (50% of them) had this glob issue (the others just had the irregular glue line).  I returned them and ordered a different brand that didn't look like it was put together by an eight year old and a stick of glue.  This obvious lack of quality control and attention to detail gives me serious doubts about the entire line of Ariat boots -- Ariat appears to be yet another Made in China company that cares more about shortcuts and keeping costs down than producing something well-made.

product_title: Clarks Women's UN Linda Falt
review_body:
Pros: Leather, nice buckle, soft inside
Cons: Too short and tight. Too low in toe area (and I have slender feet), not much arch support, insole hard and where two parts meet irritates the foot . Looks too childish .

I am becoming the biggest shoe whiner on Amazon. I am being disappointed time and time again, and I am not even that picky. I have normal feet 8 Regular/Wide, slender ankles, delicate skin, no bunions etc. I also have back problems and need shoes that fit well and are comfortable for long walks. I even got Amazon Prime, because I was tired of searching for a good shoes in stores that mainly cater to fashion girls. I just need : Stable low heel, arch support, heel cup, non-slippery inside, no rough seams or straps, adjustable straps, toe room, a little bit of elegance or at least smart/casual look. It seems that all the shoes Made in China could fit Chinese feet, not American feet, it seems like there is no (American) quality control at all. Materials are cheap, shoes look cheap and they feel awful. It also seems like companies don't test their shoes on REAL people. I also feel guilty every time I return the shoes and order other ones, knowing that I am contributing to more fumes in the air.

product_title: Under Armour Men's UA Wall Hanger Leather Boots
review_headline: Just purchased today, but good initial experience.
review_body: I just bought these boots today so I have not had a chance to wear them out in the field yet.  I tried them on at Cabela's and thought they were very supportive and very comfortable even though I had to try on a 1/2 size too big in the camo version..  I plan to use them for hunting, but also for hiking so I didn't particularly want the camo version.  The leather and rubber seem to be very durable.  I was surprised at how comfortable they were especially before being broke in.  I had trouble finding my size (10.5). Cabela's only had a 9 and 13.  I also checked on Amazon and my size was not available there either.  I was finally successful on UnderArmour.com and they had free 2 day shipping.  Cabela's was going to charge $20 for standard shipping and I didn't even check Amazon' shipping price. I also avoided paying sales tax on underarmour.com. I apparently got the last 10.5 from underarmour.com because when I went back to the website to look at the boot again I searched my size and the 10.5 were no longer available.  I assume that these boots are either highly popular, or they are low on inventory because they are brand new. I am excited to wear them for the upcoming hunting season.  I will submit a new review once I have worn them in the field a for a few months.  From what I have discovered by trying them on is that the size is true to fit, and they are very comfortable.  Based on my initial experience I would recommend this product.

review_body: Hello,    I'd first like to say that I've bought a total of three pairs of these shoes. They have been my go-to work shoes for about four years now. I'm not sure what happened but I received a pair of shoes that don't look like previous pairs or the picture posted on this page.    Don't get me wrong. It is the same shoe with the same designs but something is wrong with the stripe that goes parallel to the ground and the laces. The picture (and previous shoes) have had tan laces with a light white stripe on the shoe. The ones I received have dark laces and the white stripe is now dark gray. This leaves the shoe to appear incredibly dark and has no contrasting white/dark colors.    I haven't decided if I'll return these (or even looked to see if I can).    Overall, these are still decent shoes if you don't mind the fully dark color.    Thanks    Side Note:  My first pair lasted a little over two and a half years. My second pair lasted under a year and now need to be replaced. I either got a funk pair or the quality is going down.

product_title: Sun Shield Fit Over Sunglasses with Blue Blocker HD Driving Lens & Spring Hinges - Fit Over Prescription Glasses
review_headline: Does the job, at a great price
review_body:
You can find cheaper fit-over sunglasses (if you look hard) but these are quite inexpensive and are worth every penny. You'll find that you can spend a huge amount more without any real added value.

First of all, the color. Blue blocking results in a pleasing seemingly sharper view, and some experts hold that blue blocking keeps out harmful rays that are not otherwise avoided.

These fit-overs feature the small windows at the front of the temples, which facilitate peripheral vision--a possible lifesaver in driving use.

For even less money you can get [[ASIN:B00741IHSU Blue Blocking Driving Wayfarers Sunglasses Amber Tinted Lens]], which unlike conventional fit-overs can easily be stowed in an ordinary eyeglass case. I use both. The problem with using Wayfarers as fit-overs is that there's no real protection against the sun's creeping in over the top. So I use them only when I'm also wearing a broad-brimmed hat.

The chief downside of these SunShields is that they won't fit into a conventional eyeglass case. The case that accompanies them is usable but not very practical. For a case I've chosen [[ASIN:B001OA8YZS Extra Large Clamshell Sunglass Case (AS179)]] currently at under $9.00.

UPDATE: The \\"Extra Large\\" case has arrived, and though it's plenty large, the SunShields won't fit! I'll be returning the case and searching for a different one.

review_headline: Satisfied with quality but not with sizing
review_body:
This is my fourth year buying these shoes from this vendor. I am definitely satisfied with the quality of the shoes as these get worn every day (except games day) and they hold up well. Last school year, my older daughter who is soon to be 7 years old wore a size 2(Big Kid).

I bought these also for my younger daughter who started the same school last year. I bought her shoes online as well, but when they came (Size 9 - Little Kid), they were very tight, almost like 2 sizes smaller than we expected it to be and surprisingly, when I purchased these from the local retailer that same month I only had to move up to a size 10 which was very very roomy. With that fact, I decided that it would be better to source shoes for both my daughters from the local retailer this year, but they told me they only carried up to Size 2.

I therefore had to revert to getting these online 3(Big Kid) for my older daughter! When it arrived, I realized it was not much larger than the size 2 that I bought the previous year. From common sense I knew that I would have to take into account the fact that my child's feet would have grown, but consistently each year I purchased these and one size up was always the right fit. Not so this year. My daughter complained that it was very tight, so we had to revert to the size 2 that she wore the last school year since it had been broken in pretty well and had somewhat stretched. We are hoping that this size 3 will get broken in soon enough and get stretched enough that she can wear it to school comfortably with her regular school socks and not just with the thinnest socks we can find.

Outside of the sizing woes for this school year, I have to say that I am very satisfied with these shoes as they are light weight but very durable. These were also recommended by the school because from experience the younger children would "trip up" a lot while wearing the heavier shoes. These are flexible and durable!! I would recommend these but would say that they run a little smaller than you would expect so always buy one size up.would recommend these but would say that they run a little smaller than you would expect so always buy one size up.

He is 55, but stylish and "young." This shoe style would suit any age. Skechers gives you both a set of brown shoe laces and a more sporty yellow/brown striped lace. product_title: Rismart Women's Sneakers Punk Knee High Costumes Lace Ups Canvas Boots
review_headline: Much smaller than advertised; four sets of too-short laces.
review_body:
I really want to love these. They came with four (four!) pairs of shoelaces - black, white, bright blue and lime green, an unexpected bonus. BUT... the shoelaces are too short to lace up the boots all the way to the top and tie. I do have wide feet, but I order up a half-size and that almost always accommodates them, and wouldn't account for the short laces, which are really, really too short, by about 8 inches. My calves are slim, so that doesn't account for it, either.

The boots claim, on a tag inside, to be a size 39. That's usually more of an 8 1/2 US. Sorry, but these are nowhere near a 39, nor even an 8. They're short on my feet; my toes are almost at the end. That *never* happens to me in an 8. They're also too narrow compared with every other 8 I've tried on that is a B width - these are more like a 7 1/2 N or a 7 B. I'm really bummed because I didn't want to have to send them back, but I'm going to have to do so.

UPDATE, one month later: I contacted the seller to try to return the boots, and they told me to keep them, and that they'd send me another, larger pair. I chose a full size up, which is slightly too big, but much closer to a real European size 39 than the ones labeled 39 were. They also included two pairs of longer laces, these just barely long enough to lace the boots up tightly to the top (and I do mean tightly -- with loose lacing, these laces still aren't long enough to make it to the top).

So I have to give the seller kudos for shipping me a new larger pair and letting me keep the small ones, which I guess I'll give away. But I do still wish they'd change their sizing info, and that the laces were truly plenty long.

product_title: Vionic with Orthaheel Technology Womens Yara Sandal
review_body:
I have had plantar f problems in the past, due to my flat feet. It was so bad, I couldn't finish basic training in the army because of my foot problems.

Finding comfortable shoes has always been a hassle for me.

I just got these shoes yesterday and I have to say that the footbed on them is amazing. Its not just soft. It actually 'props up' my fallen arches, making it to where I don't have so much of an ankle roll anymore. These sandals feel like I'm wearing tennis shoes, but better!

Now for the reason why I gave it 4 instead of 5 stars. The upper part of the sandal has a design issue, and I'm thinking its just this particular sandal of theirs that has this problem. The upper part hits the top of my foot in a weird way as if its too long, so its constantly creating a rubbing sore. Its only a little bit, but its enough to make it painful. My feet are long, so I never had this problem before with any other shoe.

The top part is made out of pvc-type material that isn't likely to get softer after more wear, so I'm thinking it will always feel like this.

However, now that I know of this shoe company, I am going to try other shoes of theirs, because the footbed, again, is awesome. If you have flat feet, I recommend trying this company! (Just not this particular sandal.)

product_title: Donald J Pliner Women's Blis Ankle Boot
review_body:
I got these in the leopard print. Knowing & loving Donald Pliner shoes, I know they run small so I ordered up.
I wear a true 7. I order a 7.5 usually in boots to be able to accommodate wearing socks with them. In this, I ordered the size 8 knowing how Pliners run small. It was good I did, also with the pointed toe. They fit well in the 8 with thin socks. I also have a slightly narrow foot (which is good considering Pliners are always narrow).
These are pretty for sure but I didnt think they looked quite as nice in person (which is the opposite reaction I normally have with Pliners).
The leopard print is painted on and had a couple minor flaws that looked a bit on the tacky side.
Otherwise, they look nice-they went on and off easily/nicely. Smooth zipper action, etc.
******I am RETURNING them - here is why:
I'm not great with high heels and 3.5 is my absolute max heel height if there is no platform to help.
These are listed as having a 3.5 inch heel, but it is actually just barely under 4" tall (apx. 3 ⅞").
With that angle, it makes the ball of the foot feet really hard when walking and it hurt just taking a couple steps (for me).
In addition, the boot comes up just a little too high for that high of an angle/heel, making it cut into the back of your leg a bit…not horribly, but enough to be uncomfortable after just a min. or two.
All this said, if you are good with high heels, have narrow feet, and don't mind a slight discomfort in the name of fashion, then you'd probably be happy with these.
For me, any shoe near or over $100 must be incredible to look at and incredibly comfortable for me to justify the price.

product_title: New Balance Men's MX20v3 Minimus Cross-Training Shoe
review_body:
I Crossfit 3-5 times every week. These shoes are perfect for high interval training. They are lightweight, with enough flex for cardio and intense TABATA, but provide plenty of support and a very firm base for weightlifting. product_title: Superfeet GREEN Full Length Insole
review_headline: Superfeet do a good job of lifting up a fallen arch or supporting ...
review_body:
There seems to be a lot of confusion out there in terms of what type of insole people need for different types of feet. I'll try to make sense of it for you.

If you have low arches, you need to raise your arch up so that your foot and knee are in correct alignmnet. So you are going to need a lot of arch support. People with high arches are also going to need a lot of arch support. Their arches are so high up, that they need to use an insole with lots of arch support so that contact is made between the insole and arch. So, people with low and high arches will benefit from an insole with high arch support. If you have low arches, DON't get an insole with low arches, Get one with high arches. You need to elevate your arches!!!

Superfeet do a good job of lifting up a fallen arch or supporting a high arch. So they work for both low arches or high arches. My problem with them is that they don't provide enough arch support. The Sof Sole have a lot more arch support and I think will give more comfort.

review_body: I immediately had two thoughts upon puling the first boot from the box. Man, these are nice! Darn, these are to small! I did retry the boot with a thin sock and the boot did fit better but the break-in would not have been fun and I like being able to wear a nice comforting sock on my feet. Amazon must have realized this would happen and the boot came with free return shipping, so cool! Good thought ! it's not going to cost me any money for return shipping, I'll just return them and get another pair that fits. More disappointment. The boot only comes in a D width. I could order a size 10 but it would still be to narrow.Disappointment, the final chapter. I loved this boot but they didn't have one available that would fit me properly, but if you have a narrow foot this may be the boot for you. So the boot is a three but Amazon gets a five for free return shipping.

product_title: West Blvd Womens Paris Cowboy Boots
review_body:
Be prepared for a REAL medium-thin fit with these. Even if you THINK you're wide width, you shouldn't get them. They're GORGEOUS, and that's why I gave them a 4, but very slim fit.

That said:
-Shipping time was great and they came in a nicely stuff, properly sized yellow shoe box that I lined with a towel and use to store them in.
-They're very soft, but sturdy. Silky texture, very thin material, with good support around the actual foot, if not the ankle.
-Scuffing isn't too bad, for being worn up and down stairs or around the supermarket. DO NOT wear in dirt or sand. You'll have a hell of a time getting them back to glossy black when you clean them.
- VERY GOOD traction on these. I have NO problem walking on a damp tile kitchen in them. I have NOT tried anything more than an already-wiped spill, so don't go skipping through puddles on my word alone.

Overall, a nice buy. If they came in a wide or a 12, I'd be back for other colors. :)

review_headline: The Great Purple Purse Search of 2014 is over.
review_body:
I love it. It just arrived and in time for my trip this week. I have had a massive six month hunt for the just right purple purse - The Great Purple Purse Search of 2014. I had narrowed it down to this $60 and two Baggallini's, the Palermo $120 and the Stanza $180. Obviously going thru the lower cost items first. Well the eggplant is a muted purple very nice, with a taupe inner lining. Lots of pockets and pouches in and out. More than ample storage for a tablet and large smart phone in cases. This sucker would definitely hold a 15" laptop too. I love the bottom straps for holding a jacket while traveling too. The side pouches will each hold a slim 16 oz. bottle of water.

Also has a pad on the very long shoulder strap. This strap is really nice and long so this round girl can still wear as a cross body and not look too dumpy, not that I really care because I wanted function over form. This should have plenty of room for carrying a change of clothing or two while traveling as a just in case along with all the requisite chargers and other electronic paraphernalia modern life requires. Looks it will also hold another smaller bag quite easily. I assumed the bottom zipper on the back side was so the purse would slip over the handles of a rolling bag but is for the straps for holding jackets or yoga mats instead. That was my fault for assuming so no stars deducted for that. It my be too large for some people but I carry a really big hobo bag now and I need something with more organization and usable space so looking forward to this. Next purse will be the Piazza Day bag for when I don't need gigantor here.

FYI I quit using a very nice black Prada double messenger because the strap is not long enough and the inside is like staring into the black hole of Calcutta. It was good size but the buckle fasteners and unconstructed hobo shape made all my stuff clump together so I retired that years ago for something more cheery. I considered bring it out ofretirement but to save some $$ but once again function won over form and name brand.

product_title: Women's Brooks Ghost 7 Running Shoe
review_headline: My favorite shoe just got better...
review_body: I have been running in Brooks Ghost 5s and then the 6s for the last couple of years.  I love the Ghosts, but the Ghost7s are by far my favorite generation so far.  For some reason the other Ghosts always required a "breaking-in period" of a week or two (depending on mileage) before I could use them on long runs.  They were always a little stiff and caused some foot pain if I tried to do too much too soon in them.  The 7s somehow managed to fix that.  They feel somewhat lighter, but more importantly, they feel a lot more flexible!  I think this is due to the new style of meshing used.  They felt fantastic right after the first run.  The next day I chanced a lengthier run and they still felt amazing - supportive but light and cushy - and no weird pains at all! And it seems with the 7s they have finally learned to bring in a better design team for zippier, fun colors! Gray and white with a sad pop of color is so boring.  I need something fun to look at after 20+miles of running - I like shoes that have a "super hero" feel.  Brooks finally got all of this right without sacrificing the Ghost shoe I originally fell in love with.

product_title: Merrell Men's Vapor Glove Trail Running Shoe
review_body: As many of the reviews on Amazon.com and the Merrell website state, the shoe runs half a size large. I wear a 12 and the 11.5 fits perfectly. The previous minimalist shoes I wore were the original New Balance Minimus MT10 which were probably the best constructed training shoe I have ever worn. However, their new versions are made poorly and fall apart after only a few weeks of non strenuous use. Because of this, I searched for a new shoe and the Merrell Vapor Glove Trail Running Shoe seemed like it would be a good replacement. However, many of the reviews mentioned that the mesh in the front of the shoe would begin tearing away from the Vibram sole. Most of these reviews came from individuals who wore the shoe for running. I planned to only walk in the shoes and use it occasionally for training in the gym, but not for activities like running, which would cause my toes to create constant heavier pressure against the mesh and cause it to tear. The shoes are extremely light and flexible, and made the NB Minimus feel thick and heavy. Both use Vibram technology for the soles. I was extremely happy with the shoe as they were very comfortable as well. However, now after having them for almost 5 months, the mesh is tearing on each shoe even though I am not using them for strenuous training or activity. If Merrell can fix this issue, I would recommend these shoes to everyone who wants a great minimalist shoe. But unfortunately, it seems many companies are sacrificing the quality of their products.

product_title: Merrell Men's Vapor Glove Trail Running Shoe
review_headline: Ignore the reviews telling you to order small!
review_body:
Much of what needs to be said about these shoes in the 200+ other reviews has been said (e.g. they are great shoes; they are the next best thing to walking or running barefoot; they provide some much-needed protection against sharp rocks, roots, & broken glass; they are light; they are easy to wash; etc.) But here are a couple of additional things that need mention:

1. Following the advice of a few reviews I read, I ordered a half-size smaller than I normally wear. Big mistake. My toes were jammed uncomfortably up against the front edge of the show (which is rather non-flexible). Both with and without socks, it was a problem, and I had to exchange them. Order your true size!

2. The color of the "black" shoes is really more of a "dragon fly green" or "Green Lantern silver." They are by no stretch of the imagination black in color. There is a very pronounced translucent green thing going on and the wavy stripes are clearly green and grey or silver. I'm not complaining. The color is actually very cool! These shoes are still passable for around the office on casual days, but Amazon really should either update the picture with a more accurate one, or change the "black" reference to "grey green" or something else.

review_headline: Very durable, lightweight, regulation compliant, and a real boot - not a running shoe.
review_body:
The odd pitch of the boot initially made them feel a bit uncomfortable, especially if they're laced to tight. However, after a week or two of break in, they feel very comfortable. I've already put in a few ruck marches and airborne ops in these, and I actually prefer them over my old Nike SFBs - primarily because of the additional support.

UPDATE: These boots are quite durable. I recently bought a second pair; not because my first pair were no longer serviceable, but due to stains from heavy field use. My first pair have undergone long marches, airborne ops, and months of time in the field. They have held together very well, and so far all the stitching has remained tight and intact, the canvas sides have not frayed or torn at all, and the soles exhibit minimal wear. I'll continue to wear my first pair whenever I go to the field for several more years, I'm sure - I expect to continue using these boots until the wear-out date for tan boots in 2019, and will replace them with the darker coyote brown version.

product_title: Texcyngoods Pebbled Leather Organizer Purse Handbag 3 Compartments Pockets
review_body: I am on a quest to find the perfect purse for myself. I thought this one might be it, but No! This bag arrived today. Upon taking it out of the packaging I immediately noticed its weight. It's very heavy before even loading it up with everything I like to carry. I will start with the Pros of the bag. I like the handle lenght, the 12" length makes it easy to get your arm in and out to put on the shoulder. It seems to stay put on my shoulder although I've only use the bag walking around my house since I just got it today. I love all the pockets on the outside plenty of storage with easy access for your hand to fit in them. Now for the cons: purse is made of heavy car seat quality leather. So if it's heavy before loading it with stuff it's even heavier after the fact which could be an issue for someone pettite or with back, shoulder or neck problems. Next the inside of the 3 main pockets 2 zippered & 1 snap closure are plenty deep but have no additional pockets or slots sewn on them for items you may want to keep inside. It would have been nice if they had put a pen holder or two on the purse as well as a snap on key ring holder and a place for cosmetics. The last thing i dont like is the lining on the inside does not start from the bottom of the zipper. The lining starts about 1/2' below the zipper leaving exposed the back side of the leather. Don't understand the reason for that and it does not look good. So if you can live with those flaws then I would recommend this bag. I will be keeping the bag because I think I can live without the cons i mentioned. The biggest issue for me will be it's weight. I'll see how it goes.

review_body: I was hesitant to purchase this boots after seeing some of the negative reviews. However, I'm very happy that I did because these boots have worked out great for me so far! I work outdoors in the Sierra Nevada during the summer time and sometimes have to hike several miles a day. The Sundowner's not only have worked well so far for my moderate day hikes of maybe ten to twelve total miles, but will hold a great shine when I'm asked to work indoors and be presentable as well. The stream crossings that I made in the spring with them did not to the best of my recollection result in wet feet so I can say that the Gore-Tex lining is pretty solid. I'm completely confident that these boots will last at least five seasons which to me is threshold of what I would consider to be a good boot.With this in mind, I'm planning on getting a pair for my own personal use outside of work. In sum, I would recommend these boots to a friend.

product_title: Dr. Martens Unisex Premium Insoles
review_headline: Great replacement insole for my Doc Martens Commercial Work Shoes
review_body:
The first thing people need to know is that this insole is a replacement for Doc Martens shoes that come with insoles. These are primarily the professional work shoes and boots. If your Doc Martens do not have a removable insole, you should not buy them.
I bought these after the original insoles of my Doc Martens work shoes wore out after eight years. When I first put them in, they seemed a little big. My shoes felt tight for about half of the first day using them. The additional arch support was a little uncomfortable as well. By the end of the first day wearing them, they fit a lot better. After the second day, they felt exactly like the original insoles. My feet seem a little less fatigued at the end of the day compared to the old insoles. I do not know if this is because of the 'advanced design' or because the old insoles were worn out and starting to fall apart at the heel. I hope to wear the shoes for another eight years and only need to replace the insoles then as well.

product_title: Dickies Men's Raider 8" Steel-Toed Work Boot
review_headline: Second Pair I've Owned -- Not So Great This Time
review_body: Upon wearing, this pair proved not to be waterproof.  There was a defect somewhere on the left boot that allowed water in.  I stepped in water about 1-1/2 to 2 inches deep for maybe five or six seconds and my sock was wet.  I had to return them.      This was disappointing because I really liked the first pair of these that I owned.  I bought a pair of Golden Retriever loggers instead that were $89 compared to these $62 Dickies.   Those prices include suppressive sales taxes and \\"free\\" shipping.     Another gripe I have is that none of these boots have a really good insole.  You always have to buy aftermarket insoles.  The first pair of Dickies had a significantly better insole. The Golden Retrievers are better, but I still think I will have to upgrade.  Really, do you have to spend $150 on boots to get a decent insole?    At least Dickies appears to make boots that are the actual size stated, while many manufacturers seem to build in extra room -- possibly for thick boot socks?  In any case, the Golden Retrievers are the same 13M but they are noticeably larger compared to the Dickies. Go figure.      I am not sure I will give Dickies another chance later to win back my business.  Maybe I just got a bad pair, but it seems like that their quality has declined. I may change my mind at some point, but I'm just not feeling it at the moment.

UPDATE: I contacted Amazon about this issue, and they ended up refunding me for the purchase after all. Thank you! So, I've increased the rating to \\"3\\": a rating of \\"1\\" for the product, but a \\"5\\" for Amazon's great customer service.

ORIGINAL POST:

This pair of shoes had two fatal problems:

First, there was a small blotch on the surface of the top of the shoe, approximately 1/8 inch round, where the brown coloring did not completely soak into the shoe. Nothing major, but a small flaw that was very visible from the top of the shoe.

But much worse, one of the shoes simply did not fit. I ordered a size 10D pair of the brown (cognac) oxfords, and received them very quickly. Unfortunately, I let the shoes sit on the closet shelf for about 5 weeks before putting them on to wear. Big mistake! The left shoe was actually painful after only a minute on my foot - although the size was marked correctly.

Do not buy these shoes from Amazon! From now on, I will go to the brick and mortar store to try the pair of shoes on before buying them -- especially important in light of Amazon's draconian return policy of only 30 days!

review_headline: THESE ARE FAKE, DO NOT BUY.
review_body:
I bought these TOMS thinking that I was buying directly from the company's amazon store. WRONG. These are just really believable knock offs. I have real TOMS that I purchased from Nordstrom and these do not compare in quality, fit, color, ect. These shoes are not even lined, the sole is not glued in all the way and I'm almost positive that the sole is not leather. The telltale sign that these were fakes was that the logo was completely wrong; It was a different shade of blue and the size was much bigger than my real TOMS. Also, the font was very wrong and did not look like the regular TOMS trademark logo. The box it came in also looked very suspect. I called Amazon and luckily their customer service is stellar and they gave me a refund and are looking into the seller.

Again, DO NOT BUY, save your time and money and go to the TOMS website or a reputable store like Nordstrom, Journeys or Whole Foods Market. It's shameful that people are trying to ripoff a charity.

So far, I've experience three significant improvements since using these:
1) Mobility in squats - this has always been my problem. I tend to roll forward in front squats and squat snatches but so far, I have been more stable in these.
2) Less knee pains - this could really be an extension of me rolling onto my toes but I have noticed a reduction of knee pain. Which is always awesome because I hate trying to put on those crazy knee pads!
3) Ankle flexibility - Again, it might be because my feet don't feel unstable. I am looking forward to trying these soon for pistols!

product_title: Rocket Dog Women's Spotlightcr Flip Flop
review_headline: Didn't get what I ordered, but I love rocket dogs, so...
review_body:
I love rocket dog flip flops. Last year I replaced my black pair because they finally wore out after years of wear. This year I decided I'd like a brown pair, maybe with some color on them.

I ordered the "natural" which still as I write this has a picture of brown-soled shoes with an earth-tone striped strap. What I received was brown-soled shoes with big blue and red flowers. They're actually pretty cute and I might have even ordered them if they had been an option (again, as I write this I don't see any shoes that look like the ones I got as a choice). I didn't bother to contact amazon or the seller because I decided I'd rather just keep them but if I'd had my heart set on the subtler stripes I would have been upset. I can't really hold it against the company since I didn't give them a chance to fix it, so I don't know how that might have gone.

That said, I kept the shoes and I love them as much as my old ones, maybe even more, because they're much more colorful! There is not much tread, as other reviewers have said, so they are slippery at first before the bottoms get scuffed up, but my older ones aren't slippery at all anymore and they're super comfortable. I have wide feet and they fit perfectly. I have noticed a few reviews on different styles of rocket dog flip flops that complain that they aren't the same quality they used to be but I haven't noticed that at all and I like these, and the ones I got last year, just as much as the ones I'd had for so many years before.

review_headline: ... only rated this 3 stars because I didn't really like the style once I opened the box & looked ...
review_body:
I only rated this 3 stars because I didn't really like the style once I opened the box & looked at them. I'd wanted a different color, but black was the only color I could get in my size. I may have liked the brown or tan ones better. Then again, this is just personal preference & I probably should have shopped around a little more. I haven't worn the shoes, so can't say whether they're comfortable to walk in. I don't wear shoes around the house unless they're something I can slip my feet into & out of quickly & are light & soft (I'm a barefoot girl!). But it does look like a well made shoe & probably, once worn a while, will be comfortable. The price was good.I did order 1/2 size larger than my normal size because I'd wanted to be able to wear socks with them to walk in. These were delivered much faster than what I expected, & in perfect condition. So, for someone else, they might be the perfect shoe.

This is an edited addition to my previous review above. I have had a chance to wear the shoes now, & other than being too tight with socks on, they still aren't too uncomfortable to walk in. What I have found out is, if you buy shoes from another country, no matter what their size chart says, they are not true to American sizes. I've always worn a 5 1/2M in American sizes. I bought a half size larger in these, thinking they wouldn't be too tight with socks on. I've never worn a wide shoe in my life, but if I'd bought a 5 1/2 wide, I'm thinking that would have been perfect for me. So, be aware, if you buy shoes online, you might consider buying a wide width if you normally wear a medium. Bumping up the size didn't really help me because it just made the shoe too long & the width was still the same. So, I've learned a hard lesson about buying shoes online. These shoes (as well as the other 2 pr. I bought online) run small (more in the width than length). You might consider going up to a wide width if you want them to be comfortable walking shoes.

review_headline: Lightweight, comfortable water sandal - I wouldn't change a thing
review_body:
I went through 2 other water sandals before I found a pair that made the cut. I was looking for a sandal that could perform well on a trail and in the water.

Pros:
- Dries very quickly
- Easy to put on. There's only one part to tighten: the elastic cord on top.
- Lightweight and sleek looking for a water sandal
- Excellent traction. I've worn it on slimy river rocks and am very pleased.
- Rubber toe helps prevent toe stubbing. Very comfortable.

Comparison to the Teva Omnium water sandal, which I purchased before this sandal.
The Teva sandal is much stiffer and has an awkward upward curve to it at the front. The heel strap is very harsh. It also doesn't look as nice as the KEEN sandal. If anyone is debating between these two sandals, the obvious winner is the Clearwater by KEEN. In fact, I don't understand why Teva didn't opt for a heel strap like the one on the Clearwater. The Teva has too many useless straps and also looks and feels "clunkier."

Which surprised me, since I have several other pairs of New Balance shoes and they are not nearly as snug as these. These feel at least a half size smaller than my other 2 pairs of New Balance shoes.

However I do still wear these, even with them being snug. They are too cute not to. They are light weight and easy to walk in. The mesh is extremely breathable, so it keeps feet cool on hot days or when active.

I have these in the dark grey/purple color and they look just the same in person as in the photos. They are a dark grey color with a sort of periwinkle contrast and a few hot pink accents. These are great walking shoes and perfect for warmer temperatures. However you may want to go a half size up from your normal size for a more conferrable fit.

product_title: Pearl iZUMi Men's E:Motion Road N 2 Running Shoe
review_body:
I Got these shoes blind.
I ordered the EM Trail N2s as a resupply pair for a road hike I was on, from Bend Oregon to Klamath Falls Oregon.
I didnt get N2 Trails - I got N2 Roads.

The N2 Trail Shoes were Hands Down THE BEST SHOES I have ever owned. I payed $130 for mine at Footzone.
THESE ROAD N2s ARE THE SECOND BEST SHOES I HAVE EVER OWNED!
I payed $76 for them on Amazon.com, sold to me 3rd party. Hence the Confusion.

Uhhh, I never owned a car. I never owned a bike. I Walk a Ton.
Some people might say \\"Psshh get WALKING shoes!\\" - Find some Walkers as lightweight as running shoes. Runners feel better on my feet anyway, and whats more- I can run in them too.
I tell people sometimes of the recent walks I made that day and they bring up the military, am I a vet? Am I Gonna Join? No And No. I just Walk like a Soldier. Two 4 month hikes on the PCT (Sauconys) - A 2013 500+ Hike California to Oregon (Rocky S2V Combat Boots), 3+ everyday for a year around town and in the woods(Pearl Izumi N2 Trails), and back 100 miles (the same Rocky S2V Combat Boots)... now 10-20mi days easy in the Bay looking for work (Pearl Izumi N2 Roads)...
I have walked at least 5 miles everyday for the last year alone and Im 28 now. I recently did 3 30mi days in the east bay metropolitan area- IN THESE SHOES- on Sidewalk and pavement.
If amazon still allows pics I will post them.

\\"N2 ROAD SHOES\\"
These have low weight, always awesome breathability, and I believe the same no seam construction that allows to be worn easier in bare feet.
The tread? Not really there at all
These are Definitely Road Shoes.
I have a bit of trouble on Dirt Trails - WALKING - so these are Road Shoes for sure.
I have light Pronation- a healthy amount from what I can tell - I dont risk injury and I dont suffer in my trekking. These soles were a little narrow- I had to catch myself before I rolled my ankle a couple times- you maynot have this problem- I offer as an observation from the Trail N2s...

Soles are tough. And though I believe these are Five Star Shoes- I believe that for me the Trail N2s are better for walking on pavement.
However, Trail N2s are more expensive in my experience. The N2 Trails arent made for pavement- I understand - but after 30mi on pavement in Road N2s I can Say I feel it more in my feet than with Trail N2s. Bones. Flesh.
Again thats just My observation. Im 180lbs 5'11 with a 25-45lb 3 Day Pack everywhere I go - So I will be heavier than a Great many of you Runners out there.

The Soles are TOUGH! - not walk on broken bottles tough - but they Last a Long Time!
Thinnish- Ive been expecting to burn through any day but they are hanging in there!
Construction is True. No delamination or peeling of the details- ive dragged these over some curbs too! Soft interior foam doesnt shred, sharp toenails could perf the toe capsule on the top but otherwise - Light and Strong Construction.

I try looking for shoes sold by amazon now - as to avoid seeing and buying something that isnt the same as what is shipped- but Pearl Izumi named all their products almost the same thing- and I like these shoes so... its all good.
If I bought shoes and got these- for the price- I would be happy.
Hope this helps you decide that these shoes are SIIIIIIICK and you are gonna walk to work now everyday in them.
500 miles is not an exaggeration in these shoes- though not very much more...

product_title: Baggallini A La Carte Travel Tote
review_body:
I was looking for a versatile bag to use as my personal carry on for an extended European vacation. I had seen this in use by a woman on a flight earlier in the year and I liked the look. The design of the bag is good. Lightweight, good pocket placement and fashionable. However, I should have paid attention to the negative reports about the straps. I used the bag on 2 short trips before the vacation. In packing for the trip, I noticed that the straps were breaking at the place where they attach to the ring. I had to 'fix' with black electrical tape. After 6 flight legs, the handles are cracked in numerous places. I am not a person to stuff my bag so the straps were not subject to heavy loads.

I have other Baggallini products and have been very happy with those. They all work together nicely as a travel system. I am very disappointed in this bag. The straps are a design flaw. A bag at a fraction of the cost would have served me as well.

A side note: After I received the bag and before the vacation, I purchased one as a graduation gift. I am disappointed in knowing that this gift will not hold up well for my niece.

product_title: KEEN Men's Newport H2 Sandal
review_headline: Comfie Sandals, Healed my Metatarsalgia, ... but Schweddy Feet!
review_body:
I bought this sandal after wearing Birkenstocks for the past 15 years. Recently I was wearing my Milano Birks, which were getting old and developed a crack on the insole. I was running after my daughter at the playground and then the next day developed soreness over the balls of my feet (believe I had "metatarsalgia"). This may have been from the crack hitting my foot, but Birks do have highly firm insoles. This soreness went on for 6 week until I bought my Keens. After wearing for one week, my foot pain is almost gone! Take home points:

(1) Very Comfortable - Insoles combined with "sneaker" like out-sole gives a nice cushion to your foot, but not too squishy. The insole is like a Birk - designed to conform to the the average foot. I like the good arch support. I never thought I would find a sandal more comfortable than my Birks, but I would say that is true. Birks have firm, hard soles and this has just the right amount of give.

(2) My feet are so hot, sweaty wearing these! As the picture implies, you are trading functionality for foot breath-ability. I love the patented toe protection from the hard rubber and the straps/soles really support your foot 360 degrees. But to do this, there are few areas of skin showing. Granted, I have narrow feet and probably wear my sandals a little snug. I also am living in 90-degree humid weather, but my feet remain warm inside where it is air-conditioned. (This sandals will probably be perfect in cooler climates or in the Spring/Fall). It's not an unbearable warm feet sensation, but sometimes feels like my feet have been in sneakers all day. I am thinking about finding a pair of flip-flops with good support to give my feet a "breather".

(3) SMALL SIZING --- ASK YOURSELF WHAT SIZE YOU USUALLY WEAR, THEN BUY THE NEXT SIZE UP --- TRUST ME ON THIS. I agree with the other reviewers that the sandals are made a little small. I sometimes take a mens size 12 and sometimes a 13. So I was debating on which one. Then I noticed that a lot of my shoes I had been buying the last few years were mostly size 12 (casual shoes; my Birks are size 46; only my sneakers are usually size 13). So I first bought the size 12 Keens. It was immediately clear they were small - feel and appearance. I returned them and bought the size 13 which fits fine. So my advice is that even if you are certain every shoe or sandal you have ever bought is size "X", trust me and order size "X+1/2" or "X+1". At my size, there was no size 12 1/2.

(4) FYI -- Bungee "laces" - It wasn't apparent from the description or reviews how to tighten the sandal until it arrived. There is an elastic cord that loops through each eyelet. To fasten the sandal, one pulls the end of the bungee cord and slides the tightening clasp down until the shoe is comfortable. Then you have to tuck the plastic end of the bungee cord until one the lace crossings - this can be a little difficult if you like your sandals tighter.

product_title: Flogg Women's Cassie Ankle-Strap Sandal
review_body: I bought these for running around the city in areas where the ground wasn't smooth enough for thin high heels or stilettos. The footbed is foam from front to back - which should make them super springy and comfortable. And they are, that is, they are when you walk around your house imagining how great they are going to feel tomorrow.  However, in the real world, the shoe feels somewhat off balance, or maybe it's just the disconnect between the foam cushion which changes how you feel your steps. Perhaps this is a matter of getting used to the shoe. I wear 6 inch heels normally and these feel super tall and precarious for some reason.  The biggest issue was the front toe strap. To say it was narrow wouldn't be descriptive enough. I have normal feet and after a half hour of walking in these shoes, I literally couldn't walk anymore. The leather was cutting into my skin terribly. I don't think this is a matter of "breaking in" pains. I had to bring it to a shoe repair place and have them put extra holes in the strap to accommodate my foot. It would be so much better if they had some sort of elastic built into that strap to begin with. It's surprising that a company who seems to consider comfort a priority would not make a better strap design.  As far as overall fit, I wear a 7 normally and had to get a 6.5 in these to fit lengthwise.  On the positive side, they are really cute. I haven't worn them much since fixing them, I guess I have memories of the pain and it's made me avoid them. I think once I break them in more and get used to the feeling, I'll probably love them. I haven't met many high heels that I don't.   ----Update ---- June 2015  These are now my go to sandals when I need to run errands. They really do get super comfortable as you wear them!

product_title: Allen Edmonds Men's Strand Cap-Toe Oxford
review_body:
I was very excited to order a pair of Walnut Strands on sale from Amazon. Unfortunately, the pair of shoes that I received fell far short of my expectations for a few reasons:
1. Right out of the box, one shoe already outside of the shoe bag, and had a 1" or so scratch on the side.
2. The detail of the cap-toe on the left shoe was poorly done. It's as if it was fed through crooked.
3. The stitching of the sole on the right shoe is crooked. The leather sole has a channel that the stitching should follow, but there is a 1" section of this stitching that completely misses the channel. If I continue wearing this pair of shoes, I'm worried that this stitching will quickly wear out as it is directly contacting the ground.

I am still deciding whether I should keep this pair, try to exchange it for another pair, or just return it and just write off Allen Edmonds due to this quality control failure.

review_headline: Very comfortable shoe for the money!
review_body:
I received this shoe a few days ago. Here's a little back story. I came from 2 pairs of UA shoes, that were comfortable, but I could not be in them for extended periods of time, as my shins started to hurt. (So I went to a Dr Scholls foot mapping center, and got arch supports for them) I was excited for them to wear out, as I hate to waste money on shoes that still have life in them. I had tried these on at Famous Footwear back before getting the UA shoes (and would have gotten these then if I could have found a size 9). These shoes were comfortable out of the box, and I have no problem working in them. The first night I had them, I broke them in (bad choice but not a bad experience) at the gym, with an hour on an elliptical. Be sure of your shoe size, as I range from an 8.5 - 9.5 depending on brand. They are a little awkward t walk in at first because of the tubes, but very rewarding, and as with all shoes you get used to the way they walk. I have found that with most shoes I have to use the spare eyelets at the ankle to keep the shoe from feeling loose and sloppy from the start, these do not require me to do this (Yet?!?!?)

Overall this is a great value for around 45 Dollars with Prime

review_headline: Nice LEATHER boots. Not plastic or pleather.
review_body:
Stop the madness people.
They are just regular leather boots. They don't feel or look like "pleather" or vinyl or aluminum.
They do not make your feet sweat. They will not cause unsightly warts or decrease your stamina.
They are not the greatest quality leather - because you get what you pay for. They are a little stiff and they don't seem like they will break in as nicely as a pair of Frye boots. But they cost half as much. So there is that.

They do have quite a heel - like a Beatle boot. So you will feel taller - as long as you don't trip over them.
Since your heels are elevated - your feet are are on a slope. sliding down into the toebox.
I ordered 1 full size small and they were tight - especially on the sides of the feet at the widest point - where your toes start.
I put some shoe trees in them, wore them a couple days later and they are mostly fine.
Not like slippers - but not a whole lot of discomfort - especially considering the style points you get for wearing them.

I would advise buying them, putting some of that leather stretch fluid in them and then wear them for a couple hours.
Just like any boots.
Then strap on your guitar and head on stage.

product_title: Goodyear Neolite Rubber Heels, Mens Shoe Repair Top Lifts- 1/4" Thick 1pair
review_headline: Made the heels of my boots much quieter!!
review_body:
I got these to quiet the clunking noise from my boots with tapered hallow plastic heels. They worked like a charm! I'm no longer self-conscious from the noise of every step. These were a little hard to cut to size. After tracing them to fit my heels, I cut them with a scroll saw which worked well. A utility knife would probably work, but take much longer. I attached them with Shoe Goo and found you don't need much. I read that some people clamped them on to dry. I had trouble with them sliding, so I used small nails from a set of hard cheap heel plates that I had tried and removed, as they didn't help. I bet tight rubber bands would have worked well too.

At first, I took my boots to 2 shoe repair shops to see if they had anything that could quiet my heels. They said they're cheap hallow plastic and nothing would work, or hold. Well, they were wrong and I did it myself!

But they definitely let your feet breathe when it's hot outside, which it is most of the time here. These shoes provided great stability and are very comfortable. I opted for the B width but probably should have stuck with the D's. The sides of my feet get a little sore after wearing them for a long time, but hopefully they will stretch over time. Another great shoe from NB!

product_title: Alegria Women's Etta Lace-Up
review_headline: Not my favorite Alegria shoe, not recommended for narrow feet
review_body: UPDATE:  Though I bought these shoes in May, I haven't had much opportunity to wear them, have worn them on 2 work trips, for a total of 9 days.  Not only are these shoes very uncomfortable, the bottom of the right heel fell off, not sure when or where.  I used inserts to give more arch support and to take up some of the extra space because the shoes were too loose (need 41 for length).  The heels were slipping when walking, so put in some rubber heel grips.  No matter what I tried, the shoes were uncomfortable and too loose.  Now that I've had them for a few months, even though I've only worn them a total of 9 days, I can't return them even though they've started to fall apart.  WOULD NOT recommend these shoes.     Ordered these because I wanted a dressier shoe for office work that had a bit of height and the comfort that I love with Alegria.  I have the Ella mary jane type pump with the same footbed and platform, so figured the fit should be similar.  However, with a narrowish foot, wasn't sure whether I'd be able to tie the laces tight enough as Alegria styles tend to run wide.  The leather is very, very stiff and somewhat hard to tie, difficult to open up the laces very much.  Didn't really need to as they are roomy and do run a bit big overall.  For length I'm a solid size 10 and the 41 fit well in length.  The heel was loose and the shoes slipped when walking, so had to put some rubber heel grips in them.  When tying them, the two sides meet together, can't get them any tighter, and they are still a bit loose on me, even with a sock, not a nylon.  Tried putting some ball of foot pads on the footbed to take up some room but need to try repositioning them, still not comfortable.  I don't like to have to do that much padding and modification to $100 shoes to make them comfortable, and the 2 other pairs of Alegrias haven't needed anything, just comfort right out of the box.  Wouldn't purchase again, but will get more Alegria styles in the future.

review_body: I just developed plantar fasciitis and after anytime sitting, standing up and walking was extremely painful. My sister had had the same condition and had run into these shoes and found that they helped manage her pain. The doctor said that the cute little flats that I was wearing this summer were only aggravating the situation. I was still a little skeptical but ordered a pair anyway. Well, I ended up with 4 pair. The arch support and padded insole gave my foot exactly the help it needed. I wear them at all times and rotate between the four pair. Our planned trip to Disney World was worrying me but with these I think I'll make it. They took great and they feel great. The only thing I would mention, and others have mentioned it too, is that the strap could have been made a little shorter so that the narrow foot would have a little more grip on the velcro. My strap doesn't touch the floor as some have said. There is about 1/2 an inch short of the floor, nothing that would offset it's positives. I normally wear a 7 but I got the 6 in these and they fit nicely. I've had them wet and they rebound with no problem nor color runoff ,though I can't speak about the darker shades. I got the gray, orange, beige and natural (Ziggy). The Rasta is supposed to come in a shade called "natural" which is an off white color but I couldn't find them anywhere. I did find, though, that Reggae-Ziggy looked just the same as the Reggae-Rasta and did come in that color so that's what I got. I found no difference between the two styles. Even if you have no problem with your feet these might be just what you need to keep it that way and look darling at the same time.

product_title: Vasque Men's Lotic Performance Water Shoe
review_headline: Terrible water shoe with a nice sole. Multi-layer fabric dries slowly and traps sand against your feet.
review_body:
Took these shoes hiking, kayaking, and white water rafting.

Pros: The grip on wet rocks is phenomenal. When dry, the shoe is comfortable enough to wear, in a low-drop minimalist sort of way.

Cons: The shoe upper is constructed of 3-4 layers of fabric, that holds moisture and traps sand. Key wear points on the fabric are coated with a thin rubber film that eliminates any way for embedded sand to exit the mesh. Once sand gets trapped in the fabric, it is very difficult to get out. After a brief walk on a sandy river bottom, the shoe quickly becomes painfully abrasive against bare feet. No amount of rinsing in river water will get the sand out. After you get out of the water, the shoes take several days to dry.

product_title: Teva Women's Tirra Athletic Sandal
review_body:
I absolutely love these shoes! Although I am fairly young, I have been having problems with my joints for several years. I can't wear most shoes because by the end of the day I am in so much pain because of the lack of support in most shoes. I started wearing the teva mushii flip flops a few years ago and found that those are nice when you just get them, but as you continue to wear them they become less and less comfortable. I bought these shoes about a month or two ago and absolutely fell in love.

These shoes mold to every curve of your food, which makes them really comfortable but also incredibly supportive. I also like that the straps by the ankle and feet are adjustable. In the summer, my feet tend to swell, especially when I walk a lot, the adjustable straps make it so that I can tighten them or loosen them depending on how swollen my feet are that day. I also really like the look of these shoes. I bought them in black, and I found that I can wear them with nearly anything. I wear them with yoga pants, jeans, and even some of my summer dresses. Buying them on Amazon is also a plus because you can often find them for cheaper than they are in stores. (Don't quote me, but I believe they run about $80.00 in store + tax)

The only thing that I don't like about these shoes is the fact that when you put them on, if you have any crumbs, dirt, or anything on your feet it hurts to put them on. This isn't a huge issue though; I just wipe off my feet before I put on these shoes.

Overall, I think that these shoes are really great. A little bit more expensive than I was hoping to spend on shoes, but worth the money. I can wear these shoes all day and I don't have a single problem. They are incredibly comfortable, but you don't have to compromise on style. I would recommend these shoes to anyone that is looking for a shoe that not only supports your foot but also looks good while doing it.

product_title: Vivobarefoot Women's 200040 Slingback Sandal
review_body:
Since I got these shoes I have been wearing them around trying to like them... but so far I can't. I have almost nothing good to say about them, though I haven't given up completely.

First, sizing. Amazon sent me the wrong size... although it ended up being possibly the right size after all. I wear an 8-8.5 in merrell barefoots and a 7.5 in most standard casual shoes, so I ordered a 39 (thinking better to have these a little big than a little small). I own vivobarefoot hikers in size 39, and they fit alright apart from the toebox not being wide enough. So, basically the 39 sounded like the right size. I ordered 39s. They sent me 38s.

The sole length on the 38 is actually alright, but the toe thong and heel straps are rather tight front to back. I think they may stretch out a bit with wear, but honestly I may not get that far given the other issues with the shoe. The width is quite wide in both the heel and the toe, and my feet slide around despite multiple strap adjustments. I do have slightly narrow heels, but I prefer a wide toe box for natural toe splay in minimalist shoes. This shoe has width in excess in the heel and toe for me, especially considering that I'm tight for length. I have to wonder if this is really a women's shoe, since this kind of length to width ratio is typical of a scaled down men's shoe.

Going back to the width, there's at least 3/4\\" of extra empty space between the side of my foot and the side strap anchor points. The midsole of the shoe is actually quite narrow, but the medial anchor strap comes out from the sole horizontally for quite a distance before rising up to act as a strap, so there's no fit benefit whatsoever from the narrower midsole. The surface of the shoe is slippery regardless of whether my feet are sweaty or dry, so I'm constantly sliding from one side to the other with that 3/4\\" gap. Further, the heel straps are not high enough to stay on top of my heel bone in the back (despite being quite tight), so they slide down over time.

These sandals are also much heavier than what I expect from a minimalist shoe. The sole, while fairly thin and not padded/cushiony, is very heavy, dense, and rigid with minimal ground feel. If I point or flex my feet, the elastic portions of the straps stretch while the sole stays put doing nothing. It doesn't conform to my feet at all. While walking, they do flex more than a backless flip flop, but I think you'd get equal or better flexibility by just adding a heel strap to standard flops.

I got these in teal. Color wise, the sole is light like the picture shows, the plastic-ish portions of the strap are a darker turquoise, and the fabric parts of the strap are a duller, grayish browner version of the rest of the straps. They are more technical-looking than dollar store flip flops. I think they have a bit of an \\"outdoor adventure\\" vibe. The extra width is not that noticeable from a visual standpoint, so they aren't unflattering.

Since I've been wearing these around outside, I can no longer return them. I may try pinching the sides in vise grips for a while to see if I can make the fit narrower (particularly the medial strap since it emerges where the sole is narrow). I think narrowing the sides will also raise the heel strap a bit. If the soles curve up a bit too, that may further reduce my side-to-side sliding problem. Or, since I'm in early pregnancy right now, they might fit better later on if my feet swell? Haha, who knows. Probably nothing will make the soles into the flexible, foot-conforming minimalist footwear I was seeking, but maaaybe I can make them wearable.

review_headline: Takes getting used to but no more headaches
review_body:
I get headaches from the "arm" pressure of most sunglasses. I was looking for armless sunglasses of some sort for protection and comfort., without the headaches.I remember seeing a strap type of sunglasses but could not find them and found these instead. The fit is a little funny depending on your hat and head but after getting used to it, I would say it is a near perfect system if you don not mind wearing a cap. The blue tinting makes these a bit less than perfect for me because of the way the tint affects colors, I would prefer these in a dark yelllow/amber color.

Pros:
-No pressure from arms means no headaches for me
-wrap around design offers good coverage once you get them adjusted to the right angle and hat position.
-changing hats is pretty easy
-ratcheting flip-up joints makes it convenient to "take off" your sunglasses while still leaving them attached

Cons:
-More tint color choices would be nice, I will try they more neutral tint next time.
-An optional nose piece might make snugly adjusted fit more comfortable, if you adjust them close, the nose can make contact with the hard edge of the lens, making it more desirable to move the lens away, but this lets more light in from the sides.

review_headline: A horrible update on a classic boot
review_body: I bought my first pair of Brasher Supalite II boots in the early 2000s and have loved them ever since. The new version of these boots is nothing like the old: the leather is significantly stiffer and the heel rougher. After two years of experimentation with various sock and insole combinations I am relegating these boots to expensive junk. Without exception they have given me blisters on my heels after < 1 mile hiking under any conditions. They ruined my recent backpacking trip in the Adirondacks, where I ended up hiking in sandals where possible(!). review_body:

It fits OK, but it kinda hurts your foot at that part with the metal accessory thingy on the top. I thought it might loosen up with time, but after wearing it for more than 6 months now, it hasn't loosened up at all, and it stills hurts my foot if I wear it for an extended period of time.

This is kinda sad because the shoes actually look very nice, and I always get complimented on them whenever I convince myself to wear them. However, my fear of the pain makes that decision rather rare.

I would only recommend these shoes if you won't be wearing them the whole day, or if you have unnaturally tiny feet.

product_title: Rockport Women's Juliet Pump
review_headline: I tried three different sizes and it still didn't work.
review_body:
I was really hoping for this shoe to work out for me. My coworker warned me that this shoe can slip in the back and the toe box will be tight at first, but if you wear it out for a bit the leather will stretch and it will fit a lot better. I'm on my feet 8 hours a day at work, I do not have the time or the endurance for pain to stretch out a pair of shoes that might or might not fit.

I bought three sizes, 6.5, 7 and 7.5 hoping one of them will fit. Size 6.5 was too small altogether, I couldn't even fit my foot into the shoe. I was able to put my foot through size 7 but the toe box was REALLY tight and was hurting my feet. So I figured a 7.5 should do the trick. The toe box fits PERFECTLY, but as I tried to walk in them, it was very clear that it was a 7.5. There was too much space in the heel for it to cling onto anything.

While I wanted these shoes to work out for me so badly, they clearly aren't made for women with normal or wide feet.

product_title: adidas Men's Adipure Motion Golf Shoe
review_body: I have bought a couple of different (non-golfing) shoes online in the past, and until now have been very disappointed in the outcome.. These shoes, however, have given me hope!  I'll be honest, I had found a pair of FootJoy's that I really liked and intended on purchasing, but nowhere around carried the men's 11 in wide.. So I came home with the intention of buying those same shoes online when I came across these and was caught by their look.  Then I looked up their reviews and they were overwhelmingly positive, so I found a seller on Amazon selling them at a reasonable price in 11 wide and I jumped.. Have never made a better purchase!  They arrived earlier today and I skeptically tried them on right away.. and... they fit perfect!  So I took them out to the course and tried them with a few swings and... they're perfect!!  Never been happier with a pair of purpose built shoes!  I imagine this is what it is like to have an 1800's style custom shoe maker build something specifically for your feet.. I've owned, and been satisfied with golf shoes from both FootJoy and Callaway.. and if I'd never tried these on I would give good reviews to them too.. but, having worn these.. .. I don't know how to say it other than they blow anything else I've tried out of the water! I have bunions - hence wide feet - and these shoes fit me perfectly... I highly recommend!  Thank you Adidas for taking the time and putting in the effort to make such a well designed/built shoe.

product_title: Durango Men's TR820 Boot
review_body:
First of all, it was midday on a Thursday when I discovered my old boots were falling apart. That night I went online and ordered these boots with free 2 day shipping via Amazon Prime. I had just finished my lunch the following Saturday when they arrived at my door. I tried them on and they fit perfectly.
New boots are a blessing and a curse in most instances. Even when they are properly fitted, they take a bit of wearing in to feel comfortable. These boots fit snugly with very little pinching or discomfort when first worn.
I do have one complaint though, even though I am sure this will work itself out eventually. The top edge of the right boot, which works the foot brake on my motorcycle, digs in and has left an unsightly purplish bruise on my ankle. No worries, I am not planning on entering a pretty legs contest anytime soon, and it doesn't really hurt all that much when I am not riding, but I would think if they added just a smidge of padding around the rim of the boots. It would have spared me this minor complaint.
I am very happy with my purchase, the ease of ordering and the prompt delivery.

product_title: adidas Men's Adizero Tour Golf Shoe
review_body:
first of all lets get the good out of the way. people say the shoe is narrow, but it's adidas and i actually found mine to fit pretty normal. it feels tight at first and by the time you're on the second hole you have to tighten it up a little. very comfortable and definitely waterproof. i was in some deepish water during an early round and my feet stayed bone dry. they are also very good looking as a matter of personal preference. they are also very light.

here is the bad: they have a different spike lock on the bottom of the shoe than footjoy or nike. you insert the spike and then half twist it. that means you are buying adidas replacements. it also means if you are a big guy (the guy i spoke to about the warranty told me 200+) they will not stay in for very long. after 3 rounds and 2 or 3 range visits the spikes on the outside of my left shoe (where you put pressure when you finish your swing) will come out during my swing. put them back and they will come out again. the bracket itself looks like it may have taken some damage. i was told by the guy servicing my warranty (not taylormade/adidas, but my store rep) that this is a common problem and he's seen many returns and the re-return when they send them a replacement for the same problem.

take it for what it's worth, but if you are a bigger guy you might want to look elsewhere for a shoe. i don't want to go too low on the rating because they're good shoes, just not for me.

EDIT* Adidas has replaced the shoe with the newer model. The spike pattern is different, but i'll put my comments on that shoe's page. It's called the adizero one. I am glad adidas remedied the situation.

review_body: So I have been cycling a lot lately, training for the B2VT ride. I started experiencing hip pain in my right side the more I trained. Looking down it was obvious that my knee was going inwards with every pedal stroke, which was messing with my hip alignment. I went to the Local Bike Shop and they wanted to give me the delux fit for $350...I said I'd think about it. A friend recommended I try some insoles before dropping that much cash. I gave it a go. $45 vs. $350, why not? I got the insoles and followed the directions on how to shape them to your feet. Very easy, took 5 minutes total. As soon as I slipped them on I noticed a huge difference in my cycling. The arch support it provided was phenomenal. My leg still tracks a little inward but not as bad as before. I no longer have any hip pain late in my rides, and I go for 70+ miles now. If you have high arches, I highly recommend this product.
