product_title: Timberland Men's Earthkeepers 6" Lace-Up Boot
review_headline: A few nitpicks keep this from being 4 or 5 stars...
review_body:
Ok, so first the good:

They look great.

They seem sturdy enough for my intended use. That is to say, daily wear and "casual" hiking. I have my doubts that they would hold up under very rugged conditions, but then again, I didn't buy them for any sort of aggressive hiking conditions. I'll wear my Merrells for that.

The leather is surprisingly soft right out of the box. This was nice as the boots required almost no breaking in time, unlike almost all other leather boots I've bought. Within a few days of purchase, I wound up wearing them at an all day photo shoot. They were comfortable all day long and, most importantly, by the time I got home, my feet were not screaming at me.

Now the nitpicks:

Prior to purchase, I read a number of reviews complaining about the sizing. I'm glad I did. Based on what others said, I ordered a half-size smaller than normal (I went with a size 10, instead of my usual 10.5). Even then, the boots feel just a tad on the large size -- not enough to justify going down a half a size again, but just a touch more roomy in the toes than I'd like. If I were going to do any sort of aggressive hiking in these, I don't feel like I'd have a good feel for the trail due to the extra "play" in the toe area.

The second nitpick is that there appears to be a defect with the sole on the left side. The toe "squishes" when I step, as though air is rushing out. It did this right out of the box, so I know it was nothing I did to the boot. Like the sizing issue, it's not enough of a problem to justify a return, but it's a disappointing lapse in quality. If the soles wear out as quickly as some other reviews suggest, this problem will take care of itself when I have theme resoled. But this shouldn't be an issue with brand new shoes to begin with.

review_headline: Review for Unique Soles AWFUL customer service
review_body:
This review is more for the AWFUL customer service of Unique Soles than the shoe I bought from them, which was the Itasca Harbor Lite Mens Black Slip On Bungee Trail Athletic Sandals, a moderately decent shoe that I give 3.5 stars.

I bought these shoes as a gift, with little time to spare.

After my credit card was charged, the confirmation email the company sent me was for a different shoe than I had ordered. I immediately emailed the company asking for an explanation. When the response came, it was a non-response, listing only their policy of keeping copies of correspondence between customers and the company. It did not address my question at all, and there was no signature, no customer service contact.

I then contacted Amazon customer support and was told I should file a complaint specifically about the non-response, that companies will sometimes do this, send an empty email just so they can say they responded. So I did that and also complained that Unique Soles sent me a confirmation on shoes I did not order.

The short version of the story is that I emailed the company repeatedly about the discrepancy between what I had ordered and what they said they were sending me. The best I got was a couple of one-line responses (after I’d let them know I’d filed a complaint with Amazon) saying “We sent you the right shoes.” The “right shoes” were never listed in any email I received from the company, nor were the “right shoes” ever listed in my Open Orders on Amazon.

Eventually I received a phone call from someone from the company who never identified herself by name or position, repeated that I had been sent the right shoes but could not tell me what those shoes were, and raised her voice to talk all over me. She did offer me a refund for my trouble, which I said yes, I would like. Especially since I had had to buy a second gift for my friend, since I had no confidence that when the shoes actually arrived they would be the correct ones.

No refund was ever posted to my account.

The shoes came, which I no longer needed. They were in fact the correct ones, and it’s a shame that Unique Soles’ customer service was so bad that even though it’s a decent shoe my experience just trying to get a simple confirmation that it was the right shoe ruined the experience. No way would I trust this company to order from them again.

product_title: Kidzuu Soft Sole Baby Infant Leather Crib Shoes Purple 3 White Flowers
review_body:
OK...here is the skinny on these cute little shoes that most people want to read.
-Are they Cute? YES
-How is the quality? Decent quality leather for what they are to be used for---crib and crawling. The vamp is cotton lined.
Suede sole. Some soles are thinner than others. I recommend wearing socks for the first few wears until the
get acclimated to the suede feel of the sole. The colors are vibrant and well saturated (not dull).
-Sizing? The sizing is true. A 0-6 is for that age range unless you have a large baby. Same for 6-12, etc...
You can't measure the sole and then measure your child's foot exactly. You need toe room and most of all you must remember they
are slip-ons and have an elastic stretch entry. If you measure exact sole to foot it will most often be tight at the ankles
because you are not allowing the elastic to give for the foot to slide in. If your child is 5/6 months size up and leave toe
room. HOWEVER...every now and again you may get a pair that are a bit misshapen and may throw the sizing off.
Price? Good pricing for the quality.
Other tips -- Because these shoes are genuine leather, take a damp cloth and wipe the interior sole off. Some soles have a little
grit in them from the manufacturing process (particularly the white and light colored soles).

Please remember these are just recommendations based upon my experience.

product_title: Onitsuka Tiger Tiger Corsair Le Fashion Sneaker
review_body:
My appreciation for this company goes back to 1972. I got into Tigers for several years, then they vanished from the shelves. The best shoe they made was a killer cross-trainer similar to this model with a thicker sole. Now, as far as I can tell, Tiger's resurrected the folio to appeal to retro-shoppers seeking shoes with some sort of underground legacy.

I make this claim because, so far, I haven't seen the above referenced serious cross-trainer. I only see the shoes made with the least support, what I heard sporting goods retailers refer to, 40-years ago, as "flat-track shoes". So is this brand about appealing to a retro-market or is Tiger serious about beefing up their scope of products?

Anyway, I use these shoes today as an all-round, everyday shoe. I don't train in them. Just walking, etc. Mainly because there's no support - they're stripped down, and that's cool if you want super light. Which they are.

The quality's still the same as I remember. And, having worn my first pair (since Tiger re-launched) for a year now, they're holding up very well.

The pride and attention to detail introduced by Kihachiro Onitsuka remains intact. And judging by how few I see of these being worn, rest assured; these shoes are an underground secret.

product_title: Kenneth Cole REACTION Women's Full Of Life Oxford
review_headline: Kenneth Cole Reaction Full of Life Oxford - Black & Burgundy 9.5M
review_body:
At the time of my purchase, Amazon has the same shoe in different colours listed on separate pages. Just an FYI if you are having trouble finding your size or a colour you like. I ordered both the black patent and the full leather burgundy pairs. I ordered a half size larger than normal in both. The full leather burgundy pair fits a bit snugger and is stiffer than the black patent pair, which is softer and more flexible. The burgundy pair looks more expensive and both seem to go great with suits for my office job.

Both pairs are stunning. The black pair is more subtle and tough to see the detail. The burgundy colour of the toe part is a bit brownish, not LOOK-AT-ME-RED, which I really like. The croc textured part is more berry-burgundy than brown and my favorite part! The insoles of these are surprisingly comfortable. The heel height is perfect. If you are thinking about buying a pair of these, I would highly recommend that you do.

A couple notes of warning. First, the laces on both pairs are really stiff. They are Extremely Difficult to loosen and tighten. It takes me a good minute or two to get these on and off. However, once on they stay put because of those laces, so no blisters or flopping around so far. I worry that the softer black patent pair will not last as long as the burgundy ones, which look and feel like a higher quality sturdier material around the laces though are slightly less comfortable because of it. That being said, I will probably be more likely to get crease marks over time on that burgundy pair. Perhaps everyone should try two pairs. There's a lot of variance in this wonderful design. Good luck.

product_title: Shoe Horn Pro Comfort - Extra Long Handled Telescopic, Personally Adjustable 16" to 31”, Extendable & Collapsible, Stainless Steel (Black)
review_body:
This looks like a wonderful shoe horn. I loved that it extended. I loved the narrower and longer horn. BUT, the very flexible 1 3/4" heavy-duty spring that connects the horn to the extendable handle makes it almost impossible to use it.

It is like trying to use a broken stick as a shoe horn. (The "broken" part being the bendable spring.) What were the designers thinking? And the five and four star reviews--did those reviewers actually try to use the shoe horn without bending down? Obviously not!

A shoehorn needs a fulcrum and torque to work. You have to be able to put pressure at the top of the horn to help angle your heel into your shoe. With the handle being able to flex because of the spring, you can't exert any pressure on the horn, UNLESS you hold it down below the spring. That makes the nice long handle worthless. You still have to bend down to your heel. (The handle extends ABOVE the spring.)

Not only that, the spring allows the horn to revolve 360 degrees. There is absolutely no way to keep the horn at the back of your heel unless you are holding onto the horn below the spring.

*I received a sample product from Living Concept.

product_title: 5.11 Tactical A.T.A.C. 8" Storm Boot
review_headline: Great quality boots live up to my expectations.
review_body:
I see a lot of size complaints on here. As always, when shopping for boots, one should consider getting a full size lower than their normal shoe size to get a proper fit ( example, I am 10.5 so I purchased 9.5; and don't exaggerate your foot size either, guys!). They fit snug and comfortably, although a tiny bit tight at first; but they do stretch to conform to your foots size. They are well suited to step into puddles whether it be water or blood. Nothing's going to get in. However, as applies to all waterproof products, they limit breathability. These boots will perform a fantastic job at keeping your feet warm in cold environments, but if you plan to work in a hot, arid atmosphere, I suggest looking for something more breathable. The zipper feature is a true blessing. I'm personally lazy about untying and tying up laces, and I am very satisfied with the ability to essentially slide my boots on and off at a moments notice.
Summary:
Pros - Snug fit, warm, high quality material, waterproof, zip up feature, side key/knife pockets,
Cons - not suited for extremely hot environments
All in all, it's a good product and you won't regret it unless it has a defect.

product_title: Brooks Men's Adrenaline GTS 13 Running Shoes
review_headline: Two pairs of shoes tore after a few months of usage each
review_body:
I bought my first Brooks running shoes in 2010 and have been buying them regularly since. However, the last two shoes I got have been very disappointing. I bought a Brooks Addiction in July 13 and it started developing a tear in the fabric over the pinky. I got the Brooks Adrenaline (the shoe featured here) in Jan 14 and started using it heavily only in late Feb and this one has also torn over my right pinky. In addition, the heel of the left shoe is coming apart. I run 10-15 miles per week on road and trails - so not heavy use. Very disappointed. I will move to Saucony or Mizuni

UPDATE: I contacted Brooks Running. They said I should buy wide shoes because they are tearing over the pinkies - this is bogus because two specialty running stores and a cycling store has said I have normal width feet and even if the fit was tight it should pinch not tear! They also did not have an explanation for the sole coming apart. The final response was I can file a defective product report but Brooks shoes life expectancy is 4-6 months with normal usage. Seriously? 4-6 months for a $120 product? And I hadn't even used it for that long and due it being winter did not even put in that much mileage.

Sorry, Brooks, you lost a customer for good.

UPDATE: 6/3/2014

I've updated my rating to three stars for the following reason - I submitted a proper defective item report complete with pictures. Brooks responded saying that this was likely due to trail use and sent me a replacement pair. I have since bought a Brooks Cascadia for my combination trail and road running.

product_title: Shimano Men's Comfort On or Off The Bike For Weekend Tours Shoes SH-CT40 Black/Orange-44.0
review_headline: Finally, a cycling shoe for wide feet
review_body:
Thank you Shimano for finally realizing that not all cyclists have D-width feet. Until now I've been wearing your M088 which was one of the very few "wide" shoes offered by any cycling shoe company and even then I had to buy them a size too large to get anywhere near the width I needed (I wear a US 9.5/EU 44 EE+). Wearing the larger size gave me marginally adequate room, but placed the cleats further forward than I would have liked.

These shoes with your new Performance Tour lasts fit perfectly in the correct size. I also like that they don't look like road cycling shoes and are very comfortable to walk in, so you don't get stares as you click across the floor walking like a deer on ice to get a soda at the convenience store. Perfect for the recreational rider, commuting, touring, or general fitness riding. They are still at home on a mountain bike or road bike.

review_headline: Moving from T90 Lazers to Hypervenom Phantoms
review_body:
I had bought my first pair of good shoes about two and a half years ago, those being the T90 Lazers. I had absolutely loved the fit and feel when passing, although the shots with the shoes took a little getting used to. Unfortunately, I tore a few of the cleats off the base plates when doing some step overs and had to get another pair. Since nike no longer makes the T90 line, I decided to try out the Hypervenoms and I could not be happier with the shoe.

Things to note:
* The top of the shoe is very thin, some players complain about this, but I for one am a fan
* Since the top is thin, your foot will get under the ball a little more, so adjust for harder shots to avoid skying the ball
* These shoes are VERY grippy, be ready for the ball to stick to the shoe a little more on quick touches and skill moves

All in all, great shoe that I would recommend to anyone who's serious about their game!

review_body:
UPDATE 11/2015: The newest version of these are slightly different. I just bought my second pair and there is an obvious difference in sizing. I bought 12's again but probably really needed a 13 now. They are slightly narrower and my toes are kind of crammed. At first I just thought it was because my old ones were stretched and worn, but the newer version is definitely tighter feeling....to the point I barely ever pull the laces tight...my foot gets sucked in, as is. Still a great boot, just not sure why they made changes. Especially if you wear thick socks err on the larger size if you're in between.

ORIGINAL: Been in law enforcement for almost a decade and worn everything from 8" 5.11 waterproof boots, to Nike Shocks. Wish I would have found these years ago. I work in a hot/wet climate and these are great for both. I have weak ankles and these provide adequate support (I wouldn't wear a low cut type boot). If your department allows you to wear this type of boot (non-shine-able toe box) I would highly recommend them; they're a perfect mix of an athletic shoe and boot. I wear a 12 or 13 depending on the type/brand of shoe and the 12 fits very well. If I had a thick insole I think they would be too small....but I think a 13 would be too big.

The quick-lace feature is awesome. Even better than a side zip boot because you can still them tight every time you put them on. Awesome for middle of the night call-outs or when you're in a hurry.

product_title: Skechers Performance Men's Go Walk Rookie Shoe
review_body: I just ordered 4 more of these in case Skecher's stops making them.  They are the lightest, most comfortable shoes I have ever worn.  I generally hate shoes and prefer to be barefoot or wearing sandles but these are as close as I have ever been able to find while still looking acceptable for a business casual environment.  Huge portions of the shoe are netted so they breath well.  For that same reason, they don't handle deep puddles very well, but you only make that mistake once.  :)  The soles are very soft and do wear down more quickly than a normal tennis or track shoe.  I am not very hard on my shoes and generally get 2-3 years out of them and these lasted right about a year.  The sole is worn down enough now that I am worried about cracking and letting water in from the bottom.  They are great for general walking at work, home or on a solid surface.  They are not a good shoe for walking over uneven or rocky areas as the soles are soft and you can feel the rocks through them.  They also do not provide the stability that a harder sole provides.  For general use, especially in doors where you will be on your feet a lot but walking on softer surfaces, I recommend these 100%.  If you are buying them to walk with outside, just be aware they will not last as long as you may be used to.  A well worth it sacrifice, IMHO.

product_title: Havaianas Men's Power Flip Flop
review_headline: Expensive  'WATER' Flip Flops that fits BIG and comes with a big design flaw!
review_body:
I needed to replace some old sponge foam Teva thongs and after shopping around I realized the issue with the sponge foam soles is they are not water proof. They soak in water easily and remain damp on your feet after leaving the pool area. These Havaianas' Power flip flop are a hard neoprene foam that do not soak in any water and stay dry all the time.

I love the groves under your feet as they add grip and act as flow channels to push out any water trapped between your feet and the surface of the flip flop.

The comfort level is awesome BUT these fit big and slightly wide for the size. I normally wear size 10 in all other flip flops and 10.5 in shoes but I had to size down to a Men's Size 9 in these Power to get a decent fit (to get an idea of how big these fit see the pictures in my Product Gallery)

One gripe I have with them and one major weakness of these is the toe thong anchor piece (take a look at the product pictures showing the underside of these flip flops). It is not imbedded inside the base but pokes thru and is a floating nub that hangs out on the underside. This means if you get the nub stuck on something sharp whiles walking that tears it off then the toe thongs separate from the base and these flip flops are dead.

For $36 retail I expected a much BETTER design. Even many $20 flip flops today now have imbedded thong anchors that do not poke thru to the bottom of the soles.

Still for the price paid (please buy them on sale at $20 to $30) you can't find a better 'water' flip flops that stay dry and repel water.

I'm a size 9 and relatively high arches, but the straps are never snug on purchase. Further, and worst of all, I have NEVER had a pair of Rocket Dogs NOT come apart at the strap. They are evidently (that is, all of my evidence reports) NOT constructed with much depth nor strength at strap connection points. In fact, these very flip flops: on minute 62 of wearing them, the front point detached on the left shoe. What had been attached was all of about 1/4 inch of fabric, barely glued into the first layer of the sole
I LOVE the look of Rocket Dogs, these so much I gave the brand one last chance. 5'10\\" and made for a circus, I thought they were made for me. Style ratings continue at 8-9 from the Atlanta judge.
But sadly, I could not prove any improvement in construction, durability or service by paying four times what I otherwise would for flip flops. I hoped. My hopes were dashed.

product_title: Salomon Men's XT Wings 3 Trail Running Shoe
review_body:
For those people that don't like running around with disco balls on their feet (per the current 'bright is right' trend), these are the shoes for you. They really are way smarter and slicker looking than your typical running shoe. That's the aesthetics, now on with nitty gritty...

I note one reviewer stated that these were great 'tennis' shoes. What?!? Nope, these are not tennis shoes, they're trail running shoes. Consequently the sole is considerably harder than your typical road running shoe because you're expected to be running on soft ground. So if you're a heavy, high impact runner I wouldn't recommend these over a typical road running shoe if you're primarily going to be doing your thing on ye old black top.

These shoes also provide support for people who pronate, but I don't think it's that excessive and would be ok for a neutral runner. If you supinate, I wouldn't recommend these.

For me, I'll use these for the odd trail run I do, I have visions of going for a tough mudder, but these shoes are not water proof, so for that kind of pursuit, you'd need the goretex variety that Salomon manufacture. I'm not that keen to use them for road running as they are not as springy as I would have hoped, which is why I gave them 4 stars. I'm therefore getting some Nike Air Pegasus for that purpose. I'd say I'd be bigger than your average runner at 6'3" and 220lbs, so I like something comfortable on tar.

The lacing system is pretty cool, though I am familiar with it having had Salomons before, but they can loosen over time, but not really any worse than a normal lacing system, and I don't how, but they don't break (based on previous shoes I've owned).

Anyway, that's my 2c. I like them, and I haven't come across anything that looks better.

product_title: Persol PO3019S Sunglasses
review_body:
I used to be a diehard Ray-Ban fan, but I have to say that Persol is now my go to brand when it comes to sunglasses (and probably prescription frames if I ever need them). I've been wearing these things nearly every day for the past couple of weeks - you don't want to take these things off once you put them on - and now I'm trying to find excuses just to go outside so I can wear them.

This is for the 95/31 model - Black frame with Crystal Green Lens (55mm)

PROS:

-Quality: From the box, to the carrying case, to the cleaning cloth, and most importantly, to the glasses - everything just screams quality. Compared to my Ray-Ban 2132 New Wayfarer frames, the Persols win it by a mile. The Meflecto system is clever yet functional and, coupled with the Supreme Arrow, looks great too. The lenses are good (true colors, no noticeable distortion, crystal clarity), but nothing to write home about really. As far as I can tell, they are nearly identical to the Ray-Ban G-15 XLT lenses that you'll find in most Aviators and Wayfarers, which isn't too surprising considering that both Ray-Ban and Persol are Luxottica subsidiaries. That's not to say the lenses aren't great; they do their job well, but if you're coming from a pair of Ray-Bans you shouldn't expect to notice any difference in lens performance.

-Style: To sum it up into one word: refined. These glasses are simple, elegant, subtle, classy, etc. There's very little branding: just Persol etched into the upper right corner of the right lens, and on the ear pieces of the frames. This is a major plus for me because all of the blatant Ray-Ban branding (especially on the Wayfarers) gets tacky after a little while. This pair doesn't need logos to separate it from other brands, the Supreme Arrow and the Meflecto bands are just distinguishable enough for some of your culturally aware friends to notice and for others to wonder about.

-Being Different: If you're one of those people who likes to be separate from the pack, any pair of Persols will do it. Everybody seems to have a pair of Ray-Bans or Oakleys, but you really don't see too many people going around with a classy pair of Persols on. Walking to the coffee shop, I see about two dozen Wayfarers and maybe one or two Persols on a good day, and I'm yet to see a single person wearing the 3019S. Come to think of it, I've never run across two pairs of the same Persols in public. So if you pride yourself on being unique, Persol is the brand for you.

CONS:

-Fit: From what I've read, Persols tend to run a little large. I have a medium sized face and head (22.25 inches around), and these Persols tended to slip down my nose after moving my head around a bit, while my Wayfarers (which have the exact same measurements as the 55mm 3019S), didn't have this problem. Nothing a quick trip to the local optometrist couldn't fix. It took (literally) less than a minute for him to adjust the frame near the ear pieces, and now they fit like a glove. He did it for free, hopefully your optometrist is as generous.

-Price: These glasses do cost a pretty penny. They're considerably more expensive than a comparable pair of Ray-Bans, and what you get for the extra money is a more refined, more stylish pair of glasses with comparable performance. That being said, you can expect to get quite a bit of life out of these things. My Wayfarers have held up to 3+ years of abuse with only a few nicks here and there, so it's not unreasonable to expect these Persols to last 5+ years with moderate abuse, and much much longer if you take decent care of them.

OVERALL

product_title: Corcoran Men's Field Work Boot
review_body:
Awesome looking boots. A word of warning though: they run about 1/2 to a full size big. So if you normally wear a size 10, order a 9.5 or even a 9 if you like your boots a little more snug. I originally ordered them a half size down, and they were still too big, so I sent them back and went down a full size.

Word of warning #2: MAKE SURE YOU ORDER THE ORIGINAL ONES. Corcoran started making another boot that looks like the jump boot, but it's a way cheaper version. In short: they suck. The ones you want are the "1500 Original Jump Boot" OR these field boots.

POSITIVES: As far as the boots themselves, they are fantastic. They're already pretty shiny right out of the box; didn't take much at all to polish them to mirrors. The leather is high quality, and the field sole still looks really nice. IMO the smooth soled version is slightly more handsome, but they are kind of limited in their use. The field tread definitely gives you a bit more versatility, so I went with that. They also come up a little higher on your leg than normal boots, which makes them look a lot better when you blouse them.

NEGATIVES: Not many. They do have a unique fit to them. Depending on your foot shape, I could see these being pretty rowdy to break in. Fortunately, my feet fit these really well, so it wasn't an issue. The only other thing is that while these boots have speed lace eyelets, they don't come with actual speed laces. They are generic, crappy nylon laces that don't work real well due to their puffiness. Easy fix though. Paracord is cheap.

Overall, they are totally worth the money. There is no better looking boot anywhere on earth than a set of Corcorans.

product_title: Ray-Ban RB3025 Aviator Metal Sunglasses
review_body:
I'm extremely disappointed that it took me 6 months to realize the pair of aviators I bought were fake. Honestly, the only reason I even realized this is because I recently bought an exact pair again (my original pair got stolen....funny now knowing whoever stole them, stole fake ones!) through Amazon and noticed they were a bit different from the ones I initially got. Out of curiosity I decided to check online to see if there were different types of the gold frame/crystal blue gradient lens, but instead I stumbled upon some of the reviews on here (which I probably should have read before purchasing my original pair) stating some were fake. After doing some online research and reviewing the original case, info pamphlet, and lens wiper given to me, I realized the ones I originally purchased were in fact replicas!

For those of you buying these aviators, MAKE SURE the pair you are buying are being sold from Amazon, as these are authentic. However, if you see anything being "sold by Lunettes4me fulfilled by Amazon," do yourself a favor and do not buy them. You will be wasting your money.

review_body:

Hi Rachel,

I'm so sorry to hear that you're dissatisfied with the fit of your pair of the Jolyn flat. We have not previously encountered this issue with the style. I would recommend that you consult your local cobbler about this issue and indicate the problem areas. Oftentimes they can stretch shoes up to a half size and this can elevate the level of comfort, thereby prolonging the life span of the shoe.

Thank you for contacting us with your concerns and please let me know if you have any other questions that I can look into on your behalf!
Stephanie

Not a fan of a company that says "deal with it yourself" instead of offering some advice, offering to switch sizes, etc. I spend a lot of money with this company and I have been hesitant to buy anything since. That being said, I won't wear these shoes because they hurt too bad. My feet aren't wide and I don't wear a large 8... they should fit.

review_body: These are great sandals. Incredibly comfortable foot bed. Great support and most importantly, very stylish. I am usually a 37 or 38. The 38 fit best.

product_title: Reef Men's Convertible-Strap Sandal
review_body:
If the shoes didn't fall apart it would definitely get a 5 star. And I just missed the return window by 15 days.

I have had many Reef Convertibles over the years, some of which have lasted me 3-4 years with quite a bit of usage. For some reason this years' model has a glue issue with the straps. I purchased a pair at Ron Jon's, and the strap came unglued. I called Reef and they were really good about wanting to exchange it, but the problem is they are now discontinued [so they cannot]. I purchased 2 additional pairs off the internet, as these are the only things that will fit my feet, and after about 10 times wearing it the strap came unglued. I have another pair left that I am going to open & wear, hopefully they will last longer than a month.

I love these shoes, but it looks like there is a manufacturing defect.

product_title: Dr. Scholl's Women's Marlee Ballet Flat
review_headline: comfy enough, but a few adjustments would help
review_body: The heels of these bother me and cause blisters, and I've been told by others who buy Dr. Scholl's that you typically have to buy their insoles to suit your specific feet.  that is very annoying - despite the fact that it is nice to be able to personalize the shoes, I don't usually plan to have to buy insoles for shoes, so I'm disappointed that these might not really be comfy without spending more money.

product_title: Fila Skele-Toes Bay Runner 3 Sandal (Toddler/Little Kid/Big Kid)
review_body: My son (age 9) wore these twice and the material on one of the big toes is almost worn through.  The rubber on the bottom is also coming apart.  I would say you could wear them around the house as slippers and they might last awhile but they are definitely not for outdoor use such as on the school playground or going to the park.

product_title: Toms Women's Glitter Slip-On,Bronze,8 M
review_body: This is my first pair of Toms.  They are very comfortable and flashy looking. I would recommend them to friends and family.

product_title: Nautilus 110 Slip Resistant Comp Safety Toe No Exposed Metal Slip-On
review_body: the size that fits right sucks. It is a little to tight at the toe so causes pain in your big toe and the shoe's elastic is to weak so it tends to eat short shocks and slip out. It is very easy to put on and they look good.

product_title: New Balance KJ554 Running Shoe (Infant/Toddler/Little Kid/Big Kid)
review_body: Made with great quality.  Sole on the shoe is good for an energetic child.  My daughter was delighted to receive these shoes.  Colors are vibrant as well.

product_title: Dr. Martens Women's Clemency Boot

review_body: i usually get us 8.5 in shoes. Reading various reviews for this particular Dr. Martens I got UK6 US8 EU39 and it fits good. Of course it has a breakin period. review_body:

These are well made and attractive enough to be worn with dress slacks.
I am very satisfied with the look and comfort.

product_title: ASICS Men's GEL-Fuji Racer Running Shoe
review_body: Bought this for my 14 year old that runs track. Colors match the school colors. Very light shoes. Seems durable.

product_title: Softspots - Womens - Bonnie Lite
review_headline: Should have listened to other reviewers
review_body: Reviewers who said the sole is too hard and feels like walking on a brick didn't exaggerate. These shoes are too hard and making standing and walking in them over a long period painful. Also the seam in the back rubbed against my heel. Unfortunately I'm stuck with shoes I'll never wear.

product_title: Shoe Goo Repair Adhesive for Fixing Worn Shoes or Boots, Clear, 3.7-Ounce Tube
review_body: I don't often give out a 5 star rating but this glue, polymer or whatever it is really works.  I took a pair of sneakers ready for the trash and made them into a great pair of gardening and lawn mowing shoes.

product_title: Merrell Women's Crush Glove Minimalist Cross-Training Shoe
review_body: this is a great shoe.  it pulled out near the lacing after a few weeks.  I took it to the shoe repairs because I like them so much and had passed the return time.

product_title: Steve Madden Women's Xfoliate Wedge Sandal
review_body:
Favorite shoe in my closet right now! I wear a size 9, but had to order these in a 10. So if you have short toes go a half size up, long toes go a whole size up. I love the 6 inch heel and because of the platform it is easy to walk in.

Ok updated review, month later: first time wearing this shoe out I tripped a couple of times never falling because I was holding my finances hand. You need to practice wearing this shoe, before going out in public. After wearing them the second time I was much more comfortable and walking was easy. PRACTICE PRACTICE PRACTICE! I love being tall so these babies will defiantly make you feel, like a model. I have the stone color, but now I have black. still love this shoe!!! Good luck.

product_title: Teva Barracuda Kids Sandal
review_body: I would have got these in toddler size but the largest in toddlers was not large enough.  Thought I would try these, but they are a little big for my 4 yr old grandson.  He will grow into them so I will save them.  Great bargain thanks to Amazon.com.

product_title: Nike Men's Air Max Run Lite 4 Running Shoe
review_body: It's a bit tight, but that's normal, they just have to be worn in. This pair is replacing another of the exact same shoe, the other ones wore out from wear-and-tear of over a year. These last awhile!

product_title: Vivanz Women's Ginger Wedge Slide
review_body: These are the most expensive shoes I've bought in a very long time, if ever.  But they're worth Every Penny!  They're so comfortable!  It says the heels are 3 inches, but I think they're a little less than that, maybe 2 1/2.  They almost seem to be made of rubber, but it's kind of a flexible cushy plastic with a wooden print.  The straps are all elastic except the one that goes across the top.  I wear them all day running errands and my feet rejoice!  I originally saw these at Zappos, which has the best customer service on the planet, but they were $132 there and $120 here, both with free shipping.

product_title: Cushe Men's M Rubber Sole Fashion Sneaker
review_body:
My husband has slightly narrow heels so it's always a chore finding shoes that fit. Unfortunately, these were really loose around the heel & the sides of his feet. They are soft so would probably not rub his feet raw but they looked silly loose so we sent them back. A shame because he likes this style & they are cushy soft.

One thing that is a potential problem with these shoes is the sole. The front sole (under the toes) is built up a bit higher in from the edge so your feet can tend to tilt inward (kind of a "pigeon-toe" effect). I think Cushe went a little overboard in the "style" over foot health with this sole. The odd sole could be a tripping hazard for the elderly or anyone who has problems with walking.

product_title: FASH Limited Giraffe Print Faux Leather Tote Shoulder Handbag,Brown,One Size
review_body: Loving this bag!  Though I'm thinking I will be cutting out the zipper close. Kinda in the way. Other then that. It's so cute. I will worn u that this bag is a large size & the inside is plastic not fabric. But for $20.00 who's complaining. Love it!

product_title: PUMA Momentta Vulcanized Sala Indoor Soccer Shoe
review_body: I resumed playing football after 4 years or so, and needed to get some indoor shoes. These fit perfectly! I have also played for a club, so I kinda do know when I am talking about football shoes (yes, these are the real football shoes). The shape is perfect for getting some good quality shots on goal, and they have lasted me a while now. Would totally recommend this product.

product_title: Coco Brown Faux Suede Wrap Tie Ankle Strap Platform Chunky High Heels Swat
review_body: This is my new favorite shoe as it is simply gorgeous and has a vintage look. I have narrow feet and this shoe was true to size. I would recommend that if you have broad feet to go half size up.

product_title: Rockport Men's M7100 Milprowlkr
review_body: Ive only had my shoes for a week but so far i love them. Easy on the feet(comfortable), stylish and White! I do not know much about the brand and have not had a pair from them before but i am very impressed this far.

product_title: Converse Men's Chuck Taylor All Star Leather Hi
review_body: High quality leather fit great and of course are Converse brand. Delivered as hoped and came in original packaging inside another box. May pay more for name brand but they're quality that lasts longer.

product_title: New Balance Men's MT610v2 Trail Running Shoe
review_body: I think they come untied to easily plus they seem big to me.  The last 4e I got fit perfectly even if it got untied my foot stayed in the shoe.  Maybe These are what 4e is supposed to be maybe not IDK.

product_title: ASICS Women's GEL-Kinsei 4 Running Shoe
review_body: LOVE LOVE LOVE!!! I love the colors, the comfort, the sizing and the quality.  SUPER amazing.  I have bought 2 pairs and will be buying a third soon.  They are cross trainers, not the ideal light shoe, but for the gym and weightlifting - perfect!

product_title: Dunham Men's REVchase Slip-On
review_body: I tried a pair of these on in a local shoe store. They had brown, but, I wanted black. They said it would be 2 weeks before they could get them in. Price was the same on here and I had Prime. So, I paid the extra couple bucks to have them shipped overnight. These are light on the feet and the correct width. Be sure to have your foot measured by a professional for the correct fit and size!

product_title: DailyShoes Women's Fashion-Hi Over-the-Knee Thigh High Flat Slouchly Shaft Low Heel Boots
review_body: Wonderful fit, proportionate all the way up the leg for the large size. Exceptionally comfortable and sturdy. A great buy!

product_title: EVE Mens' Snake Embossed Slide Scruff Slippers (1512)
review_body: Although these are listed as inside-outside, they are way too flimsy for outside use.  Not what I was looking for.

product_title: Propet Mens Village Walker Mid
review_headline: Excellent shoe, with enough room for orthotics.
review_body: These shoes are very comfortable, and don't require much break in. Room in the toe area for my orthotics, otherwise would run a little large and wide. My new favorite shoe.

product_title: White Mountain Women's Carly Sandal
review_body: Love these sandals.  This is my third pair.  I have worn out the others.  I wear them almost everywhere because they are comfortable and durable.

product_title: BOBS from Skechers Women's Plush Memories Flat
review_body: I always thought KEDS were the only rubber soled shoe I could wear comfortably.  BOB's has certainly changed my mind.  Very comfortable and stylish.

product_title: Robeez Far Out Crib Shoe (Infant/Toddler)
review_body: I am finding that all "crib" style shoes run bigger than what you would expect. for example i ordered these in 0-6 months and at 9 months they just now fit right and my daughter is of average size. I have ordered other brands and they are even bigger! so i think you need to just size down or be mindful that anything that is sold in 6 month increments in sizing is not going to be form fitting...otherwise they would be infant 1, infant 1.5, infant 2, etc in sizing. This being said, these shoes are precious and fit great and STAY ON little feet! They are well made and hold up. For that reason I give them 5 stars and not 4...sizing is something we as parents just have to figure out...sadly it seems nothing is really consistent in children's apparel.

product_title: Scarleton Vintage Satchel H1169
review_body: Like the purse but larger than expected. Beautiful color and well made. I just wish it was smaller, I won't use it and will probably give to my daughter.

product_title: Original S.W.A.T. Men's Classic 9" Side Zip Work Boot
review_body:
fit perfect and very comfortable. A little more expensive than what I would pay but the are worth it.
I never bought any boots online but these are great

product_title: Skechers Performance Women's Go Walk 2-Axis Fashion Sneaker
review_body: Perfect length but for me just a little bit wide for a thin sport sock. With a heavier winter sock will be perfect. I am just on the medium width so those who are a true medium these are perfect. So comfortable. Like walking on air.

product_title: Skechers Women's BOBS Plush Joyful

product_title: Chie Mihara Women's Angelina Dress Sandal
review_body: Shoe is very high quality in terms of design and materials. Fit is spot on. Comfort is 5 stars. Just could not get past the odd green color teamed with the black and brown. Sent them back due to color.

product_title: KEEN Utility Men's PTC Oxford Work Shoe
review_body: Keens are the only shoes I'm truly comfortable in. They feel great from day one and I know they will last because I work in an old pair that still feel great.

product_title: BTP! Hippie Hobo Sling Crossbody Bag Messenger Purse Elephant Swirl Print in Black XL EWL1
review_body: I love mine and just bought  another! ( But I wish they would line this with muslin). I did alter mine so I would not have a saggy bottom. I cut out the bottom, then laid out the bag flat with the side seam in the center.(you want to do it this way so it hangs properly). Pinned and then re-stitched  the bottom. Then bought a Kilofly diaper bag organizer (turn it inside out so the pockets are inside.) to give the bag some shape and pockets for stuff. It was easy and makes this bag very comfortable for use as a shoulder bag. From the center top of the bag to the bottom you will have about 13".

product_title: Aviator Fashion Sunglasses 30011c Silver Frame Yellow Lens for Men and Women
review_body: got for my husband who has trouble driving in the night and when its raining. these glasses do the trick. he has no problems now when driving in those conditions

product_title: Five Ten Men's Aescent (2013) Shoe
review_body:
I climb/scramble up a mountain everyday in these things- they are sturdy, comfortable and a great grip.
And fun colors

product_title: Badgley Mischka Women's Thora D'Orsay Pump
review_body:
I took a chance getting the 8.5 as I usually wear 8.5 but sometimes a 9. Well I went for the 8.5. They fit just great! Comfortable fit and easy to walk in. Also, they are just beautiful. Sweet soft pink color and the decorative ruffle flower is soft and lovely. I have tried them and my feet are comfortable.

I am 5'6" tall so I usually don't wear high heels due to the fact that the average height of the American woman over the age of 25 is 5'1" or 5'2". product_title: Orthaheel Carey Casual Flat
review_body: Because my previous pair of ortho heel shoes were slightly large, I ordered an half six smaller this time.  I'm very happy with both the fit and comfort of these cute shoes.  I will most certainly purchase more of this brand because of my pronation issues.

product_title: Wild Diva Lounge Kandall-12 High Heel Wedge Pump Colorblock Black (10)
review_body: these shoes are not true to size my toes are long and they are a size 10 I can fit them but will be giving these to my daughters

product_title: crocs Men's Yukon Two-Strap Sandal
review_body: I live in regular Crocs, they are good for my arches! During the summer, I prefer sandals, and I have worn other Crocs sandals, like the XTG and Tookali, but these Yukon are absolutely the best! I am a woman, but these are perfect for me, I need something sturdy and durable yet fairly lightweight, and all the women's sandals are little flimsy things that are not fit for long walks, etc.  The  Yukon sandals fit perfectly, are attractive, have good arch support, and I can slip my foot in, not having to fiddle with the strap, which is nice, since the Tookali takes effort to get on and off, which is annoying. I am going to stock up on these so I have them around for many years, in case Crocs discontinues them. CROCS RULE!!!!!

product_title: Ollio Women's Ballet Shoe Pointed Toe Weave Comfort Multi Color Flat
review_body:
Basic black flats with a decorative edge, very comfortable, and sturdy. I will be able to get good use out of them for work!
Recommend it!

product_title: Bandolino Women's Yaffa Wedge Sandal
review_body: So happy I took a chance on the Bandolino sandals.  I've worn this brand before and decided to go for it.  Glad I did.  Had never bought a pair of shoes without trying them first.  Very happy with my purchase.

product_title: Women's Qupid Chunky Platform High Heel Over Knee High Thigh High Boots Fashion Shoes
review_body: These boots are beautiful!  They take a little time to zip up BUT that's due to my muscular calves. Once I got them on I fell in love. They aren't hard to walk in at all. When my fiancée saw them his jaw dropped open.  These are definitely a keeper!

product_title: ASICS Men's GEL-Kahana 6 Trail-Running Shoe
review_headline: Wanted something wide, was a little disappointed.
review_body:
I bought the Gel-Kahana 6 sized 11.5 4E and thought I'd try out ASICS over NB for once. Coming from a size 11 4E MT610 which felt decently snug but not tight all around, the Gel-Kahana did nothing but disappoint. The front of the shoe provides ample room and the shoe might even slide around if it wasn't for the fact that the sides towards the middle of my foot were so tight. Maybe it'll get better as I wear it. I'll provide an update if it does.

If you're coming from NB for wide shoes, stay far away or risk ordering 1 size bigger because half a size bigger wasn't enough for me.

product_title: Vince Camuto Women's Kastern Cuffed Thong Sandal
review_body: This shoe is gorgeous and fits wonderfully. I am usually a 71/2 but the size seven fits perfectly and doesn't hurt my ankle.

product_title: Naturalizer Womens Bina Fabric Wedge Sandals, Orange, Size 7.5
review_body: Boy, was this a steal.  I scored these in my size for $15 and free shipping! Naturalizers are so comfortable.  I wore these for 4 hours, standing the whole time, and my feet were not hurting by the end of the party, which is amazing.  They add just the right amount of height without making it difficult to walk.  The color is pink, with a very slight hint of coral.  If you're wondering, the square embellishment on the front is made of plastic, but it's not cheapy looking.  Even if more expensive, these would be worth the price.  I usually wear an 8 or 7 1/2.  I ordered these in a 7 1/2 because they were significantly cheaper in that size, and they fit fine.  They're both comfortable and cute, which is a rarity in shoes.

review_body: Not winter boots, but I helped a buddy move in 14 degree weather while it was snowing, alot.  While active, they were warm and dry.  They are NOT for winter and if you're not moving your feet get cold.  Great for casual wear and wet weather.

product_title: New Starbay Brand Women's Gladiator Sandals Flats with Metal Links

product_title: Clarks Women's Leisa Sahara Mule

product_title: KEEN Women's Toyah Shoe
review_headline: Most comfortable pair of shoes I own!!!!
review_body: I hesitated spending a chunk of change on these shoes and after a year I decided to just buy them.  I am glad I did.  I work in an office with concrete floors and am on my feet quite a bit! On top of this I have tile floor through out my home and wearing these shoes I would never know I was on my 12-16 hours a day. I also love the style of the shoes, casual yet also looks great w/jeans.  There is no break in period, take them out of the box and you ready to go.  LOVE LOVE LOVE them!!!!  I suggest these shoes to anyone who is on their feet a lot or if you have back or feet issues.  Plenty of room for your whole foot yet not too much room either.  These are amazing shoes!!!!

product_title: UGG Australia Women's Laela Quilted Slip-on Shoes
review_body: I think they could be wider in the arch, since it's practically impossible to wear them quickly without a shoe spoon, otherwise they are true to size.

review_body: I love these shoes. I specifically bought these to hike Zion National Park, Subway route as well as Bryce Canyon.  These shoes shoes are very stiff so I would recommend breaking them in a few weeks before any big hikes. I broke mine in by working out in them. They are actually great for box jumps, squats and dead lifts. After hiking through Utah for three days my feet feel great! I would also recommend getting their mid GTX hiking boots if you plan on hiking in snow. Great company, awesome product!

product_title: Earth Women's Bellflower Pump
review_body: Very comfy and cute! Love Earth shoes! The work well with any color and with oants, dresses, skirts and shorts!

product_title: Kamik Women's Flora Rain Boot
review_headline: Love the fit on my thin calves.
review_body: So I just received the Flora Rain Boot today.  I was a little worried about fit due to other reviews.  If you are thin, order your normal size.  I am 5'7" and 113lbs and I normally wear an 8 1/2, but sometimes a 9.  I ordered a 9 and they are perfect.  I can still wear a thick sock when it is cold (I already put on the thick socks to confirm).  The only thing that keeps me from giving them a five is that the 2 boots are completely different even though they are based on the same pattern.  I would have liked them to be the same.  The fact that they are different is not that important though, as I mainly wear them to fish and do yard work when it's muddy.  They are not nearly as vibrant in person as they are in the picture.  After 2 seasons my Sperry rainboots sprouted a leak due to a break in the seam and the way these boots are designed it looks impossible for that to happen.  If my opinion changes, I will update my review.  Also it is a "cloth boot base", which is wear the design is, and then that is coated with clearish rubber.  They appear to be a quality boot.

product_title: Clarks Women's Clarks Alto Disco Wedge Sandal
review_body: Love these sandals.  The fit is perfect. The arch provides comfortable support. They will definitely be my "go to" shoes when looking for comfort.  Thank you!

product_title: ASICS Men's GEL-Venture 4

product_title: Calvin Klein Men's Magnus Slip-On Loafer
review_headline: Too big, the size run bigger
review_body: All my shoes are US Size 9, I bought this shoes 9 size, but the shoes is bigger,  I feel disappointed with this.

product_title: Sanuk Women's Yoga Sling 2 Flip Flop
review_body: I found out about Sanuk brand last summer while visiting Charleston, SC. I came home with 2 pairs of flip flops and a black pair of the yoga slings. I love them all because they are like walking on air. With a new summer season on the way, I wanted to see if I could find the slings in other colors. Found these pink/charcoal and ordered. The colors are perfect and as soon as I put them on, they were broken in.  Both my two daughters and I wear them almost exclusively in the summer!!  I would recommend Sanuk to everyone for the comfort, durability and breast pricing!!

product_title: RYKA Women's Illusion Running Shoe
review_body: I have never written Ryka shoes, but decided to go for it after reading so many rave reviewson them. Well, these are about the worst fitting athletic shoes ever. They are way too shallow in the heel well & are too wide in the heel, as well. They slipped all over the place. review_body:

The clamping force of the glasses seems about right, so I'm not sure how they ended up looking wide. Lenses are 1.5" high and 2 1/8" wide at their widest point.

Since I wear them practically everyday at work, I'm on my feet a lot and black goes with any outfit, it's smart to have an extra pair. The patent crock looks so sleek that even with my dress suits it looks classy and complimenting that I get asked a lot what brand they are or where I got them from. The first thing I do when I get home is take my shoes off right away and change into my sports shoes and walk my pooch.. But believe it or not, when I have this pair on, I don't bother changing. product_title: Skechers Performance Men's Go Run Ride 2-Nite Owl Glow-In-the-Dark Running Shoe
review_body: These shoes fit perfectly on my slightly wide forefoot/toes. I love the small arch support in the shoe. I recovered from a plantar fasciitis injury 6 months ago and had a hard time finding a running shoe to train long distance runs longer than 12 miles. I've had heavy cushioned, large heel to toe proportion over 8mm shoes as well as 4mm to zero drop minimalist shoes. I just ran a 13 mile run yesterday morning in these Skechers Go Ride Run 2's that were amazing. They were more pleasant to run with than what I imagined. I've had heavy shoes such as the Brooks Dyad 7 suggested by the Marathon Sports' store for my feet but the Skechers' shoes blow them out of the water. These shoes are lightweight but with excellent cushioning for hard roads and low enough to the ground for runners gravitating towards a minimalist approach. Plus I can't forget to mention the cool colors when it glows in the dark at night.

product_title: Merrell Women's Jacardia Sandal
review_headline: Lovely, Supportive - But Darn that buckle
review_body: There is much to love about these sandals.  From the top, they are strappy and attractive enough to be worn with dresses to a nice occasion.  But they are VERY supportive - as Merrell's tend to be.  I bought them because I love my Merrell hiking boot and wanted some of the same toughness on the sole but something I could wear with dresses and skirts.  I was not disappointed!  They do seem to run a bit large, which is strange since I'm usually a solid size 9 in Merrell shoes.  There are velcro adjustments at the back of the heel, but these are maxed out for me with still a little room.  Still, they aren't so big as to cause blisters or anything.  My one real complaint is the buckle on the side.  It is small and feels delicate - though I haven't had any breakage yet.  But it is completely impossible to open.  It's a squeeze from the sides type buckle and I just cannot get it to release.  I understand that for such a narrow strap, a narrow buckle is required but I think they should've gone with a different type.  I've been just slipping the sandals on, since there's a little extra room, but this pulls at the velcro back and I fear may eventually cause some problems.  Still!  Lovely, comfortable sandals at such a price - both stylish and practical - that's pretty good.

product_title: Kamik Women's Olivia Rain Boot
review_body:
Let me start by stating these boots are very cute and even though they do fit snuggly, I liked them A LOT. I normally wear an 8.5-9 and I ordered them in charcoal size 9. They seemed comfortable although I only wore them once for a few hours so I did not have much time to really judge.

I bought them in mid-February and the first time I had the opportunity to wear them, the grommet holding the buckle to the boot just fell apart! I'm not sure when it happened exactly but I felt the the buckle dangling off the boot and found the back of the grommet inside the boot. I came online but Amazon no longer had the boot available in my size. I went online to the Kamik website and saw they had a 1 year warranty. So I sent them an email explaining the problem and why I couldn't exchange them at the place of purchase. I included proof of purchase and pictures of the defect in my email as the site instructed. After 3 weeks I still had not heard back so I emailed them again. I got a response the following day offering to mail me a new buckle. While this was a nice offer, it didn't fix my problem. The buckle of my boot is not broken, the grommet attaching it is and because and I have no way to reattach it. So I replied immediately explaining the problem again and I got another reply stating to simply exchange them at the store where I purchased them! Ahhh! I replied immediately AGAIN and explained the situation AGAIN. I finally got a reply stating that \\"As a gesture of goodwill\\" they would send me a replacement pair. A gesture of goodwill? That sounds a bit condescending and like they feel they really have no responsibility for their defective product. And I don't care if they send me brand new boots anyway. I would have been thrilled with an offer to send them my boot so they could just fix it! And to add to it all, they said they are sold out of the boot until June so my new boots would come them. I'm so frustrated!

So, while the boots are cute and seem comfortable, buyer beware! I would suggest to keep looking and buy a more durable boot from a company that stands behind their product a bit better. Luckily for me, Amazon is amazing as always and I'm sending the boots back and opting for a different brand entirely.

product_title: ASICS Women's GEL-Kahana 6 Trail Running Shoe
review_headline: I really, really wanted to like these shoes, but ...
review_body: They run way too narrow. I normally wear a wide width 6.5 shoe ("duck feet" - narrow heel, wide at the front, with an incredibly high arch), and so, after carefully reading all of the other customer reviews, I order a 7 C/D in these. They arrived promptly, and I LOVED the smashing orange detail. Couldn't wait to put them on and get out the door, so I shoved my feet in them and grimaced - they were TIGHT. I thought "well, maybe they'll stretch a little", so I loosened the laces to their capacity and set off. I've been running in them and wearing them every day for weeks, and I have to face the music - things are not going to get any better. They fit kind of weird (or maybe it's just me that's weird): across the top of my foot, they're actually pretty ok, but the things they do to the bottoms of my feet is bizarre. I haven't had any issues with rubbing, blisters, or the like - they actually make the bottom of my feet numb. It's maddening; I really can't stand it anymore, so yesterday I gave up and ordered a pair of New Balance runners - my old stand-by. Sorry, Asics - I really wanted to love your product, but the relationship is suffocating ...

product_title: Cudas Women's Tsunami-Wos Water Shoe
review_headline: Decent enough at a reasonable price
review_body: Well, that doesn't sound very exciting, does it? But these are pretty good shoes. I bought them for water aerobics as several of the reviews I read said they were "perfect" for that, and my old ones were falling apart. They are nice and light weight and have all the necessary drainage needed for water aerobics. They definately look more grey in real life than they did on my iPad--not quite as cute and purple. They feel well constructed and I expect to get good use out of them. My one concern is that, while the top is adjustable thanks to the elasticated tie, there is no way to tighten or loosen the shoes on the sides---which is a common feature in other better made water aerobic shoes. These may be great for fun in the river or playing around occasionally in wet areas. But with repeated use in regular water aerobics classes, shoes have a way of stretching out quickly. So having the the ability to tighten then in multiple places would be a bonus. Time will tell whether or not these will hold up to the punishment of my routine. But they were relatively inexpensive, and I will have to see if you get what you pay for. So far, so good!

product_title: Baffin Men's Maximum Canadian Made Industrial Boot
review_headline: They do their job as work boots for wet jobs
review_body:
I do sanitation and qa work at a water bottling plant and believe me, I see a lot of water every night. Having your feet submerged in ankle deep water for long periods of time is an everyday occurrence and our soaps and cleaners have pH ranges of 3.00 to 12.00. Needless to say, leather boots do NOT last a long time in this environment.

These beasts however, are champions. They stand up to all the chemicals and all the deep water without a worry in the world. I abuse my boots since I'm sometimes forced to kick things "into place" so to speak and I did manage to split the toe after about 6 months. It came apart at a seam along the front. However, I just glued it back shut with some epoxy and went on with life like it was no big deal. I also bought mine too big and because of that, I noticed that sometimes water could splash down inside. But to be honest, that was usually only when we were flushing something out and there's 100s of gallons of water flowing at that time.

BUY A PAIR OF INSOLES!!! These aren't like wearing Timberlands. I highly recommend getting a really good insole if you plan to use them a lot. Otherwise, best work boots for the money if you work in a more "unique" environment

product_title: Calvin Klein Key Item Pebble Hobo
review_body:
I am not a person who buys multiple purses, or even changes out purses for the season. The last purse I bought was in Memphis, after katrina, in 2006. It was leather and cost 55 dollars, at that time the most I ever spent on a purse. So, 8 years later it is showing some wear and I was on the search for another black leather purse. I wanted something big enough for my tablet, kindle, and other purse stuff, but not so big I felt I was carrying a suitcase. I wanted something I could wear comfortably over my shoulder.

The Calvin Klein hobo is a great purse. It's roomy and generous with space. The side buckles can be adjusted for shorter or taller people, I have them set at the farthest setting on each side and it easily goes over my shoulder and stays on. The zipper is solid. A leather pebble exterior is attractive.

There is only one small zipper compartment on the inside, and one on the outside, so everything pretty much is just loose and free inside the purse. If you're looking for separation and lots of zippers this isn't the purse. When it hangs over my shoulder it does sag slightly on top, it doesn't bother me.

I really like this purse and hope to have the long term relationship I had with my last one. It holds a lot and fits comfortably over my shoulder. The stitching seems quality and I haven't seen any signs of anything lose or poorly crafted. This is a great basic sling over your shoulder and go purse.

product_title: Timberland Men's Chocorua Trail Gore-Tex Mid Hiking Boot
review_headline: I am on my third pair of these
review_body:
These are by far the best boots I have ever owned. I just bought my third pair. They are warm and rugged enough for New England winters, yard work and outdoor sporting games. The GoreTex lining keeps your feet dry. Once you break them in, they will fit you like socks. I use them for beekeeping, gardening, hiking, winter/ fall/ spring hiking, etc. My feet are always warm and dry.

They are not steel toed, but Timberland makes other models that are. The toes are substantial even without steel, and even on my old pairs, I have dropped heavy things on my feet and the boots have protected my toes. The reason my last two pairs wore out (after years of frequent use): the treads wore down. I practically live in these boots for half of each year, so that isn't surprising. They are not waterproof, but the water would need to be over an inch deep to get inside your boot, and the GoreTex will wick it out. I wear these in the rain all the time and am comfortable.

They are exceptionally sturdy, provide great ankle support, and are not too heavy to feel comfortable. review_body:

I removed its thinly thin-base foam (I was surprise to see how thin it was) and added my custom made insert; the boot was still ok with that addition. my heels still felt very low, so i added under the inserts a pair of heel-cushion which then made the boots very comfortable! All that addition made the foot feels a little tighter but i think in short time the leather will give in to the new shape!
From previous experience with other waterproof keen boots, Before using it outside for the first time i sprayed Silicone water shield for extra protection, and that I normally do each season which seems to help preserve the leather and keep the rain out!
This pair feels warm and cozy, and looks very attractive! All in all i am very happy i purchased them!

product_title: MuckBoots Men's Excursion Low Hunting Shoe
review_headline: As good as it can be?  Think of it as a boot, even though it looks like a shoe
review_body:
April 7, 2014 update; After wearing these for a month or more every day in this cold, wet, icy, snowy spring, I wanted to boost rating to a 5. These shoe/boots are all that I said / hoped for in my original review. As I said - ended up with a size 10. They fit slightly loose, like a normal winter snow boot, but not so much that they are annoying or do they fall off. Once, walking in moderately deep mud, the heal stuck and I had to \\"work the boot out\\" so not to end up walking through the mud with only a sock on . But when I head out to do chores or other, it is a pleasure to put this shoe / boot on!! Great in stalls - ankle fits just tight enough to keep debris out and yet not be annoying at all. Have even used it occasionally for trail walks in snow (2\\"-4\\"). As in stalls, ankle elastic is just enough to keep foot dry and warm. Normally I don't bother to snug up the easy to use elastic draw string laces. But on occasion (like the trail walk in the shallow snow), I do snug it up. But normally the shoe / boot stays on just fine with out snugging it up. Tread and waterproof has been tested well this spring. Nice traction and feet are always warm and dry. Other making it in half sizes, there isn't much to make this boot better.

Had a little trouble even trying to title this feed back. Three bears - too big, too small, just right? Too loose in the heal? Easy on and off. Too hard to get on and off? Reviews on these shoes / boots are ALL OVER THE PLACE. I have had a number of Muck boots as well as others - Jobber, Arctic Sport, etc. I love the Arctic Sports, don't like the Jobbers (tread is way too slippery in snowy / icy conditions.
In order to review them properly, it is important to know what I was looking for. I have a horse farm and wanted an easy on / easy off boot / shoe, that is warm, waterproof, keeps out shavings when doing stalls, snow (for snow in the 2\\" range), comfortable, fits well, durable, and has good traction. The Excursion ALMOST fits the bill perfectly - a tough order trying to score highly in all these categories.
Here are my scores:
- easy on / easy off - a qualified 5 stars. Must be the right size!!
- warm - so far so good!! Temps in the single digits and foot is fine! - 5 stars
- waterproof - no question about that. Perfect. - 5 stars
- keeps out shavings. Fit as snug as they can be around the ankle. - 5 stars. But see comments under The Fit The challenge
- keeps out snow - ditto as for shavings - 5 stars
- Fits well - see a whole separate section on this - 4 stars
- Durable - too soon to tell. But based on initial impressions and simply look and feel. - 5 stars
- Traction - this sole looks fantastic, exactly what I was looking for. Traction was a major issue with the Jobber. Not so with the Excursion - 5 stars.

The big issue is Fit. The majority of reviews have this as an issue / topic. Me too. Some reviews say it runs big, so order down a size. Some reviews say it runs small so order up a size. My Arctics and Jobbers were a 10 - 101/2; 10 respectively. I ordered a 10. Upon arrival, they fits loosely, especially in the heel, as a lot of reviewers noted. In fact the overall fit seemed a little loose. I ordered a 9 thinking that would solve the problem. Hmmm - not so. The 9 was a little tight around the ankle (a comment of some); and after wearing around the house to test, were just a tad too tight in the toe. Put the 10's back on. Still seemed a little on the loose side. But from past experience - too small is BADDD!! Feet get cold, and a little too tight in the toe quickly becomes an issue . Then I reflected on what I had and other boots. I love the Arctics. Do they fit a little loose - YES, but I don't mind that in a boot for snow, that I don't want to struggle with and keep my feet warm and dry. What I wanted in the Excursion was much more \\"boot like\\" than shoe like. I think that the Excursion does about as well as it possibly can relative to fit. As a few reviewers acknowledged - yes it is a little loose, not so that it feels like it is going to fall off. If you want the easy on / easy off (another feature that was non existent on the smaller size), comfortable, warm etc - this shoe meets all that. The only thing that Muck could possible do is offer it in half sizes. A 9-1/2 might have made the fit a tad better.

Bottom line - I am very happy with this boot!!!

review_body:

These have only a couple of holes, which has made them more functional for outside use. (Note if Croc's made one which went up even another inch, I would like that even better, but these are still great.)

There were a couple of reviews implying the Blitzen might be tight. Although my Evo's were a 9, I tried a 10. Bad idea - too big, even with the lining. Returned for a 9 and these are great.

Also one complaint about sweating ? The Blitzen only has 2 breathing holes (even these are located in a position to deter dirt or snow from entering), a GOOD thing if you intend to use them outside in the winter!! They obviously keep your feet warmer, and if worn indoors or warmer climates, could result in a sweaty foot. The solution - DER, buy a shoe (the EVO) with more ventilation holes in it. This shoe is great!!!

So this one's going right back.
PRODUCT SUGGESTION: I might add that I wish Keen made a water sandal that didn't have such a big, obvious rubber toe guard. For example, we vacation in Florida & have to travel there by air. So I'd like to be able to wear a closed-toe sandal on the plane that will look good, that I can also wear in the water. It is now January 2015 about a year later and I am not so pleased with these shoes. The soles are paper thin and if you step on the most miniscule of pebbles while walking on pavement it will feel like you stepped on a tack. The \\"leather\\" uppers have split on the inside of the right shoe. Also the \\"leather\\" upper has pulled (torn) away from the sole along the right forefoot.
