product_title: Vibram KSO EVO
review_headline: Great update to Vibram's line of fitness/running shoes.
review_body: This review was posted to birthdayshoes.com    Please do a quick search for KSO EVO birthdayshoes for the full review.   Background: this review was written after running 30 miles on asphalt (in freezing Cape Cod weather!) and 40 treadmill miles, mixed in with some gym work, including weights and an automatic rock wall. My other Vibram shoes include the Bikila LS, KSO Remix, KSO TREK, and EL-X. I have relatively flat feet and wear a size 41 for all Vibrams. For additional sizing reference, I also wear a size 41 for Vivobarefoot's minimalist offerings.    The KSO EVO may be the best toe shoe Vibram has ever offered. It carries on the lofty name of its predecessor in style and vastly improves upon the EL-X that it's based on. No other shoe in the lineup strikes such a perfect balance between weight, flexibility, and stability. The KSO EVO has replaced the EL-X as my \\"go to\\" shoe for just about anything.    Vibram uses initializations for the naming of some of their models. In the case of the KSO EVO, the name is meant to signify an evolution (EVO) of the original KSO (keep stuff out); a shoe that aims for versatility as an \\"all-around\\" model that can fill multiple roles, including running on both roads and trails and for cross fitness. In addition to the naming fun, this shoe is also known as the EL-X LS, where EL-X stands for \\"Entry Level Crosstrainer\\" and LS stands for \\"lace system\\".     KSO EVO is more of an evolution of the EL-X than the original KSO. It can be best described as an EL-X with added features for a more secure fit, both in the heel and the around the foot.    The major differences between the KSO EVO and EL-X are:    The welcome addition of Vibram's speed lace system  Added structure around the heel for a tighter fit  Before the KSO EVO, I would have said that the EL-X is the best in the FiveFingers lineup, followed by the Bikila LS. However, the KSO EVO trumps both shoes by being a near-perfect combination of the security of the Bikila LS and the weight and ground feel of the EL-X.  While the EL-X is the featherweight of the vibram lineup at 4.23 oz for a size 43, the KSO EVO is only a shade heavier at 4.9 oz. By comparison, the Bikila LS can almost be considered heavy at 6 oz and even the Seeya LS clocks in above the EVO at 5.07 oz.    Overall, the KSO EVO is the second lightest shoe in the Vibram lineup.    The Upper  The KSO EVO features the same polyester stretch mesh upper as the EL-X and the Seeya. More breathable than the coconut active upper used in the Bikila LS, the stretch upper in the KSO EVO is very comfortable and fits like a glove (well, my foot anyways).    Because the KSO EVO has such a breathable upper, I would not recommend it for cold weather fitness activities. Of course, that didn't stop me from running six miles each day in 25 degrees, but the original KSO, Bikila, Spyridon, KMD, Flow, Maiori and Lonta all provide better insulation for the cold.    In addition to the stretchy mesh upper, the KSO EVO also features the same \\"painted on\\" rubber first utilized in the EL-X to add a little structure to the shoe and keep it tight on your foot, but these painted sections hinder breathability in the sections of the mesh where they are present.    Unlike the EL-X, which has nothing else but the mesh+painted rubber combination to keep the shoe on your foot, the KSO EVO has the addition of a lace system to maintain tightness and does not rely on the the painted-on for security, so its usage seems redundant and inhibits breathability. It may also cause hot spots, which I experienced on my instep where there is some of the painted-on material (near the Vibram logo). This went away after a few runs, but it was quite the initial annoyance. I had a similar experience with the EL-X and I think both shoes just require a little bit of a break-in period to eliminate any hotspots or tightness due to the non-breathable rubber material.    Overall, the upper for the KSO is very breathable and comfortable, but Idid experience a short-lived hotspot on my instep, which rubbed some of the unnecessary(IMO) rubber material on the shoe.    The KSO EVO features the same closed-loop bungee and velcro strap as other LS shoes for FiveFingers (minus the Seeya LS and Speed, which have traditional laces). With the lace system, the the KSO EVO should be able to accommodate a wider range of foot shapes, including those with flat feet (like mine) and high arches.    I also found that the KSO EVO does not look quite as \\"strange\\" as the EL-X because the lace system and tongue of the shoe makes it a little taller, where-as the EL-X is a very low attention-getting shoe.    I find the lace system that Vibram uses to be far superior to traditional laces. There is no need to tie and knot floppy laces; just grab the bungee, dial in the right fit, slap the plastic but onto the velcro strip and you are good to go!    If there was any issue that I found with the lace system is that the opening of the shoe and tongue is not as large as other Vibram LS shoes. Whereas I am able to quickly slip into my Bikila LS, the KSO EVO requires a bit of a struggle to get into it at first, but it becomes easier as you break in the shoe. In addition, the reinforced leather portions of the shoe around the collar and heel are not stretchy, so that also makes it a little more difficult to get the shoes on.    Overall, the lace system is absolutely perfect for finding a perfect fit for a variety of feet. You will wonder why you bothered with velcro or traditional laces in the past.    The KSO EVO has a similar sole to the EL-X. They are both part of the \\"max feel\\" category from Vibram, alongside the women's Alitza. They all feature a zig-zagging, sliced up Vibram rubber sole that provides good traction in a variety of surfaces and is miles ahead of the smooth sole of the original KSO.    With the \\"max feel\\" line, Vibram has truly put itself back ahead of other \\"barefoot\\" shoes in terms of flexibility and ground feel.The KSO EVO has a \\"max sole thickness\\" of 4.7mm which includes a 2mm EVA foam insole in the figure and something like a 2.7mm Vibram rubber outsole. The EVA compresses pretty quickly and will begin to mold itself to the shape of the bottom of your foot after running just a few miles, making the overall stack height of the shoe even lower as a result.    With such thin soles, both the KSO EVO and EL-X are very floppy and you can roll them up in any direction with a single finger. You can even roll up one shoe and cram it into it's opposite (but not, like, evil version), if you so choose to. While all vibrams allow you to flex your toes up, only the EL-X and KSO EVO (and the KSO Remix) allow for you to flex your toes down, which is an amazing feeling and a testament to how thin and flexible the shoes are.    Ground feel with the KSO EVO is fantastic. You can feel every little thing as you run, including tiny pebbles and even the stems of leaves as you jog to your heart's desire. The sole provides just enough protection, while maintaining a near-barefoot experience. Because the sole is so thin, it can help you figure out proper running form and technique. By comparison, when I run in my Bikila LS shoes, I definitely notice that I can land a little harder because of the extra padding that the Bikila has over the KSO EVO.    I will caution that the KSO EVO may not be a good choice for those who are looking to transition into minimalist running as its thin sole does not allow for a lot of room for error in running form. If you heel step in the KSO EVO, you will hurt yourself. Something like the KMD or Bikila may be better suited for anyone planning to make the transition from bulkier shoes to Vibrams, while the KSO EVO is more of a shoe for barefoot enthusiasts looking to hone their barefoot technique.    The Heel  The single best improvement the KSO EVO made over the EL-X (aside from the lace system) is in the heel fit. Vibram greatly enhanced the sections that wrap around your heel to make the KSO EVO a fantastic shoe for running and making sharp turns. In the comparison photos between the EL-X and KSO EVO, you can clearly see that Vibram added additional height to the heel and structure to the \\"wings\\" on either side of the heel (See this photo), which really hugs the back of your foot and completely eliminates the heel sloppiness you may experience when running with the EL-X or Seeya.    When running with the EL-X, I was constantly reminded of the heel as it moved up and down with every step (luckily, no hot spots ever developed). Despite that issue, the shoe was adequate for running in a straight line at moderate speeds, but the EL-X was definitely a let down if I ever had to quickly move around. With the improvements found in the KSO EVO, I can confidently run and make turns as quickly as I please.    The lace system and the heel \\"wings\\" are a perfect combination for security, stability, and a glove-like fit with the KSO EVO.    Durability  I have not had enough time with the KSO EVO to assess the durability of its upper or sole, but I've run about 100 miles with the EL-X and it's held up perfectly with zero issues and the sole has yet to show any wear. By comparison, my pair of Bikila LS have--all things considered--held up very well after about 750 miles, but they did sprout a small hole on the inside of the big toe, which I was able to patch with some shoe goo and about 40% of the treading has worn away around the outer toes and the ball of the foot.    Vibram has really outdone itself this time around. I was initially skeptical when I heard that they were replacing the beloved KSO with the EL-X-based KSO EVO. All of the skepticism was swept aside after I went on my first run with them.    The KSO EVO strikes a balance between the fit and security of the Bikila LS, the heel tightness of the KMD, and the thin and flexible sole of the EL-X. The improvements Vibram made on the EL-X were absolutely fantastic and it has becomemy new favorite running and gym shoe. My only regret was that the KSO EVO was not available in black at the time of writing this review.

product_title: Bed Stu Women's Gogo Boot
review_headline: In Search of the Perfect Boot
review_body:
I love boots and am always on the search for the perfect boot. I'd say these are the closest I've come to finding the perfect boot. I love how the leather on these is already \\"broken in\\". They are soft and flexible like I've worn them for years. The first time I put them on, they felt like an old friend. I wore them all day to a craft festival and they did not hurt my feet and did not leave a blister. No break-in period needed! I got compliments on them all day long and many asked where I got them. They just have that expensive, designer look.

I did order a half size up from my normal size in a shoe because I like to wear socks with my boots. They fit perfectly and were very roomy, even with socks, so I'm not sure going up a half size was necessary. My legs have shape and the top was plenty wide for me.

I love the look, the feel, and the fit. Are they the perfect boot? The only thing I'd change to make them \\"perfect\\" is to make them a bit taller. I made some boot cuffs to wear at the top to fill in the gap to my knee and was happy with the look. I highly recommend these and even considered getting a second pair to keep in case something happened to these. I love them that much!

review_headline: Comfortable but they TURNED PURPLE IN TWO MONTHS!

Very disappointed! My other Born shoes are five years old now and they still look good -- a bit worn, but not faded out like these. I will definitely be contacted the vendor to see if these can be replaced. Unacceptable to pay nearly $100 for shoes that \\"wear out\\" within 8 weeks! Especially when I only wear these shoes only a few hours each week!

Several pics uploaded that show the \\"new\\" shoes compared with my 5 year old pair. The 5 year old pair looks used but still in very good condition, while the 2 month old pair looks ancient and ready to fall apart!

If I stood on my tippy toes when wearing the sandals, the strap slipped right off the back, even on the tightest setting. It's just an odd shoe layout, if you ask me. I returned them in favor of another pair of Keens.

Comfort wise, I thought they were mostly fine. There's certainly the Keen padding in the foot bed that you'd expect! review_body: I bought a pair of Hi-Tec shoes about 4 years ago at my local Dunham's store because they were on sale and seemed like a decent shoe for the price. review_body: These were a gift for my son. He is very pleased with them. They are fur lined and therefor nice and warm. They are a bit on the narrow side so if you guys have a wide foot just keep that in mind.

review_body: I've always wanted a pair of cowboy boots, and didn't want to spend a lot on first pair in case I didn't find them comfortable. They fit great and way more comfortable than I expected. product_title: Baggallini Transport Carryall Shoulder Bag
review_body: I bought this as an everyday carryall for my dance clothes and was not disappointed.  This is a very spacious bag with numerous compartments and is very, very light.  It stays on my shoulder without falling and has two outside compartments for drinks & umbrella. I had also wanted a waterproof bag with a top zipper in case of rain. I am keeping the longer strap inside, in case I need it.  On the whole, I am happy with this bag and its looks.  My only regrets is that It is a little larger than I need and does have the appearance of a small piece of luggage,  rather than a large tote.

product_title: Aquatalia Women's Starry Riding Boot
review_body: I gave this boot a 5 star rating because of the quality of the leather, the comfort of the fit in the foot and the substantial lug soles.  It runs true to size and easily allows jeans to fit inside the boot.  The elastic fabric that accommodates different sized calves is pretty discreet - - You are not aware of a whole lot of fabric, it's just enough.  The zipper worked well and made it easy to slip the boots on and off.  The rounded toe also makes for a comfortable fit.  The brown is a beautiful chocolate tone and would go with any color.  These are definitely on the casual side as far as style is concerned.  However, it's important to keep in mind that these are truly an all weather boot and compromise a little where sleek design is concerned.  I could, however wear them to work or most places my boring life takes me.  The one negative is that the leather is prone to scuffing, probably because it's so soft and flexible.  Also, the ankle area tends to wrinkle a bit if you have thin ankles.  Heavy socks should take care of  that problem.

product_title: Cole Haan Men's Lenox Hill Cap Oxford
review_body: Great build and the shipping was top notch. Beautiful shoe and with the sale the price was great. Gotta love Cole Haan!

product_title: DV by Dolce Vita Women's Janna Wedge Sandal
review_body: The shoes fit perfect! I had these shoes last year (2013) and wore them OUT! I was so excited to find them on Amazon and at a GREAT price!

review_body: Bought these for my daughter who usually wears a mens 7.5 . I would suggest getting one size larger than your normal size.

review_body: My first pair lasted almost a year, and when I say lasted I mean the insulation layer at the bottom moved around like a cheap pillow, its unbearable to wear and walk with them on. review_body: I have been ordering New Balance shoes for years from appos in size 13 for both the velcro and shoestring type shoes and have sent them back.  This is the first time for this problem.

product_title: Orla Kiely Ella Bag Shoulder Bag
review_body: So I got this bag on Friday 2/21.  I love it's cheerful print.  Some folks have said that it is a coated cotton, but it actually says vinyl on the card.  Love that it is lined, with an interior zipper pocket and two slightly different size cell phone pockets on the opposite wall.  Two large outside pockets, one on either side.  It is a fairly large bag and somewhat heavy to carry, I am used to my Vera Bradley bags.  What I don't like is that the outside pockets gap somewhat when you fill the inside.  I will use them for paperwork and nothing very bulky.  Not really sure what I think about the little leather closure on the two outside pockets, maybe after using it for a while it won't be so hard to get the hang of those.  Never seen anything like it before.  I use this bag as a basic purse, work bag.  Though it is great to take back and forth to work, it is too huge and heavy to carry during a long day of shopping.  I have a Vera Bradley wristlet that is fairly small that I will carry inside it for the necessity's like a couple of check blanks, debit card, credit card, cash, cell phone. I love the tiny little leather pocket on the front, it is very cute and mostly just adds interest since it is too small to actually put anything in other than an earing or a quarter. :)  Some of the Orla Kiely bags aren't lined so I was glad to see this was.  The gold hardware is lovely and I appreciate that it has a cross body strap and I was pleasantly surprised to find an Orla Kiely dust cover bag included inside the bag when it came.  I also love the little elastic keyfob thingy inside it but it really isn't practical for me,  I bet someone out there has a great idea for what else I can use it for though.  All and all, I have only had it for a day but it seems to be a fairly well made bag with cute details and just enough organization to keep me happy.

product_title: Bearpaw Women's Tama Rabbit Fur Boots
review_body: These boots were a little stiff at first, and I was concerned that they were too tight taking on and off, but they loosened up in no time. We had a harsh winter this year in Indiana and these boots were perfect. They are very comfortable for walking. They are very warm, so I would suggest taking an extra pair of shoes if you're going to be inside, say grocery shopping, or at the mall, for a long time. They are very stylish and look great over a pair of jeans, even if you're a little stocky like me. There are fur balls that hang on the side of each boot (pictured), and they are really cute when you just want to make a fashion statement, but they are an annoyance when you're walking in high snow. I tried tying them up higher, but they don't stay tied. I hope I can figure out a way to shorten them, if not, I may have to cut them off.

review_headline: 1st pair Defective but will try a replacement just in case
review_body: First off these shoes are adorable and seem like they were made for my daughter, who's 5 and loves everything rainbow/sparkly/shiny/glittery.  We got the black/multi color. That's not a complaint, just trying to share in case someone finds this helpful.  On day 1 of wearing them, the right shoe's top 2 lights got stuck on... they wouldn't turn off.  The rest of the right shoe's lights did not turn on after this, so only her left shoe had the motion lights when walking.  On the "bright" side, we had a new nightlight in the room.  Day 3 the lights are still stuck on.  Also on day 3, the left shoe's first Velcro strap broke in half... the glitter top part separated from the bottom part.  I contacted Amazon and they were quick to help.  They are sending us a replacement free of charge and have upgraded the shipping.  I hope the second pair works out better and will update this accordingly with a higher review.  We may just have gotten a defective pair.

product_title: Kamik Women's Jennifer Rain Boot
review_body:
Love these boots!! I have athletic calves (16in) and these work great so far with my leggings and even a pit of jeggings. That being said I gave them only four stars because after the first time wearing them I noticed the front on one has scuffs that I haven't been able to get off that were caused by the sole of the other boot rubbing against it. I wish they had made the soles non-marking so this didn't occur but it's not the end of the world.
For anyone saying these aren't really wide calf, if you do research standard boot circumference is 12-14 inches. Anything 15-16 inch in circumference IS by standard shoe sizing considered wide calf. If you have a calf larger than that you'll have to search for boots that are considered extra wide calf.

product_title: Nike Benassi Swoosh Men's Slide
review_body: Length-wise these were true to size (I wear a size 12) but they are a much too narrow for me.  I literally have to squeeze my foot into them and then tap on a wall to further get them in all the way.  I figured wearing them for a week or two would stretch them out but they didn't stretch one bit and left my feet aching.  I don't believe that ordering a size up would have fixed the problem either - I just think they're not wide enough.  For the record, I don't have wide/fat feet either and I'm not a big guy (I'm 6'1" 190 lbs).  Don't get me wrong, the overall quality of these are very good.  They are very well made and I could see them lasting a long time.  If you're looking for a tight fit then go ahead and order these...otherwise I wouldn't recommend them.

I did not try to return them, I just took my loss and learned my lesson.
Robert Lawson, Ft. Worth, Texas

review_body: It pained me to pay this much for boots, it really did. But I've sucked it up and paid for La Canadienne boots before, and always ended up being glad I did. This pair is no exception -- comfortable, stylish, warm, great arch support. Tempted to wear them every day. I would rather buy one pair of really fabulous, versatile boots a year than a bunch of mediocre ones that make my feet hurt. I was glad I spent the money on these.

product_title: Baggallini Triple Zip Bagg
review_body: I love this little bag.  The color is lovely and it's quality made.  I love the long shoulder strap and all the zippered compartments!

product_title: Anuschka 1071 Wallet
review_headline: Cheers me up even though I'm spending money
review_body: I bought this wallet for myself because my tired, plain brown one wore out.  It is very cheery, well made and has just the right number of card slots for my purposes.  It's important to look at several styles of these wallets before you decide what will work for you, but all the designs are beautiful.  Even though this wallet was expensive, I'm sure I'll have it for many years.

product_title: Merrell Women's Mimosa Lace
review_body:
The shoe rubs hard against my ankles and heel bones. I haven't been able to wear them for longer than a couple hours because I know it will make me blister and bleed. This is very disappointing- I waited for MONTHS to buy these with my tax return only to find out that they hurt! The inside of the shoe fits fine, but for some reason the rim is really hard and tight.. and it doesn't stretch so you can't kick the shoes off when they are tied.

These were going to be my new all-the-time sneakers. Not only that, they were supposed to be my first great-quality sneakers not bought from Payless. Now I will have to return them.
Very VERY disappointed.

review_body: Fits like any nimbus shoe.  I had the 13s and loved them.  The 15s are just like its predecessor only getting better over time.  In training for a half marathon and run on both treadmills and street.  These keep my knees in tact.

review_body:
i have these and some inspire 9
the outer material of the inspire 8 is more firm then inspire 9
the inspire 9 were easier to break in
i alternate days of shoe wearing between these the inspire 9 and an asics pair
after 2 weeks the inspire 8 still have not broken in and hurt

product_title: Stride Rite Soft Motion Bambi Sneaker (Infant/Toddler)
review_headline: Great shoe but runs a little small
review_body: I was looking for a gage in sizing and couldn't find a review with the info I was looking for so hopefully this will help someone out.  My daughter was 12 and a half months when I purchased these with pretty average size feet, width wise.  They measure about 4.5" and is generally a 4 toddler shoe size.  I purchased the 4 regular and they were tiny, she could barely fit her feet into them.  So I returned them and ordered a 5 regular.  These are about a half inch too long and fit snug width wise which I think it should. I'll keep these to avoid the trouble but if I needed the perfect fit, I probably should have ordered the 4.5 regular.  If you are worried they will be too snug, go for the wide fit.

product_title: Badgley Mischka Women's Goodie Peep-Toe Pump
review_body: I purchased these shoes for my wedding day. The bling on the right shoe is slightly to the left instead of in the middle, but it doesn't really show. Definitely worth the price! After reading some reviews, I purchased them a half size smaller and they fit perfectly. Super comfy and definitely worth the dollar!

product_title: Vasque Men's Sundowner Gore-Tex Waterproof Backpacking Boot
review_body: These are the only boots I will buy.  I worked in construction for 10yrs.  After trying multiple brands of works boots, I went back to the classic hiker I wore in high school. product_title: Ariat Men's Rambler Flint Boot
review_headline: The Flint is going to need a breaking in period.
review_body:
Very Rustic and attitude driven appearance. Although a little narrow, I am very happy with the fit , comfort and like the darkening tan towards the toe for a really great look.
Good feel of control while walking. I bought two pairs with one click at 30% off regular Amazon price. I write this review into the second week of wearing them, and am very satisfied. For the time being I will break these in wearing a very thin soc.

product_title: Dr. Martens Unisex Wonder Balsam Shoe Polish
review_headline: Good product for keeping everyday leather looking nice
review_body:
This product conditions leather and substitutes for polish in many cases, at least if you're dealing with every day shoes (Docs, Blundstones, oxfords) as opposed to something you'd wear in a black tie situation, where you might want a high shine. I've used it on everyday shoes and bags and it has softened them and made the leather look new.

It may alter the shade slightly, but doesn't change the color beyond this.

It won't cover marks. If you have serious scuffs or marks then you might want something with a color instead.

product_title: kate spade new york Sedgwick Place Lacey Wallet
review_body: I absolutely love this wallet.  I have been looking for a great-looking and yet roomy wallet for forever and finally found it with this one.  It is very pretty and has a ton of compartments.  The quality is great and sturdy as well.

product_title: Ladies' Itasca 200 Gram Pull-on Boots Navy
review_headline: Longest wearing pair of boots EVER
review_body: I have had these boots (blue - exactly the ones in the picture) for 12 years.  I LOVE them.  You do have to get one size up as they run small (otherwise I think you would get the ankle chafing some others have talked about).  They are so warm I only have to wear them with a light pair of socks or even stockings to work!  I bought my son a brown pair at the same time, and he is much harder on them than I am...his are still in perfect shape as well! Just amazing.  I'll never own another brand as long as they make these, and what a price!

product_title: Mens Under Armour Micro G Renegade Mid Running Shoe Black/Black/Metallic Silver
review_headline: Great running shoe with one serious downfall....
review_body: This shoe felt great from the first time that I put it on.  Very light, breathable, and stable.  Run 10-15 miles per week and this shoe always performed very well.  The only problem is that the shoe wears out quickly.  In five months of wearing this shoe only to run in, I started getting shin splints indicating the insole and sole were wearing out beyond use.  Furthermore the strap that goes across the top of your foot started ripping out of the stitching.  Overall a great shoe but it wears out faster than it should.

product_title: Dockers Men's Trustee Oxford

review_body: I had to return these shoes for a smaller size; which I am waiting to arrive. The show is nice, and feel comfortable, although since they were too big it's hard to tell.

Thinking of getting red too. Very happy with these.

product_title: Pajar Women's Aventure Boot
review_headline: not *quite* what I was looking for.
review_body: I really wanted to love these boots, but I was hoping for something with more structure in the foot. Otherwise I liked the boot, and could have gotten used to it if it weren't for the fact that I was sent the light brown boot in the black boot box.. alas, the combination of the odd color and the odd fit was too much for me.

product_title: Luichiny Women's Whoa Girl Bootie
review_headline: Nice Boots with a Big Caveat
review_body:
When I received these, I loved the boot but hated the decorative leather and chain link at the top of them. I thought it made them look cheap. However, I liked everything else about them so much that I decided to take matters into my own hands. I cut off the offending leather and chain so that all that is left from it are 2 small leather nibs on the inside of the boot. Now it looks like they came that way. With the offending hardware gone, the boot looks classic and clean; could pass for very expensive boots.

I would have given it 5 stars, however the handful of times I wore them, they can be a challenge to walk in. They are VERY high. I live in high heels and joke that I was born in them, but for some reason, there is a bit of the teeter walk with these. Look great with black leggings. Will have to spend more time walking in them to get used to the height.

product_title: Skechers Sport Women's Heirloom Glimmer Bungee Sneaker
review_body: Spongy feel on the foot. Feels like youre walking on clouds. Love Sketchers, have got many pairs and they never let you down

product_title: Sanita Women's Ditto Boot
review_headline: Cutest and Most Comfortable Boots EVER!!
review_body:
I have been wearing Dansko shoes for a year now. I ordered my first pair here on Amazon. They fit perfectly, are very comfortable (I stand on my feet all day for work), are cute too! I get compliments on my shiny black Dansko shoes all the time.

Well, someone who wears Dansko's told me about their boots! I ordered THREE pair of Dansko's last week - these boots and two others. I wanted to change up my shoes, as I was wearing the same shoes all the time, even at home. I have bad knees and bone spurs. Without the use of all these Dansko shoes, I would not be able to work, walk or stand.

I very highly recommend these and any other Dansko shoes to anyone!

product_title: RYKA Women's Exertion Shoe
review_headline: Order on 1/2 size larger than normal
review_body: Shoes fit great because read the review that stated to buy larger than normal size. I appreciate the fact that some did take the time to write the review and let us know that the shoes did run a bit small. They are light and great for working out and walking in.

product_title: Wolverine Men's Hudson W02194 Work Boot
review_headline: Poor quality. Be careful they are NOT water-proof
review_body: These boots worked ok  in a dry  environment, but I often walk in places with sleet on the ground and found out that water is leaking inside. So if you have to work in places with water or sleet on the ground I definitely NOT recommend them. I would not have expected this by a company like Wolverine, so it's last time ever that I buy their boots. PS And by they way they are not made in the US

product_title: Jambu Women's Napa Mary Jane Pump

Thanks to EMU for making these cause you cant ever find ugg ones in your size

product_title: Capezio Women's 459 Suede Sole Jr. Footlight Character Shoe

product_title: Spring Step Women's Tayla Mary Janes

product_title: Eastland Women's Kelsey,Brown,8 M US
review_body: This is my 2nd pair of Eastland shoes and I love the fit and comfort! I will definitely keep buying Eastlands.

product_title: Teva Women's De La Vina Boot

product_title: Skechers Performance Women's On-The-Go Chugga Bootie
review_body: I've hardly taken these off since I got them!  In the middle of a long Denver cold snap, warm & comfortable boots are a treasure.  These have a springy and comfy sole, are warm and easy to wear.  Great find!

product_title: Aquatalia Women's Operate Riding Boot
review_body: This boot runs slightly long, since the 10 fit my foot perfectly, and my feet measure 10.5. I think the low, but not completely flat, heel is perfect for a casual boot -- a bit more flattering to the leg and giving more arch support. However, I didn't like the way the shaft looked on my leg. It fit because of the stretch, but emphasized the heaviness of my 16" calf. I returned them. In the future, I plan to buy only non-stretch boots and have my shoemaker stretch the calves enough to be slightly loose in the calf and at the top.

product_title: El Naturalista Women's N007 Boot
review_body: Great price and lovely product, but i will be giving them to my daughter in law as they are a bit too small

product_title: Sorel Women's Winter Fancy Boot

review_body:

My only problem is that after wearing the boots for only 2 days, the bottom sole started to separate from the shoe. I feel that if I'm paying almost $100 for boots, I shouldn't have to worry about that.

product_title: Havaianas Women's Top Flip Flop,Fuchsia,37 BR/7-8 M US

product_title: Muk Luks Women's Scuff Slipper
review_headline: Bought a pair for someone else, and then bought a pair for me :)

product_title: 5.11 Tactical A.T.A.C.  8" Shield Boot
review_body:
I worked at Pulaski Regional Detention Facility (jail in Little Rock) for 6 years. I tried a few different boots, including Bates and Converse, but I kept coming back to 5.11. They look great, feel great, and last forever. They have great grip and the sole on my first pair lasted almost two years. This is saying something, as my fiends and I wore pedometers and sometimes logged around eight miles in an eight-hour shift. I actually went through inserts and laces quicker than the boots.

Now though, I work at a factory. As a sworn deputy, I was not allowed to wear protective toe shoes, and now I am required to. I normally wear a size 11 with normal width in 5.11. When I ordered 11s in these though, I found the protective toe box was too small. I tried a few pair until I found I had to go up to 12 wide to make it work, so if you have semi-big toes, these will probably run small on you too. For the shoe itself, the laces have to go immediately. The factory laces don't have grip and slip during wear almost immediately, making tight spots on your ankles and lower legs. Swapping out for a $2 pair of 60" Kiwi laces at Wal-Mart fixed this problem. I need arch support, and these have none, so I had to get inserts. I sometimes have to fight the side zipper up and down, but the last few didn't have this problem.

Lastly, I've seen one or two people complain about the water proofing on this boot. Honestly, I don't see how. The tongue is stitched to the side all the way up to the top of the boots, so it won't get in. The water proofing 5.11 added to the boot is fantastic and lasts. The factory I work at now makes frozen foods, and I get all kinds of tomato paste, garlic puree, and grease from cooked meat on them. On each break and when I leave, I spray them off with a high pressure hose and go.

review_body:
I've played soccer for over 30 years. I've also habitually used sandals for over 20 years. Hey, I'm from California, it happens. I even wear them to work (startups).

I love non-thong sports sandals. These have the advantage over regular plastic/synthetic soccer sandals of having a little more ventilation, thus allowing feet to dry off easier after matches. They aren't perfect, though, and sweat can build up. It does not soak into the cushioned material, as I thought it might.

Speaking of the cushion -- it's remarkable. When you've played three hours on Saturday morning, it's perfect way to relax the feet when coming home and starting on house chores :)

When used for all day activities they tend to start "rubbing" on my feet and cause some very slight discomfort. This is after 8 hours or so. My "Tevas" never had this problem -- probably because they were meant for long term use. I suppose not having the support strap on the back causes this issue, so it is really not what they are meant for.

product_title: Clarks Men's Portland 2 Easy Slip-On
review_headline: These are slightly large, but I was aware of this from Amazon customer reviews and was able to order the correct size for me

I prefer the look of the [[ASIN:B002WWT6B8 Clarks Unstructured Men's Un.Ravel Casual Oxford]] for work in an office environment, but these Clarks \\"Portland 2 Easy Slip-On\\" are really comfortable and I think are okay for less formal office environments. They are as comfortable as wearing a pair of hard soled slippers!

As other Amazon customer reviews have mentioned, the Clarks sizes run slightly large. Since I was aware of this from Amazon customer reviews, I was able to order the correct size for me

I have WIDE feet. In high school I wore Men's 9 1/2, but as I have aged my feet have gotten wider and I have had to go as large as size 11 to get a wide enough shoe. This means a typical shoe is way too long for me in order to get an acceptable width.

For size comparison, I wear:
- \\"New Balance\\" tennis shoes, which are about the widest tennis shoes I can find, in size 10 Extra Wide
- [[ASIN:B008JBNG7G Reebok Men's Pheehan Running Shoe]], in size 10 4E
- and most other shoes in a 10 1/2 Wide.
- For these \\"Portland 2 Easy Slip-On\\" I would say my \\"perfect fit\\" is somewhere in between 9 1/2 and 10 in the 3E. The 10 3E is a little long for me, the 9 1/2 3E is a little narrow and short for me. Both sizes are comfortable enough that I could wear them without a problem.

After my first pair of [[ASIN:B002WWT6B8 Clarks Unstructured Men's Un.Ravel Casual Oxford]] arrived, I liked them so much I bought the same shoes in another color; as well as these Clarks \\"Portland\\".

I would say that you can get away with buying these shoes a little on the small side because they are INCREDIBLY soft, right out of the box. The opening is tight, as these are slip-ons, but the leather in the toe box feels more like a pair of leather dress gloves than shoe leather.

product_title: Skull and Flowers Wallet
review_headline: Great for people who used to be spooky but who don't get out much to the clubs these days
review_body:

Cons:
- the change pocket is HORRIBLY small. Will not hold more than a few coins at a time. And DO NOT try to get change out of it if you are in any kind of hurry at all, as it will likely cause you to scatter your change all over the floor (has happened to me multiple times).
- the ID area is very tight, making it difficult to get my ID out
- is kind of huge (I hate carrying a purse, but I do it anyway; it fits well in my purse, but wouldn't fit in 3 pants pockets, so there's no way I'd carry it without a purse)

I'm quite fond of this wallet in spite of the items I listed as cons, but with wallets I tend to be more concerned with aesthetics than function. And as aesthetics go, It's sort of... spooky-classy, in a grandma way. The image will help you memento mori and all of that without getting all morose and mopey about it. It is actually quite a tranquil image, and it seems odd for it to be on a wallet, but think about the times you are using a wallet. You could probably use some tranquility during those times, right? Unless of course you need change; the frustration of pulling out change will destroy that tranquility pretty quickly. I eventually just bought a separate change purse.

product_title: Propet Men's Blizzard Ankle Zip Boot
review_headline: Just remember it is a boot, not a shoe!
review_body:
Propet has created footwear that I did not know I needed: an ankle zip boot. I found this boot when I was looking for something to replace my aging hikers. It was waaay below zero outside when I ran across Propet's appropriately named 'Blizzard.' Perfect, I thought and pushed the order button. I own another pair of Propet shoes, so I trusted that the fit would be accurate, I liked the fact that the insulation is Thinsulate by 3M, and the rubber toe combined with a leather (breathable) upper make this boot look terrific.

I am thoroughly satisfied with the fit and blown away by the warmth. Confession: I live in Minnesota and the winter of 2012-2013 has been brutal. That minus 20 temp reading the day I ordered these seems to have become the norm and the snow that has accompanied the cold is nothing short of memorable. In the 10 days that I have owned these boots I have blown our 150 foot curved driveway at least three times (along with attendant shoveling). That means that these boots have gotten a workout, along with me. They pass with five stars. My feet are warm and dry, and I the grip from the treaded sole is incredible.

The only draw back to these boots is that they are not a shoe. By that I mean that, though I have been wearing them as a shoe for everything from grocery shopping to runs to the bowling alley, they are a bit heavy and clunky for that duty. But when you want your feet to be warm and dry, and you don't want to slip slide away, they can't be beat. Highly recommended!

product_title: Brooks Men's PureDrift Lightweight Running Shoes
review_headline: Great Racing Shoe - these are like track spikes for road running
review_body: Although I shouldn't have, I ran a half marathon race in these the day after I bought them because they felt so good.  I achieved a PR even though I was less prepared for the race than usual.  I believe I did well because these shoes are really built for forefoot running, which naturally encourages a faster pace.  I am naturally a forefoot runner but in longer races I tend to fall back into the bad habit of running on my heels.  These shoes don't let you do that.  The downside of not taking more time to get used to them was that my calves burned at the end of the race, because forefoot running relies more heavily on the calves/achilles/foot arch (like jump roping).  If you are a heel striker and like a heavily cushioned heel, don't buy these.  However, if you want to be a better runner, I would encourage you to gradually get away from heel running and transition to forefoot running, which is not only faster but also less impact on the joints.  These shoes can help you make that transition, but do it more gradually than I did, because you need to build up the strength of the calves/achilles/foot arch.  Although I prefer these for races, I train in them too, especially for speed interval training.  I've started jump roping in them too.  I do wish they would make the tread on the outside forefoot more durable.  That's the irony of these minimalist shoes--they are built for forefoot running but still make the tread most durable in the heel (go figure).

review_headline: Asics Shoes are the Best Shoe on the Market today.
review_body: I have had feet problems since returning from the jungles of Viet Namn. I was a door gunner on the Spook and was outside on the platform and it took a direct hit from ground fire. My feet went numb for a few seconds and then the pain set in. As anyone was there if they can patch you up for any kind of duty they will. When I got got back to our Base of Operations I went and had my feet x-rayed. Two broken toes on the right one on the left. They had started to heal, from where the Medic on board the A/C had taped them together with another toe. They decided to not re-break the toes, but gave me walking casts and sent back to duty on my A/C. I have had several surgeris on my feet, including amupating two of them. Asics has been a "God Send" for me. The best support, comfort, wear and not braggin g but I have bought over 20 pairs of Asics. Only one I had trouble with as the size was smaller than expected and it binded my feet and I gave them to my son who loved them, now he owns 4 pairs. Asics also has relieved a lot of lower back pain for me and to put Asics Shoes in one word it would be "AWESOME". I will continue to buy these shoes and have set aside of one pair, my favorite of all I have ever ordered to wear to the next world when I leave this place.

product_title: Superfeet GREEN Full Length Insole
review_body: I am a moderate over-pronator who wears these in all my athletic shoes.  I went to a specialty sports store (NOT a big chain, but a local shop that offers gait analysis and recommendations for sneakers for your specific type of activity you're doing) and was fitted with the green pair.  It is important to order the correct color to get the correct degree of correction, and I recommend seeing a professional to get that done BEFORE ordering off Amazon.  However, once you get fitted, there is no reason you can't order your replacement pairs here because they do wear out after about a year of moderate use (my husband gets maybe 6 months use out of his and he puts about 30 to 40 miles a week on his sneakers; I in turn do about 10 to 20 miles a week on my sneakers and got almost a year out of mine).  They have saved my feet and legs from an untimely suffering of shin splints and knee pain, but note: these are not miracle cures!  You must pair them with the correct pair of shoes to get the right degree of support necessary to correct your pronation.  The other thing you must remember is, if you are purchasing these as a remedy from shin splints/knee pain/leg pain/etc, you must wait to heal completely before you can begin your running/exercise regimen again.  But I love Superfeet.  They have saved me the costly process of getting custom orthodics since I'm only a moderate over-pronator, and I am very happy with them.  Highly recommended!

product_title: Dr. Weil by Orthaheel Aida
review_body: I like these shoes.  I have worn Orthaheel/Vionic and Dr. Weil brands for a few years now because I have a very high arch and suffer from plantar fasciitis as well as what I think is called Morton's Neuroma - the pain in between the joints near the ball of the foot.  Anyway, suffice it to say that I am kinda picky with my shoes, because I don't like being in pain all day.  These shoes have excellent support.  Excellent!  The arch, heel cup, and even the ball of foot area is balanced and really good.  They are firm.  Even for this brand.  These are a cork foot bed with leather on top, think birkenstalk-type footwear.  The shape is different, but that is the "hardness" of it.  They look a little bit like those too.  So if you want/need a lot of "squish" or padding in a shoe, this isn't it.  But, they do support the right part of your feet, and I find that my feet feel good in them, even after walking and standing.  I don't get hot spots of pain and I feel like my whole foot is supported and the weight is spread out like it should be.  The shoe is very stable; your feet stay put, and you're not going to flop an ankle over with these.  They have a roomy toe box, and the fit is maybe slightly large...I usually wear a 7 in "regular" shoes (a 6 in Orthaheel), but in these I'd probably have been good with a 6.5, except that they don't have half sizes.  That said, the 7s don't fall off or anything, they are just roomy, and easily accommodate socks.  I don't have wide feet, so if you do, this might be a great feature.  My issue, and the main reason they didn't get 5 stars, is that they could be cuter.  They do rather look like birkenstalks, which isn't quite the look I was going for, but given that I'm comfortable, I can deal with it.  The materials are high quality, and I'm not having any issues with breaking them in or anything like that.  I think it's a quality shoe with good support.  I'll report back if anything catastrophic goes wrong with them over time.

product_title: Salomon Women's XR Mission Running Shoe
review_body:
I dealt with a lot of ankle twisting in years past but these shoes have served me well & I have not had any injuries in the 2 years I've been running in them. They have a very big base and they are also very flexible and light. Landed on a rock? Instead of your ankle twisting horribly off to one side, the shoes' soles bend around it and you are on your way. I run on trails and my treadmill. I never get rocks or other debris in my shoes, and that happens with all the other shoes I have. I am a sloppy runner at times and interfere sometimes (my shoes sometimes hit my ankles of the other foot) so this is important to me. I love that the lacing is no-fuss. I literally slip these on. They have incredibly tacky soles. I never slip or slide in them. I ran 4 miles on snowy (1-2" of snow) trails today and they did really well. They also have a very generous toe box, which is nice for me because I have narrow feet but they get wider up through my toes and I need the extra room. My feet get hot but you can literally feel the air going through these shoes. On the other hand, I have run in them all winter long (in the teens and above) and I just wear wool socks.
I also do endurance riding w/ my horses, and these double as my go-to shoes for that as well. I can ride 50 miles comfortably with very little ankle, knee, or pain in the ball of my feet..
I wear them everywhere---grocery shopping, riding, to the barn, driving, and, well, running.
Don't hesitiate to buy them. Just bought my second pair that will take me through 1014.

product_title: Foot Sox Original Sanitary Disposable Try on Socks
review_headline: Thin, but they do what they're suppose to do
review_body: I actually did not purchase these for using on feet. Some years ago, I was trying on shoes before I headed out on a road trip and as I was grabbing a foot sox some of them fell on the floor so I gathered them up and slipped 'em in my pocket. Fast forward: shopping's done, car's gassed up, & we're on the freeway where I pull out my knitting...ah, knitting!! Not really, I was fussing with keeping my yarn from skittering around the car. At a rest stop I reached in my pocket for some candy bar change & found the foot sox I'd put in my pocket earlier. Woo hoo, perfect! I put the yarn with which I was working in the little sox & problem solved...no more skittering about the car & even if it did this helped keep it mostly clean. They fit small & medium skeins & balls of all types of yarn, and as the skein is reduced the nylon footie shrinks with it. This brand , and this is the only reason I'm not giving it a 5* rating, doesn't have the bands of thin elastic that my first ones did so the top doesn't really close up the way I like it, but it works! I love that I can wind yarn on my yarn winder & wrap a footie sox around it, take it off & toss it in my bag & no other yarn fibers, crumbs or crap get stuck to it (as long as it's not soda or something else sticky & wet). Another thing is that I can still see what yarn it is :)

product_title: Hi-Tec Men's Altitude IV Waterproof Hiking Boot
review_headline: Back to order another pair after three winters.
review_body:
~Perfect sizing (for me)
~Great mix between being waterproof and breathable
~A little lighter than equivalent boots
~Extremely good grip in slippery conditions
~Very slow tread wear

Ordered 12 2E (12 wide) as that is what I normally purchase and these are true to size. The break-in period is non-existent. They are still extremely comfortable after over two years.

I ordered these in November of 2011 as an everyday winter waterproof boot for delivering mail on walking routes during our snowy WI winters. This is now the third winter and I just now have worn down the outside heels to the point the boots need replacing. I'm glad to see the price is only $2 more than when I first purchased them over two years ago.

As far as "waterproof" I quickly found out long ago that darn near no boot is actually waterproof. The only exception would be ones that offer no breathability - which just cause my feet to become wet from sweat anyway. I found a product (available via Amazon) called Sno-Seal that I melted onto the outside of these boots very liberally and with the careful help of a propane torch. The waterproof-ness is about 8 out of 10 while breathability rates about 9 out of 10. During cold weather I wear liner socks under wool socks and despite severe cold snaps of -15 before wind chill my feet have not become uncomfortably cold.

The only negative I experienced is that during the first winter a small gap appeared between where the rubber from underneath meets the rounded toe, on both shoes. I did not deduct a star because it was nothing a little Shoe Goo couldn't fix.

Buy with confidence: Mailman tested and approved!

review_headline: There's always something new in the pattern that you didn't see before
review_body:
This is a pretty great backpack. It looks small, but actually holds a significant amount of textbooks and binders, and it hasn't shown any signs of wear and tear yet. There's enough pockets for me to store all my supplies. A psychology, calculus, and English textbook later, the straps and seams still seem to be holding up well.

The zippers were surprisingly durable, also. Another bag, similar to this one, had zippers that weren't especially smooth to begin with, but this one was great.

My only issue with this backpack is that the waterbottle pocket is a bit too small to actually fit my waterbottles. If you had a plastic bottle, it's fine, but if you go for ones a little bigger than that, it's a bit more of a struggle to get it in.

It's withheld the elements so far--rain and snow don't seem to affect it much, which is good.

It's a fun backpack. The zippers are rainbow and the pattern of the material makes little to no sense, but that's partially why it's so great. Zoning off in class? Just take a glance at your bag and you'll discover some random picture you'd never noticed before.

I like it, at any rate. A little on the eccentric side, but hey, who doesn't love a little eccentricity every now and then?

review_body:

I normally wear an 8.5 in shoes, but I ordered the 9 to have room for thick socks and tucking in pants. The foot is a little larger than I expected (I have very narrow feet), but the slim ankle prevents you from slipping around in the boot. If you have larger calves, you may have trouble zipping this boot.

The white lining does eventually get discolored, especially if you tuck in dark jeans or other pants. I get compliments on these boots all the time!

product_title: Johnston & Murphy Men's Hutchins Cap Toe Boot
review_body:
Perfect fit, very comfortble, with full leather lining and a high quality of manufacture, and a very elegant, quite slim look. The is latter quite deceiving, since M width IS exactly that, despite the boot looking narrower.

The boot can be worn with a suit as easily as with jeans, and (providing it is polished!) will look equally well in either \\"setting.\\" As with any high quality shoe/boot, I would avoid exposing it to the extremes of weathern (heavy rain, snowy-salty surfaces, etc.) Nonetheless, my boots survived several \\"weather calamities\\" very well, although proper care after each event IS mandatory (shoe trees, good shoe cream, etc. One must remember that Hutchins is not a work boot, and mustn't be treated as such!

Drawbacks? Initially rather stiff leather. However, this turned to be a passing inconvenience: frequent wearing and repeated applications of a high quality shoe polish softened the leather substantially. The verdict: I am highly satisfied with the the boots (whose overall quality readily compares to the similar products by the other two, substantially more epensive, prime US manufacturers whose boots I also wear). In fact, I ended purchasing the black variety of the Hutchins as well, and am equally happy with those.

By all means, worth purchasing!

review_headline: Toasty warm and lightweight boots to the rescue

I've only been wearing these boots for a day and I love them already.

Pros:
-They're lightweight and very warm
- Very easy to get on and off
- I like that the sole and toe is stiff because I don't hurt my little toesies when I kick them against the front step to knock snow off.
- I don't have to wear extra socks if I don't want to; they're plenty warm with my regular trouser socks.
- They're decent to look at!

Slight cons:
- I wear a 9 or a 10 so I bought a 9.5. They're just big enough for me to wear one thick pair of socks; any more and my feet won't fit.

product_title: SORRENTINO Sori Collection Spacious Messenger & Cross Body for Young Women and Girl Handbag
review_headline: Nice but colors wrong, really bad main pocket design, wears poorly
review_body: Agree with the person who said the strap is too short to be cross-body.  I can kind of, sort of, just barely wear it cross-body with the strap at the longest setting, and I'm 5'2".  Color is not as depicted (I ordered turquoise).  I think the seller used the wrong photos to go with the colors they have in stock.  If you look at the item on Amazon listed as "B & D Simple Stylish Cross Body Handbag That Will Never Go Out Of Style" it is exactly the same bag as this but sold in a wider range of colors and with accurate color photos.  When I ordered the item listed as "turquoise" here I got the item labeled "teal" in the "B & D" listing.  Fortunately I love teal and think the color is great.  Fabric is very nice, soft, colorful, and lightweight. Interior organizers like the pen holder are very handy but look like they might not last, since they're just made out of liner.  The main pocket isn't very big but it can hold more than you think because of the zillion exterior pockets, which are very useful for organizing.  In fact the number of pockets is kind of ridiculous, and a couple of the pockets seem like they are probably too small to be that useful.  I do appreciate that there are pockets on both sides of the purse, so I can have two different RFID cards in my purse and they don't interfere with each other.  I wish the main pockets were zippers rather than snaps (personal preference).  The main zippered pocket isn't structurally attached to the interior of the bag, but rather sewn into it as a separate pocket, so you have to hold the bag shut to close the zipper, because the compartment isn't anchored firmly enough to the bag to zip without help -- trying to zip it with one hand the entire compartment tries to pull forward and you would probably tear it out of the bag before you closed the zipper.  Also the zipper extends far past the length of the compartment in this little "tail" --it looks fine when you tuck it into the bag, but it can also come untucked and looks really silly when it gets that way.  Another problem is that the reviewers who say it's hard to put your hand in the main pockets are totally right!  The three main pockets are only divided by liner, not by anything structural, so if you have bulky object like a wallet in one main compartment it will put pressure on the side of the compartment next to it and make it surprisingly difficult to reach into.  I also don't like that there is no mechanism to keep rain out of the two snap-closed main compartments on the top -- not a big deal as it doesn't rain much where I live, but it limits what you can put in those pockets.  Finally, after only one month of use, it shows definite signs of wear.  Two of the zipper pulls have fallen off; I don't even know how that happened, since the pulls appear to be securely attached, but...well, they're clearly not.  Also, any part of the fabric that gets mechanical strain has whitened, including the strap, the tops of several pockets, and in one noticeable place the outline of where I put my passport and it pressed against the edge of the fabric.  UPDATE: After about 18 months of daily use, this purse is pretty much falling apart.  The color layer on the outside is flaking off in many places and revealing the ugly, uncolored fabric underneath.  On the other hand, it was really cheap, so I'm not sure what I expected.

review_headline: im flat footed, needed more support and something wider
review_body:
When I wore this, I noticed that there was something poking on my inner sole. It was the support for my non existent arch. It was supporting the wrong section of my foot. It was nearer the heel than where my arch needs to be.

I love the colors of this shoe that I kept looking for a wide version of this shoe but it wasn't there. I ordered the Mizuno wave inspire 8 too together with this but the same support and the same narrowness was the problem.

In the end I went to my Local running shop. Told them That I would always cramp at mile 9 or 10 in my half marathons. I have done 4. I would always wear normal width shoes and that was a mistake. I have very wide feet and the reason I cramp is because of the tightness in the front that no circulation was going on anymore. They offered me the brooks beast 12 with a width of 2E. And the fit is just about right.

I would suggest people who are going to be running regularly to go a local running shop and let them take a look at your feet. They will watch you run, walk and some other stuff. They will give you a suggestion. Go with that then buy it from them, then go buy your next pairs here. It is better that someone who knows more about shoe fits for a living do you before doing it on your own.

product_title: Otter Wax Fabric & Canvas Wax | Regular Bar | All-Natural Water Repellent | Made in USA
review_headline: Work great to touch up my Levi's
review_body:
I happened into waxed denim from an internet purchase of some Levi's. I knew I liked the appearance of the pictures, they didn't say they were waxed, but after receiving them and researching I realized what I had received.

I loved the jeans. I also read that most people recommend not washing them. The pair I got was a bit big, so I did wash them once on gentle, no soap, and still the waxed finished faded a bit in some spots, and some typical wear spots also appeared in the crotch area, above my back pocket where I keep my wallet, and along the outside seam down the outsides of the legs. My research on Youtube started about what I had and how to fix it.

There were several options and this is the one I settled on. The bar is far smaller than I expected by eyeballing it, but it lasted much longer than I expected. I touched up the entire jeans, front to back, and could probably do so 5 more times with this small bar. That being said, if I order again I will probably order the larger one.

The texture (tack) of the jeans I had were already cured. Adding this made them feel more oily and different-- the beeswax content is apparent by the tack. I froze them first to set, and chose not to do the blow dryer because I don't own one, and because I had no "white".

Freezing first didn't get rid of the tack for me. So I decided to throw them in the dryer for about 5 minutes on low. This did a great job of sealing and removing the tack and smoothing it out and make it more like what I received originally from Levis.

As some other reviewers stated, I couldn't see waxing an entire denim garment with this product. It seems like "dry" denim would take a tremendous amount of this product. I am interested in some of the other soft cream type products meant for this activity and if I try one I will compare it here.

Finally, some people remarked about the smell. I consider this an extremely low fragrance product, and any scent that it does have seem very natural. It has an organic smell, not floral and not spicy, more of a muted saddle soap type smell, or a mild shoe cream smell. Maybe a potato-ish, leather-ish smell. The product contains no animal products, and is a mix of bees wax and plant based oils.oduct, and any scent that it does have seem very natural. It has an organic smell, not floral and not spicy, more of a muted saddle soap type smell, or a mild shoe cream smell. Maybe a potato-ish, leather-ish smell. product_title: 5.11 Men's HRT Advance 6" Boot
review_headline: Excellent boots, Excellent rubber toe guard, Wear better with time
review_body:
I begin by exclaiming my love for these boots. I've never had boots before, let alone shoes that I actually enjoy to wear. The zipper system on these make taking them on or off a breeze. The flexibility from day 1 in these is great, and over the year or so I have had these boots they have just gotten better. They are wearing very nicely with no real pattern or issues with tearing or over wear. I have seen reports saying that you need to baby the zipper systems on boots which employ the type, and with these I have not been gentle to say the least, and have had no problems whatsoever.

One of the better features on these boots which cannot be seen that well, is the rubber skirt around the front of the boot which in the pictures look like a darker part of leather. It is in fact a very hard rubber bumper which both functions as a stiffener to help toe stubs not hurt, and to keep the booth from wearing. Mine look brand new, after many 4 wheeling, dirt biking, hiking, and aggressive uses. I purchased an 8 inch similar version to these boots as well, which have the same zipper system, but no rubber skirt. I use these boots as often as possible when I can solely for the rubber guard.

As far as heat goes, these stay surprisingly cool. They have 2 vents where the arch of your foot goes, and they expel and intake air as you walk, which help extremely well in regulating the temps inside the boot. In the hottest of hot days, or after running in them for extended periods of times, you can also unzip the sides of these and walk around for a bit and they drop temperature incredibly fast. I also do this in airports when I'm traveling, and it makes going through security a non event in the shoe department. It also makes sitting on planes much nicer as well.

All in all these fit similar to what you expect with boots, they wear excellent with extreme comfort, and I love the rubber toe guard. They stay cool, and don't absorb heat as other colors do.

I would recommend these for anybody looking for an extremely comfortable and easy to wear boot. They are great in airports, being quick to put on and take off. I wear mine everywhere and am extremely happy with my purchase.

The foot bed is a little stiff now (to be expected) and they did require some pulling to get my socked foot past the shaft (compared to no pulling in a zippered boot), but from a sitting position, it wasn't too bad, and should only get easier once the leather becomes more pliable.

Speaking of leather, it is thick, sewn beautifully, smells like a dream and (tan boot) is exactly as represented in the images. (And to my delight, there's a discreet little leather pocket sewn into the top of each boot, for cash/ID, maybe?) My calves are a little on the larger side, so there's not as much slouch/gapping against my legs as in some photos I've seen, but even buckled as shown, I have plenty of room (with wool socks on, even) and I'm betting I could even get them over some skinny jeans (if I had any). They're poking out from under my bootlegs now, and I cannot wait to pair them with some flouncy, feminine dresses and a jean jacket!

Just *LOVE* these boots; grab a pair NOW, while they last!

product_title: Vasque Men's Clarion GTX Hiking Boot
review_body: These are the most impressive boots I have ever owned.  Actually, these qualify as the most impressive footwear of any sort that I have ever owned.  I purchased a pair of these boots in an outdoor store in Artesia, New Mexico about 8 years ago.  For the first 3 or 4 years, I wore these as casual boots around town in Louisiana (not rugged 'off road' usage).  About 4 years ago, I moved to California and discovered geocaching.  Because these boots were still in great condition, I decided to use them for my geocaching adventures.  Every chance I get, I'm out there climbing the hills of Southern California looking for geocaches in the woods and wilds.  Trekking over degraded granite and limestone, these boots have NEVER missed a beat and they have NEVER failed me once, not even in the slightest bit.  I have another pair of boots from New Balance that I use strictly as a casual 'around town' boot.  The New Balance boots are only 1.5 years old.  After 3 or 4 years of casual use and 4 years of rugged use, my Vasque Clarions are in better condition than the 1.5 year old boots!  And the soles have shown absolutely no signs of cracking or splitting.  Even the materials on the inside of the boot have held up perfectly.  After 7 or 8 years, you would expect the material on the inside of the boot in the heel to have a hole in it from friction with the heel rubbing up and down in the boot.  Not a hint.  None.  The ONLY difference between my boots and a brand new pair (besides a layer of dust) is that my soles have about 70% of the original tread.  After 8 years of use, I am simply astounded by these things.  I daresay these things might even be bulletproof, but please don't test that!!!  The only reason I rated these boots with 5 stars is because there were no more stars to give them.  Oh, and I am buying another pair as well. ;)

review_headline: Sure would like Dansko to improve the footbed of these shoes
review_body:
I have loved Danskos for years! And these are quite cute :) I was looking forward to a softer, rubberized sole and the comfort I thought I would find. Not so much...

The toe box is roomy, which feels great for my toes. Check. The sole just isn't the same support nor last as the arch-supporting harder Dansko clogs, etc. Shucks. But beyond that, it is actually UNCOMFORTABLE to me.

I pulled out the insoles to look more closely. Beneath the padding, only about 1/16 inch in depth, is hard plastic in a sort of web-like configuration. When my foot weighs down on it, I feel the hard, bumpy construction, and just feel \\"ouch\\" or almost.

So I decided to go shopping for little pads for the \\"balls\\" of one's feet which you see for high heels, etc. I tried one brand. Could not get it placed comfortably. They just felt like lumps under the balls of my feet. I am currently trying a second brand, which has gel pads -- I have positioned the centers under my metatarsal arch area which seems better than just under the balls.

I want these to work, but seriously, they are not as comfy as I would like. I still feel the \\"lumpy.\\" Perhaps I will try an all-in-one insole pad. I really do like the shoes and want them to work --- and have that all-day comfort I had hoped for.

product_title: Skechers USA Men's Talus-Burk Oxford
review_headline: Unwearable after 3 months. Poor Sketchers cusomer service.
review_body:
Pros:
Comfortable, inexpensive, all-purpose type shoe.

Cons:
As the title describes, these shoes became unwearable after three months. More specifically, as I was putting my shoes on one morning, the tongue/lip on the left shoe simply tore off. Obviously, you can't really wear a pair of shoes without this.

What's more, I contacted Sketchers customer service via e-mail to describe the issue. I included a clear picture of the shoes with the torn lip, and also attached the Amazon invoice as a proof of purchase. No response after 7 days. I followed up with a phone call- they apologized for not getting back to me. The representative explained to me that I could ship them to the quality assurance division, and they would determine whether they were defective and go from there. However, they refused to provide me with a return shipping label without some formal review or management approval. This first representative assured me that I would hear back within a day or two via e-mail.

Another week goes by, no response. I follow up via phone- I get the same song-and-dance. I could send them in to QA...can't get a shipping label without approval, but they could send the case for review, etc. Apparently they have no record of my first call, and they also wouldn't provide me anything to reference (case # or similar). This second rep also assured me that I would hear back within one business day. I still haven't heard back.

At this point I consider it a lost cause. It doesn't make sense to me to pay an extra $10 out of pocket to ship these to QA on the *chance* they might refund or replace them, since I'm already out fifty bucks. Between the obvious poor quality and poor customer service, I don't think I will be buying Sketchers again any time soon.

In all fairness, I did wear these shoes almost every day for the three months, but that still doesn't warrant them becoming unwearable after that short time, and certainly doesn't excuse the poor customer service.
