product_title: Icebug Men's Speed BUGrip Studded Hiking Boot
review_body: I've been using these for long walks with the dog under winter conditions.  They have great traction and I am comfortable going on walks even when it appears icy.  You do have to be careful as the metal studs can/will damage floors if you wear them inside.

product_title: NEW BALANCE Men's 609 Medium
review_body: These are my day to day shoes when I don't need anything fancy.  I've owned multiple pairs of these or their predecessors and what I like about them is there relatively inexpensive, hold up well, and are consistently the same size.  I wear a 12 regular and I know that when I order them they will fit.

product_title: New Balance Men's 574 Core Plus Fashion Sneaker
review_body: The shoe color is as shown,My friend like it so much, They are true to size and width,very comfortable .Nice buy

product_title: Mens Garden Clogs
review_body: These are pretty comfortable I wear them all around the house.  I took the strap off it just seemed bothersome inside, it might work better if I was going to wear them outside.  But I usually wear work boots for that.

product_title: Report Signature Women's Taliaa Ballet Flat
review_headline: I wear a 9-9.5 These fit perfectly.
review_body: I LOVE these shoes, they're very stylish, edgy, fun.  They finish an outfit.  I can also wear them all day!

product_title: Crocs Women's Kadee Flat
review_body: These are the most comfortable shoes I've had the pleasure of using for my purposes.  My work requires me to stand for long periods of time and these shoes, though not the most stylish, are good for preventing leg, ankle, and foot fatigue.  I love the sheer utility and how they prevent fatigue!  I'm a 7.5 and the 8 works perfectly for me.  I have been using them for several months now.  They are so comfortable that I've told everyone about them and have even purchased a pair for my mother.

product_title: Inov-8 F-lite 240 Shoe
review_headline: Great shoe but a big size
review_body: I originally order a US7 but returned them as they were far too big. I went down a whole size but in hindsight should've only gone 1/2 a size as they are a little bit narrow. Love the shoes though, awesome to train in and sooo light! Will definitely get another pair when these wear out.

product_title: Capelli New York Striped Knit Ladies Boot Slipper With Wood Buttons
review_body: I was very hesitant to buy slippers online because I am picky about how they fit and feel because I have very poor circulation to my feet. I love these because I am a 7.5 so there is enough room to snugly fit a pair of fuzzy socks in (without constricting my feet), they stay up around the ankles, and they have a soft indoor only sole that I love. The color is pretty spot on from the picture and they were delivered quickly! Will look to this company when I need slippers again!

product_title: ASICS Women's Gel-Excite Running Shoe
review_headline: Best shoe for my small feet
review_body: This is the 4th pair of these I've owned and they fit great every time. I wear a women's size 5 and shoes in that size that are comfortable and reasonably priced are hard to come by. I do a variety of cardio exercises and they feel great no matter what I'm doing.

product_title: Etnies Fader LS Skate Shoe
review_body: They were exactly as they appeared.  My son loved them, and the fit was perfect.  I do not usually purchase sneakers on line but the first time was a charm.

product_title: Speedo Women's Beach Runner Water Shoe
review_body:
I used this shoe on our vacation to Hawaii. Most of the time I ended up taking them off because they were too big and slid off my heel once I was in the water, also the took on a lot of sand. I don't think I would have had that problem if I had ordered a smaller size. I did read the reviews and ordered a size down from what I normally wear but what I really needed to do was order 2 sizes smaller. I am going to try them again at a pool or lake this summer and see if they are better than for the ocean.

I have a fluid retention problem in my feet and legs so what was great about this shoe was the strap across it allowed for a very flexible fit. I would buy them again.

product_title: Skechers Performance Women's Go Walk Slip-On Walking Shoe
review_body: After reading several Amazon reviews, I went for this model. They are now my favorite shoe. They fit true to size. I now have a literal " spring in my step!"

product_title: Adidas Mens Adizero Feather 2 M Bright BlueWhiteRed Running-Shoes US 13 NIB
review_body: I like this show model very  light and awsome....i run 12miles easy every day with it.recommend evry one to try it

product_title: Dr. Martens 1940 Boot
review_body: These leather boots are just what I wanted. They are for fashion and not work boots in that they will not protect your feet in a working environment. That said, they are awesome for what I wanted - boots I could wear that would allow me to shovel the drive and then go out without changing them.

product_title: Crocs Unisex Classic Clog
review_body: the crocs were great but just a tad on the small side. they still fit but just a bit snuggly.

product_title: shoewhatever Fur Lined Mid-calf Snow Boots
review_body: Cute in theory but to hard and sterdy. The bottoms are very slippery and this web looking fabric starts coming off the bottoms while your walking . The boots are cheaply made thats why they are cheap. Save your money there not worth it.

product_title: Timberland Men's Chocorua Trail Gore-Tex Mid Hiking Boot
review_body:
This is the fifth pair of these boots I've purchased over the past ten years or so. They can't be beat for comfort, warmth, and durability. They are pretty much weather and water proof, as well as lightweight and flexible enough for hiking and climbing.
And for the price, wow!

product_title: Tony Lama Men's Exotic Western Boot
review_body: I ordered the same size as 3 pairs of Tony Lama boots that I already owned and these were so narrow that I couldn't even get them on my foot.  They are really good looking however.

product_title: Reebok Men's Club C Gum Fashion Sneaker
review_body: Clean and simple sneaker that is quality. Give them a few wearings to break in a little bit to get rid of the snug fit.

product_title: Sanuk Women's Ohm My Slip-On
review_body: I am so glad that others post because when  I read the posts on these shoes they were spot on.  I normally wear an 8- 8.5M and if I had bought the 8 they would've been too short.  So read others posts to help you figure out what size to order.  Shoes are very comfortable.  I see why others love them!

product_title: Saucony Women's ProGrid Triumph 8 Running Shoe
review_body: I almost always purchase saucony shoes. For me, there are none more comfortable. I wear a larger size than I do in street shoes, but the fit is consistent. I can always order the same size and know they will fit well. Great shoe for high arches. I have a problem with plantar faciatis and this shoe works well for me.

product_title: Skechers Women's Infantry Soldier Hidden Wedge Combat Boot
review_headline: Really Nice, Comfortable Boot if it Didn't have the Wedge
review_body:
I bought these boots during a lightning deal. I thought they looked really nice and still different from a lot of other boots on the market. When they arrived I tried them on and they fit perfectly. I tried walking around in them in the house for a few days to see if I could get use to the heel wedge. I knew that they came with the hidden wedge, but never expected it to be so high.
I never expected that they would feel like I was walking around in high heels. And after about 10 minutes the ball of each foot was throbbing. I thought maybe I could remove the wedge, but that was not possible.
Good boot if you like to look good, but not if you are buying them to walk around in and be comfortable.
If they could remake these boots without the wedge I would definitely buy them again.

product_title: Crocs Unisex Mammoth EVO Lined Clog
review_body:
Purchased for my Father, who swiped my Mother's to wear around the house after having some Medical issues.
Needless to say, she got hers back, and now they're both happy.
Comfortable, warm, and easy on / off. Recommended.

product_title: Saucony Women's Fastwitch 6 Running Shoe
review_body: Originally bought my usual size, an 8, but was too small. 8.5 fits perfectly. Would recommend buying a half size up from your regular size.

product_title: Tamarac by Slippers International Men's Suede Moccasin Slipper
review_body: We purchased these for my dad, a very difficult slipper/shoe/clothing kinda guy... He loves them. Really loves them. He tells us it's like walking on the plushest carpet. They are well made and attractive. My dad usually wears an 11-11.5 and sizing up was the right choice - fit perfectly.

product_title: Drew Shoe Women's Kelly Slip-On
review_body: This is my second pair of Drew shoes and I'm glad I found a brand that accommodates my orthodic inserts and is made for wide feet.

product_title: Dr. Martens Men's Lachlan Shoe
review_body: After wearing this shoe for few week It's my favorite shoe, very comfortable and looks good in any jeans. On my left pair from the side it started wearing, I can see glued part is seperating and I am scared it will get worse. I would recommend it for comfort.

product_title: ACORN Women's C2G Lite Mule
review_body: After reading reviews I thought these shoes might be a wider shoe. They are just a little to tight for my wide foot, but I think will be fine after some use. The shoe is a very nice construction, lightweight. Other than the snug fit, I like them.

product_title: CALL IT SPRING Call It Spring Finkelman Mens Ankle Boots, Black

product_title: R2 Women's Skye Flat Boot
review_body: cute books that are great with jean. i would buy another pair. thet are very comfy and stylish. give them a try.

review_body: I love the style of the boots but the sizing runs big. It feels like I should have ordered a nine and a half when I'm actually a ten.

product_title: ASICS Men's GEL-Precision TR Cross-Training Shoe
review_body: I ordered a 11.5 4E size and found the shoe to be comfortable and true to size.  I have wide feet and finding a comfortable shoe that lasts can be a challenge.  These worked out great.

product_title: ASICS Men's GEL-180 TR Cross-Training Shoe
review_body: My husband loves the shoes. They fit perfectly and he is really happy with them.  Asics is a wonderful brand and if you can find the correct size they almost always fit right. A great brand, really comfortable.

product_title: Breckelle's GEORGIA-41 Women's Lace Up Combat Ankle Boots Booties
review_body: I'm not into fashion statements but these are just what I wanted.  They're comfortable, keep my feet warm and are still attractive enough to go anywhere.  I'm a grandmother and my granddaughter was delighted with my "combat boots".

product_title: Portlandia Women's Calistoga Ankle Boot
review_body:
Never has a shoe brought me to cursing before these.

These shoes are cute and super comfy, HOWEVER thanks to my high arches, the weakly velcro'd straps pop off every few steps. This is so frustrating and actually dangerous as I nearly tripped on the flapping straps at one point.

If you're going to put non-flexible straps over a flexible foot, you had better attach them firmly, or at the very least not use the weakest/cheapest velcro around.

I am going to have to take these to a cobbler to get them into a wearable position. Ugh.

product_title: Nine West Women's Margot Dress Pump
review_body: The shoes are beautiful. They are very narrow in the toe. Even with a larger size, my foot slid forward and the toes were still too narrow.

product_title: Columbia Powderbug Plus II Print Waterproof Winter Boot
review_body: great boots!!  very sturdy construction.  comfortable.  The first time the kids wore their boots was during a blizzard in NYC and they walked all over the city and their feet stayed warm and dry.  I will defnitely order Columbia again!  You can also tighten the top string so you can tuck pant legs into them and keep your pants dry as well.

review_body: I wear an 11W, it's very hard to find this size and then when you do it's hard to find something CUTE.  These boots are cuter in person, they fit true to size and keep my feet warm while walking in the snow here in Nevada.

review_body: This deserves 5 star. They are somewhat large, but with my socks they work fine. I have wore the birkenstocks most of the winter. I highly recommend these shoes they really do keep your feet warm.

product_title: Stuart Weitzman Women's Pocosling Pump
review_body: I love Stuart Weitzman and these are gorgeous. I purchased them for my daughter's wedding and received many compliments. They are fairly comfortable for a heel and the quality is great.

product_title: swedish hasbeens Women's Zip It Victoria Boot
review_body: These are my favorite SHBs! I have the Zip It Emy also, and these fit similarly except they are a bit narrower by the ball of the foot. I am a 6.5 so a 37 fits me perfectly with a little room for my wide, low-arched feet. If you've never had SHBs before, these are amazingly comfortable. I usually wear sneakers or boots without a heel, and I can do my 45 minute walk to work on the sidewalks of NYC in these (and back) no problem!

product_title: KEEN Utility Men's Portland Puncture Resistant Slip On Work Boot
review_body: Overall, good quality. Very stiff with the steel toe. Bought these for motorcycle riding. They tend to fit well around some areas of my feet but around others, somewhat loose.

product_title: LaCrosse Men's Ice King Liner Shoe Care,Brown 3/4" Foam,15
review_body: didn't realize how bad mine were wore out till I got these. They fit great and my feet are so much warmer

product_title: Baffin Women's Chloe Insulated Boot
review_headline: I have been wearing these every day!
review_body: I bought this pair of Baffin boots after I bought a (different) pair for my daughter and saw what great boots they are. The sizing does run somewhat small; I ordered a size 9, as I usually wear a size 8 1/2-9. The boots fit with a regular pair of socks, but if you want to wear heavy, thick socks with your boots I would advise sizing up. Having said that, the boots are EXTREMELY warm, even with regular socks, and they are rated that way. So, I kept them and have been wearing them every day and they have kept my feet toasty warm...the temp outside right now is -25, so I am very happy!! I highly recommend this boot.

product_title: Tamarac by Slippers International Women's Galaxie Shearling Slipper
review_body:
Purchased for my Mother who has a REALLY HIGH arch!! Any slipper that fully covers the foot does not fit or rubs the top to the point of blister.
She was skeptical at first, but after slipping them on... She was in heaven!

product_title: ASICS Men's GEL-Contend Running Shoe
review_body: they are very comfortable for running and walking and the price is reasonable.  You can't have better choice with this price.

product_title: Bordello By Pleaser Women's Teeze-02 Platform Pump
review_headline: I love them! But know what you're buying...
review_body:
I love all the Bordello Teeze shoes and I get compliments on these everywhere I go. I've noticed complaints about the size but they work in my situation. I wear a 6 1/2 and have narrow feet. These are a tiny bit loose in the length and a little loose in the width. I prefer my heels snug, not tight but snug because I feel they offer better support that way. That said, the strap helps a lot. These are sky high heels so you have to be prepared for that. HOWEVER, for heels of this height I find them to be a lot more comfortable and wearable than others. Major points for me being the insole aren't rock hard stiff like so many heels and the platform is large and provides a good stepping space (there has been a big trend of tapering platforms so you have a teeny tiny pad to walk on, which leads to disaster).

Either way, taking these things into account I'm a big fan of these shoes.

product_title: Madden Men's M-Expo Loafer
review_body: You get what you pay for.  This is not top of the line and the leather heel cups are quite thin.  Not for day after day wear.  But nice for a casual look with jeans.

review_body: I found that these don't stay on my nose properly and slip constantly. There is no traction on the nose pad. Well, maybe I should expect too much from fashion sunglasses. product_title: Bostonian Men's Quarry Oxford
review_body: They fit great, same size as my last pair of Bostonian's which is why I felt comfortable ordering them online. Classic look, very clean.

product_title: New Balance Men's MX608V3 Cross-Training Shoe
review_body:
I'm a UPS driver/delivery person. I have yet to wear a pedometer, but I walk a good five miles a day, in varied terrain. Sidewalks, stairwells, yards. I go through a couple pairs of shoes per year, and I keep my eye out for a good deal. These shoes are a good deal! They're on their fifth month, got me through the holiday rush, and are still in good shape, they've got at least three months left in them. I'll be replacing these with the same make and model.

Only caveat: the long wear is at the expense of some "grippiness" of the tread - they're just a little slick, and noticeably so on wet surfaces.

review_headline: Love the slipper, not sized properly
review_body: I used to purchase only LLBean slippers and when they stopped carrying my favorite, I found these slippers - priced right. I ordered my size and the left foot is about 1 1/2 sizes too large, right foot 1/2 size too large - so both feet aren't even the same size shoe. I do love the durable soles, look and feel of the slippers. I would purchase again, except choose at least one full size smaller because once the fur matts down some, the shoes will then be so substantially too big for me that they'll probably be unable to wear.

The leather is super soft and smooth, the lining too! love the rubber grip soles too, makes it easier to walk on surfaces like gravel or even dirt! the heel is a perfect sexy hight, without being uncomfortably too high! My only regret is not buying two pairs while it was on sale!!! I shoulda gotten one in each color!

product_title: FiveFingers Mens Lontra Black/Grey Cross Trainer - 45
review_headline: Love them for running, not so much for walking
review_body:
I have a pair of Bikelas that fit like a glove and I have no problem matching the toes into their respective pockets. I purchased the Lontra for running in outdoors in Chicago area winters(actually I purchased the Bikelas for winter but they just didn't cut it)

First thing I noticed was the stiffness of the sole, I am a barefoot runner in the summer so this concerned me.
Second was the fit. It took longer to get my toes into the correct pockets and they seem a lot wider (and stiffer) than the Bikelas.
My toes seemed to be more spread out than normal, again concerning me.

I have run in them 3 times (average 6 miles each run) and while I am running, all the perceived fit problems went away.
I ran a 10k trail run this weekend and the trails were slushy and icy (30 F). The grip on the bottom worked great (except the sheer ice parts) The neoprene ankle and waterproofing worked great even in ankle deep slush/water, my feet remained dry.

After today's run, I am extremely happy with these shoes, Time will tell how long they remain waterproof, I will try to update if anything changes

review_headline: Love the shoes but comes without cleats

product_title: Bearpaw Women's Emma
review_body:
I've yet to take my boots into the Ohio winter, so this review will require updating. As a long time lover of my now battered Uggs, I wanted a new pair but couldn't stomach the price when I know they will be subjected to salt and ice. I found these: all the same "ingredients" as Uggs, but a fraction of the price.

The outside looks good. The stitching and suede have a nice, expensive look. The sole is a bit heavier than Ugg, but it's a nice rubber one with good traction. I actually list this as a pro. The inside has a little less shearling (mainly less in the foot part) than my Uggs--but not $150 less, so I'm over it. They are nice and soft on the inside.

The shearling DOES matter for this reason--consider your sizing. I wear a 5.5 to 6 usually, and wear a 5 in Uggs because the shearling does compress and the boots stretch a bit. These have less shearling, so there will be less compression. They feel a bit snug to me, but again, I haven't really worn them out. I think they will stretch enough for me, but I like a snugger shoe. So, shop prepared.

Also--I have a slim calf but these are pretty snug to the calf. Those who need a wider calf for clothing or physical comfort reasons might want to explore a different brand OR perhaps the shorter option.

I loved my Uggs because I'm lazy about socks and hate cold feet. These definitely answer the first and are cute to boot (ha!). Will have to see with time if they offer the same warmth.

product_title: Irish Setter Men's 840 Havoc Waterproof 800 Gram 10" Big Game Boot
review_headline: Excellent pair of boots for my needs, can handle extreme cold weather
review_body:
Absolutely love the boots that I got. I bought this pair at the Red Wings Shoe store but was so satisfied with the product that I had to write a review online. The person helping me in the store was kind enough to order the normal and wide sizes for 2 different sizes for me to try on. Once the boots came in, they gave me a call and I came into the store to buy the pair of Irish Setter hunting boots. It was the best pair of boots for my uses, hiking and being in extreme cold weather (eg Iceland and Canada). I could even wear it to the dog park in NYC. It has 800g of insulation. I could easily just stand at the dog park in the snow and my feet would be warm for at least 2 hrs. The boots are also high enough so that I could hike through mud, streams, and some rivers without getting my feet wet. Great for photography when I want to setup a tripod in the middle of the stream. Another reason for this product is the FlexLock handsewn construction. It makes wearing the boots that much more comfortable. The flexible soles allows me to be on my tippy toes when need be and I've been able to run in these boots without difficulty. I also bought from this company because the "tune up". I've used their services twice now and on my second time, they gave me a new pair of laces. Also, for some reason, the 2nd time around, whoever did it, did a much better job. I could tell that the boots were cleaned and "tuned" up. Only downside to the company is the cost. The boots were quite expensive and the biggest discount I've seen so far was 20% off during Black Friday for the Red Wings Shoe store.

PROS:
- flexible sole
- water proof
- insulation
- comfortable
- can handle extreme cold weather (eg Iceland and Canada)

CONS:
- cost
- not as "fashionable"

product_title: ASICS Men's GEL-Kinsei 5 Running Shoe
review_body:
I have used all the Asics Kinsei in its evolution and I opine that this has been true until the KInsei 5. Whilst Asics claims to have made advances in this new model, I would like to disagree from a number of points.
Kinsei 3 and 4 had upper material that kept your feet cool in the summer and warm in the winter. I tried that Kinsei 5 on a very chilly morning and noticed immediately that the new FluidFit material does not afford such benefits - for the first time in years my feet have had to adapt to the natural temperatures - and that is a huge negative for me. I have resorted back to my extra pair of new Kinsei 4 for the winter. FluidFit might be a technological leap for Asics but I see it as a step back, as my feet eventually adapt to any running shoe.
The under sole of Kinsei 5 has less grip than its predecessors 3 and 4 and that has probably been forsaken for the benefit of a lighter shoes - from a weigh perspective that is. The guidance line has been redesigned and is less pronounced and I can feel this when I am running.
I have also noticed that Kinsei 5 does not have strong reflective properties compared to the 3 and 4 and this is perplexing as I always run very early in the morning and need those reflective properties to warn the frequent vehicles of my presence. Asics has always been strong on safety and so I am concerned by this glaring omission.
The laces of the shoes are too long and I wonder why this was not discovered and corrected as I would prefer not to have excess lace material hitting against my shoes and distracting me in my runs
I do judge the Kinsei 5 to be a comfortable running shoe but no more so than its immediate predecessor and I believe that Kinsei 4 still remains the benchmark for the Kinsei range.

product_title: ASICS Men's Kinsei 4 Running Shoe
review_headline: Technique matters most, your "mileage" may vary.
review_body:
After my stint in the Army over 10 years ago, I had not been able to run again. I tried multiple times, but found myself re-injured after each attempt. This year, I did a lot of research first before trying again. I researched chi walking and chi running. I researched running form. I saw Youtube videos of Racewalkers. I saw Youtube videos of olympic runners. What I got from my research is these four things: 1. Lean forward 2. Use a short stride 3. Minimize breaking 4. Minimize how high you come off the ground

In my physical therapy way back when, they stressed the importance of working and stretching the muscle opposing the calf muscle through various exercises. Part of the problem is that if you're using and stretching one muscle and set of tendons but not the opposing muscle and tendons, there's an imbalance that leads to injury. This is where the beauty of leaning forward lies: you are working and stretching the muscles and tendons on the other side of your calf muscle during your workout, not as a workout recovery.

I began working on a technique that worked for me. I lean forward and imagine myself grabbing the ground with my toes as the ground moves under my feet. In this way, I am working with momentum and flowing with the movement across the ground, as opposed to fighting the ground by stopping and breaking. (Chi running literature calls it "using gravity", but this is wrong).

I started my journey using my New Balance trail shoes. They are not as insanely unpadded as Vibram Five Fingers, but they give enough flexibility and feedback that I know when I'm hitting the ground too hard. I work on not feeling the ground at all... just grabbing it and pushing it back.

From playing piano, I know that it's best to keep your fingers close to the keys to achieve the greatest efficiency. Using the same approach, I keep my feet as close to the ground without dragging, all the while maintaining my stride length.

I started fast walking 2 miles, then 4, then 6. Now I'm running 4 miles, working up to 6. It's like a new lease on life. Running in the evening through the park as the sun was setting, feeling the adrenaline flow through my body... this was an experience that was limited to my dreams. Not anymore.

Have these shoes helped get me there? Yes, they have. I do believe they have helped me heal my once-fractured shins after only a few runs with them. After recovery, I feel less pain than I had before. It took less time to warm up on my next run. I'm now down to not feeling that tightness and pain I used to feel in my ankles and shins every time I started to run.

There are some downsides, though. I can't feel the ground. One the one hand, that's nice, because they are insanely comfortable. On the other hand, it's not so good, because in an activity that's become for me about being mindful of my body and movement, I feel like I'm going about it blindfolded, with no feedback from the ground to go on. Also, and most unfortunately, my knees hate them. Despite the miracles they have done with my ankles and shins, I feel a lot of pain in my knees after a run that I do not feel with the New Balance trail shoes. So it's back to my old shoes.

So what's the verdict? It was a bit (emotionally) painful at first to realize that I would be using my old shoes again after dropping $150.00 on these new ones. However, I do believe these shoes have helped me run again, in a way that the old shoes alone could not have done. That was worth the money for me.

Ultimately, everyone is different, and the technique you use matters most. The risk with any running shoe you buy is that you won't know if they are right for you until you wear them in. With these, however, you'll be out a Benjamin and a half if you find that you can't use them for what you intended.stride length.

review_headline: Carhartt Men's CMH6110 6 Work Boot - What I Expected EXCEPT FOR...
review_body: These Carhartt Men's CMH6110 6 Work Boots are What I Expected. I receive mine back in the summer and true they can get a little to warm to wear, however they are water resistant which probably hinders their breathing and allowing any cooling effect. They are nice to wear in the cold and wet time of the year. Be it summer or winter, keeping dry is very important to me and these do that. There is wear-in period but less than most boots I have had. They are very comfortable to wear once broken in. I would have given them 5 stars, except the right boot toe tip appears to be slowly breaking away from the toe. Not alarmed about it yet. The last pair of Carhartt boots I had (not this model, one similar) the soles broke away and the bottom of the soles and heals basically disintegrated within a couple of years. I hope these don't.    UPDATE 1/10/2015: Lowered from 5 stars to 3 stars. I have had these boots since July 29, 2013 and like them very much EXCEPT for the right boot's sole is separating from the boot from the tip to about a third of the way back. It kind of flaps when I walk, which is a little dangerous. I am not rough on boots as is evident by the wear of the upper material and the tread wear and feel they should last longer than this. I am trying to glue them back together, but don't have much hope for this to last long. I wonder what the mfg. uses for glue? Carhartt seems to have trouble with their boot soles, as my last pair's soles basically disintegrated within a couple of years.

I got the black suede. They fit so much better around the ankle and shaft for a sleeker fit, and the suede is so beautiful. They're surprisingly versatile boots, and look just as good worn casually with my Target clearance rack skirts as they do with my better skirts and dresses for work. I was a hesitant about being able to pull off the over-the-knee look, but I don't dress like Beyonce, so it's not an issue. I'm still in the honeymoon phase with the 5050s, and wear them at every opportunity, but I know I'll love 'em and wear 'em forever.

review_body:

They were a little stiff at first to use but have loosened up nicely. I chalk this breaking-in period to their hefty gauge.

The lining is solid color (I believe it's cotton?, says on the tag, I'm just too lazy to go look, lol) and well sewn with one zippered pocket and two patch cell-phone sized pockets. I would have preferred a beautiful fashion forward print lining instead, but taking into account the high quality of the materials, construction and quality of this bag and the price, it wouldn't be fair to take a star off for such a trivial preference.

With care, this beautiful purse should last you many years.

product_title: Under Armour Men's UA Micro G Defend Training Shoes
review_body: I am a soldier, cross country runner, and track runner. I originally bought these shoes for traveling but when I got back to my station it was all I had for physical training. I run more than most. I am the kind of guy that goes to the weight room and can't avoid the treadmill. Now, I used to be a shoes salesman and these shoes are exactly what I would have advised not to where. They lack arch support. The theory is arch support is best for your feet, but I beg to differ. Nothing beats good technique. The most natural way of running is on balls of your feet and not striking the heel so much. Heel striking is bad for your knees and shin, and exerts you much more quickly. Heel to toe running is best used as a reserve muscle group after you can no longer run on your toes. So if you run with the natural technique and have already adapted your muscles to that kind of run, these shoes are excellent! If you run heel to toe I encourage you no matter how long you have been running to train into the natural technique. I ran heel to toe most of my life, until last year when a friend introduced me this technique and it changed my running life completely. No knee pain. No shin splints, no hip pain, no arch pain, and slower exertion. Get this shoe! Check out the natural technique while you are at it!

I really like these and am happy with my purchase.

I don't typically wear a heel due to some old injuries that make them painful, but this boot has a sturdy and thicker heel which makes it a bit more stable for my old ankle. The heel is dressy but not overly high, and I could see them paired with a casual outfit as well. The \\"leather\\" is naturally not real, and thus not soft and supple, but the look passes well enough for a leather looking boot.

The sole has good grip at the ball of the foot, not too sure on the plastic heel cap though- it feels a bit slick, but with the majority of my weight on the ball area, they should be okay.

They are a bit big (I wear a 9.5 to 10 in most all shoes). I ordered the ten, but a 9.5 might have been a better fit for me. I'd say they run true to size to a bit large... my other size ten boots don't have nearly as much wiggle room. I figure with thick winter socks, they'll be about right, and I'd rather have some wiggle room than for them to be too tight against my toes.

I guess I have HUGE calves because my male friends always comment enviously on my calf muscles. That said, I am a former ballet dancer who kept her great legs even when the rest of me went to pot (haha). My legs are pretty slim, thought not quite what I'd call skinny-- but my calves are 15.5 inches at the widest part of the muscle. These boots fit over my freaky calves just fine- and have a plenty of room to spare. With a skinny jean I can still wear a thick knee sock and have about 2 fingers room around the top of the boot. If you have super skinny legs... they might be too big for you if you want a snug fit around the upper part of the boot. I have a feeling in the picture they'd been clipped or altered for a snug fit on the model's thin legs. They are roomy, not form fitting. ;)

I am happy with them, and think they will wear just fine. They seem to be decent quality for the price. Should they fall apart before their time or have any other issues, I'll update. But for now, new out of the box, they are exactly what I wanted. =)eaky calves just fine- and have a plenty of room to spare. The upper part is soft and there was lots of room. I exchanged it for the size 9, and it fits much better, still with wiggle room for my toes. They are very comfortable, and the best part is that they are easy to throw on, while still being somewhat fashionable. I would recommend going for a half size smaller, if you are normally a half size like me.

**UPDATE** I feel I should update my original review. First, I am not entirely certain if the uppers are real leather now, after comparing the material to a known leather boot, but I can't find anything on the boots that say otherwise (unless I am totally blind). That being said, they are still a very well made boot, even if they are not real leather. These things made it through the worst MN winter in over 15 years. Six months straight of the most heavy, wet snow that you could imagine, and they still kept my feet warm and dry. They are super easy to clean, and I have yet to see any loose stitching. I would say these are very durable.

review_headline: works for over pronation and knee pain
review_body: I work at home and Orthaheel slippers are my everyday shoes. I have severe over pronation resulting in knee and hip pain and these work wonderfully in easing it. My physical therapist recommended orthotics(arch supports)  but cautioned against being totally dependent on them. I was told to work with the orthotic and let it help me retrain myself how to walk on the outer portion of my foot instead of the arch. It involves building new muscle strength and it threw my body into a slightly different alignment so there was actually a temporary increase in knee discomfort for a couple weeks but I adapted and now I'm almost pain-free and my posture is even better. I've found that it's important to keep them adjusted snugly for the best support. This is my second pair and I just got the insole type support for dress shoes as well. I'm so glad I found these!

I put them on almost new and walked the Coast to Coast Trail across England (200 miles) without a single blister. There was a lot of very wet, boggy trail but my toes stayed dry(!) and snug inside. We then reinvented ourselves as tourists in Europe, and to my own surprise, I continued to wear the boots in the cities. They were sure footed on slick, wet cobblestone as well. We've got snow on the ground now, and I slip them on (easy!) to walk the dog and stay warm and dry.
Forget the brands that look big and tough. Montara has them beat and does it with style.

product_title: Clarks Men's Wave.Vortex Slip-On
review_headline: Before you ride the Wave style
review_body:
I like Clarks very much. I tore up a pair of their Mocs by accident and looked for a replacement on Amazon. I noted the very high reviews for this model and ordered it. They are very well made and have a few neat features I didn't expect--like the heel cup having a textured material with something of a grain meant to help gently lock the sock and heel into the shoe when walking. That's the first time I've seen this in a shoe. They are more loose than the Mocs but only about a 1/2 size.

What I did not know, and didn't see elaboration on in the reviews, is what Clarks Wave Walk is. The shoe is \\"smile\\" molded--the center of the shoe touches the ground while the heel and the rear of the toe are off the ground. You can see this by setting it on a table. You will FEEL this if you walk in them. If you're a \\"heel-striker\\" when you run, you'll note that these feel like they have no heel at all! They are designed this way. They \\"roll\\" (Wave) on the center of the shoe like the Sketchers that are much more exaggerated in such a design. If you like the Wave, you'll likely love this shoe (as another reviewer notes). I'm not a big fan so far. I miss the heel contact and feeling of support and cushioning in the heel. To put it another way, if you've ever had a heel break off a dress shoe or owned Nike Air Max shoes that \\"went flat\\", that's the initial sensation that you'll have walking in Clarks Wave. \\"Where's the heel?\\"--literally.

I'm keeping these and working with them for a couple of months (then I'll add to this review). I would not have bought them if I tried them on in a store (and I understand that I could return these easily with Amazon's generous guidelines), but I've decided to see if they grow on me. 3 1/2 stars, really; but I'll round up for the overall quality of the Clark brand and hope to find that they know something that I don't as I try to grow accustomed to them for a while.

review_body:
I fell in love with these shoes last year when my Mother in Law bought them, but at $90 I figured they weren't an option for me. The gold is not too golden, so it is a perfect neutral and looks great with almost everything. I wanted a shoe to wear with my skinny jeans, other than ballet flats and riding boots and these are perfect.

I normally wear a 7.5 or an 8 depending on the shoe, so based on reviews I ordered the 7.5, after wearing them once the backs were not staying on my heel, but with a heel saver I'm sure they will fit better. If I bought a 7 I know my toes would be pinched and I would be miserable, and I have issues with getting ingrown toe nails so too large is better than too snug for me. If you go between both sizes, I would go with the smaller of the two. I did notice even after wearing them once they began to stretch a bit but the leather is getting even more comfortable. I can't say enough about how much I like these shoes, and at these great prices I am tempted to buy a second and third!

product_title: FRYE Women's Dorado Riding Boot
review_headline: Maybe DON'T order a size down
review_body:
A large portion of the reviews for this boot - not just on Amazon, but everywhere - suggest to order a half-size down. This is not universally good advice.
About me: 5'6", size 7.5 shoe, somewhat high-arched feet, 15.5" calves.
I initially ordered my regular size (7.5). They were very tight, both across the top of the foot and at the top of the shaft shaft. I exchanged them for an 8, which fit much better. Arguably, a good cobbler could have stretched the boots out in those areas, but I'm much happier with the bigger size, which leave room for insoles or thick socks.
If you have a high arch and slightly-larger-than-average calves, consider going with your size, or 1/2 size up.
(Also, Amazon's measurement for the calves - 13.5 inches - is totally wrong. Don't let that scare you away.)

product_title: Olukai Ohana Sandal - Women's
review_body: I've been a Reef sandal fan for 7 years. I walked two miles a day in Reef flip flops when my pregnant feet swelled too much to wear real shoes. When my friend's dog chewed up my last pair of Reefs, I let a salesgirl talk me into this much more expensive pair of flip flops. Within hours of wearing them my feet felt bruised, but I thought they just needed to be broken in. Within days I had plantar fasciitis. I spent so much money on these flip flops that I felt compelled to just grit my teeth and force my feet to get used to them, but they never did. After a two month break I pulled these out of my closet this weekend to wear on a beach getaway. After less than two days of wear the bottoms of my feet are so tender and bruised I can barely walk. I will never wear these outrageously expensive flip flops again and I will definitely never buy another pair of OluKai shoes. These are not worth the myriad of problems they caused!

review_headline: I bought mens boots instead of womens
review_body: I was looking for a boot that would hold up well to a solid beating and these seem like they will do a good job at that. I am a woman with feet that are a bit wider than some so I wanted a boot that would give me a bit more room than a woman's boot. I wear a woman's 8 so I initially ordered a 7 and a 1/2 and they were just a tad to small if i wanted to wear them with wool socks, so I returned them with free shipping and ordered a size 8 and they fit perfect. They were a bit stiff the first few days I wore them but they broke in with not much trouble, no blisters or any real discomfort. On the third day wearing them, my horse refused to cross the creek so I had to get off and lead her over, I found that the boots are beautifully water proof and that the water proofing works both ways. An hour later when i got back to the truck and took off my boots i poured about a half cup of water out of each boot. I brought them home, took the inserts out of them and left them to dry under my bed. It took three days for them to dry totally but they are as good as new with no shrinking or discoloration. I pulled them out from under the bed, and took them to the New Mexico desert for a week of blowing things up and they held up swimmingly and were perfectly comfortable. If this is any indication on the quality of these boots I expect them to last me for a very long time.

product_title: Ahnu Women's Montara Boot
review_body: First, I didn't buy these from Amazon, I bought them at REI.  If you have the option of shopping at REI, I recommend it because their staff will help you find the right fit and you can test them out on a pretend rock hill in the store.  If not, Amazon has easy returns, so no big deal.  These boots are the nicest I've ever owned.  I bought them to replace Columbia brand boots that were causing blisters all over my feet, especially on the heel.  The Ahnu's had absolutely no break in time and I haven't had a blister yet.  The first time I wore them was on a 7 or 8 mile day hike.  After several more day hikes, I used them on a 4 day, ~36 mile backpacking trip in Olympic National Park.  I had no trouble with blisters or hot spots.  The only complaint I have about these boots is that the part that covers the ankle comes up a little higher than on most boots.  It feels pretty strange at first, but I got used to it fairly quickly.  The extra height makes my ankles sweat like crazy in hot weather, which is gross and annoying.  It's also worth noting that these boots run a bit small, I got a half side larger than usual. But I guess it's pretty common to need a slightly larger hiking boot than other shoes.  Since it was such a nice summer, I haven't had a chance to try these on a rainy, muddy trial yet, but I have a feeling that the water proofing will work really well.  I did walk through some small streams on a few of my hikes and I didn't have any leakage or wet feet.  Overall, these are a fantastic pair of boots and I highly recommend them.  September 2015 Update:  I've owned these boots for 2 full years and they're still going strong! Since the original review, I have had the opportunity to use them when hiking on muddy trails and through stream crossings. I am pleased to report that they keep my feet totally dry, even when walking through several inches of water. I highly recommend these boots!

product_title: SPIRA Women's Classic Leather Walking Shoe
review_headline: Absolutely the best shoes for paiful feet, thanks Spira!
review_body:
I am a 33y.o. female who is currently suffering from a severe unspecified spondyloarthritis (type of inflammatory arthritis) flare-up. My both knees and feet, particularly ankles and heels are inflamed, swolled and very painful. I haven`t been able to exercise, or even do much walking, apart from doing small chores around the house. Despite the pain meds and anti-inflammatory meds a trip to a supermarket is a torture.
I wish i had found these shoes earlier! I loved them the second i wore them, they are so springy, soft and cushy! I also like the fact that they don`t look huge, and in fact are quite compact for an orthotic shoe. Because of the thick soles and the heel, they also make me look taller, which is great, since i can`t wear sexy heels. These are the ONLY shoes which i can wear at the moment, the only shoes which make my walking/standing less hellish. I would without any doubt purchase one more pair if i ever need to.

I bought them after reading the reviews here, particularly from other arthritis sufferers, and i hope that my review will help people too.
They have enough room to put in a pair of Dr.Scholl`s orthotic insoles too. But even without it, these shoes are brilliant.
They are very thick and warm all around, so they might be a little too warm in the summer.
I am going to recommend them to my doctor, so she can pass the word around.

Elena

product_title: Timberland Men's Earthkeepers 6" Lace-Up Boot
review_body:
I've had these for about a month now. They are my very first pair of leather boots ever and I love them. I wanted one boot that I could wear for winter, hiking, and just because, and these fit the bill. They look really good and have held up well through several hikes of about five or six miles each. A couple of the hikes the weather was pretty wet and no moisture got in. Of course, the tongue is loose, so I'm sure stepping in a deep puddle or hanging out in a constant downpour will allow some water in. They are also quite comfortable. I even wore them for about 19 hours straight walking all over Munich, Germany. My feet were sore, of course, but not as sore as they've been after a day in my usual low-profile trainers.

The sizing, like everyone else says, is pretty large. I wear an eleven normally, but I went with a 10.5. Everyone said to go a size down, but my foot is a bit wide, so I thought I'd see how half a size went. Turns out I probably could have done with a size down, and maybe even a size and a half if I wanted a snug fit. But these were partly meant for hiking and for hiking you want your boots to fit just a bit large so you have plenty of toe room, so I've decided to stay with the 10.5, though if/when I buy another pair I might go down to 10.

I got them in burnished brown, which ended up being a dark reddish brown, which I actually prefer.

They were pretty much broken in and ready to wear right away, but have actually broken in even more. The leather is supple and comfortable. I've read some reviews saying that the sole wears out quickly, but that they would be happy to re-sole them. I haven't noticed any such wear yet, but if the boots last as long as I imagine they will, I'll be happy to re-sole them whenever. And I've never re-soled ANYTHING.

TL;DR, If you're looking for a good boot for light hikes that can also be worn on a night out on the town, look no further. Just go a size down.

product_title: KEEN Men's Targhee II Mid WP Hiking Boot
review_body:
I usually love Keen shoes – have owned 6-7 others in various styles – but I’m pretty disappointed in these boots. Firstly, they are very light duty with little ankle support and a pretty soft sole, but they still feel clunky on my feet because of the massive toe bumper. I knew they weren’t backpacking boots going in, but in my opinion these are barely light hikers – better suited for park paths than a real trail. Still, that would be okay, except…
Barely a year (and not heavy use) and the straps that hold the laces are ripping. Two have torn all the way through, meaning I really can’t tie the boots anymore, and several others are badly frayed. They should have leather or metal, and this is a pretty big design flaw because the fabric straps (look at the top or front of the boot, you’ll see what I mean) are not very durable and once they go, the boot becomes unwearable (or at least untie-able).
I usually save old hiking boots for yardwork or muddy jobs around the house, but these are looking like garbage after a pretty short life.

product_title: Danner Men's Quarry GTX 8" AT Boot
review_headline: The sole will come off after a couple of years.
review_body:
So I have purchased three Danner Quarry boots since 2005. The first pair were great, durable, and I wore them out under very tough use in the construction work that I do. So the second pair I purchased a couple of years ago worked great until the glue that adheres the sole to the boot failed. The bottom sole just peeled off the boot as a result. I guess they began using a different sole or glue, or something different in the build.

I brought the boot to the company store here in Portland knowing that a great brand like Danner would just fix the defect and glue another sole on or at least repair it. What they offered was to charge me a hundred dollars to fix a defect in the product they sold me. So not wanting to put good money after bad into a flawed product I left the boots with them. I am very brand loyal, and I do love the product, but I expect them to stand by the product they sell. If you are considering purchasing the Danner Quarry, I can say they produce a very comfortable boot. If the boot has a defect after the one year period of the warranty they will not fix it. For many people two solid years out of a pair of work boots is fine. But I want you all to know that the sole is going to fail a lot faster than you would expect out of boot with the reputation of Danner Quarry. Also know that Danner isn't going to help you once the product fails, or any defect at all past that warranty. So I am now on my third pair and I will update this review to see how long they last. But I think I will shop a little harder and find a better brand in the future for my next purchase.

product_title: Chaco Men's Z/2 Unaweep Sandal
review_headline: Comfortable once adjusted and callous forms
review_body: These sandals are a very nice open design and are quite adjustable. The adjustments are not easy; considerable loosening and adjustment is needed initially to get them to a point of being comfortable. The force required to pull the straps through the sole channels is considerable, but with persistence you can get each segment of the continuous-loop strap system to a condition that fits, does not bind, nor cuts into you. This adjustment includes the diameter of the great toe, the tightness of the strap across the instep, and the strap going back to the ankle and around the heel. So over a period of a couple of days/wearings you can get each one to fit its corresponding foot very nicely, securely, and comfortably. The sole does have one uncomfortable aspect; there is a build-up of the sole material reinforcing the penetration by the outside strap near the heel. This material rubbed the edge of each foot there, raising a deep blister and callous over several wearings. Initially this became painful, but as the summer progressed the callous hardened and there was a lot less discomfort. Ultimately these sandals were far more comfortable than the Terra-Fi sandals that they replaced. The wrapping (foot fitting) thin straps are what make it comfortable in the straps. The sole is very durable, protective, and gives plenty of traction. There are many color choices; this one was versatile for me. Without the required callous production, these would have earned 5 stars.

product_title: Tactical Coyote Tan Concealed Carry Fanny Pack with Holster Roma 6502
review_headline: Doesn't hold a whole lot else
review_body:
Construction, finish seem average quality. The included nylon \\"holster\\" seems oddly shaped for a J frame revolver but it fits OK. There are some tab/pulls that are seemingly supposed to allow quick access to the gun compartment. One of those pulls came off immediately after my trying to use it. I sewed it back on. There are loops inside the gun compartment I assume meant to hold magazines or similar. But if you put a magazine, speed loader, miniMag lite or Kubaton in there, it makes the pack really bulky and difficult to zip closed.

The triangle shaped compartments on the edges hardly fit anything. It would probably fit ONE car key. It won't fit a few keys on a ring or a typical alarm fob, at least without a LOT of cramming and then the stuff is difficult to get out.

The other major compartment, on the front of the pack, holds wallet, cellphone etc ok but it's not very tall. A standard wallet and a write-in-the-rain nylon folder fill the thing up. ALMOST tall enough to fit a standard mini-Maglite but if you have an endcap switch on your miniMag, closing the pack tends to turn on the light.

Seems to carry ok. Adjustable from very, very small to very, very big. Main plastic side release buckle seems stout. I can wear it on a mtn bike and not worry about it coming undone.

product_title: Men's Corcoran 1500 10" Jump Boot 1500, Black
review_body:
These are the classic combat boot that never goes out of style. I have worn them for years, and NEVER stop getting compliments. A few things to know before you buy them:

If they aren't cared for properly, they WILL crack along the top between the toe seam and the bottom of the lacing over time. The leather needs to be cared for and conditioned to prevent this. Also, the soles are not *super* thick on these- I love them because they are great for casual wear and don't have that clunky "hot topic" feel to them (they are also light enough that I can hike/etc in them really comfortably!) But that does mean that the sole may wear out before the rest of the boot does. I am a "hard walker" and I wear mine down to the screws from daily wear in about 2 years.

A final note- I ordered a pair of these from a local shoe store once and found out I had been wearing the wrong size for years. (length AND width) I was SHOCKED at how much more comfortable they were just from having the advice from someone who knows what proportions to look for and how it should fit your foot. So I would def. say that one of the perks of buying a boot like this locally is that they will measures you, and if that size isn't perfectly comfortable when it arrives, they will know what adjustments need to be made.

review_body: First, I can't recommend this product for everyone, because different feet require different types of exercise shoes. Finding the appropriate shoe for yourself really makes a difference in how your feet tolerate exercise. I learned about this shoe by going to an athletic-shoe store and having the salesman there do an analysis of what I need through their pressure-point machine, by looking at my feet, by watching me walk, and by talking with me. This is technically a running shoe, but I use it for walking. On my own, I know it's important to replace my walking shoes every few months or at least once a year after the cushioning starts to wear out. In all fairness I have purchased my replacement shoes at the store that helped me, but this time I needed the shoes and I wasn't traveling hours north to Portland, Maine, where that store is located. It was nice to be able to buy these through Amazon, on sale at that, and have them delivered to my door. I love these shoes, but that's just me!

product_title: Merrell Men's Mix Master Trail Running Shoe Trail Running Shoe
review_headline: Might not be for you, but a great shoe for some.
review_body:
These are a great 'transition' shoe to barefoot running/walking. they have more sole than a true barefoot shoe (trail glove and road glove) and they don't have as much drop.

These look like they would be great light trail runners but the sole is thin and very flexible and I felt every rock. Where I run/walk has lots of rocks from marble size to softball sized half buried in the dirt. Depending on your tastes in shoes this thin/flexible sole might be good for you or might not be. For me (and my 55 yr old feet) they were too flexible and I would get pain in the ball of my foot. The thin soles made them unsuitable for long walks (10+ miles) on paved surfaces. My feet would feel beat by the end of the day. (I am used to 'barefeet' shoes. I have the Merrell Trail Glove and Fila Skele-toes (the Running and Trail model.

These shoe come with a very thin 'micro-cushioning' insole. Just something to keep in mind. It will give you a more 'barefoot' shoe feel. I put a little thicker insoles in mine since I have plenty of barefoot shoes.

As people have said the first model of these shoes would rip in the front of the shoe. Merrell now sells them as 'defect' shoes for a very low price in their outlet stores.

There is a model of the 1st Gen Mix Master that has a rock plate in the forefoot, but good luck finding a sales person who knows this, and or has them in the store. I haven't tried them yet but I think they are going to be awesome for what I need.

I would say these run true to size but if you don't have a wide foot you may find them feeling big. That is pretty much true for all Merrell shoes.

I'm not sure how to sum up my feelings about this shoe. It looked like it would be a great all-around shoe, but for they ended up not being very good for anything. But they are a great shoe, especially as a transition shoe to a barefoot shoe, and you might love them.

product_title: United Nude Women's Abstract Rome Sandal

review_body: I couldn't walk in them. Stood up and felt like I was going to tip over. NO WAY !! They are so gorgeous. The issue with why they didn't work for me...TOO STEEP. product_title: Capezio Daisy 205 Ballet Shoe (Toddler/Little Kid)
review_body: I was so happy with the price and quality of these shoes.  I purchased these for my 2 daughters' first ballet class.  I have prime, & with free returns, I did order 2 sizes each.  I was able to try them on and pick the best pair for each girl.  The shoes feel nice, and are holding up fine so far (through 4 classes so far, no signs of wear).  Great find!

product_title: Dearfoams Womens Velour Bootie Slipper
review_headline: A good solution to my problem.
review_body: These are relatively easy to put on and off and are very comfortable. Once  on- they stay put.  I am in a wheelchair , unable to walk-so these features are important to me.

product_title: Avia A325M Men's Walking Shoe
review_body: I bought these shoes strictly for their comfort and black color since I wear them with my work uniform. I walk all day and comfort is the most important factor. These shoes were extremely comfortable for my feet, however I found out very quickly(1 day of use) that they have no support whatsoever on the inside arch area. I have flat feet so that is important. If you look at the picture of them, you can see there is nothing but foam rubber in the center. That makes for a good first impression of comfort, but no longevity. The shoes pretty much just fell over on the inside and looked like they were many months old after one day of use. I was experiencing knee pain as a result of it. I can't wear these shoes again for any length of time or I will tear up my knees. If you have a large foot size or have any arch support needs, I cannot recommend these shoes. I think a person with smaller feet might be able to wear these.

product_title: ASICS Men's GEL-Lyte33 Running Shoe
review_headline: Light, cushioned, but not as other ASICS
review_body:
Well, first of all, I'm 6feet tall, and I weght 180pounds. Thats important because when I bought this shoes, I was awared they are mostly for thin guys who have high paces (I'm a slow runner), but I wanted them for tempo training and short distances. I used a pair of ASICS Cumulus 13 for over a year, and they had to suffer my 200 pounds for 3 months.

First of all, I have used them for 2 months, and their sole is too worn. It seems to be weaker than I spected. They are definitly not for long distances. After 5miles, their cushioning disapears. I had to admit I spected them to be dead by christmas when I bought Them.

The GOOD part, is that they are incredibly light and flexible, and helped me to run a lot faster. I have to admit that their cushioning surprised me and thei are incredibly breathable.

Anyway, I had to buy a pair of Saucony Triupmh 10 for the long runs, and I'm planing to use the Lyte's for intervals, speed work, and short races (up to 5 miles).

product_title: Miz Mooz Women's Petula Pump
review_body: Beautiful, stylish and comfortable.  l've never been disappointed with the quality of Miz Mooz though sometimes I've gotten a heal that is too high for me.  These are perfect.  I can spend the whole day on my feet and still be comfortable.

product_title: Timberland Adventure Seeker Two-Strap Sandal (Toddler/Little Kid)
review_body:
Bought this for my son, fit great and still looks good.

Has survived the summer with my son wearing them. That is a feat in itself. Soles are looking worn, natually, but the upper still looks great.

product_title: Skechers USA Men's Pebble Galeno Oxford
review_body: Ordered and received in August.  Now it's October and with light wear (about 3-4 days a week around campus for the last couple of months) the seams along the top are ripping apart. Ridiculous! Of course, it's too late for a refund. Won't be buying shoes through Amazon again, and probably won't be buying any more Sketchers period. product_title: Bloch Women's Prolite II Hybrid Ballet Slipper
review_body: My daughter had been fitted at a dance store for the size 6 C in pink. Then her director decided she needed white. When ordering from Amazon we saw there was a B width. Since she tends to have thinner feet, though not a true narrow, we decided to try the B width. They fit better than the ones from the store!

product_title: Sanuk Dotty V Slip-On (Toddler/Little Kid)
review_body: Bought for 4 yr old granddaughter and they were hard to get on, but when we did, her toes were at the end.  She wears an 11-12, went with the 11 from the reviews.  Disappointed and returning.  Adorable we'll made shoes. If they fit would have given 4 stars.

review_body: I really love these shoes. They are trendy but not silly-looking. I usually wear a size 5 but 5.5 is fine in these shoes because the cross strapping keeps the shoe in place. review_body:
I have an old pair of brown Flip Flop thong sandals that I love so decided to get a new pair - and try a different style.
The navy Slingback Sandal is actually more comfortable than the thongs and is so comfortable that it feels as though I'm not wearing anything on my feet - HEAVEN!

review_body:

review_body: These glasses are way too tinted for my taste. When I walk around, I see reflections from the inside of the glasses coming back into my eyes which is very distracting. These might be better for welding than for normal sun protection.

review_headline: The shoe part itself is comfortable, but it doesn't fit over my calf

I'm by no means fat (115lbs, 5', xtra small sized clothing and size 0-4 jeans) - it just seems that most manufacturers scale down leg size in proportion with foot size, which is not cool when you actually use your legs to walk/run/bike and build a normal amount of muscle.  The top part was fine over my thighs, and the shoe part was surprisingly comfortable (only tested standing since I obviously couldn't walk about with the top parts flapping about).

product_title: Irish Setter Men's 860 Elk Tracker Waterproof 1000 Gram 12" Big Game Hunting Boot
review_headline: Irish Setter Men's Elk Tracker WP 1000 grm. Insulation- 12" Big Game Boot
review_body: I purchased a pair of this same boot with 200 grm. insulation 5 years ago from a "Outdoor Supply Store" and have been very satisfied with the excellent comfort- until last winter- I started to have ingrown nails and was limited by the distance I could hike. I went back to the same store and got fitted for a new pair, at 56 years young, my feet had grown from a size 12 E to a 13 EE- much to my surprise they wanted $58.00 more !! It was in the middle of summer (I had not worn my old pair since winter) I also wanted the 1000 gram of insulation, the salesman said that was going to be an extra $20.00 (total $80.00 more than my original pair)- being in the middle of summer, I put the purchase off. I live in extreme N.E. Wyoming at 4,800 ft. and the winters get down to -40 at times.  I also have severe R.A. Knowing that the high quality  and wonderful fit of the Irish Setter line of Red Wing Footwear and how well my old ones still are in wonderful shape, I was going to look elsewhere (I live 70 miles from any city with a boot store)- I should not have been surprised to find that Amazon carries ALL of the high quality boots (they carry everything else I need- even the "Sno-seal" I use)- These boots are without a doubt, the best hunting/hiking winter footwear- I do a lot of sub- zero camping on our ranch as well as keep the 2 mile driveway and some times the county road clear- The last thing I need to worry about is "cold feet"- I can't say enough about the very High Quality of "Irish Setter"- use 3 coats of sno- seal (heat the boots before and after applying) and work it into the seams- Thanks Amazon for the speedy shipping and the great price

product_title: FRYE Women's Veronica Slouch Boot
review_headline: Why did I wait so long?

product_title: RFID Wallet Modern Money Clip - Eliminate Card Damage & Static, Slim Card Case Men & Women
review_body:
I've had it for 2 weeks now and it seems to be holding up pretty well. As some reviewers have noted, it is not meant to be a back pocket wallet. It is not sturdy enough to withstand that kind of weight or pressure. You can easily put a bend in it. Also, be careful where you set it down or what other items you put it with in your pocket, backpack, or purse (if you're a woman). The finish is susceptible to scratches. You also have to load 6 cards in there. If you load it with any less, it's easy to mis-align the cards with the slots, rendering useless the lever mechanism that pushes the cards out.

The concept of the wallet is great though! I've been wanting to get this for a few years now and finally have it. It beats struggling to get your credit cards out of a leather wallet and dealing with a wallet that stretches or comes apart at the seams after a few years. Also I like that people can't really see what cards you have. With a traditional wallet you have to open it up and people can see if you have money in there and also see which and what type of cards you have in there, potentially tempting would-be thieves who may be in line with you or near you at a cash register. I didn't get this to hold cash or receipts since money clip type accessories aren't the best at protecting. I use this ACM wallet in combination with a Taxi wallet that I put in my other front pocket. So I have two compact wallets specifically designed for easy removal of credit cards (the ACM wallet) and cash/receipts (the Taxi wallet.) Hopefully this'll be the last wallet I buy for the next decade or longer! Now if they only could put a cover to protect the finish but allow you to still operate the buttons, this would be a 5-star product!

product_title: Polo PH1129 Eyeglasses-9233 Matte Brusched Gunmetal-53mm
review_headline: This is the best balance for today's glasses.
review_body:
Glasses like a computer mouse are as individual as the people that wear them. The first consideration is the individual.

In searching for glasses unless you have deep pockets and pick a different pair for each outfit you will need to strike a balance. Balance that can still be individual but you will have to take in consideration that you are just looking at of them whereas others are looking at them. There are some classics in design and material that are timeless yet run the risk of appearing outdated. Others can be glitzy or structurally unsound and in style for a year or two.

I usually make a quick decision on what I like or what I will buy; however in this case I needed to strike that balance of one pair of glasses that works for work, works for play, and works for me.

I tried gold wire rims but they look like something out of a World War I movie. I tried some expensive designer thick black rimmed glasses however they look like military issue that I had in the Vietnam War.

I also had to take in consideration the amount of glass that I will be using it as I have progressive lenses. Another consideration is to use magnetically attached sunglasses or drugstore over sunglasses.

I finally settled on Polo Ralph Lauren PH 1129 Eyeglasses (MATTE BRUSCHED DARK GUNMETAL) to match my skin tone and closer to where. I was a little nervous at first as they look different. However now just like buying a car you think you have a unique card to you go down the road and find out every other car is the same one.

Wearing these glasses will not make you unique however you will have that feeling of a new haircut that you know you look good.

review_body: I waited too long to order these at a department store, and they were gone, so I was thrilled to see them on Amazon.  This is the most comfortable shoe I've ever worn in my life.  I have a wide foot and was sure they weren't going to fit, but I took a chance.  I was shocked that they were actually a little too big when I first put them on (though a little tight on the top of my foot, but is stretching out a little).  My heel almost slipped out.  However, I decided to give them a try and I'm thrilled I did.  After years of thinking the wedge is what made the difference in a comfortable shoe, I finally figured out that it's the wedge INTO the platform rise that makes all the difference in the world.  I first discovered this phenomenon in the Carlos Santana Baja sandal (which previously held the distinction of "Most Comfortable Shoe Ever").  Had I known at the time, I would have ordered a lifetime supply.  However, most shoe companies (including my beloved Carlos Santana) now make the actual base of the shoe narrow/skinny, which causes a stability problem.  Not this shoe!  The base is actually wide enough to support the foot, making it possible to walk in them with confidence and without fear of falling off the shoe and breaking an ankle.  And they're lightweight!  They're dreamy!  I love them!

product_title: New Balance Women's WW895 Walking Shoe
review_headline: I love these walking shoes! My first!
review_body:
I've never bought any kind of walking shoes (or any other sports shoes) for myself until I bought two pairs of these recently. Reason: I'm doing physical therapy for leg muscle problems, and I hoped these would help me with my balance problems.

I went with New Balance because I had good experiences with their shoes for my son when he was young.

I was not disappointed. These are feather-light, I almost don't know I am wearing any shoes at all. The arch support could be better, but I have inserts for that if I feel I need it.

I walk a *lot*. I go through shoe soles like crazy. But these are holding out very well after a couple of months. Very pleased!

Please note, they fit well at the stated size if I wear lightweight hosiery or thin socks. If I were planning to wear thicker socks I would go up a half size.

I've been grabbing these up whenever I see them on sale because I love them so much.

product_title: Salomon Men's XA PRO 3D Ultra 2 Trail Running Shoe
review_headline: Hot feet!  and they don't last
review_body:
I have had this shoe for a few months and did a week of heavy hiking in Glacier National Park with them. So I cannot speak to the long term durability of the shoe. But it is very comfortable, and I think it is a very good looking trail shoe.

My one complaint is that this shoe does not breath, and my feet get very hot--definitely hotter than they do in my leather Asolo boots. When I wear them while working on the computer at home I eventually have to take them off because the heat becomes too uncomfortable.

UPDATE: I've had these shoes for three years now, and just in the last two weeks the glue attaching the sole to the shoe has deteriorated, separating the sole from the shoe. By the time I noticed this was happening, enough moisture had already gotten into the shoe to break apart the shoe itself. I put shoe goo on everything, but I must have missed a spot somewhere because just wearing them in wet grass yesterday I came home with two wet feet.

In short, these shoes have less than a 3-year life. I have good hiking shoes that are 20 years old. They just don't hold up well at all.

I forgot they are British sized, not American so mine are a little on the big side but that's ok with me as it's winter and thicker socks will take care of that.  At my age my feet have gotten a little bigger and roomy shoes are a good thing. If they bother me later there's room for a pair of inner soles and that will take up all the extra room.  Bottom line the feel and quality of Clarks originals Desert Boot are the same now as I remember them 50 years ago. Incredibly comfortable out of the box and long lasting as always. The thing about Clarks, weather Desert Boots, Wallabees, Desert Treks, in a short time they stop being your shoes and become your best friends. The toe strap does tighten with wear, but it takes two seconds to readjust. Directions for fitting arrive in your box. Familiarize yourself with the technique and you're all set.

product_title: Vasque Men's Sundowner Gore-Tex Waterproof Backpacking Boot
review_headline: Don't waste your money on these boots
review_body:
In 1986 I purchased a pair of Vasque Sundowners and right out of the box they were as soft as butter and unbelievably comfortable. The break in time was extremely minimal and I love everything about these boots. I wore these boots for fifteen years or more and had LITERALLY thousands of miles on them. I don't ever remember getting a blister in these boots and the traction, support and overall comfort were great.

When they wore out of course I didn't think twice about what the next pair of boots was going to be so I went out and got another pair. It didn't take long at all...week or two, for me to notice these WERE NOT the same high quality boot I had come to love. They didn't fit right and I was getting blisters. The sole had been changed and traction on rock and especially wet rock was extremely diminished. This was not a quality boot. After calling Red Wing (US Distributor) the answer was apparent. These boots used to be hand made in Italy until Vasque decided to save a buck and move production to China. Yee Ha! They would not take my boots back but I was told I could pay a bunch more money and upgrade to the next level which were supposedly still made in Italy. I wore the boots for a few years and they never did break in...still getting blisters after hundreds and hundreds of miles so I finally threw them away and got a pair of Asolo boots. Don't waste your money here.

My only issue so far is that the toe box is a little narrow compared to other shoes. I never buy wide shoes, but in this case I might have considered it if I could try them on.

An alternative to look at is the Saucony Omni 12, which has just slightly more drop (1/2 mm difference), less heel cushioning, a slightly less pronation control, more stiffness, and a slightly different shape. It's a Runners World editor's pick. I decided between those two by running in them a bit in a store and choosing which felt more natural. In my case it was the Hurricane.

product_title: Kamik Women's Jennifer Rain Boot
review_headline: Great boot, but calves are small
review_body:
I didn't buy this off Amazon, but I got it in the bright red (not the burgundy red). The picture here is off - the red is a beautiful true red (I will post a pic later). That particular color has been discontinued, so get it quickly if you want it!

The boots are made in Canada and the quality seems excellent. I called the company and asked a few questions and they were exceptionally nice and helpful. The little emblem on the side kind of looks like a Ferrari symbol and really adds to the boots' polished look.

If you are wanting a pair of boots to stick your pants down in, note that these are tight, stylish boots that come up high on your leg and are meant to be worn with leggings, skinny jeans, a skirt, or similar. I am pretty average all around, so I imagine my calf is pretty average and they are skin tight on me - I can barely wear them and cannot get my skinny jeans in them. I get kind of claustrophobic when I am trying to take them off. They seem true to size and fit well in the arch. I have a wider foot and they feel comfortable on me.

I haven't decided if I am going to keep them yet. I need a pair that is very open at the top, but these are just so pretty and well-made that I will probably keep them for days when I am wearing a skirt or shorts and need them. I read of a way you can cut rain boots down the back and add grommets and ribbon to open them up and make them adjustable to your needs. I feel like that would ruin the clean lines of this particular boot, but it is an option to consider if you are having difficulties finding a boot to suit your calves.

Bottom line: Quality and style for sure, just think about what you want in a boot and how the tightness fits your needs.
