product_title: La Sportiva Men's Tarantula Climbing Shoe
review_body:
I see all the kids at the gym knocking around in the Evolv Defy VCS and feel sorry for them; those things don't hold a candle to Sportivas' Tarantula. As entry level shoes go, they are hard to beat. When I began climbing this spring I tried on all the shoes under $120, and nothing (with maybe the exception of the nago for all around comfort, tho I think the tarantula is more aggressive) fit my feet and climbed as well as these. They fit my heel like a suction cup, edge well, have great sensitivity, and the suede is very comfortable and form fitting. What I can't edge I can smear with no problem, great traction! I started out on 5.8/5.9 this spring, now working 5.11b/c and V4 and these green machines haven't let me down at all. In fact I only just this week bought more aggressive shoes for super steep stuff.

**A note on sizing** These do run very big! Try them on if possible. My current pair is 42, but I wear 44-45 in most other climbing shoes. Buy them tight, the suede stretches some (not tons) and the rubber forms really well to my feet once warm- in fact I can see slight swells in the rand where my toe knuckles push into it, and I climb with great comfort.

My ONLY complaint is that the stitching in the pull loops in the heel area digs into my feet like knives. I have been solving this problem with sports tape on my heel, has worked well but leaves residue on the shoes. Haven't seen this complaint from others, so it may just be my feet.

La Sportiva customer service has also been second to none! I actually started with a pair of tarantulace shoes which developed an early sole delamination. Not only was Sportiva customer support super prompt and accommodating, they replaced my shoes for the easier to put on model and at a half size down (first ones stretched more than I thought they would). Thanks Sportiva, you rock!

I looked at dozens of comments on sizing on several sites and came to this conclusion - order 3 sizes down from your regular US size (I wear a women's 7M so I took a shot and ordered a AU size 4. PERFECT! AU sizing is hard to translate into US. If you order a 6-1/2, it's still a size 6 only wider. Their half sizes are just a wider version of the full size so keep this in mind. They also run a tad wide (C in this model - D in the others) so without the extra insoles they're a bit loose but with them the fit is excellent. The quality of the leather is terrific too. I just wonder how long the pull tabs are going to last. They're made to be durable so I'm hoping thru the life of the boot. I'm starting to save up now to get a pair in black now too. HAPPY DANCE!

review_body:

review_body:

You give up a degree of precision in your choice when you shop online (vs. trying on the shoes and walking around inside the brick & mortar store). But, the tradeoffs are well worth it, and I'm glad I was able to shop this way.

review_headline: Fantastic and well worth the price!
review_body: It's tough to find a good pair of sunglasses. After going years with cheap $20 pairs, I decided to look for a good upgrade and spend a bit extra. Well, this pair is near flawless. The sides are thick, so you get a bit of privacy from people viewing you from the side (i.e. when you take a nap on the bus.) Also, something to note is the way it sits on your face, obviously there are different shaped faces, but for me, the glasses sit far enough away so it doesn't press on your cheeks when you move your mouth or smile. The contact points are the sides of the ear and bridge of the nose - perfect. They also have a nice green tint to them, very subtle and providing a good amount of shading. They're also polarized, which adds to the cost, but increases the benefit. They also come with a large case, a little minus because it's so large, but they're specifically made for these so they won't get bent or crushed. Give these a try, I think you'll be quite happy you did.

review_headline: Bad circulation? Take a look at this shoe!
review_body:
My husband needed a pair of shoes he could wear out to lunch, something without socks to go with shorts, but because he has horrible circulation problems in his legs it was hard to find Mr. Goodshoe.

So I needed a shoe for him that was soft enough inside that it wouldn't cause any sore spots with bare feet, and high enough in the arch that it wouldn't put too much pressure on the tops of his feet, and generous toe room to keep his pinkies happy.
Basically, he needed a slipper shoe that provided all the comfort of a house slipper, but didn't look like like a house slipper.

These fit him really good (sizing seems right on), high enough they don't put undue pressure on the tops of his feet, generous toe room, and furry soft and comfy inside. He loves them. Yes, they do stretch a little over time, but so far not excessively. I was so happy, I'd looked at tons of shoes trying to find exactly this style, and I had no idea if i'd ever find it.

It fits him so perfectly with no pressure in the places that count.

Hey all you old guys with bad circulation, take a look at this shoe!

review_body:

The button on the inside of each foot has caused blisters on both feet of both of my sons. Upon examining the older Crocs (being replaced because they are worn out, not outgrown), the strap attachment button definitely sticks out farther on both new pairs versus the older pairs. This feature on the old pairs appears to be recessed, probably due to a tighter clamping force during manufacturing. This change in manufacturing appears to be the root cause of the blisters. This change appears on both the size C10/11 and C8/9 pairs that I purchased.

As long as the attachment button protrudes from the inside of the shoe, I cannot recommend purchasing this product.

review_headline: Perfect Sunglasses!  Incredible price for the quality!

But I also wear contacts and did not want to make the huge investment in prescription sunglasses. So I came online and went through Amazon's selections, and I kept coming back to these. The reviews are tip top and addressed the concerns I had. So I measured my glasses and figured that the medium-sized pair would just fit over my glasses. Another plus was that these fit over sunglasses were eligible for free returns. So there was nothing to lose. Well, I made the right choice. These are exactly as described and fit perfectly. They are comfortable, and the sun does not leak in over or under the sunglasses. Optical quality is excellent, and my vision through my glasses and these fitovers is perfect. The measurement instructions were also accurate and as precise as possible when you're talking about three different sizes.

I'm going to order another pair to keep in the car so that I have one in my purse. The price can't be beat for the quality. I'm pleased and impressed, and thankful for the many reviews that steered me to these wonderful sunglasses.

product_title: KEEN Women's Harvest Shoe
review_body: First off, I got these on super sale, so $29 total for a pair of Keens is a great deal.  So because they were on sale, it made me want to make these shoes work.  I wear orthotics on all my closed toe shoes, and the main problem for me is that the orthotics make the shoes slip off.  Well, there is a little slippage, but nothing that those pedi socks can't solve.  Even with orthotics on, the sides of the shoes skim the lower part of my ankle.  I tried the shoes without the orth. and they definitely cut in.  On the other hand, with orth, the middle strap became a problem.  The stitching of the canvas where it fold under the strap is rough, so that dug into my foot.  I wore thicker socks around the house to break them in a little, hoping the strap will have a little more give.  In the end, after about a few days of indecision, I decided to keep them.  The middle strap no longer bugs me (though there's still a very light indentation on the top of my foot).  I like the thick soles (as I've tried on other keens and with those, I could feel pebbles underfoot).  Per suggestions I read on other reviews, I bought a 1/2 size smaller.  I normally wear an 8M and got a 7.5M.  They are true to width and length for me.  These were not my first choice in color, but couldn't pass up on deal.

product_title: Tommy Bahama Men's Tahiti Sandal
review_headline: Knock off product and seller wouldn't stand behind it.
review_body: First off, I've purchased numerous Tommy Bahama products ranging from candles to camp shirts. If you've paid the larger price tag for this brand you know, the quality is generally better than average and rarely a disappointment. I splurged and bought these $45 flip-flops thinking they'd be extra comfortable and last a while like most of the TB products I've purchased. Within a couple days, the left sandal was fading rapidly and the right wasn't at all. I immediately contacted Tommy Bahama directly to ask about a replacement for the defect and submitted it with pictures. Tommy Bahama's response was that this wasn't a product that they offer on their website or in their stores, so they couldn't help. They recommended I submit my issue to the seller, which I did as I'd purchased these through Amazon. The seller responded by stating that they wouldn't do anything as the sandal had been worn, even if only for a few days. When I stated the obvious that the sandal's defect couldn't possibly be noticed until it was worn, they stood firm. They only offered a $10 refund for the problem when I warned them that I would leave negative feedback on here if they didn't stand behind the product and at least replace it with a new sandal. I never received the $10.

product_title: Vivobarefoot Women's Ultra L-W
review_headline: They are too big but awesome shoes
review_body: I had previously ordered some Vivo running shoes unaware that the running line tends to run small, I normally wear Vivobarefoot shoes and I usually wear a 37, but in most of the running shoes I have to size up to a 38. I had read reviews on here that lead me to believe I needed to size up in the Ultra's and wish I hadn't, they are WAY too big! I actually could probably have sized down in these shoes to a 36, although my husband got them in his regular Vivo size and they fit him perfectly. I should have sent them back to get the 37, but didn't...and now the price has gone up or I would have just bought a new pair :,( so I will have to wait it out now. I tried to wear them instead of sending them back because I was really in need of some running shoes. I wish I had sized down though. Other than that, these are amazing shoes, great for running and almost anything else outdoor you can think up. I love the sock liner. They don't rub funny anywhere, and I have had tons and tons of compliments on these shoes when I wear them. They are super light and easy to wash off! Great shoes!!! Oh one last note on this: a few reviewers complained about these shoes wearing out quickly, neither my husband nor I have had this problem, and even though mine were too big I wore them A LOT, and I wore them on HOT trails all summer because we run a lot and we live in the Mojave desert.... We love the heat so we don't shy away from running, hiking, etc in the middle of a hot summer day and my shoes have never had any issues of wearing down at all. I wore them all summer. I believe this is due to the fact that we run with proper barefoot form, and that those who wore the shoes out must have been running improperly. The Vivobarefoot website has a great deal of information on how to correctly run properly barefoot, if you aren't a seasoned barefoot runner, or if you are and haven't checked it out, then check it out because its great info and will save you and your shoes from a lot of pain! (and Idon't work for Vivobarefoot, although I probably should since I love their products so much! Lol)

review_body:
I selected this sandal because it's not as "clunky" looking as a lot of other Birkestocks. The slightly angular position and cut of the multiple straps makes them a bit more feminine, I think. A few years ago I had an issue with my foot (plantar fascitis), did a lot of research, and saw that a lot of folks were able to alleviate some of the pain by wearing Birkenstocks. Well, it worked for me, too, although a recent siege of the same ailment was not as quick to respond. But, the first time, I got immediate relief!

I've been wearing these shoes around the house and on my daily travels ever since, and even purchased some Birkenstock inserts for other shoes. My feet respond so well to these shoes! I do wear regular leather shoes (Clarks and such) but my feet just feel at home in these hardy, German-made shoes!

I've purchased the black as well as another grayish color, and even though they're simulated leather (uppers), I find them sturdy and long wearing. I have other Birkenstocks that I've had for well over 7 years, and they're just as nice as when I first bought them.

The sizing is a bit tricky. Always thought I had a medium-wide (B) foot, but have found that I need the "filled-in" (narrow) sole for best fit. Once you find the right size and break them in, you'll find it's often your "go-to" shoe!!

product_title: Mens Hoka One One Bondi 2
review_body:
I am a relatively large runner (6'2\\", 195 lbs., 20 miles per week) and historically have intermittent knee pain. The Hoka One One Bondi's were recommended to me to try as they are generally very well received by heavier runners with knee and ankle pain.

My initial impressions were very favorable: they are extremely comfortable and walking on them is almost like walking on pillows. They are very isolating from the surface, so much so that it took me a while to get comfortable with a normal walking gait (they felt positively clumsy on stairs.) I did run on them on a treadmill and that took far more adjustment than expected and I didn't feel particularly secure in them because they are so isolating. I generally wear a size 12, and these felt overall reasonably true to size, though my subjective experience is that the toe box is wider than I'm used to (I generally run in ASICS, normally Noosas.) During the days I wore them I became more and more aware of a defect that I am sure is unique to my individual pair: the left shoe is very comfortable with no hot spots, but in the right shoe on the outboard side of the area where the tongue attaches to the structure of the toe box there is a large ridge of fabric that feels very prominent within the shoe, rubbing the top of my foot and irritating it greatly. It was this defect combined with the isolation from the surface being walked or run on that made me finally elect to return these shoes as unsuitable for me.

While I am sure that these are great shoes for very heavy people or people who value a very plush footwear experience and are willing to trade off much of the sensation of the surface they are running on, I have no regrets about returning mine. The apparent defect in the right shoe was the only blemish on what looked like otherwise beautifully constructed shoes, and I can't comment on durability as I had them for a relatively short time and never raced in them (I ran substantially slower in them on my treadmill as I didn't feel very secure in them; I feel confident my speed would have returned to some degree after getting more used to them.) I have returned to other shoes and am glad I tried the Hoka's and certainly wish they had worked for me as minimizing knee trauma is something I need to be constantly aware of and it's one area the Hoka's reportedly excel in. Unfortunately the negatives outweighed the benefits these shoes could have held for my joints.n my treadmill as I didn't feel very secure in them; I feel confident my speed would have returned to some degree after getting more used to them.) Two front zip pocket extend out, so it won't take any inside space. Plus, the zipper is very easy to open with one hand (Its good for a busy mommy to grab cleansing wipes all the time...)
So, one pocket has baby rice crackers, and small packages of formula. The other has sunscreen, diaper cream, and two type of cleansing wipes.)

Behind the 2 pop out zip pockets, there's another big zip pocket outside the main opening.
Since this will take up space inside, I usually keep some flat stuff here( breastfeeding cover, thin blanket to cover baby if too cold, soft waterproof bib, spoon, and small jacket for the baby)

Inside the main opening, there's another big zip pocket inside on the back side wall. I still some flat stuff here like disposable changing pad and some small towels incase baby accident..(throw up, or anything that tissue doesn't work....can't imagine but just in case...)

In the main opening area, I put an ergo baby carrier in it, and still have room for the thermo container, Sippy cup, water bottle, diapers(5-7 pieces), wipes, cleaning cloths, changing pad, and a bag of toys...

Yeh, anything you can think of, I should have it inside this bag, and the weight is not that heavy.

I usually keep the crossing strap short so I can put it directly over the stroller arms and carry it over my shoulder since the shoulder strip is longer than the Kipling diaper bag...which solve the issue of this travel bag doesn't have the adjustable strip forstroller arms.

The plus is....once the baby grow up, I can still use this as a carryon travel bag or day to day bag. I think it will last for a long time, since the quality of Kipling is really good.

Hope my review will help any mom out there who are searching a perfect diaper bag.
Good Luck!! ^_^

product_title: 5.11 Tactical A.T.A.C. 6" Shield Side Zip Boot
review_headline: Run a Little Large, but Go Through Metal Detector!
review_body:
I have very small feet and usually wear size 6 or 6.5. I ordered a size 6, which were much too large. Thankfully, Amazon's exchange service is excellent, and I shipped back the large ones and had size 5 in my hands in just a couple days, at no extra cost. The size 5 fits great, very comfortable at first try walking around the house. I took them to work in the box to test whether they go through the metal detector without getting them dirty, and they *DO* go through just fine! The zipper is very convenient, just get your laces all tightened up once and then use the zipper from then on out. Like I said they feel very comfortable and secure at this point, I will update after I have more day-to-day use of them. So far so good - you just might want to try a size smaller than you're used to.

[UPDATE after 3 Months of Wear]
Wow! I love these boots! For the first month or so, they made my feet very sore. Definitely took a good while to break them in. However, now that they're broken in, they're my favorite shoes. I wear them at home and on the weekends as well as at work now because I like them so much.

There are only a couple tiny annoyances with them at this point. Number one is that the zipper needs to have more room in it when you unzip it. When you unzip the zipper, it has a fold inside that gives you enough room to slide your foot in without untying the laces. Well, that fold needs to allow for more room. When I put the shoes on it takes a good bit of effort to wiggle and wrench my feet in there. It's a very tight squeeze. Once the boots are on, they feel wonderful, though, so it's not a huge deal, just kind of annoying. The other thing is very minor. I hate the shoelaces that come with these. They're round and slick-ish. Even though I've double-knotted them twice over as tight as I can get them, they still come untied, usually a couple times a day. It's really annoying, I'm probably going to go out and find some flatlaces that will fit these so they'll stay tied.

I've gotten these all wet and muddy and my feet inside stayed dry and comfortable. I let the mud dry on the boots and later a bit of stomping around on the concrete and they're good as new again. They still look great. These things are sexy.

product_title: John Fluevog Women's Bradenburg Oxford
review_headline: Quality shoes, however, consider your sizing strategy
review_body:
I normally wear a size 10, on occasion a 9.5 (in Frye's, for example). My foot is slightly wider than a \\"B\\" (C width is perfect but impossible to find). I ordered these in a size 10, however, potential buyers should be aware that this is a men's shoe, which Fluevog markets as a woman's shoe as well. As a result of the size conversion from men's to women's size, I was provided a size 8. The fit is right on. That considered, I would recommend that if you are a woman who has a slightly narrow foot to think twice before ordering this shoe. LIkewise, if you wear a medium width, be prepared for the possibility of having to wear socks. I realize shoe fit is a very individual thing, and with free returns, perhaps you'll want to make your own decision.

Oh yes - as for the quality: craftsmanship and leather is wonderful, and the tan color will be quite versatile for the fall and winter. They'll break in and age beautifully.

product_title: Sugar Skull Women's Bandana Clutch Coin Purse
review_body:
I have a purse, had a wallet (but returned because of the in ability to use all the compartments due to a terrible design or manufacturer mistake), card case and then ordered this coin purse to match my collection of the "skull bandana" Loungefly design series. I really really wanted to love (or at the very least) like it ---- but the only feature I expect to work in a "coin purse" is that is can successfully hold my coins. Not a bunch of coins mind you, just a few assorted ones for metered parking.

BOO! Sadly I didn't purchase this from amazon.com, instead I found this at a local mom and pop shop. unfortunately these brick and mortar businesses rarely have reasonable return policies so it can be a real crap shoot shopping the "old fashioned way." Since I didn't want to be a difficult customer - I just sucked it up and thought my DIY novice skills could fix the defective clasps. I was wrong!

Now, intellectually and business-wise, I understand why companies send they products to China for their cheap manufacturing prices per unit; however, unlike when I was a kid growing up in the 1970's and 1980's in Southern Florida....when the "made in china" sticker was no big deal (or so we all thought - now I suspect they knew all too well what they were doing adding LEAD, YES THAT SAME POISONOUS ELEMENT from the periodic table to the most random of cheap crap).

My father is a brilliant and exceedingly humble genius physician so I recently asked him why purses made in China would contain LEAD? It's a frickin fake leather or vinyl accessory for goodness sake! And his reply was that cheap lead makes their products heavier and therefore appear to be of higher quality.

Loungefly designs are so unique (this does not include their hello kitty, etc. lines), but the time has come when quality is a basic expectation for products we spend our ever inflated hard earned dollars on. This item will not keep anything you put into either of the two clasp compartment safe and instead they end up at the bottom of your handbag.

I urge companies to focus on QUALITY CONTROL before we as consumers have no choice but to boycott or flat out just stop buying products from companies that have let us down more than once or twice!anything you put into either of the two clasp compartment safe and instead they end up at the bottom of your handbag.

product_title: Palladium Women's Baggy Lite Leather Gusset Boot
review_headline: Ok, what's with the styrofoam soles?
review_body:
The product information says \\"rubber soles\\". We all know what that looks and feels like, right? Well, these shoes are very light weight because the soles are made of a styrofoam-like material, molded with a little bit of texture and of course, some treaded protrusions, however the material itself is VERY SLICK. If you put one of these in a puddle, it will float really well (think crocks). But I don't want to walk on water, I want to walk through it without falling on my butt. My concern is when I'm hiking through the mud or simply walking through the city on a rainy day, these things are going to compromise my mission. It might seem strange to say when we're talking about a \\"tactical boot\\" which got it's beginnings as the official military boot of the French Foreign Legion, but these boots are of questionable quality. Palladium now uses their history as an ad campaign to sell fashion without the function and quality once attributed to their name. It is a real bummer, but even more disappointing when one has to wait a week for something to come in the mail just top find that it is of poor quality. I have officially learned my lesson with buying shoes on Amazon. DONT, unless you've seen the exact shoe in person.

I got these for $67.00 but I would NEVER pay the $140.00 they are asking now.

product_title: Robeez Navy Braedon Soft Sole Slip-On (Infant)
review_headline: Robeez allow for natural foot development with protection from the elements
review_body: We have now used Robeez soft soles for all three of our children, and have loved them every time.  They are well constructed and cute to boot.  Be prepared for scuffed toe marks, as the pigment is only on the exterior, and holes eventually developing under the big toe.  It takes months of wear on concrete before a hole is worn under the toe, but is the nature of having a soft sole...well worth the trade off for allowing natural foot development!  Our children wore holes in many pairs, but most did not appear until they were ready to move up in size anyway.  We liked having at least two pairs of each size, which allowed for a dry pair if the first got wet from water play and needed time to dry.  Daily occurrence around our house!

product_title: Brinley Co Womens Zipper Detail Faux Leather Backpack
review_headline: a cute little bag with a GIANT smell
review_body: i wanted an inexpensive, stylish, little backpack for running errands while still healing from an injury and walking with a cane. i also thought having all those awesome outer pockets would help keep my stuff organized. the seller should really clarify that only two of the front zipper pockets are actual pockets. the rest are just sewed on zippers with no actual pockets that do nothing but add unnecessary weight (the little things you grab to unzip zipper are heavier than nickels) and they are incredibly loud and jingly, making it very annoying to walk, since basically everyone can hear you jingling along about a block away. super annoying. and then there's the smell. its horrifying. like it was dipped in fish guts aged for a year along with a dumpster full of used maxi pads. this is not an exaggeration. since using this bag in public i have overheard people remarking and/or wondering what that awful stench they smell is. this has happened more than once and in a very large classroom with my bag all the way across the room from the persons whose nostrils were being offended. it was embarrassing to say the very least. i stuffed it with dryer sheets all over to try and dissipate the smell, but its been over a month and it is still too stinky to bring to anyplace where it will be in an enclosed space with other people. its really disgusting and now there are people who think i am a smelly person when it was actually this smelly little bag. i shouldve spent more and gotten the bag i wanted. lesson: you get what you pay for. and bags from china smell really bad.

product_title: Kamik Women's Kelly Boot
review_headline: More snug than I'd like, but I'm keeping them
review_body:
I read the reviews before I ordered the boot, so I was a little nervous about sizing - and I was right to be. I'm usually about a 9 or so and these boots (which I ordered in a 10) are definitely a little snug. I tested them out with some thick wool socks and while I can get my feet in alright, there's not much room.

If they made them in a size 11 I would swap these guys out in a heartbeat, but unfortunately they don't. I like the boot enough to stick with it and hope for the best! They are extremely comfortable and cute. There's room in the calf for me to tuck in my jeans and I love, LOVE the traction on the bottom. I'm going to feel a lot better about all the snow and ice.

My only concern is that I'm going to be taking these boots to Ukraine with me, where it gets cold beyond cold, and I might end up needing more space inside for layers than the boot allows. Hopefully the fleece lining compensates for the extra socks that I won't be able to jam in there. Otherwise, no complaints! Seems like a really well-made rainboot.

product_title: Brooks Women's Glycerin 9 Running Shoe
review_headline: Don't buy Brooks - the treads tear off with minimal wear
review_body:
This was my first pair of Brooks shoes - women's Glycerin 9, which I purchased on clearance from a local outfitters store. Before this pair, I mostly wore Asics and Saucony both for running and walking, and I never had a problem with them falling apart. But only four months into this Brooks pair, the treads began to pull off the bottom of the right shoe. I did not run in them and only wore them casually a few hours a day a few days a week to run errands. They still looked brand new, including the treads with minimal treadwear, when the first tread began to tear off.

I contacted Brooks, and first they said these shoes are for running and not walking. What a joke! Like running over rocks and different terrain wouldn't tear them up faster than wearing them on a carpet or other flat surface. I understand how your feet hit the surface differently when running and how that would affect treadwear, but should anything really cause the treads to rip away from the shoe when they're basically new? Maybe working in a junkyard with sharp objects everywhere? Then Brooks told me the shoes are only meant to last 4 - 6 months. I went ahead and filed a claim for a defective item on the Brooks site (along with the photo of my new shoe with torn tread--Amazon won't let me upload because I didn't purchase it from them), and they replied: \\"When used for its intended purpose, Brooks footwear has an expected life of 300-500 miles or 4-6 months. By this measure and your described pattern of use, it's about time to update your shoes.\\" Then they offered me a 25% discount on another pair. NO THANKS. I'm guessing my shoes got about 100 miles before the tread tore.

I have worn Asics, Saucony, Nike, Adidas, New Balance, and other brands, and none of them have ever fallen apart like these Brooks. My Asics and Saucony shoes I wore for over a year with custom orthotics, and I only replaced them when the treads were slightly worn down as expected--even before I could feel they had worn. Based on the poor quality of Brooks and their poor customer service, I will never buy another pair. After searching the reviews, I noticed others had similar complaints about them falling apart easily. These Glycerin 9's weren't even worth the clearance price for four months of gentle casual wear.uld feel they had worn. review_body:
These sights are wonderful, some people say Troy are better and I do not disagree that troy are quality back up sights. But magpul are cost effective and in a drop test they seemed more durable than Diamondhead/Troy. Not only did they retain zero better than the others, but they seemed to handle impact better than metal.

Taken from an article on KitUp

\\"In order to test whether certain popular BUIS would still be serviceable after taking a hard hit, I attached three different types of BUIS - Troy Industries, Magpul Industries and Diamondhead USA - to an AR-15 rifle chambered in .300 AAC Blackout weighing 7 pounds and dropped the rifle upside down from a height of 5 feet onto a concrete surface.

Other portions of the rifle were protected from damage, and each set of BUIS took a solid hit from the drop. The ammunition used was Remington Premier Match .300 AAC Blackout 125 gr OTM. Each sighting device was installed according to the manufacturer's instructions, then points of impact was established from a stable shooting position at 25 and 200 yards. After the drop, the rifle was fired again, and any change in point of impact noted.

The first BUIS dropped was the Diamondhead. At first, damage appeared cosmetic only; however, the apertures could no longer be rotated, windage could not be adjusted, and there was a definite cant to the BUIS. Point of impact shifted approximately 16 MOA. We contacted Diamondhead with this result. They replied that a newer version was available which was more durable. We offered to test the new model but production issues meant they could not ship one to us.

Next came the Troy sight. Cosmetic damage was apparent, but the sight could still be operated normally. Point of impact shift was approximately 3 MOA.

The last set of BUIS was the Magpul MBUS. Damage was purely cosmetic and the sight remained fully functional. Point of impact shift was less than 1 MOA. Unlike the other sighting devices, a second drop was performed. Results did not change, and the sight remained functional.\\"

Now my personal experience with these is on my M&P15-22 but I'm ordering an additional MBUS for the AR I am building. They are really good quality, just make sure you don't get a PTS sight from a bad retailer.

product_title: Brooks Women's PureCadence 2 Lightweight Running Shoes
review_body:
I got the original PureCadences on sale at DSW a few months ago when I wanted to give running another try. After years of thinking I couldn't run because of knee, hip and back pain, learning to land with a mid-foot strike and wearing less-cushy, more \\"minimal\\" shoes was a revelation. I not only don't hate running, I now actually enjoy it!

So having found a love for running, I did what the experts tell you to do and went to my local running store to get fitted for shoes. Lo and behold, the best pair I tried out was the Brooks PureCadence 2s (I tried pairs from Saucony, Asics and New Balance as well). They fit well, are true to size (I wear a pretty standard women's 8M). They have enough cushioning to be comfortable to a slightly overweight newbie runner, but still are minimal enough to encourage a mid-foot strike. They offer a little more stability control than the other shoes in the Pure line-up, but still have a minimal 4mm drop and a stiff enough ride that you can feel the ground somewhat as you run. All in all it's a great balance: not too minimal for a beginner, but not too much shoe either.

I should also note that my running store recommended replacement insoles ([[ASIN:B004K1FIES Superfeet Black Premium Insoles]]) for these and even let me try out the shoes with and without the insoles before I paid for them. The insole is the cheapest part of any shoe, and if the ones that don't come with the shoes do not support your arch properly or cause you pain, it is easy and fairly inexpensive to change them out. Also, they had me try some different running socks ([[ASIN:B009I067QE Feetures! Elite Merino Light Cushion No Show Tab Socks]]) that were a HUGE improvement over the cheap-o ones I got at Target. Socks can change how the shoes fit, how comfortably and how long you can run in them, how much cushioning you have on your run, everything.

review_headline: Customer Satisfaction is Not a Priority
review_body:
I received these boots this morning and was pleasantly surprised as to how fast the shipping speed was. The boots themselves look nice, but are WAY TOO SMALL. Some reviewers said to order half a size up, but you need to order AT LEAST 2 sizes up. I have tiny feet... I wear a size 3 in girls. So I thought ordering the smallest size available (size 5) would allow me plenty of room for socks... My foot hardly fits into these boots even without socks. I have skinny legs too yet zipping in the zipper in the back made the boots too tight on my calves.

I addressed this issue to the seller who responded that if I were to return the item, I must pay the return postage which is over $15- I bought these boots for $23 and yet I will only get a few dollars back because as the seller responded, \\"it is not economical for us to pay the postage.\\" Had I worn the true size 5, sure it makes sense that I should pay the postage because it was my fault for ordering the true size. But when I order two sizes larger and they don't fit, it's THE SELLER'S FAULT.

Making a few bucks from me and losing a customer over such lousy customer service should be worth it for you guys. I have told my friends and family to never order from this company again.

I am extremely disappointed with this company and will be notifying amazon of my experience.

product_title: Vasque Men's Bitterroot GTX Boot
review_body:
I've been wearing my new Vasque Bitterroot boots for about a week and they are breaking in nicely. I got these from a different online retailer for less than $100. They can be bought on Amazon in my size (10M) for $108. At this price these are an outstanding buy. I don't think I'd pay full retail for them, but for around a hundred bucks these are good boots.

I also have a pair of Zamberlan Vioz GT boots and a pair of Scarpa SL M3's. The higher quality of the Italian made boots over these Chinese made Vasque boots is unmistakeable, but you will pay for it. The Zamberlan Vioz GT's are my favorite boots ever and can be found on ebay for about $225 which is $25 more than full retail for these Vasque's. If you are considering buying these Vasque Bitterroots at full retail, do yourself a favor and spend a little more and get the Zamberlan's.

These Vasque Bitterroots are nice Sturdy boots that break in easily. I don't know yet how they'll stand up over time, but I'm confident I'll get my money's worth out of them. They are mostly true to size allowing that they run a little wide. If you like a lot of room in the toe box you will like these. To me they are a little too wide, but not so bad that my foot slips around in them. I can definitely live with it. They are not as comfortable out of the box as the Zamberlans, but I'm not having any problems getting them broken in. They are not nearly as Stiff as the Scarpas, but they are still a pretty sturdy boot. I have noticed that my feet sweat in these boots much more than any other boots I've worn.

Bottom line is these might be the best one-hundred dollar backpacking boots out there. At twice that price the Italian competition beats them severely.

As of 12/16/13 I've been wearing these 3 or 4 times a week for over 4 months. My impression of them is still about the same with a couple additional insights. First when the weather is warm my feet are hot in these boots and sweat a lot. I'venever had this problem with any other boots. When the weather is cold my feet get cold if I'm not constantly moving. I don't notice this with any of my other boots.

The second thing is these boots eat bootlaces like they are Lay's potato chips. I went through the two pairs of laces that came with these right away. Then I put a set from a pair of Red Wings on them and they ate those up too. Now I'm trying some Kevlar bootlaces which haven't broken yet, but are definitely showing a lot of wear.

These have broken in well and they fit pretty good. While they are far from the most comfortable boots I wear, I wouldn't go so far as to call them uncomfortable, other than my feet getting hot and cold in them. They have good soles that work well in most conditions, and the leather seems pretty sturdy.

I still say they are a decent buy for under $100. I also would say that I like my Zamberlans and Scarpas so much more than these that there really is no comparison.

product_title: Chaco Women's Updraft Genweb-W Sandal
review_body: I had been wanting Chacos for awhile, but didn't want to spend $100 on shoes, and wanted something lighter (I am a rafter as well as a hiker) I'm a thrifty person, always trying to find deals, etc and was stoked on the price of these. The reviews for these shoes piqued my interest, talking about their reduced weight and less bulky style. So I decided to try them out. I was so excited to try them on and they were extremely comfortable for the first few minutes until I started getting about 3 gnarly blisters on each foot (the toe under the strap and the sides where the plastic hit). \\"NO!\\" I thought. Because I really wanted to like them and stylistically, I was definitely into how they looked. I searched through more reviews and other people had mentioned how the plastic on the sides (as opposed to the webbing on older versions) had also given them blisters. I know my feet blister easily so I decided to give them a week or two. And I'm soooo glad I did! I wore them, blisters and all, for about 5 days. I would wear them for about an hour each day (walking to and from work) and it was painful sometimes, but now my blisters have healed and they are incredibly comfortable. I am in love with how they look and feel and will probably be wearing them all the time for the rest of the summer. Haven't been on the water with them yet, but I have a feeling they'll be great!

ABSOLUTELY recommend this shoe for anyone on their feet anywhere- this coming from someone with constant lower back pain and achey achey feet- these types of shoes make a significant difference in both areas. review_headline: The perfect sexy cold weather boot
review_body:
I was a little bit hesitant when I purchased these about the practicality of buying fall/winter boots that were black - suede - over the knee and heels...would I look like a bad Julia Roberts knock-off in Pretty Woman? But my fears were unfounded, and these boots are eminently practical...for winter, for work, for going out. First point in practicality: these boots are WARM! Maybe not arctic expedition warm, but I live in Syracuse, NY, which wins the Golden Snowball award nine years out of ten and the boots work great. If you order a half size up you can wear your tights + thick socks and be really toasty, I didn't even bother though and they still worked great because of point two: OTK means snow doesn't get in over the top of them and your feet will stay dry(ok Syracuse: sometimes there IS that much snow and it can get into even thigh-high boots...but this is not the norm for most people). Practical point three: Black and Suede are quite doable in wet, salty winter SO LONG AS you take proper preservative measures beforehand. AS SOON AS YOU BUY THESE, you should waterproof them. Don't wear them out even once. Don't let a speck of dust land upon them. I did this, and then wore them in snow, rain, ice, for two years now - they still look brand-new. The other thing you should get is one of those soft bristle brushes, they make them specifically for suede but a larger one for nails or body might be easier to use to brush off any salt. Point four: these boots are very comfortable. They have a low heel, are well-balanced and easy to walk in...leading into point five: these boots are versatile. Wear them with sheer hose for evening, skinny jeans for casual, or opaque black tights for a more conservative workplace. Balance really matters. I think being able to stay upright is a key criteria for judging the \\"workplace appropriateness\\" of a particular pair of footwear. Seeing someone teeter around the office in a pair of too-high heels always makes me cringe, and I don't even know why since its not like I aspire to be the fashion police, lurking in wait with a scan gun and citation booklet in wait for girls to offend...but anyway,you won't have to put in extra hours on the balance beam or take tight-rope lessons to walk with confidence wearing these boots. Not to mention the effect that knowing you look good wearing these hot boots. Resist the urge to vogue while wearing, but buy them; try them; you'll love them.

Epilogue: my personal notes in re: fit - I have narrow feet and a skinny calf. I saw one reviewer who said she had trouble getting them over her calf, and I imagine that people with shapely calves pay attention to shapely-calf reviewers. product_title: Under Armour Men's Core Sunglass
review_body: It's a little early to write a review because I haven't really used these glasses, yet, as I'm still recovering from an injury and slogging away indoors on the elliptical machine, but Amazon wants a review, so here goes:  I bought these glasses for running and maybe biking. The glasses are as shown and the vision is clear and sharp with both the lighter and darker lenses. The replaceable lenses are fast and simple to change, as advertised. The real test will come when I use them to run outdoors in the Florida heat. My previous pair of glasses bounce on my nose and start slipping when the sweat starts to pour, causing me to not use them. My eye doctor has scolded me that UV rays are worse for the eyes than the skin, so I'm giving these glasses a try. If these stay in place, they'll get a 5-star.  As far as appearance, these glasses look just as portrayed in the posting. They are sleek and sporty. The do have a fairly extreme wraparound, which is good for what they're designed to do. I had hoped that maybe they would be suitable for every day use, not just sports, but unless you're one of those guys who wears glasses on your head or hat - day and night, inside or out - as a misconceived fashion statement, these are definitely active wear only.  Update: I'm upgrading my rating of these glasses from a 4-star to 5-star. After using these glasses for a few months, I'm sold. I have some serious problems with my left eye, which forces me to wear a special contact lens and makes the eye very easily irritated by glare, especially for long periods. I've used these glasses several times for coaching my kid's little league practice and golfing in a variety of brightness/cloud conditions. They have performed excellently. I'm especially happy with the lighter tint lenses for use on those variable light, partly cloudy days. They provide plenty of protection from glare off of water, glass, etc., while providing exceptionally sharp vision.  Update v2 (10/27/14): Please note that whenyou take the lenses out to clean them, or if the glasses become wet from sweat, the lenses should not be put back into the frames until they're completely dry. There has been some rusting on the magnets on mine. Still, I'm happy with the glasses and their performance.

product_title: Vasque Women's Wasatch GTX Hiking Boot
review_body:
I just returned from a two week backpacking trip in Wyoming, during which time I put these boots to the test. They are rugged, and they take a beating. I usually wear hiking shoes rather than boots, but I had to buy these for a NOLS course that I will be taking in the mountains in Washington next month, and for something that wouldn't have been my first choice, I liked them well enough.

PROS
You can relentlessly bang your toes against rocks all day and not feel a THING
The tread kept me sure-footed on scrambles when everyone else was stumbling and sliding
The extra ankle support is nice

CONS
This boot is HEAVY, it took me a while to get used to the extra weight
Without the proper sock, the all leather upper will keep your feet uncomfortably hot on warmer days (I wear FITS socks and don't have a problem with this)

In short, Vasque is well-known for a reason. If full hikers are your thing, I would recommend this boot.

product_title: Men's SKECHERS GO Run
review_body:
I first started using this pair of Go Run's on the 7th June 2013. Between then and now I have put in 215km total on these, 95% of which constitutes jogging/running. I run four times a week with workouts spanning between 3.7km on one \\"easy\\" day, 10k each on two \\"medium\\" days and 15km on one \\"hard\\" day.

I am a relatively heavy guy at 180 lbs, 5\\"11'. Thanks to running only I have been able to drop my weight to this from approximately 260 lbs!!.

I waited this long because I wanted to put these shoes through their paces before making a premature comment. I will put some salient thoughts from off the top of my head down in point form for your ease of reading. Additional things may be added as I remember them.

*Sizing*

Absolutely no problems here. I normally wear 11.5 us size and this sizing did not disappoint. Fit was perfect. I got the light grey/black which I found to be the most visually appealing to me.

*Comfort*

These shoes are incredibly light and VERY comfortable. From the moment I put them on I realized that I would have no issues. I jogged around the yard to test and they were perfect. 215 km later, this is still the case. Never once did any part of my foot hurt or blister. It may also be worth noting that I do not wear socks with these but this is no issue.

It is a \\"low cut\\" shoe so you do not get the ankle support found on conventional running shoes, however, this was not a problem for me at all. Never once have I felt any pain on my feet, ankle or knees. The design of the shoe promotes running, as you already know. Walking in them feels a bit strange and it actually feels unnatural to walk; takes more effort. Running on the other hand is a dream and the design is leaps and bounds better than my old pair of Asics running shoes. The sole is more than sufficiently padded and it feels like I am running on cushions the entire time. All of these advantages are supplemented by the extremelylow weight. This shoe has allowed me to significantly reduce my times over all of my distances. Just as an example, I was able to reduce my time over a distance of 3.7 km from 17m 45s to 16m 38secs!!!

*Durability*

The soft, extremely breathable manmade upper is still in pristine condition. The sole of the shoe is soft. This last point was worrysome to me as I was unsure how it would stand up after some time on the road. While there is some visible wear on the impact point of the soles, it is nowhere near as bad as I thought it would have been when I first started using them. After all, this pair cost only $50 so I wasn't expecting miracles in the durability department, especially because of how soft the soles feel. I am happy to report that I was wrong! I could easily see these shoes giving me another 300km easily before I will consider changing them (not because they would be destroyed but rather prefer to retire them before they are completely spent).

*Hygene*

As mentioned before, I use these shoes without socks. It goes without saying that it doesn't take too long for any shoe to become dirty inside when being worn in this manner. After the third week of use I washed them by hand. Because the material is thin and light, washing was easy and drying was quick in the hot sunshine. I just washed them for the second time this weekend and they almost look brand new!

*Extras*

The package came with some nice unexpected extras, a nice touch for an inexpensive pair of shoes such as this. An extra pair of laces as well as a cloth-like carry bag (perhaps big enough to fir the pair of shoes, i've never tried to do this) as well as a couple booklets espousing the virtues of the product. (Interesting read).

*Cons*

None that I can think of.

*General consensus*

I am VERY pleased with this purchase and would definitely buy this model again, or perhaps look at the successor, the Go Run 2. In short, regardless of if you are a beginner, intermediate or expert runner, this is definitely the tool for you!!

I purchased a pair years ago in New York (Macy's Herald Square is the only place I have ever seen them in a brick and mortar store) and they became my travel shoe, putting lots of miles on them.  They stretched out a lot over time (sometimes they were worn in pouring rain, even), and on the pale blonde saddle colour they used to make, they did scuff up and fade over time (reasonable, considering how much they've been through), so I decided to replace them.  Luckily various online sites now carry the Kendra, and there are multiple colours to choose from.  Note that the \\"Smoke\\"/grey is more of a brownish grey or greige, not a true grey, but more mixed and subtle.  Very versatile.  The Havanna is a very dark cool-toned espresso brown.  The heel height is fairly low and to me, the perfect height.  Too flat and you have no arch support, too high and you'll get pressure on the foot pad.  These are just right.  There are definite size variations, as I ordered 4 in varying colours and they did not all fit exactly the same.  They are fairly long, but overall fit on the small side, so order up if unsure.  They are European sizing, so my normal size 9 is their 40 (8.5/9) and it is a bit snug, but I know from experience that they're going to loosen up quite a lot over time (as soft, supple, thin leathers do), so I'm sticking with the size.  Thicker socks and/or inserts easily takes care of the stretching, but I prefer extra room anyway, as feet expand so much when you're on them for prolonged periods, and so only in cold weather do I find it necessary.  Better to have more room than less.  The leather is soft and supple.  I don't remember a bad break-in period, with blisters, and whatnot.  The only reason I didn't give them 5/5 stars is that the inner bed could be lined with something a little nicer than just felt.  I think this is a design/practical decision so your feet don't slide around, but I think it's a missed opportunity to add yet another layer ofextra cushioning.  I have a lot of problems with my feet and walking or standing for hours is very painful on the ball of the foot, so to me these boots are about the most comfortable thing that exists.  Highly highly recommended.

These fit like a glove and provide stability without feeling like they are fighting against my gait. The lightness and flexibility for a stability-oriented trainer are exceptional.

product_title: Touch Ups Women's Diane Leather Ankle-Strap Sandal
review_body:
I first got these shoes in silver and then decided to also get them in black. Of the two, the black ones are definitely my favorites. I have fair skin and the silver looks a bit washed out on me whereas the black looks much nicer (strangely enough).

The heel height of these is very comfortable, and that's coming from someone who does not like to wear heels at all (Note: Amazon lists them as 2 1/4\\", where I bought these they were listed as 2 1/2 and I think that's more accurate). I am a Converse/Birkenstock/Merrell/Teva, etc. kind of person in my every day life. So I hope that this can encourage other women to give these a try. I also have a friend who had foot surgery in the past and told me that she cannot wear heels. She tried these on, however, and her verdict was \\"I think I can wear heels after all!\\". So if you are like me and hate heels or thought you simply can't wear them, this might just be the shoe for you.

The bling is tasteful and not too much yet sparkly, and the ankle strap accommodates even larger ankles plus it gives added stability when walking. It also has a bit of elastic in it which definitely adds to the comfortable feeling.

These are really great dress shoes and I am actually looking forward to wearing these as a wedding guest at an upcoming fall wedding.

product_title: Sorel Women's Snowlion Boot
review_body:
I have not had the opportunity to wear these yet, as I purchased them at the end of the season. I purchased both the size 11 and 12 in this boot, because my previous experience with Sorel boots is that they run a bit large. The 11 arrived first and I must say, I was impressed with the study look and feel of the boot. The boot itself is a rubberized plastic shell at the bottom that looks like it will be completely waterproof up to the point where the nylon material meets the rubber. The boot shell itself is rather bulky and and wide. This boot comes with a "sleeve" or inner boot that is a felt like material and fits snugly on my foot.
The 11 fit just fine for my normal size 12 foot, as expected. I will not be able to wear super thick socks with this liner, but don't think I will need them. In fact, the shell of the boot is large enough that when I find the need to reorder the inner sleeve, I believe I could order the size 12 and be just fine. The drawstring closure at the ankle stablizes the foot in the boot and the drawstring at the top looks like it will keep out snow and wind. I will report again after I actually have the opportunity to wear these in some cold snowy weather. Make no mistake about it it, these are bulky wide boots. While they look good in the white color, they certainly are not a fashion statement and don't make your foot look smaller or more feminine! But that is not why I bought them.

review_body: I have been wearing 9.5 narrow shoes and sandals for years. I grew up knowing how to have my foot measured and what size then to buy. I don't recommend this sandal or brand for anyone with a true narrow width foot.  The shoe it self looked nice enough and I think it would have been comfortable if it wasn't so wide.

product_title: Suncloud Optics 2014 Conductor Polarized Sunglasses (Tortoise - Golden Mirror Polarized)
review_headline: Much better quality than the price would lead on.
review_body:
Quite simply these are some of the best sunglasses you can get. Quality construction, no lens disfiguring, can take a punch.

The only drawback is that the polarization pattern is cheap. Its great for fishing or looking at anything with a glare but the problem comes when trying to look at LCD displays, ipads, phones, or readouts. If you look at your ipad or look at your car stereo you won't see the readout. Tilt your head 90 and you can see it perfect. It's the way the polarization is laid out on the lens. Not a real problem for me but could be for someone who uses an ipadin the sun all day. Minus 1 star.

I will be buying another when I eventually lose these.

product_title: Rainbow Sandals Men's Premier Leather Single Layer,Large,Sand [Apparel]
review_body:
These are my second pair of Rainbow sandals in about 6 years. Had the replace the old pair as my dog destroyed them to an almost unrecognizable form (oh puppies...). Before purchasing my first pair of Rainbows I had owned many a pair of sandals and none have ever come close to the comfort of Rainbows. I will almost certainly buy no other pair of sandals in the future and recommend them for everyone.

Note, however, they do require a break-in period, particularly in the leather strap. They will almost certainly feel tight or even constraining at first but will loosen up within a few weeks of regular use. The insole, if you will, also molds to your foot during this break in period making a pair of Rainbows truly your pair of sandals.

I highly recommend them if you're looking for a very comfortable thong sandal by a company that always stands behind their products.

If you have narrow feet, and/or don't mind your toes being crammed together not able to splay while running, you may not mind these shoes. You may also like Nikes and Pumas in this case.

After two months in Altra Torin shoes that have a crazy roomy toe box, my toes got used to space and freedom, and these shoes did not provide that, unfortunately.

I can't even comment on the sole, because I just could not wait to get the shoes off my feet again.

Too bad! They look great, and I was excited to try out this new technology - maybe at some point, more shoe companies will look at how feet are shaped and try to shape their shoes after our feet.

I rate them 2 stars, one for beng innovative, and one for the pretty look.

product_title: Kork-Ease Women's Ava Platform Sandal
review_headline: Change of location of manufacture makes a huge difference!
review_body:
I have purchased this same style of shoe in the past; loved them and have no issues whatever with the shoes manufactured in Brazil. HOWEVER, this latest purchase was manufactured in China (and not disclosed) and while the footbed itself is more cushiony, and the leather seems about the same, a major difference can be found: at the intersection where the straps that go both behind the ankle and in front of the ankle meet, on either side of the front ankle strap, and hidden beneath the back strap, the leather ceases and some very flimsy fabric and a bit of elastic connects the straps to the shoe beds! In other words, that fabric/elastic, when it stretches out, breaks, and believe me, even with the front strap relatively loose over the arch, the missing leather makes the shoe far less durable. I am about to take the shoes in for what I expect will be a fairly expensive repair, and I've only had the sandals (and don't wear them more than 2x per week) for a couple of months! I ran into someone else with the same shoes and she had the same problem -- in fact, she commented that she returned them to the brick-and-mortar store where she bought them, and the salesperson commented that other people had returned the shoes for the same reason.

The lesson is: ask for the country of manufacture, examine the shoe VERY closely before wearing, and beware buying anything you cannot return!

review_body: This shoe was recommended by a gf who swears by them!  They are offered from various sellers in different styles. I use these other brands of ortho-friendly shoes with mixed results.  This shoe actually made it possible for me to go all day long walking & standing, and I did not even think about needing to get off my feet!  I do have high arches and these shoes do not give that bump for support.  But the thickness of the sole seems to be the area I needed most help and didn't realize it.  I also have custom orthotics to use in my other shoes but still had this problem with achy, tired feet.  Now with summer I have these sandals which are much needed for the hot weather and I am totally pleased with how they fit and feel!

product_title: ASICS Men's Lethal Stats SK Soccer Shoe
review_body:
On size, I'm a size 13 and I own a pair of soft ground ASICS rugby boots in size 13 that fits like a dream, so I was a little surprised when I tried this pair on and noted how snug they were. However, let me clear the air by saying that now that I've worn them for two weeks at practice and two tournaments, the fit is perfect. It's not that they're tight per se, it's just that they fit your foot like you would expect a fitted glove to wrap around your fingers. They don't slide around even when wet which meant zero blisters where usually I would have expected a ton of them. Plus, the cushioning in the sole is super comfortable.

The outer material is slick-looking, and gets good grip on the ball even when wet. Plus, as it was the main reason that I purchased these, the grip on natural turf is outstanding. A huge fan of these. I don't think I'll stray from ASICS boots anytime soon. If I had to nitpick, I'd say the laces seem like they could be more durable, but a very minor concern.

product_title: Reebok Women's Princess Sneaker
review_headline: Reebok turned an perfectly ugly comfortable shoe to an ugly UNcomfortable shoe....what was the point?????
review_body:
Reebok changed this shoe from Leather to synthetic and changed the last!
Two pairs of shoes returned!! Two pairs in the trash!! All in the past 6 months!
I admit it. I have painful feet and have had forever. The Reebok Princess shoe has been my standard footwear since 1970. I even wear the black ones with a business suit! People have laughed at my shoes from New York to Malaysia! I have been buying 4 + pairs a year so they are always fresh looking. I threw away a pair because though they looked good, they hurt and I assumed there was something wrong with the manufacture and bought another pair. These were equally as painful and tossed them as well. Now on the third go I realize that Reebok changed the shoe from leather to synthetic! I am now wearing my ancient old white leather ones, and some slightly less disgusting black ones that thank god I kept because though they look like hell they do not hurt! I called Reebok to complain, and the agent said that many people have called to complain about the NEW Princess. He said Doctors recommended the old princess to their patients for its nice arch and good fit for hurty feet.
REEBOK!!!! Up the price, bring back the leather and the old last!!

review_body: The shoe is very cute and I give it 4 stars for cuteness! I have narrow feet and the shoe is too wide for me, my toes hang off the front of the shoe and this is not a good look. product_title: Circa Joan & David Women's Xallie Wedge Sandal
review_body: These shoes are cute, comfortable, and fit true to size. The only problem is that they have a slick, felt-like sole. If you walk on tile, polished concrete, wood/laminate floors, or linoleum, you will slip and slide.  I've almost lost my footing several times wearing these. I would not recommend them.

product_title: Report Women's Chris Ballet Flat
review_body: I'm very happy with my tan ballet flat. The color is a rich tan not a pale one. This is my second pair of Report flats.  I bought a pale tan pair a few years ago and needed to replace them.  I don't wear these as an everyday shoes (I'm a Mom of two small children so sneakers are my everyday footwear) but they do get worn a couple of times a week for a few hours while I'm out and about sans kiddos.  My last pair lasted a good couple of years. I love that they are neutral and can be worn with capris, jeans or dresses.  The leather is quite a good quality.  It is very soft which I wanted as it means they will be comfortable almost straight out of the box.  These have proved to be just that.  They are low at the front leaving some of your toe cleavage exposed.  If you don't like this then these shoes are not for you.  It doesn't bother me particularly and it's not excessive.  I'm an 8 or an 8.5 depending on brand and bought an 8.5 in these.  (The climate in the summer where I live is hot hot so feet can swell a little.) They are perfect, loose but not loose enough to fall away from my feet when walking.  They have turned out to be pretty perfect for my needs and I'm ordering a silver pair.

product_title: Rocky Duty Men's Alpha Force 6" Swat Boot
review_body: THESE BOOTS ARE TOTALLY AWESOME!!! JUST WALKED AROUND THE MOUNTAINS OF MONTANA AND THE BLACK HILLS OF SOUTH DAKOTA AND MY FEET NEVER GOT SORE.

product_title: Merrell Women's Barefoot Pace Glove
review_headline: Too tight for my wide feet
review_body: The laces are made in a fashion that they only expand to a certain point. I have the first generation of these shoes and I absolutely love them! But the fact that these can only open so far is really disappointing.  There is a piece of fabric attached to the tongue that has loops that go through the lace holes, and I thought an easy solution would to be bypassing these loops and just sticking the laces themselves through the lace holes.  Nope.  The lace holes are slits and are not even wide enough to fit the laces! Not only that, they don't fit any laces at any of the running shops in town. Extremely disappointed. I eventually just flattened the lace tips as much as possible with pliers and made them fit through the lace holes and the cut off the fabric the laces are made to go through. All in all, I paid over $100 for these shoes and then ended up modifying them. I'll be putting in a complaint directly to Merrell as well.

product_title: Nike Dual Fusion Run Men's Running Shoes
review_body: I love this shoe! It's great to wear during hit days, especially in the summer, because it's light, air flows into the show and it keeps your feet from sweating excessively. I use it when working out at home or going to the gym and it feels very comfortable. I wouldn't recommend using it while running on a dirt track because it's easy for dirt to get inside your shoes. When working out on hard surfaces or if looking for a comfortable shoe, I definitely recommend this one.

product_title: Altama Olive Drab Jungle Vulcanized Boot - Domestic
review_headline: Great Boots at a Great Price
review_body: I've worn Jungle boots since 1979 when I blasted out of planes into central america and put them through hell all over the world. So I know my boots and I know that these boots are the real deal. Solid Stitching and Good Leather. They come with a good generic insole, but as a pro, I always recommend taking good care of your feet and putting in good insoles that meet your objective. There are other boots out there saying they are the "original Nam Boony Boots" but these boots I'm wearing are like some good old friends that will never let you down. I absolutely recommend them! so what are you waiting for?? Happy Trails Mates!

If you want a boot that feels like armor but wears comfortably like a quality hiking boot, this is it.  I have no regrets other than wishing I could ride my Vulcan with them.  Maybe it's time to swap out the shifter with a toe/heel lever.

product_title: Calabria Readers Reading Glasses - Lighted Reader - Tortoise / 1.50

product_title: Volatile Women's Dragon Thong Sandal
review_headline: But now I want them in every color
review_body:
This was my second venture into Volatile footwear, first time as a high wedge sandal. Now I'm smitten.
As a retail wench, I'm on my feet all day and more often than not, even in my casual attire, opt for comfort in my footwear. Heels, shoes that offer height, are not usually part of that equation.
But having upgraded midlife to a man who is substantially taller than I am makes me want to get some stilts. That and somehow my short little legs cover more ground more quickly than his long stems, I figured if sometimes when we're out, something slowing my stride (like heels) would keep me at his pace.
These were chosen for looks first, but the fact that they're dragon sandals, well, slay me.
I heeded the advice to size up for my half size. Depending on the shoe, I'm usually in the 7, 7 1/2, 8 range. Usually in sandals, I'll lean toward the smaller. With these, the 8 was the right size (I later confirmed this by ordering a pair of more basic Volatile thong sandals on a Warehouse Deal in a 7 - the 7 fits, but not as comfortably).
I just spent my weekend in my dragon sandals, and only at the very end were my feet a little tired. One day was spent touring a brewery, walking the boardwalk, playing pinball. The other day was spent at my retail job that has the hardest floors I have ever encountered in my very experienced years. I did have to be a touch more mindful when climbing the ladder in the stockroom, but I'm wearing these shoes like a champ.
Volatile seems to use for some of their styles this incredible foam for creating a platform. It's supportively firm, but much more lightweight than most materials. This means even though you've got much shoe transporting you, you don't feel too anchored. This same material makes for a less fatiguing foot bed. The rounded front and back edges on these shoes also keeps things light, in addition to making it a little less likely that a klutz like me will trip herself.

My only critique is an aesthetic one... The whitish/greyish stripes on top are sort of "painted" on. These stripes started to crackle the first time I wore them. The suede (I bought the fawn/taupe color) was soft and decent in quality. The size is true (i bought a pair in size 6, which is my normal size). because of the lacing, they can be adjusted to fit wide or narrow feet.

The size zip is a BIG plus for easy in and out.

The ankle is padded which adds comfort.

The studs seem well made and hopefully will stay on.

The insole is THICK! You need to take it out and marvel at it. The thickness makes walking comfortable.

The inside is lined with terry cloth, which can absorb sweat if worn bare footed and keep foot from sliding around.

They look great with my ankle skinny, regular skinny, boy friend rolled khaki/jeans, short skirts, shorts, and even a few dresses I own.

Highly recommend if you are into high tops that are slimming (no unnecessary padding) and walkable (not a hidden wedge fan).

review_headline: My RB2132 sizing wasnt right so I swapped that with my wife for this one. Perfect!

I received it the next working day from what was estimated by Amazon. The glasses are the Made in Italy original Ray-Ban Wayfarer RB2140s with the classic black frame and green-tinted lens. My wife chose these when we bought them, but it turned out to not fit her perfectly. The bridge didn't sit comfortably atop her nose. I put them on and it sat perfectly on mine. The lens size at 50mm (ironically) was also larger than the 2132's 52mm and suits my face much better.

My wife put on my RB2132s and that fit her very well, and the lens size also suited her much better. It turned out fine for us since we could just swap the ones with each other's. If you're a guy with an oval or a long face buying the RB2140 with the 50mm lens is a great fit. But if you want the new Wayfarer RB2132 (which I did initially) you should consider the 55mm lens instead of the 52mm.

I have been wearing Chacos, which have less heel support but fit snugly and so therefore in the end offer a more comfortable landing with each step because they don't shift around at all.  Of course there is no way to adjust the tightness of the thong straps on the Orthaheels, so here I am.  The diameter of my foot just under the metatarsal heads is 8\\".  I could try a sole insert made for thongs to see if I can raise my foot up high enough to snug the fit, but it may not be enough and when you pay this much for a pair of flips, you shouldn't have to do that.  Not happy.  Buyer beware.

product_title: Skechers USA Men's Solver Casual Slip-On
review_body:
I have had a pair of Solver slip-ons for years and years. During that time I wore them as my main shoes, often day in and day out. I never had an uncomfortable moment. The story goes: this guy's wife at the shoe store saw a pair of these and told her husband, \\"These look nice.\\" He responded \\"I don't need any prissy shoes.\\" So I looked to see what he thought was prissy, and bought a pair in black and brown. Guessin' I'm jus' prissy. I lost the brown pair in storage until recently--my luck, now I still have a new pair!

The back part of the sole will wear down fairly quickly if you drag at all, or if you have a narrow heel and the shoe naturally drags as your foot lifts a bit out of the back on a step. However, the wear doesn't seem to compromise the entire shoe, and it could only be seen when you are walking by someone staring at your heels. Eventually that wear will lead to the rubber separating...for me that probably happened after about 3000 hours of being on my feet in these shoes, about 80% indoors, 20% outdoors. Eccos at 3x the price may crack at the ball of the foot by then. Leather-soled shoes will probably have been resoled by then...so I think 3000 hours afoot is a pretty good track record. Oh, in that time the cloth on the side of the heel area also wore through; again, nothing visible from the outside. Also the toes 'took up' dye/polish really well over the years, so it was easy to keep them looking unscuffed, at least from any natural distance.

Now that they are beyond worn out I have found that they are PERFECT for crawling around doing repairs in my unfinished attic...no shoes even come close to the highly flexible sole with cleat-like rubber knobs for going over joists in an attic! I even mow the lawn in them...note that the suade on the sides (the 'swoop' is suade) will stain a little from grass.

Unlike some Sketchers I've owned, these are probably a little bit larger than you would expect from the given size...so I'man 11, for example, and they are about right with the tough-fiber Odor-Eaters inserted.
