product_title: New Balance Men's MT00 Minimus Zero Trail Running Shoe
review_body:
I'm not a runner, but having lacked an outdoors shoe for long enough, I thought it was time for a new pair. I am reviewing these shoes with the intent for use as comfortable shoes for sitting at the desk, everyday walking, and the occasional hiking and jog.

For work, I sit at a desk for hours a day. My sole pair of shoes for over a year now has been a pair of Ecco Oxfords. Though they look great, I have finally realized that the dress shoe heel is causing me great soreness when I am sitting and driving my heel into the floor. I have wide feet, measured myself a EE. Ecco's shoes feel somewhat wider than most, but could be better. Thus, I went searching for the lightest, widest, heel-less shoe I could find. Extra points if I could wear as business casual. Gold star if it passed as a dress shoe. After much research I've concluded there is no such lightweight, heel-less dress shoe, though a few companies are working on that.

Besides the Minimus Zero, I also tried on various other New Balance barefoot-esque trail shoes, the Vivobarefoot Ray (styled as moccasins) and Merrell Gloves, all barefoot shoes in varying degrees.

The non-Zer Minimus New Balances shoes I tried on were too narrow in the heel and toe box for my comfort. The Vivobarefoots were wide, but could have been even wider for me personally. There was something about the fit or fabric that did not feel right for my feet - I experienced pain when I placed weight onto the balls of my feet. I think there was not enough stretch. The Merrell Gloves had too much of an ache.

The MT00 Minimus Zero Trail: I got the size 10, 4E width and my feet fit perfectly, sockless. I wouldn't want to wear socks as I think that would make them too tight. Note that I measure myself as a EE, so either I measured incorrectly or these shoes run narrow by default. No heel, no arch. Wide toe box. I can freely wiggle my toes and it feels awesome.

It feels very close to being barefoot inthese, though I would say the Vivo Ray's were probably even closer still with the inserts taken out. I feel my feet "wrap" around the sidewalk curb and I do notice rocks and pebbles on the ground.

The vibram sole comes from underneath to partially climb up the toe box, so that protects your toes from accidentally stubs in the forward motion, but wouldn't protect your toes from objects falling onto them - no protection at all.

Mesh fabric covers your toe box - felt odd at first but now I love waving my foot around to get some air in them. You can sort of see your feet through the mesh, so that further takes you away from business casual if you are going for that.

By themselves, the shoes look pretty decent as running shoes go - you can't pull off business casual by any means but I see plenty of people wearing sneakers to work now a days as part of the "outdoor chic" style.

I wear them sockless and my feet do get really moist as you would expect to happen but I am dealing with that over cramped, sore feet. During a run, the mesh might cool your feet enough to keep dry but I haven't tested it out.

A bit annoying is that the shoes make pitter patter noise when you step, I think owing to the sole being made up of "pods" as part of its tread [see the pictures] - so it sounds like you are walking around in soccer cleats. I'd rather do without that but again the comfort outweighs this annoyance.

There a some reviews of this shoe not lasting for very long and I can see that - to keep the shoes light, there is just not much there. Most of the sole is some sort of foam, with the Vibram traction part covering the heel and the ball but not the mid-foot. I can see how the foam parts would start breaking down quickly.

Since I just mean to mostly use these shoes for sitting and walking about town, I am not too concerned about it, but time will tell if they last long enough to makeit worthwhile price-wise.

product_title: Womens Water Shoes Aqua Socks Pool Beach
review_body:
This is a first impressions review and will be updating it once I use them.

The very first thing I noticed as I took them out of the package, was a very strong offensive rubber/ chemical scent I could smell from 2 feet away. I have been wearing them for 30 minutes and it is 60% gone. This should not be an ongoing problem. The color is nice. I got the yellow and it is a deeper yellow (unlike the lighter yellow shown in the pic). But it's still nice. As I put them on I noticed that they are just a tad bit small for my feet. My big toe pushes through the fabric slightly. I am a 6.5 and got a 6. I still think it's the right size for me, since I bet 7 would be too big. Plus this kind of fabric should stretch when wet. The shoe also secures on nicely once the string thing is pulled all the way. Walking feels fine (aside from my big toe pushing through a little), they feel very light and airy, there are no seams that poke at my skin. The padded insert is actually glued on (under the heel, not mid-foot or toes). That doesn't mean that it won't come off in the water, as most water shoes will do that.

I can't wait to use them in the water this summer. I can finally walk around without feeling anxious that something will cut or scratch me. Sweet!

Update Feb 2015: After 2 summers of use, I finally remember to update this! They are fantastic! Comfy to walk in, stay put in the water, show no wear (granted I have used them on about 10 occasions, but still ...). I have not had a single problem with the padded insert, as it's still glued on. They still have a little of that chemical scent. At this point, safe to say, that it is not going away. However, only at 20% the intensity from before; I basically have to put my nose to the shoe to detect it. I would purchase these again without any hesitation. Overall, great product and I remain a very happy customer. And ... I upped my star rating from 4 to 5 stars. Wouldn't it be nice if most of our belongings became more appreciated with time?

product_title: Nike Men's Lunarfly+ 4 Running Shoe
review_headline: Lightweight, Cushiony, Responsive, Stable AND COMFORTABLE
review_body:
Each year the LunarFly, as with nearly all running shoes, goes through something of a reinvention, originally known as the **'Nike - Run Avant'** It's always, supposedly 'improved', by adding more bulk of some sort to it, of course to make it better. I started with the original model, the Run Avant, and have kept with the line since, because, as a light weight runner, I didn't need an average shoe. The shoe, over about five years, had evolved into a pretty average stability shoe, aiming for the center of the running market, I'd think--In fact, I couldn't tell much difference between it than the Lunar Glide. But the entire reason I had started to wear the shoe was because it was lighter than average, more cushiony than average, yet was still responsive and comfortable enough to wear the marathon distance. And so with the prior hefty-rendition of the LunarFly I had decided that they 'improved' it too much, and was going to try something totally new, to get away from the averageness in all its characteristics. Nike: If I wanted a Lunar Glide I'd have bought a Lunar Glide.

BUT THEN I searched the specs of the Lunarfly+4. It was as light as the original **Run-Avant** model. The sole looked even more responsive. I took a chance, ordered it while holding my breath, thinking, 'this is the last time I buy a lunarFly shoe!'.

Turns out Nike has finally designed **my** perfect shoe. It has all the qualities I originally enjoyed with the Run-Avant. It's more cushiony than the other models of LunarFly, and surprisingly, thanks to the trimmed down sole, is more responsive, yet just as stable. AND, the shoe is now made with more breathable materials great for summertime running. For me, this is the perfect running shoe, and without a doubt the best of the LunarFly series.

I suppose I will need to order more before Nike starts 'improving' the model again.. because it looks like any changes they make could only have an adverse affect. I just hope they don't start bulking it back up, making it more average..I will be quick to switch models next time.

product_title: Scarpa Men's Himavan GTX Hiking Boot
review_body:
Usually I wear 44EU, but ordered 44.5 since I tried another Scarpa model in local shop and my toes hit the front.
The length is perfect, but it seems as if front is a bit too narrow, while heel is a bit wide. Maybe my feet are a bit on the wide side; somebody mentioned that this boot was better for narrow feet. Still, nothing a good sock and proper lacing can't fix.
I like the quality and feel of the boots. The materials and make are impeccable.
I didn't do a trek in them yet, just some casual hiking to break them in, but they give a lot of confidence. They are very comfortable and have a lot of grip, also on wet or dusty stones.
The only downside, is they seem to be a bit too warm for our summer :-(.
My previous boots were Garmont smth GTX with similar features (Gore-tex, Vibram sole), but these out of the box felt not less comfortable as the old ones.
Generally, these are great boots and can recommend them for all trackers.

product_title: Dansko Women's Cadence Slip-on
review_body:
I'm starting nursing school soon, and everyone I talk to says the #1 thing to bring is comfy shoes. I usually wear low-to-no support shoes, but as a college student I'm not on my feet a lot. After searching online for 'the most comfortable nursing shoes ever' I kept seeing these three brands show up: Sanita, Dansko, Cherokee, and Nurse Mates. As of this post, Amazon didn't have any Nurse Mates or Cherokees available via prime, so I started searching for Danskos and Sanitas. There's a lot of mixed reviews about these two brands. Some say Danskos are the best, others say they have gone down in quality and Sanitas are the way to go.

I decided to buy these Dansko Cadence's first, since they were the cheapest pair of shoes I could find out of both Danskos and Sanitas. They cost me $40 new, with free 2-day shipping. I figured I would try them out and if I didn't like them I would send them back and not look at another pair of Danskos ever again.

They arrived and looked decent, but definitely not fashionable by modern standards. They sort of look like mini-slipper-clogs. However, once I got into them... I fell in love. They have a removable insert that's got to be at least 2 inches thick- it's squishy yet firm. Wearing these is like walking on super thick, stable cushions. I wear a size 10 in everything, but bought these in EU 41 (10.5-11) and they fit perfectly with and without socks.

I'm so glad I got a great shoe on my first try! If all Danskos are this comfortable, they're going to be the only brand I wear.

They offer great support, and are the first exercise shoes I've purchased in years that don't leave blisters on my feet. I took them to work to wear for lunch time walks, and around the same time began to notice a smell that made me think someone had discarded rotten food in the area. Then I thought one of my co-workers must have developed horrible body odor. After a week or so, I took a trip wearing the shoes during my flight. The smell followed, so of course I thought I had developed body odor! But, after unpacking and leaving the shoes in the hotel closet for a couple days, the closet began to take on the same odor. I was able to track the smell back to the soles (not the insoles) of these shoes. The smell is a horrible gassy/chemical smell. I found the same complaint not only with other NB models, but other manufacturer's shoes. Other reviews mentioned it might be due to the shoes getting wet, or the adhesive, and/or a certain type of foam used. In any case, they smell too bad to keep in the house. So, I keep them on the patio, and put them on only when walking outdoors. They're too comfortable to toss, or they would be gone. Unfortunately, it seems as if the smell didn't fully develop until I'd owned the shoes for several weeks.

And no, it's not my feet causing the shoes to smell. And yes, I actually made my spouse to a sniff test, comparing my old, well-worn sneakers to these. It's the new shoes.

product_title: Wolverine Men's Northman 8" Steel Toe Work Boot
review_body:
Wolverine's Northman steel-toe work boot is made of excellent materials, and put together with very good workmanship.

The leather is very thick and sturdy, and most of the stitching is double or even triple row. Two additional thickness of leather are added to the back of the boot to protect the Achilles tendon. The uppers are stitched to a thick leather midsole, which is attached to a dual-density Vibram outsole with deep tread. Dual-density means that the outsole has a very firm, abrasion-resistant bottom layer for long wear, with a slightly cushy middle layer, for improved comfort when walking on hard surfaces.

Inside, the boot is lined with actual Gore-Tex, so your feet will not get wet, no matter what. There is also a removable, molded insole to provide cushioning and arch support.

All this thick leather, rubber, and waterproof lining do result in a fairly heavy boot which you won't mistake for sneakers.

As far as fit goes, the boots run slightly larger than my previous Georgia and Carhartt boots. I actually ordered one-half size smaller than my regular size (i.e. 11 rather than 11.5), and the Wolverines still are slightly roomy with one pair of medium-weight crew socks, but a perfect fit with one pair of medium-weight socks as "inners" and one pair of thicker "boot socks" as outers. It isn't as if the length is incorrect, simply that the Wolverines are a boot with more internal volume than my other boots. Many serious hiking boots are intended to be worn with two pairs of socks, and the Wolverines are built like a classic hiking boot. Alternatively, if your foot is "meatier" than mine, you might be comfortable with a single pair of socks.

One benefit of a boot sized for two pairs of socks is really luxurious comfort, since your foot is surrounded by a thick layer of soft sock material on all sides. When I take the Wolverines off at the end of the day, my feet feel great, with zero chafing or discomfort of any kind.

All in all, I'm very pleased with these boots. They are comfortable, good looking, and appear to be made with perfect attention to detail. I expect them to last a very long time. Additionally, I felt good buying something made in the U.S.A.hafing or discomfort of any kind.

One minor issue I have ( I have it often with shoes so its probably my size) is the back of the heel comes up a bit too high so I got a blister on my left foot. I just put in heel pads (often have to use them) and they are fine. I've been wearing the regularly and get lots of compliments. I can see wearing them for a while.

product_title: Oofos Ooriginal Thong Sandal Black
review_body: They are definitely soft and "cushiony" but actually promotes pronation in the foot that leads to other foot complications.  I would not recommend to people who are prone to pronation, or are flat footed.  They probably wouldn't be good for someone with a high arch as it tends to flatten it out and that soon becomes uncomfortable.  I think they are also overpriced..

product_title: Speedo Women's ZipWalker Water Shoe
review_headline: Good value, but zipper a problem.
review_body: I thought this was going to be good for my daughter because it has a zipper, but it turns out that was the problem, and my other daughter who got the Surfwalker was much happier with her pick. It is a bit easier to put on than the Surfwalker, but not a lot, and while in the surf, the zipper came down and the shoe came off. Also, while river rafting, my daughter was instructed to slide her foot under the tube for stability, and it hurt. A bit slippery bottom, and all in all, this was not the best choice.

product_title: Salomon Women's XR Mission Running Shoe
review_body:
First off, it does run a 1/2 size large. I read the other reviews and took heed. I usually wear 10 in womens flats, and 9.5 fits like a glove.
Second thing, it has some really nice arch support and it seems like it might be uncomfortable to someone with a flatter foot. I have a little bit of an arch, but it's pretty moderate arch. That being said, i am not the greatest at wearing arch supported shoes and it felt weird at first, but after some walking around it felt nice.
I've hiked in forested terrain and desert terrain in these and ran in the desert terrain. Both hiking and running, these did great. They grip well on both the dead leaves on a hill and some steep rocky areas.
They are so very lightweight that i was weary at first about support, but i was quickly assured how durable and well made these are.
People ask me about them (they're so noticeable with all those colors) and i recommend them.
As far as running on sidewalks and flat residential areas, i haven't tried that yet. But for hiking or trail running, totally recommend these.

product_title: Dockers Men's Gordon Cap-Toe Oxford
review_body:
I bought the black colored shoes to add to my wardrobe as basic work shoes. I have worn them for about 4 months about 2-3 days a week to work at the office.
Wear: They require polishing about once every two weeks. Small splinters have peeled off from the side of the sole of my pair when wearing them outside. I cut them off with scissors, so this is not noticeable yet. Other than that, they are holding up okay.
Comfort: Best if you plan to wear them in the office or somewhere where you aren't on your feet much. I wouldn't recommend their use if you plan to be on your feet all day, as they may get a bit uncomfortable. However, loosening up the laces helps. I am a light guy and don't experience this with my brown pair of Bass shoes retailing for $120 which I paid only $37 for when I was in El Paso last Summer. I guess you get what you pay for. Hopefully, I will get a year's use out of the Docker's shoes.

review_headline: Very stable and dependable motion control shoe.
review_body: I have worn out six pairs of these shoes and each time I get a new pair, I can just slip it on and run out the door. There is very little break-in time needed. My feet are very flat and I have bunions and since I am a severe over pronator, I need lots of motion control. I run around 30 miles a week and these last about six months before I need another pair. I tried Nike, New Balance and Oasics and had problems with all of them. Mostly they did not support my knees, but some of them had trim right in the area that bothered my bunions. This shoe does not have a trim that rubs it. So, for me, the mesh style is a bonus. Not only making the shoe lighter, but also making it more forgiving.

product_title: Skechers Performance Men's GO Train Athleisure
review_headline: Nice design but feels like dollar tree material...HORRIBLE!!
review_body:
The design is really nice, the airflow through the feet, very nice, however...I was shocked at how light they were on top of that when you put them on, there is no arch support (you can get insoles for this issue) however it is somewhat lopsided angling more towards the length of your little toe on both feet, as if you would be walking that part of the foot permanently. I was shocked as when you first walk in them, it is so uneven, you feel like you are going to fall over. I was unprepared for this however I got used to it (a week wearing it every other day). I work out in these however, they feel like they cannot take the stress of the movements.

The material...is the WORST part of this product. It feels like those foam boards you get from the dollar tree that you can easily cut up and make shapes out of them. I feel like one tug on the shoe flap and I would tear it apart in an instant. I am former military. and harsh on my shoes as I walk up to three or more miles a day, and I seriously don't think these will last more than three or four months (if I can make it through the summer with these, that would be awesome and worth the $40). I usually buy Merrill's, Nike or Adidas as they last forever and thought, due to the 'positive' reviews, that I was due for a change and bought these.

Very deceiving and not sure why there are so many positives on these.

Oh and on top of that all, the yellow insoles...? Well when you wear them, the yellow shows through the mesh on the front of the shoe, just a FYI. You have this black shoe and you can see the yellow poking through it. lol so odd....

All in all, I will keep them, use them for awhile and make do with it till they tear apart. Be aware when you do buy these and know what you are getting into before you buy them.

UPDATE 07/03:

After two months of wearing them every couple of days and walking and working out in them, I have noticed that the soles have been worn thin, and no longer have the padding on the bottom. I am trying to make them last for another couple of weeks to make it worth the $40 but I am not sure that will work. I WILL NEVER buy these again. Such SUCH horrible quality and build. Love the design, and mesh for the airflow, but it being Dollar Tree quality... this was the disappointing aspect of it. I am sticking with Nike's and Adidas from now on. I have lowered the rating from 2 stars to 1, though it deserves NO STARS!

product_title: KEEN Women's La Paz Wrap Sandal
review_body:
Before ordering these I read several reviews for Keen "La Paz" strappy sandals and they were all very positive. What I didn't realize was there are several different versions of the La Paz sandal - some good, some not so good. These fall into the "not so good" category.

First, check out the heel part in the picture. In this version, there is a weirdly heavy and stiff backstop of a heel piece that comes out of the footbed and stands stiffly upright. This piece is actually rounded on the top - not meant to cradle the tendon at the back of your ankle, but to poke into it with each step. Now look at the ankle strap that threads through this stiff heel piece - the ankle strap is this really thin, cheap, skinny, limp little nothing of a strap with some weak velcro on it. You can't easily open the latch of this skinny strap - at first I actually thought you couldn't open it at all, and had to dangle your entire foot through it and let the sandal swing from your ankle by the strap as you tried to stick your foot into the toe part. Awkward! Then I realized the strap WAS meant to be open and it is just incredibly hard to do, and even harder to stuff the end back through the flimsy plastic clasp once it's on. Who designed that?

You know how when you walk in a flip flop, the weight of the sole will 'flop' the heel away from your foot, and that's how it's supposed to work, and that's why flip flops sometimes slap-slap-slap as people walk? In this sandal the weight of the sole (which is very sturdy, so pretty heavy) tries to flop away at the heel, scraping the stiff heel piece along the back of your ankle, only to get caught by the flimsy, loose ankle strap catching on the front of your ankle. That skinny, cheap strap is the only thing supporting the sole of the shoe as you walk! And it isn't up to the task, so the heel piece slides, the strap digs in and the sole still flops away from your foot a few inches. It's like the worst of both worlds of a heeled shoe and a flip flop. I don't know how this design ever really flew with the designers.

Unfortunately I was dumb and wore the sandals out the door to go grocery shopping and so they weren't technically "new" so I couldn't send them back. Climbing into the car, as I turned on the ball of my foot, the heel piece actually swung around and wedged itself against the outside of my foot & had to be twisted back. Once that happened once, it kept happening. So frustrating! As I was walking down the aisle at the store I did get a compliment on my sandals from an old lady. So they do have that going for them.

Anyway, Keen usually makes great shoes, so this is a rare miss in my opinion. If you see a great price for La Paz sandles, make sure they are not this particular version with the big heel piece. The other ones seem to have a more sensible design.

product_title: New Balance Men's MT10v2 Minimus Trail Running Shoe
review_body:
UPDATE: After looking at them a bit more carefully, the problem is that I have long toes. That means that the widest part of my foot is positioned at a thinner part of the insole, which means that the ball of my foot runs partially on the insole (as it should) and partially on the hard outer sole (which is terrible). So main still stands, great for average foot people running on softer terrain, terrible for me.

I bought this in a store, not on Amazon and had them fitted, so I was excited about them. They were great the first 40(ish) miles, but after that I wore down the sole and it left an uncomfortable ridge under the ball of my foot (as mentioned in another review). It is VERY uncomfortable. I pronate heavily and run on hard surfaces, so I think this would be less important for those running on softer surfaces who don't pronate too much, but for me it rendered them useless. Bummer.

product_title: Ray-Ban RB 2132 901 52 Unisex Wayfarer Shiny Black Plastic Frame Green Lenses Sunglasses
review_body:
I have never had Ray-Bans before this...

I bought the 52mm Black Rubber Frame/Green Lens. I am really happy with the size. I purchased them anticipating for them to look nice and big (classic 80's style) but not massive. But, upon opening them they were smaller than I thought they would be. After putting them on I actually really liked how they looked and am glad I didn't get the bigger 55mm size.

Real or fake? I watched and read tons of stuff online to distinguish the two and these are definitely real except for one small thing. The case mine came with does NOT have a gold sticker/tag on it. There is simply a black stamp where it should be. Although not what I think should be there, I still believe they are real. They are VERY sturdy and nothing seems cheap about them. With these, you know you are getting quality glasses.

These fit great on my face. They do not feel like they are going to slide around at all. I have yet to try the ultimate test (motorcycle test) so I can't say for sure. The rubber frames seem to hug and 'stick' to you better than I imagine the classic Wayfarer would (but I don't know, I've never had the classic).

Oh, and it comes with the glasses, case, cleaning cloth, and little Ray-Ban pamphlet.

review_headline: mesh fabric is failing WAY too soon....disappointed with the shoe...
review_body:
I purchased these shoes the third week of March in 2013, and have never wore them for running, I have another pair of favorite shoes for that. These shoes are worn at the office (I know, casual....but hey the job pays well and I'm LUCKY!!!!) Given the shoes are less than month old and have been worn less than 2 dozen times I'd expect more.

At this time the left shoe has a frayed spot above the big toe joint. This happens because: the interior of the shoe contains a plastic mesh with holes all over. I suspect the holes over the joint allow the plastic mesh to crease and rub on itself when the foot flexes; causing the mesh to fray.

Not sure how to fix this, but way disappointed, guessing these shoes will be destined for the work bin sooner rather than later. I would NOT recommend these shoes as I question their durability, and I have purchased Merrell shoes in the past, so I trusted the brand.

product_title: David Tate Women's Atlantic Boot
review_headline: Just what I was looking for!
review_body:
I wanted some dressy boots, but they had to accommodate my orthotics. Usually I have to go to a specialty shoe store, but the boots there were 4x the price of these, so I gave them a try. I ordered the size I always wore pre-orthotics, but in the WW width. At first I wore them on the carpet for a short time, with my orthotics and nylons. When I could see that they might loosen up with wear, I tried a light pair of socks, then added a thin foam insole over the orthotics, and finally wore them on a short shopping trip.

Eventually I worked up to wearing them all day or all evening. I would probably not wear them to an event that involved a great deal of standing or walking, but that's just my feet. The leather is buttery-soft and the heels are very feminine and dressy even though they are not particularly high. They reach clear up to the bottom of my knee (I'm 5'7" and have kind of long legs). The zippers work smoothly. I get lots of compliments and I feel very sexy when I wear them!

For the price, I did not expect them to be so nice. Since I will only be wearing them for dressy occasions, I expect they will last a long time.

product_title: Women's Born, Aruba platform Sandal
review_body:
In most ways I am delighted with these sandals. They are indeed retro, very similiar to the low slope comfortable sandals we wore in the seventies. Those shoes were exceedingly comfortable, lengthened the leg line, and looked perfect with every kind of outfit, especially with a mini-dress ~ a short A-line shift ~ which really requires a chunky shoe of this type.
The mini-dress is here again ~ a dress that looks wonderful on every type of figure. These shoes are perfect for that look.
There is only one flaw in them. The line of the big toe, instead of going staight ahead in line with the shoe, thus creating a broad toe in line with the design of the entire shoe, curves sharply inward creating a rather pointed toe which is totally out of harmony with the entire design of the shoe and
is a constant source of low level pain which interferes with graceful walking and keeps your mind on your big toes instead of on being lovely, flirtatious, and fabulous.
I am keeping them because they are the closest I can find to what I am really looking for to wear with my new spring outfits, but oh, what a shame, when these shoe could so easily been perfection itself.

product_title: New Balance Men's M890B2 Running Shoe,Silver/Blue,11 2E US
review_headline: Good shoes for neutral running and pretty good for supinators
review_body:
I've been wearing my NB 890 v1 it is one of my favorite shoes in the rotation even though they had their weakness, mostly just a fast wearing tread and the aggressive toe drop. The only thing I can say I wish was that the tread was designed a little better. Since the v1s are at the point I shouldn't run in them anymore I ordered the v2s after seeing they improved the tread.

I got the shoes and they fit snugger and the toebox is just a bit snugger as well. However, I ran in them a couple times for 6 miles each time and I can say there are things that are great and some things I wish were a little different. Tirstly they are light and NB improved the treads on 890s, thank you! On the other hand, they fit like they are a half size smaller in width and the aggressive taper towards the big toe has my big toe rubbing against the shoe pretty good. After a few long runs they are starting to break in but they are snug, however I ran about 5 minutes faster immediately on my 10k runs so I can't complain.

They fit a little snug, but I'm sure I'll get used to them as they don't cause any blisters, encourage a neutral gate, and by the time I've worn through the treads a bit, I'll probably get a second pair to rotate in.

product_title: Timberland PRO Men's 53534 Titan Safety-Toe Slip-On
review_headline: Something went seriously wrong with these shoes after I bought them
review_body:
I ordered a pair of these and was pretty excited to try them out. I got them Thursday and took them for a walk the first time on Saturday just to the grocery store and back. When I got back, I noticed that my brand new pair of shoes had inexplicably developed big white gashes on the side of each where the steel toe is. It looked kind of like somebody had taken some rocks and bashed them against my shoes or something.

The material on the outside looked good and thick, so even if I for some reason was scraping them on the sidewalk or something (which I don't know how I would do that and not notice, but let's think hypothetically here) I don't really see why they would look that terrible just from a 1.5 mile trip or so to the store and back. I don't really know what to say about it since I've never seen a pair of shoes do this before. I'm guessing maybe the material on the outside was stretched too thin or something and the act of putting my feet in them tore it or something? I'm just blindly guessing...

So, I ended up sending them back. That's one thing that was nice, they come with a 30 day warranty so because they got busted up so fast I was able to send them back without issue and get a refund. It may have just been a manufacturing flaw for that particular pair of shoes: I'm not sure.

As far as the actual comfort of wearing them goes... well, they just weren't for me. I'm the kind of guy who has to wear 13W and even then my feet are still too wide or long for some of these shoes. I lost the gamble by ordering these, unfortunately. These were just a little too narrow for me and because of the steel toe I developed a couple of sores on my little toes of each foot which healed up after a day or so just from the little walk I did. They're very heavy, so if you're not strong in the legs they may not be for you.

If there's anything positive I have to say about the experience of buying these shoes, it's that I felt pretty awesome when I had them on. You feel like you can stomp some fools out, if you know what I mean!

It's a shame they turned out so badly for me. I was excited.

product_title: Saucony Men's Progrid Kinvara 3 Running Shoe
review_headline: rubs achilles bloody if you tie them too tight, but these are good shoes
review_body:
Updated Review: I said I would give them another shot, and I did. With good results. I discovered that minimalist shoes minimize in many areas, including the padding around the ankle, to drop weight. The result is a very thin layer of material around the ankle that, when the shoe is tied too tightly, will cut into your skin. The solution is obviously to loosen the laces so that the shoe fits more loosely around the ankle. This will prevent the material from rubbing and cutting the skin. Because of the severity of the injury the shoes caused, I gave it a 1 star review initially, but after giving the shoes another shot with adjustments in the laces I can endorse them.

Original Review:
I bought my first pair in a shoe store. I loved them. My running form improved. I had less aches and pains during and after runs. So happy with the shoes that I bought another pair online, from Amazon. Made the mistake of bringing the new pair on a business trip without testing them out. Ran four miles in the city and could barely walk afterwards. The back of the shoes literally rubbed a hold into my achilles. If I had not bled all over the shoes, I would have considered returning them. I am still recovering from the wounds. I guess I was in the zone because I didn't bother stop stop running as the pain increased. I unfortunately had to take a break from running to heal and have just now been able to run in my older built up shoes, but only if I wear long, thick socks to protect my achilles. I tried running again in my first Kinvara 3 shoes, but they cut into my wounds too much. Needless to say I'm pretty disappointed in the shoes. Perhaps I had the shoes on too tight during that run, but I don't think shoes should ever create the kind of wounds I received on a short 4 mile run. Now that I have two pairs of these shoes, I'm going to do my best to make them work. If I am successful, I may update the review and revise the star rating.

product_title: KEEN Men's A86 TR Hiking Shoe
review_body:
I am a big fan of Keen products, and have yet to find a another shoe manufacturer who can make a sole that outlasts Keen's! At 6' 4" and 260, I go through shoes quickly—but Keens outlast every other brand that I've ever owned.

PROS: The A86 is light, nimble, and the tread is superb
The contoured cut of the saddle and tongue really conform to the foot
The capped toe (a Keen trademark) provides good protection from sticks and stones
The sole is nice and tough (compared to other ultra-light trail running shoes I've owned, which can be thin and overly soft
Great colors and graphics

CONS: I agree with a number of reviews that you cannot lace the shoe up far enough; as every runner knows, you don't want your toes rubbing the toebox
Contrary to every Keen I've owned the A86 does NOT have good arch support. If you have a high arch like me, you'll have to use an insert or orthodic. This surprised me, based on my excellent experience with Keens and their contoured footbeds

All in all, it's a great shoe, and I would have happily given it 5 stars except for those two minor issues.

review_body:
I bought these boots specifically for romping through the nasty cobblestone streets of Savannah, GA on St. Patrick's day (think New Orleans Mardis Gras weekend). I was looking for comfort, style, and protection from the...uh...elements (read: bodily fluids and alcohol).

Pros: they are definitely comfortable. And they did a pretty good job of protecting me from light splashes and even a misty rainfall. I actually ended up taking them to Europe (Amsterdam in the winter), where it was extremely rainy. They survived in heavy rain for about three hours before I had to switch them out from being too soaked. But they were surprisingly resilient to the water (I realize they aren't rain boots but it's an added benefit I thought you should know). They also pack REALLY well. I just roll them up and they barely take up any space in my suitcase. Also the faux leather is a good quality. It looks and feels better than the average fake leather on boots.

Cons: they just don't look superb on me. I have what my friends and family lovingly refer to as \\"chicken legs\\" and these boots are more suited for a wider leg. They are fine for a casual slouchy look, but the foot is way too wide for mine and it just doesn't do much for my body. I think they would be great on a thicker leg. Also, as I have worn them, the heel has gotten pushed up into the body of the shoe so I'm now walking on the faux-leather outer.

All in all, I have to say I was pleasantly surprised for the price and would definitely buy them again since I have put them through so much abuse and they have held up rather well.

product_title: Robeez Soft Soles Baby Dragon Crib Shoe (Infant/Toddler)
review_body:
My son likes to look at and touch the tops of his dragon shoes and we always get nice comments when he wears them. These are sturdy but children can still feel the surface beneath them, which helps new walkers keep balance. My only qualm is that the elastic is very tight. I know this is meant to secure the shoes, but it leaves red indents on the ankles. My solution was to remove the existing elastic and replace it with a longer piece to make the shoe opening looser. It's an inexpensive and relatively easy way to customize the shoe.

How to:
Attach new elastic to existing elastic by sewing a stitch, hot glueing, or using a small pin. Pull the old elastic through, which will thread the new elastic into the loop. Detach old elastic. Measure you child's foot to find a good fit and mark where to cut the elastic. You can either sew or hot glue gun the ends of the elastic together. Hide the seam under the shoe fabric. Voila, tailor made shoes for your little kiddo.

product_title: ASICS Men's GEL-Kayano 18 Running Shoe
review_headline: Oh ASICS you have won me over
review_body:
I have been wearing ASICS for the better part of a decade now and I must say that i truly love the brand. They are very well made high quality running shoes. In particular I have loved the GEL-Kayano models and have owned them since model 13 and up. The are very comfortable and make a great sneaker for running or casual wear. They provide great cushion and arch support for your feet. The shoe laces are top notch and won't fray as I have had happen on all too many Nike brands. I have also found that these sneakers run true to size unlike some other manufacturers which might run a little smaller or narrower.

The only complaint I have about these shoes is that the frontal mesh just on top of the toes can get dirty quite quickly. Since it is a breathable mesh designed to let air flow freely it really does absorb a lot of dirt especially in wet weather. I have tried various cleaning products and methods but the fact is once the mesh becomes tainted its the beginning of the end.

However, most of the time when I buy a new pair of ASICS its not because of how the shoe has held but rather they just become so raggedy I'd rather not wear them. (I am vain what can I say). I want to stress though this is no way an indicator of the quality of these shoes. At any given point I still have my three previous pairs in my closet for messy work (i.e. painting, lawn mowing, mud trekking) just because I can't bring my self to throw away perfectly good running shoes. I highly recommend the ASICS brand and in particular the GEL-Kayano series.

product_title: Saucony Women's Triumph 10 Running Shoe
review_headline: The answer to my running prayers!
review_body:
I just started running again after many years, so I needed a new running shoe. I had heard that the new Skechers running shoes were good, so I gave them a try. Loved them at first, but after about two weeks and 20 miles run, my knees were killing me. And I mean BAD, like I could barely walk after a run, and to compound matters, walking was almost as bad! Many people recommended a different shoe, so off to the internet I went, and after much research decided a Saucony shoe was the one for me. I actually ordered 4 pairs in different models to give a few a try. I tried the Ride 5, and it was better than the Skechers, but not awesome. Tried the Kinvara 3, and loved, loved the colors, but it was a little tight in the toe. Tried the Omni 11 and took it right off, didn't even give it a trial on the treadmill. Last box was the Triumph 10, and when I opened it I wanted to cry. Like another reviewer mentioned, these may be the fat girl at the bar line of shoes, they are just not as pretty as some of the other Saucony's, not nearly the best color combos ( I went with the navy, white, aqua color). But then I put them on, and it was like angels singing! They were SO comfy, I couldn't believe it! Took a trial on the treadmill, and after a mile NO pain. The next day did 2 miles, still no pain! I have had these for about a week now, done about 15 miles, and I still feel great, my knees have absolutely no pain at all! I did have to get past their terrible color, they felt like a boys shoe, but the other color combos were way worse. At my hubby 's suggestion I bought some festive laces, and they cute them up a bit, so I am happy with them now. I highly recommend these for anyone with knee or hip pain, they are a dream, but hope Saucony will give us some better color, May I suggest the pink/citron/white combo, that one is the bomb!

UPDATE: I have now been in these shoes for 4 months and just hit the 100 mile mark on them, and they are still doing an awesome job for me!! Just started training for a 1/2 marathon last month, so I know I will need a new pair in 2 or 3 months, and was so stoked to see that they just released these in some new colors!! I am so glad, because I was going to try another style just to get a better choice, but the Triumph 10's in either the purple/silver/green or pink/citron are gonna be on my feet soon, no doubt!! Even with my increased running for my training, these are still a dream. I do think I will size up 1/2 a size in my next pair, but other than that these are perfect!!me!! product_title: Vibram FiveFingers Bikila LS Running Shoe - Women's
review_headline: Frog Shoes but I love them!
review_body:
I have a size 40 Lime Women's Bikila. I have had them for over a year and I have put a few hundred miles on them. They are a little silly looking; people definitely notice them and most people think they look a little strange. However, the advantages of these shoes make it worth looking a little pretentious on the trail.

I have plantar factitious to the degree that I am sometimes unable to walk. It gets especially bad when I run frequently which I really enjoy doing. As a last resort I tried the five fingers and I have to say that it was an almost instant cure. There is some adjustment to the shoe and you should not take off on a 10 mile run your first day but once I ran in mine I never put another pair of runners on again.

I have never worn socks with mine and I would not recommend socks. I have occasionally put a little baby powder in mine because it is easier to slip them on that way but I have not had a shoe or foot odor problem from not wearing socks.

They wash in the washing machine and I wash them about once a month.

I have recently purchased my second pair of five-fingers and I went with a different style but only because I wanted it to cover less of my foot. I just though it might be easier to get on and off.

My only complaint about the shoe is that the sole has worn down quickly and there is a hole in a toe already. I can still wear them and I feel that I am getting the same protection since you are really not depending upon the sole to do anything other than protect your foot from the concrete. Still I had been led to believe that these things can last for years and that they don't wear out. If you are a concrete runner; they will wear down just like any other shoe. The difference is that as they wear down you do not lose the advantage of the shoe. I have about 350 miles on my shoes and they work fine but they are showing their wear. I get about 200 miles on a pair of Nike running shoesand they start causing pain and injury even though I can't see any real signs of wear.

I highly recommend this shoe for anyone with foot problems but you do need to try them on in a store first.

ALso; the nylon Fila shoes (four-fingers) are NOT the same shoe. They are nice too; I have a pair for the lake and I feel that they protect my feet in the same way but the nylon fabric is too hot to use it as a runner. The weave material on the five-finger shoes is perfect for keeping the foot comfortable.

product_title: HICKIES Elastic No Tie Shoelaces
review_body:
I stumbled onto Hickies while searching online for elastic laces for a pair of Chuck Taylor's that my 2-year-old got for Christmas I bought two packs - one for her shoes and one for my son's school shoes since no laces ever stay tied for 5-year-olds. Each pack had two free-bie Hickies in different colors other than the colors that I ordered.

I can't say enough good things about them! They keep my daughter's shoes on and my son loves that he doesn't have to stop and tie his shoes several times per day! He just wore out a pair of school sneakers so I just put the same hickies in a new pair of sneakers. They're a little worn looking, but they are still holding up great after two months of wear. I even put them in my crossfit workout shoes by Inov8. No more stopping in the middle of my WOD to tie a shoe!

I agree with other reviews that you may not want to put a Hickie in the top most lace holes because it may feel too tight. I also don't put them in the bottom holes so that I have extra for other shoes. I am looking forward to buying at least two more packs!

product_title: Teva Men's Verdon Mid-Height Waterproof Hiking Boot
review_headline: About one size too small here
review_body:
I was looking for a waterproof, lightweight hiking boot that would be comfortable all day in wet, rocky conditions. The Teva Verdon Mid Boot fit my needs very well.

My first requirement was that they were waterproof, because I'll be getting them wet a lot and sometimes in the middle of winter. So far, I've had no problem keeping my socks dry.

My second requirement was that they were lightweight for comfort, and although I actually preferred more of a shoe, the Verdon is actually like a shoe, but with ankle protection (i.e. it has little ankle support, but protects the ankle against abrasions.) While the Verdon may not be the lightest, most comfortable boot, it is very good for a waterproof hiking boot. Overall, it's very comfortable while wearing all day and it fits my foot very well.

My third requirement was that they have a rigid sole for stability on pointed, rocky surfaces. These are real hiking boots, and not trail shoes, so the sole is quite rigid. You probably won't find a sole this rigid on a less expensive lightweight hiking boot. I don't worry about twisting my ankles on rocks in the Teva Verdon, as I do in the less expensive models found in large department stores.

I think the big issue with this boot is problems with sizing. Well, I own a lot of shoes and know my size very well, thanks to experience in numerous different brands. Still, I read dozens of reviews before ordering the Verdon and the verdict seemed to be to size up anywhere between one-half to two full sizes. Despite STP recommendations to go up one-half size, I went up a full size and it fit perfectly: if it were any smaller, then my toe would be touching the tip of the boot. My most common size is an 11 US, although my foot falls in between a 10.5-11 in most shoes, so it's not common that I size all the way up to a 12. If you normally wear an 11 like me, but fall more in between an 11-11.5, then you might want to size up one and one-half sizes, toa 12.5. In addition to the short length, they're also a little wide, although not so much that my foot slides around and the low depth in the toe box keeps them snug to my foot.

The arch support is adequate, but there's something about the design of the sole that leaves me wanting more. Still, I think it's actually more than adequate and it doesn't cause any problems for me.

Sizing issues aside, I think it's a well-built lightweight hiking boot that will last me for a long time. It's comfortable and it looks quite nice, too. So, I'm very satisfied with the Teva Verdon.

product_title: MBT Women's Pia Sandal
review_headline: Cute is not a word generaly used in association with MBT shoes, but these are...
review_body: I live in MBT shoes, and have for several years. I had read about them, but when a co-worker said they had relieved the foot and knee pain that is a professional hazard for nurses, I decided to shell-out the $260 for the Womans Sport.  They were ugly, but made an immediate difference in my ability to get through the day.. Since nursing shoes aren't glamorous anyway, that was not an concern. There weren't very many styles available then, and only a few stores in Houston carried them.  The only sandals available were the Kisumus. I have always been a shoe person, and I love cute shoes, but  I bought those ugly things because I wanted to be able to walk comfortably.  I took them on a trip to Hawaii in 2005 (along with my other fashionable shoes), and I have them on in almost every picture.  I still wear them, but I'm glad that now there are several that look more mainstream.  These and the Sadiki are the nicest looking sandals they have made.  I wear an 8.5 in American sizing and this brand tends to run a little small,so I ordered the 40, which maybe a little large, but I'm keeping them cuz they're going to be hard to find.  The strap around the ankle is a litte high and stiff, but I got on the treadmill for an hour to see if it was going to give me trouble. It didn't.  Now I'm looking at all the other sales on MBTs to stock up.. Thanks goodness they last so long.  I don't know what I'm going to do once they are no longer available.  Maybe I'll be ready for the scooter store.

product_title: Scarleton Large Shoulder Bag H1066
review_body: When I ordered this bag, I was very excited. I was looking forward to having a roomy bag with multiple compartments. The bag itself was everything promised. It had the two outer pockets for easy access on either end (they don't stay closed very well, so don't put anything too valuable there), compartments front and back, an interior zipper pocket, and interior open pockets for pens and other accessories. Be warned, this is a floppy bag. If you want a bag with structure that will stand on its own, this is probably not the bag for you. My biggest disappointment was with the color. The disclaimer about the pictures said, \\"Please note: actual color may vary from picture due to computer settings.\\" In light of this, I viewed the item across multiple devices. All of the devices on which I viewed the photos showed a dark gray bag. I understood that there may have been shade variations and was okay with the bag being slightly lighter than the pictures showed. The bag that I received was not a dark gray. It was not even just a shade or two off the picture. The bag that I received was a very light gray, a completely different color than what was shown. Had I known what the color actually was, I would have chosen a different bag. I believe that the seller needs to update this picture to be a more realistic representation of what this bag looks like. I do not believe that the color settings on all of the devices on which I viewed this item are so far off as to render the pictures of this bag a completely different color than the color the bag actually was. In the end, I opted to keep the bag; it is a little funky, which makes it fun. However, as I was not looking for a \\"fun\\" bag, I did have to go out and buy a bag that would work for what I originally needed this one to.

product_title: Thorogood Men's I-Met Technology Super I-Met Boot
review_body: Before ordering this boot, I attempted to find reviews online but could only find one, so here's some good input. Fit appears true to size.  Break-in is not immediate, but not painful either (except some shin/calf pressure), and they actually feel good as they encapsulate my feet.  These boots are built for real men, doing real work in tough conditions.  They are good solid protection, heavy and stable; just what a real boot should be.  They are waterproof and have Thinsulate 200, so are warm in the cold, but are not overly hot on mild days.  I wear them all day at work in all weather, walking on pavement, cement, steel and climbing up and down machinery.  I also often wear them on weekends, just because they are so comfortable and solid.  When I plant my foot someplace, it stays planted until I choose to move it.  No slipping, no wobbling; just firm grip.  I would buy another pair of these boots in a heartbeat, but I can't foresee this pair wearing out any year soon.

review_headline: Good shoe, not sure why it's so expensive.
review_body:
Overall this is a good shoe. It's got a lot of forefoot flex and still has enough cushioning for people who run distance. There's enough rubber on the bottom that it's durable and pretty versatile if you want to do more than run in it (pickup football, etc.). It's also priced really high for what seems like a pretty normal shoe to me. I feel like for $130+ I should be able to get rocket packs on my shoes or something, but I haven't gotten hurt in it that's pretty important.

If you decide to buy this shoe (or any New Balance shoe) make sure you get the right width. I had a different pair of New Balances when I started boot camp, and after a couple days my arches started hurting really badly. I exchanged for these and made sure to insist that I got them sized right (I ended up with a 2E width) and I haven't had any problems since.

product_title: Demonia Women's Funn19/B/PU Platform Sandal
review_body: I love these platform sandals. They are super lightweight and very easy to walk in unlike some other platforms that are made with better materials but ultimately are clunky and difficult to walk in. I bought these last summer and found them to be so comfortable, cute and easy to wear that I wore them constantly until it became too cold to wear them outside. Even then, I wore them around the house for months afterword as house slippers. My only complaints are that, due to the cheap materials used to make these, they tend to wear out rather easily if you wear them often but at such a cheap price, it's not unjustifiable to buy another pair. The Demonia tags on the insoles are actually just stickers and they began to slide around the insole not long after I began wearing them. Fortunately, you can just peel them off at that point and remove the sticker residue easily. I usually wear a size 7 1/2 shoes or 7 for sandals but bought a size 8 after seeing other reviewers say that these run too small. I didn't find that to be true though and I kind of regret not getting a size 7 after all. The 8s wear a bit lose and I found my heels sliding towards the arch and my toes starting to tip over the edges in the front. That might have been due to the straps loosening from wear but they started out pretty close to that too. Perhaps there are inconsistencies in this model that make the sizes vary from batch to batch? If I buy these again (and I mostly likely will) I'll go with my true sandal size and hope for a bit of a better fit. I also should mention that I have narrow feet but other reviewers also said they had narrow feet and still found their size was too small in these. Go figure.

review_headline: Great shoe for a great price
review_body:
one of my friends were wearing a pair of these and my girlfriend immediately noticed how minimal they were and wanted a pair. We got on amazon and found them and she fell in love with the grey and pink ones.

I ordered these and had them overnighted, they shipped and got to my house the next day. The quality of the shoe is certainly there and noticeable, even though they are made from recycled parts they are well made shoes. The stitching is double and the sole is soft but firm enough to not wear away in a few months.
They are definitely lightweight, there isn't much padding, and the material is almost like a mix between a soft rubber and an older felt covering. It is hard to pinpoint, but it does scream durability.

I only had two complaints for these shoes, the first is that they do not offer any wide sizes. They are a narrow shoe, be aware. The toe area seems to have plenty of room but through the arch in the food it narrows significantly. Also the shoe doesn't have the standard shape of a walking or tennis shoe, it is more of a lightweight sprinting shoe. It seems to taper to the inside of the arch and promote walking on the balls of the feet. This is not necessarily an issue for some people, but my girlfriend found it a little frustrating.

We did end up sending these back because they felt a little tight, although with the material I think they would've worn in perfectly, but coupled with the way the shoe tapers towards the arch she didn't want to give it a try. I would not let this hinder your decision though, the shoes are fantastic quality, look great (cute), and even if you don't like them return them to amazon at no cost to yourself and have your refund in a couple days.

product_title: The Original MuckBoots Adult Cikana Boot
review_body:
Pros: Supremely comfortable!

Cons: Not highly durable; soles can slip

I've owned the same pair of MuckBoots Cikana boots since 2005. I used them almost exclusively for offshore fishing on sport boats out of Southern and Baja California. So when Amazon offered the Cikana boots for ~$50 off retail recently, I had to jump on getting another pair to use when my current pair gives up the ghost. Fishing boots are known mainly for utility, not comfort..but the Cikana is nearly the best of both worlds, at least for my use. The footbeds are soft and well cushioned. The uppers offer plenty of room for wide and/or tall feet, unlike some other popular fishing boots out there. I replaced the stock insoles with a pair of Orange Superfeet insoles.

The fact that the Cikana boot is comfortable and lightweight likely leads to the cons I listed. The rubber sole seems quite soft and wears out rather quickly. That's not a glaring negative for me since I'm not wearing the boots 365 days a year. In fact, I maybe get in 25 days of wear per year if I'm lucky, which is why my first pair of Cikanas have lasted so long. The wear issues, however, lead to the other con - lack of traction. Even new, the tread design didn't offer superb traction. At times, I would feel the soles slip on a smooth, wet surface. Luckily, the boats I ride tend to not have too many smooth walking surfaces. But wet surfaces, uh, yeah! So I found I needed to be more careful when wearing these boots on-board if I was walking near a hatch cover or other surfaces that were smooth or non-textured.

My final rating is 4.5 stars. If your usage conditions are similar to mine, you will love the Cikanas. But I'm going with the Amazon rating of 4 to err on the side of caution due to the durability and traction issues I've experienced.

product_title: Allen Edmonds Men's Combination Cedar Shoe Tree
review_headline: A must-have for preserving the life of your shoes
review_body:
Cedar shoe trees are amazing and have two very important functions.

First, the cedar wood absorbs bad shoe odor and moisture, while keeps your leather fresh and healthy. Leftover moisture can lead to bacterial growth, which will only exaggerate any odors you may have already left from a day's wear.

Second, the tension created by the trees keep the shoes from \\"wilting.\\" When left to sit on their own, shoes will start drooping/sagging from the top down, leaving more noticeable creases. The heels also tend to sink down and bulge out from the back.

I can't compare these trees to any other models specifically, but these have done an awesome job keeping my leathers in shape. Well worth the money.

product_title: Enzo Angiolini Women's Cimino Pump
review_body: I'd read the other reviews before purchasing this shoe in an 8-1/2. I fluctuate between 8 and 8-1/2 but based on what I'd read, I went with the 8-1/2, especially because of the pointed toe. Speaking of which, many others noted that the toe box is a great fit and not at all cramped - as with moist pointed-toe shoes. And they're absolutely right! Well, the 8-1/2 was a little big and I tried putting in heel guards but they didn't work. Plus the gap between my heel and the back of the shoe was too noticeable. My feet kept slipping out. So I returned them for a smaller size 8. (Thanks, Amazon, for making the exchange process so incredibly easy and fast!) The result: Perfection! This is a well-made shoe. I'm personally not used to wearing such high, narrow heels - it's been years - so it will take getting used to (I recommend practicing wearing them on non-slip surfaces before venturing out if you're not used to heels like this). The detail in the back of the shoe is even nicer in person. Several people complained that the color shown isn't true to the real color. To those people, I say you're right, but that's the nature of how colors work on digital devices. I'm a photographer and graphic artist, and I can tell you that it's extremely rare for a product to match a merchant's website image. Your monitor also has a lot to do with color perception, as well as color space, rendering, color and monitor calibration, and so on. Not to get techie; I'm just saying it's not the webmaster's/Amazon's/merchant's fault. It's meant to be an approximation. If you need to know the exact color, go to a brick-and-mortar store. That said.... the actual shoe color - as compared to my own computer's rendition - is more of a light beige (a little darker that what you probably see on screen). But no worries there either - the color is rich and beautiful, very neutral, will work well with almost anything you wear (except grays). I actually like the real color better than the website color. So.... the toe cup is comfy, the shoe is well made and comfy once you get used to that narrow high heel, and suede is good quality. I can't wait to kick up my heels with them (they just arrived today, so they'll have to wait a bit.) I'll try to update after I've actually worn them, to see how long my feet feel good in them, but all indications so far show that they're a winner!.. the toe cup is comfy, the shoe is well made and comfy once you get used to that narrow high heel, and suede is good quality. I can't wait to kick up my heels with them (they just arrived today, so they'll have to wait a bit.) I'll try to update after I've actually worn them, to see how long my feet feel good in them, but all indications so far show that they're a winner!

product_title: Dearfoams Plush Velour Closed-Back Women’s Slipper – Padded Microfiber Slip-Ons with a Durable Outsole - 745
review_body:
I had just about given up hope of finding any such thing online as an \\"orthopedic-type\\" slipper with a regular back and without the painful elastic sewn around the top when my general search spotted this slipper. I can't believe I didn't come here first, because I've been a long-time, happy Amazon customer of a variety of (non-clothing) items.
My feet are sensitive and sore right now and I must wear socks to bed due to the cream I'm using and of course do not want to get it on the slippers. Therefore, I'm hoping these Dearfoams will fit better at the toe soon. They already do seem to be stretching out a little bit after one week. (I generally wear a 7-1/2 shoe, so I thought the size 8 would work.) BTW, I did notice something strange about the sizing during the order process. On the description page in the sizing window, the choices were S(6), M(8), etc. Yet as soon as I put the item into my cart, that window changed the size I'd ordered to: M (7-8). The store display-type hanger attached to the slippers also says \\"dearfoams M 7-8\\". It's just a shame the sizing problem is causing such confusion for us online shoppers. But -- at least with this particular slipper -- the fabric quality, color (blue), style, side fit and padding are all fine. Oh, and the price was right as well!

product_title: UGG Women's Adirondack Boot II (Pineneedle 7.5 M)
review_body:
A couple of years ago, I bought a fantastic pair of expensive hiking boots. I loved them--until I finally wore them in below-freezing temps (below zero, even). While being completely warm everywhere and with waterproof boots on, inevitably my feet would sweat while hiking through snow with snowshoes on and, in turn, would eventually freeze. It's always very miserable with frozen feet.

Since then, I've been on the lookout for a truly insulated boot that is still waterproof and has actual breathability.

So far, the Adirondack fits the bill. I'll admit, I haven't had a chance to go traipsing through zero degree temps with them yet, but the bit of everyday testing I've put these boots through in our cold and snowy weather seem to make the cut so far: very warm, insulated, and quite dry. I am ALWAYS complaining about cold feet with all kinds of boots so I'm extremely pleased so far.

FYI, on the safe side, I sprayed the boots with a couple of coats of Scotch Guard.

As for the fit, while I've never had my feet officially sized but after trying on shoes over the years, I'm under the impression that I have a slightly narrow foot but that has never stopped me from wearing anything with a "normal" width. My foot fits a size 7 best but my long toes fit better in size 7.5 closed shoes. So far, my toes do just lightly touch the toe box but comfortably so with medium weight socks on--it likely will touch less as the padding becomes slightly compressed over time. Since I have a higher arch than the average person (I LOVE wearing Chaco and Sanita shoes), I wouldn't mind additional arch support but that should be easy enough to fix by slipping something under the removable insole if needed.

Regarding looks, it's definitely more "feminine" than my other pair hiking boots--they're not as bulky and much more flexible. I merely went with the pineneedle color based on price (close to $100 less than the more popular color choices). It's a bit more green than I was expecting but I really like the overall look of the boot.

Overall? Easily a 5-star rating from this cold-footed girl in Montana.

product_title: Lucky Women's Aaid Boot
review_headline: I guess I'm the odd one out
review_body:
I'm a huge Lucky Brand fan but I was quite disappointed in the Aaid.

I need another pair of black moto boots like I need a hole in the head. But the girl can't help it. Since the majority of online reviews seemed positive and since I don't own many square-toed boots, I sprung on these at sale price.

But...straight out of the box I wasn't impressed with the leather. LB has some pretty beautiful leather shoes in this same price range but guess they skimped a bit here. The leather is thin and a bit shiny in places yet cheap and dull in other spots. Plus, the hardware embellishment is flimsy and not unlike what you'd find on a shoe 1/2 this price. Payless quality basically, IMO. I found a review on another site that mentioned how thin the leather was so perhaps this boot suffers from some inconsistency in quality.

But the overall style is cute enough so what about fit? I'm usually a 8.5 in most flat boots; I ordered the 8.5 and these were TTS, length wise. However, I found them oddly wide at the heel (they slip w/each step) but oddly tight in the middle and over the in-step. (And I have neither a wide foot nor a high instep/arch). The toe box itself is decently roomy, and perhaps they'd stretch out a bit over the the in-step but I can't see someone with a wide-ish foot finding these remotely comfy. If you're planning on wearing winter socks, I'd order a 1/2 size up.

The out sole is rugged, but soft; no clunky noise as you walk. The insole offers decent support but prolly not enough for a long day out. The shaft circumference on my average calves was more than roomy--any more gaping and they'd venture into galoshes territory...tho w/o a side zip they kinda had to be cut generously. The ample space is nice if you need to tuck in thicker pants. And I'm a fan of the 10 in high shaft-- a really versatile height for many looks.

But with the fit so wonky and the leather just 'meh', these are going back. I'm comparing them to similarly priced moto inspired boots I love like Betsey Johnson in Ariss and Kickers in Trestrep. I'll still search for a good square toe option (and certainly won't abandon my beloved LB), but the Aaid ain't it.to similarly priced moto inspired boots I love like Betsey Johnson in Ariss and Kickers in Trestrep. I'll still search for a good square toe option (and certainly won't abandon my beloved LB), but the Aaid ain't it.

review_headline: Interchangeable lenses are the way to go!
review_body:
I love these glasses. I've worn Bolle for 15 years, and the \\"Parole\\" style for 10 of those years. During that time I've always had a set of TNS gun (neutral gray), cinnamon, and clear; I've also had the vermillion lenses, as well as the weird blue tennis lenses and the red-rose too. There's a use for all of those different lenses, but for my money the BEST combination is the TNS Gun for sunny days, the cinnamon for overcast, and the clear for dark conditions.

The reason may be obvious, but it's surprising to me that more people don't do this: interchangeable lenses mean you get to wear the right lens for the specific situation you encounter.

And, with the clear lenses, it's as another reviewer reported: at night, wearing clear glasses helps keep the bugs out of your eyes! I used to ride my bike as part of my commute, and I'd be going around 20 mph at 4:30 in the morning. There is nothing like taking a bug in the eye to ruin your concentration...

The \\"Parole\\" style is a tad smaller than the \\"Vigilante\\" style. I wear a 6 1/4 hat, and the \\"Parole\\" style fits me perfectly. If you have a larger nugget, you might want to consider the \\"Vigilante.\\" Either way, these sunglasses WORK, for just about any outdoor activity you might want to pursue.

review_headline: Classic cold weather waterproof boots, unbeatable for what they are
review_body:
Eleven things you need to know about these Sorel 1964 Premium T Canvas Boots

1) This is a harsh weather boot. It's treated canvas and rubber, and it's waterproof. It's felt lined and it's very warm, even in very cold conditions. This is a boot suitable for use in places like Minnesota, Canada, and upstate New York...that is, places where you get a lot of snow, and where you need a boot that won't leak and will keep your feet warm. You can, of course, wear these in places it doesn't snow--the boot won't complain. But you may find that these boots are too warm to use as kicks on the streets of San Diego or Florida, even during a torrential downpour.

2) This boot isn't very stylish. Well, perhaps, it's stylish in an old jeans, flannel shirt, arctic cap and my boots sort of way. But you will want to change these out if you wear them to a formal office. You wouldn't want to wear these on a nice date. Etc. They are what they are: Function over style. And that's kind of chic in and of itself. But it's not chic in a \\"ooh...nice looking boots\\" way.

3) This model boot has been made for nearly half a century. So they are classic in a sense.

4) These boots were once made in Canada. Not any longer. Bowing to financial realities (like almost every mass market shoe maker), Sorel now has these made in China. The quality is still good, however.

5) Everyone who lives in a place where you get appreciable snow should own a pair of these. Your stylish boots are for when the snow has cleared and the skies are bright. These are the work boots when you need to clear the snow, or walk a mile to somewhere in bad weather. Think of these as the boots that save your stylish boots.

6) These run slightly long and wide (probably the equivalent of a EE or even EEEE for most shoes). They are intentionally sized this way to accommodate a thick sock. They are not svelte looking--think fashionable duck feet.

7) The lower part of these shoes is fairly stiff and heavy rubber--and will remain that way. These will never be the most comfortable shoes you own for simple walking.

8) This same design is available with a leather (rather than treated canvas) upper, here [[ASIN:B0037267QO Sorel Men's 1964 Premium T Boot]], for basically the same price. The leather doesn't make the boot any more attractive, and it makes the upper stiffer and less comfortable (at least until broken in, although arguably forever). I prefer the canvas. Everything else written here about these boots applies to both models.

9) The soles are ribbed and are fine for snow. They are OK, but not incredible, when walking on slick ice.

10) These shoes have very little arch support. The fit is very similar to a traditional sneaker like Converse high tops. If you need arch support, you will need to buy inserts.

11) Buy them. They will last for years.of these shoes is fairly stiff and heavy rubber--and will remain that way. These will never be the most comfortable shoes you own for simple walking.

product_title: Mizuno Women's Wave Musha 4 Running Shoe
review_headline: Not the best shoe I've had
review_body: I purchased a pair of Mizuno Wave Musha 4s on October 24, 2012. I've been running 20-25 miles a week for about two years. I'm a smaller woman (5'3\\", 115lbs.) and love the minimalist type of shoe. I was coming from wearing a Saucony Kinvara 2 that had over 300 miles on them and still kicking. I purchased the Wave Musha and began rotating it into my runs by alternating shoes during runs. However, I didn't fall in love with the shoe right away, but thought I had finally struck a decent balance sometime in mid-December. However, just over 2 months after purchasing the shoe, I went for a 5 mile treadmill run and had some slight hip pain/tightness. I slowed my run, stretched, and even walked for a bit around mile 2.5. I finished the run, but pulled out my old shoes to try for a run today to see if my hip was the problem or the shoe. I put in 3.1 miles on the treadmill at a pace a bit faster than yesterday with absolutely no issues. I read on Mizuno's website about how to tell by physically examining the shoe midsole if a shoe's life is over. Sadly, it seems that not even 200 miles in my $100 shoes have met their maker. I'm disappointed, frustrated, and sad to be running-shoeless just over two months from purchasing a brand new pair. This was my first pair of Mizunos and I suppose it will be my last. This product has not met my expectations.

product_title: Wolverine Men's W02363 Amphibian Work Boot
review_body:
I first bought a size 10.5 medium (equiv. to about a "C" or "D" width) because another reviewer said he bought his a half size larger and used heavy socks. I tried this, but even with heavier socks, they were too long/loose. The size 10's fit very nicely and seem to run pretty much true to standard size, or if anything are a tad larger than standard sizing.

They fit great right out of the box, and are surprisingly warm. I did some work out in my wet backyard - not exactly puddle jumping, but with my former boots, my shoes and socks would be very wet and with these, completely dry. Good supportive construction. The only downside (minor) is the lacing system: It's a little awkward to cinch up the shoe and to loosen prior to taking off, due to a side-mounted lace holder/clasp device that is found just before the top eyelet. It takes a little effort to get the lace inserted into that side holder. (It's kind of difficult to describe) Perhaps it will get easier as I wear them.

The lightweight carbon-fiber toe is a real great improvement over the standard heavy steel toe. Although I'm not in construction so I seldom need a crush-proof toe, its not at all noticeable and will likely be a real benefit when it IS needed.
